categories.definition: Platforms for building and running AI agents that plan and take actions across business systems with limited human involvement.
categories.name: AI agent platforms
riskIssues: Agents act with more authority than intended
There is no reliable record of what an agent did and why
Agents chain together tools and data in ways nobody reviewed

trajectoryNotes.summary: Salesforce agreed to acquire Convergence.ai, a start-up founded in 2024 that builds task-automation agents, to advance its Agentforce platform, as reported by CIO Dive on 15 May 2025. Terms were not disclosed and Salesforce expected the deal to close in its fiscal quarter ending 31 July 2025.

Automation Anywhere announced it would acquire Aisera, which builds self-service AI agents for IT service management, HR and customer service, as reported by KMWorld on 6 November 2025; the report gave no price or closing date.

ServiceNow announced on 15 December 2025 that it had completed its acquisition of Moveworks, maker of an employee AI assistant, enterprise search and a reasoning engine for agentic AI. The completion release did not state a price.

UiPath announced on 6 February 2026 that it had acquired WorkFusion, whose pre-built AI agents handle first-level analyst work in financial crime compliance, including sanctions-screening alert review, adverse media monitoring, KYC and transaction-monitoring investigations. Terms were not disclosed.

NIST's Center for AI Standards and Innovation launched the AI Agent Standards Initiative on 17 February 2026, with three strands: supporting industry-led agent standards, encouraging community-led open-source agent protocols, and research on agent security and identity. Alongside it NIST sought input through a request for information on AI agent security (due 9 March) and a concept paper on agent identity and authorisation (due 2 April).

categories.definition: Tools that use AI to write, review and change software alongside or on behalf of developers.
categories.name: AI coding assistants
riskIssues: Proprietary source code is sent to a third party
AI-written code introduces vulnerabilities or licence problems
Autonomous coding agents run commands with developer privileges

trajectoryNotes.summary: Cognition, maker of the Devin coding agent, signed a definitive agreement on 14 July 2025 to acquire Windsurf's product, IP, brand and employees; Cognition's announcement put Windsurf at US$82 million in annual recurring revenue with more than 350 enterprise customers. No price was given.

Tricentis, an enterprise software-testing company, acquired Tabnine, one of the earliest commercial AI coding assistants, as reported by CTech on 31 July 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed; CTech estimated the price at tens of millions of dollars and noted Tabnine had raised US$55 million.

Cursor announced on 14 August 2026 that its acquisition by SpaceX was complete, ending a process it said began with a model-training partnership in April. The Next Web reported the price as US$60 billion and said Cursor's legal entity remains Anysphere.

Cognition raised more than US$2 billion in a Series E led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel at a US$48 billion valuation, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 8 September 2026. That was close to double the US$26 billion valuation of its round in May 2026, and the company put run-rate revenue near US$900 million.

categories.definition: Services that supply the specialised computing capacity on which AI models are trained and run, as a cloud service or dedicated capacity.
categories.name: AI compute and inference services
riskIssues: AI workloads concentrate on a few providers and chip suppliers
Young providers carry heavy debt and customer concentration
Data and models sit in facilities the bank has not assessed

trajectoryNotes.summary: CoreWeave priced its initial public offering on 27 March 2025 at US$40.00 per share for 37.5 million Class A shares, with trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker CRWV starting 28 March 2025.

Together AI raised a US$800 million Series C led by Aramco Ventures at a US$8.3 billion valuation, with Nvidia among the participants, as reported by TechCrunch on 1 July 2026; its previous round, about 16 months earlier, valued it at US$3.3 billion.

Fireworks AI closed a US$1.5 billion Series D at a US$17.5 billion valuation, led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV with Nvidia among the other backers, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 16 July 2026.

Groq raised US$350 million led by Disruptive at a US$3.5 billion valuation, down from US$6.9 billion in September 2025, as reported by TechCrunch on 17 August 2026. TechCrunch described the company as having moved from making its own inference chips to operating data centres running Nvidia systems, after Nvidia hired its founder and other staff in a licensing deal.

NVIDIA announced on 3 September 2026 that it had agreed to acquire the model hub Hugging Face for US$12.93 billion. NVIDIA's post said Hugging Face would stay an open platform on which developers can use any model, cloud, inference provider or computing platform, and that NVIDIA compute would not be required.

categories.definition: Databases and data services built for AI workloads, especially storing and searching the embeddings that let models retrieve relevant enterprise content.
categories.name: AI data infrastructure
riskIssues: Sensitive content is copied into a new store with weaker access control
Retrieval quality limits answer quality and is hard to measure
A young vendor holds a core dependency

trajectoryNotes.summary: MongoDB announced on 24 February 2025 that it had acquired Voyage AI, a developer of embedding and reranking models used for retrieval, and said it would integrate the models with its database. The release did not state a price.

Databricks announced on 14 May 2025 that it had agreed to acquire Neon, a serverless Postgres company, subject to customary closing conditions. The release said more than 80 percent of databases provisioned on Neon were created by AI agents and gave no price.

Open-source vector search company Qdrant raised a US$50 million Series B led by AVP, with Bosch Ventures, Unusual Ventures, Spark Capital and 42CAP participating, bringing total funding to US$87.8 million, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 12 March 2026.

Ricoh's corporate venture fund, the RICOH Innovation Fund, invested in vector database company Weaviate in a round announced in March 2026, as reported by Dealroom News on 16 June 2026; the amount was not disclosed. Ricoh plans to pair its document-capture technology with Weaviate's database.

categories.definition: Platforms that keep an inventory of an organisation's models and AI use cases, apply policy and approval workflows to them, record validation and testing evidence, and report on the result to risk committees and supervisors.
categories.name: AI governance and model risk management
riskIssues: Models and AI use cases are in production without a complete inventory
Model validation and approval evidence is scattered and hard to produce for supervisors
Third-party and generative AI models enter the bank outside model-risk processes
New AI regulation requires risk classification and documentation the bank cannot yet produce

trajectoryNotes.summary: AuditBoard reached a definitive agreement to acquire San Diego-based AI governance platform FairNow, as reported on 24 October 2025; terms were not disclosed.

The Federal Reserve, OCC and FDIC issued revised model risk management guidance (SR 26-2) that supersedes SR 11-7 and SR 21-8 and takes a risk-based approach. According to Orrick's analysis, generative and agentic AI models are excluded from its scope, it is most relevant to organisations with over $30 billion in assets, and the agencies plan a request for information covering banks' use of AI.

The Council of the EU gave final approval to a regulation amending the AI Act as part of the Omnibus VII simplification package. It moves the application of high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 for stand-alone high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk systems embedded in products; these obligations had been due in August 2026.
Collibra announced the acquisition of trail ML, a Munich-based AI governance company founded in 2023 whose agents automate framework mapping and control assessment; terms were not disclosed.

categories.definition: Products that record what AI applications are asked and what they return, measure quality and safety, and alert when behaviour drifts.
categories.name: AI observability and evaluation
riskIssues: The bank cannot show what its AI systems said to customers
Quality degrades silently after a model or prompt change
Evaluation is manual and not repeatable

trajectoryNotes.summary: CoreWeave, a GPU cloud provider, agreed to acquire the AI developer platform Weights & Biases, as reported by TechCrunch on 4 March 2025. The price was not disclosed; TechCrunch cited a report by The Information of US$1.7 billion.

Database company ClickHouse acquired Langfuse, an open-source LLM observability tool that already stored its telemetry in ClickHouse, alongside a US$400 million Series D at a US$15 billion valuation, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 16 January 2026. Acquisition terms were not disclosed.

Cisco announced plans on 9 April 2026 to acquire AI observability firm Galileo and place it in its Splunk observability portfolio, as reported by Network World; no price was given. Splunk's site now states that the acquisition is complete and that Galileo has become Splunk Agent Observability.

Dynatrace announced on 1 October 2026 that it had completed its acquisition of Arize, an AI observability and LLM evaluation platform. ITPro had reported the agreed price as US$915 million when the deal was announced in August 2026.

CrowdStrike announced on 3 November 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, an AI agent observability and explainability company, for an undisclosed sum paid mostly in cash. It expects the deal to close in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2027, subject to customary conditions, and plans to sell the product within its Falcon platform as Falcon Observe.

categories.definition: Platforms on which a bank builds, deploys and operates its own machine-learning and generative AI applications, with access to models, data and tooling in one place.
categories.name: AI development platforms
riskIssues: AI is built on ungoverned tools outside the bank's controls
Applications are tied to one platform's proprietary services
Costs and usage are hard to attribute and control

trajectoryNotes.summary: DataRobot announced on 10 February 2025 that it had acquired Agnostiq and its open-source compute-orchestration platform Covalent to support agentic AI application development. Terms were not disclosed.

Anaconda announced on 29 April 2026 the acquisition of Outerbounds, the company behind the open-source ML orchestration framework Metaflow, and said it would keep developing Metaflow as open source. Terms were not disclosed.

TrueFoundry, a start-up that manages AI workloads, acquired Seldon, an open-source model-deployment platform founded in 2014 whose enterprise customers include PayPal and Experian, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 25 June 2026. The price was not disclosed.

The Council of the EU gave final approval to the Digital Omnibus on AI, which moves the application date of the EU AI Act's high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 for stand-alone systems and 2 August 2028 for systems embedded in products, according to an EU External Action Service notice of 30 June 2026. The regulation enters into force on the third day after publication in the Official Journal.

categories.definition: Products that protect AI models, applications and agents from attack and misuse: testing them before release, inspecting prompts and responses at run time, scanning model files and the AI supply chain, and discovering unsanctioned AI use.
categories.name: AI security
riskIssues: Prompt injection and jailbreaks cause AI applications to leak data or take unintended actions
Staff send confidential data to AI services the bank has not approved
Model files and open-source AI components carry malicious code or tampered weights
AI agents act with more access than intended
The bank cannot show what its AI systems were asked or what they returned

trajectoryNotes.summary: Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire AI security company Protect AI, with closing expected in the first quarter of its fiscal 2026. The price was not disclosed; SecurityWeek cited a Globes report estimating $650-700 million.

Check Point Software agreed to acquire Lakera, a Zurich and San Francisco firm offering pre-deployment testing and run-time protection for AI applications, with closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2025. The price was not disclosed; SecurityWeek cited reports estimating about $300 million.

Proofpoint announced it had acquired Acuvity, a Sunnyvale-based AI security and governance company providing run-time inspection and enforcement across applications, agents and MCP servers; terms were not disclosed.

OpenAI said it is acquiring Promptfoo, an AI security startup whose platform tests LLMs and agents against prompt injection, jailbreaks and data leakage, as reported by SecurityWeek on 11 March 2026. The price was not disclosed; Promptfoo had raised more than $23 million, and OpenAI said it would keep developing the open-source tool.

HiddenLayer raised a $100 million Series B led by Delta-v Capital, with Booz Allen Ventures, M12, Morgan Stanley and Ten Eleven Ventures participating, bringing its total raised to over $155 million, as reported on 3 September 2026. The company said the funds will extend its platform to run-time security for AI agents, including coding agents.

categories.definition: Products built into the apps a bank gives its customers, chiefly mobile banking and payment apps, so that the app's code resists reverse engineering and tampering, defends itself on devices the bank does not control, and reports attacks back to the bank.
categories.name: Mobile and in-app protection
riskIssues: The bank's mobile app is reverse engineered, modified or repackaged, and customers install a tampered copy
Malware on a customer's device uses overlays, accessibility services or screen capture to steal credentials or authorise payments
The bank's back end cannot tell a genuine copy of its app from a script, emulator or cloned app calling its APIs

trajectoryNotes.summary: OWASP's mobile verification standard groups this job into four controls: checking the integrity of the platform, anti-tampering, and resistance to static and to dynamic analysis. Vendors describe the same core and add to it. Zimperium's suite combines app shielding, in-app runtime protection with a central console, white-box key protection and security testing. Digital.ai offers obfuscation, anti-tamper, runtime self-protection, threat monitoring and white-box cryptography across mobile, web and desktop apps. Promon applies protection after the app is compiled, with no code changes, and adds app integrity checks for APIs. Appdome automates protections in the build pipeline and feeds threat data back to the business. The direction is from build-time hardening alone towards a lifecycle: telemetry from apps in the field, server-side attestation so policies change without a new release, and AI-assisted or guided configuration. The market is also consolidating: Guardsquare completed its purchase of Verimatrix's XTD application protection assets in February 2026, after Verimatrix chose to concentrate on video protection.

categories.definition: Products that find and help fix security flaws in the software a bank writes and the open-source components it depends on, from the developer's editor through to production.
categories.name: Application security
riskIssues: Vulnerable code and dependencies reach production
The bank cannot say which applications contain a newly disclosed vulnerable component
Secrets are committed to source code

trajectoryNotes.summary: Veracode announced on 6 January 2025 that it had acquired certain assets of Phylum, including its technology for detecting and blocking malicious open-source packages, to be integrated into Veracode's software composition analysis product. Terms were not disclosed.
Semgrep raised a US$100 million Series D led by Menlo Ventures, bringing its total funding to US$204 million, as reported by SecurityWeek on 5 February 2025.

Snyk announced on 24 June 2025 that it was acquiring Invariant Labs, an ETH Zurich spin-off researching AI agent security whose Guardrails product inspects agent behaviour and scans MCP servers for vulnerabilities. Terms were not disclosed.

Checkmarx acquired Tromzo, a start-up founded in 2021 whose AI agents filter false positives, prioritise vulnerabilities and generate code fixes, as reported by BankInfoSecurity on 9 December 2025. Checkmarx's chief executive told the outlet he expected further acquisitions.

The EU Cyber Resilience Act's reporting obligations began to apply on 11 September 2026, the European Commission said: manufacturers of products with digital elements sold in the EU must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents through ENISA's single reporting platform, with an early warning within 24 hours and full notification within 72 hours. The Act's main obligations apply from 11 December 2027.

categories.definition: Products that use AI to write, verify and deliver fixes for security findings, instead of only reporting them.
categories.name: Autonomous remediation
riskIssues: Findings are discovered faster than developers can fix them
AI-assisted attackers shorten the time between disclosure and exploitation
Unverified automated fixes can break working software

categories.definition: Products that find, issue, renew and govern the digital certificates a bank relies on, across the certificate authorities it uses, and that watch the health and configuration of the public key infrastructure behind them.
categories.name: Certificate and PKI management
riskIssues: An expired or mis-issued certificate takes a payment, authentication or customer-facing service offline
Certificates and certificate authorities are spread across teams and suppliers with no single inventory, owner or policy
Shorter certificate lifetimes and the move to new algorithms cannot be met with manual renewal and without knowing which algorithms are in use

trajectoryNotes.summary: Certificate lifecycle products converge on the same core. Keyfactor Command, DigiCert Trust Lifecycle Manager and Sectigo Certificate Manager each describe discovery of certificates into one inventory and automated issuance and renewal, and each says it takes in certificates from certificate authorities other than the vendor's own; Keyfactor and DigiCert also describe policy on algorithms, key sizes or lifetimes and role-based access. Two pressures are driving automation. The CA/Browser Forum adopted ballot SC-081v3 in April 2025, which reduces the maximum validity of public TLS certificates in steps from 398 days to 47 days between March 2026 and March 2029, and Keyfactor and DigiCert now present visibility of post-quantum certificates or migration to them as part of the product. A separate strand, described by PKI Solutions as posture management, monitors the certificate authorities, revocation services and hardware security modules themselves rather than issuing certificates, and is sold to run alongside a lifecycle tool.

categories.definition: Products that find and fix security weaknesses across cloud accounts, workloads and the pipelines that build them, and detect attacks on what is running.
categories.name: Cloud security
riskIssues: Misconfigured cloud resources expose customer data
The bank lacks a single view of risk across several cloud providers
Vulnerable or compromised workloads run undetected

trajectoryNotes.summary: Orca Security acquired Opus Security, an Israeli start-up whose technology orchestrates and automates cloud security remediation, as reported by SecurityWeek on 13 May 2025. The price was not disclosed.

Google completed its US$32 billion cash acquisition of Wiz on 11 March 2026, a year after announcing it and following antitrust clearance in the US in November 2025 and the EU in February 2026, as reported by TechCrunch. Wiz joins Google Cloud, keeps its brand and says it will continue to secure customers across all cloud environments.

Upwind acquired Aegis, a start-up building security for AI agents, skills and plugins, and said the Aegis team would lead a new Upwind AI Security Labs, according to a contributed article on The Next Web dated 23 September 2026. Terms were not disclosed.

Upwind raised a US$400 million Series C led by Bessemer Venture Partners at a US$3.8 billion valuation, nine months after raising US$250 million at US$1.5 billion, taking total funding past US$800 million, as reported by SecurityWeek on 28 October 2026.

categories.definition: Products that handle customer conversations by chat and voice with AI, and assist human agents during contact.
categories.name: Conversational AI for customer service
riskIssues: An AI agent gives a customer wrong or non-compliant information
Conversations contain personal and payment data
Customers cannot reach a person when they need one

trajectoryNotes.summary: NICE announced on 8 September 2025 that it had closed its acquisition of Cognigy, a conversational and agentic AI company, after receiving regulatory approvals. When the deal was announced on 28 July 2025, NICE valued Cognigy at about US$955 million.

SoundHound AI agreed to acquire the enterprise messaging company LivePerson at an equity value of about US$43 million and an implied enterprise value of about US$250 million, as reported by FinTech Global on 23 April 2026. Closing was expected in the second half of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.

Sierra, which builds AI customer-service agents, raised US$950 million led by GV and Tiger Global at a US$15 billion valuation, eight months after a round at US$10 billion, as reported by SiliconANGLE on 4 May 2026.

Banking-platform vendor Backbase announced on 23 June 2026 that it had acquired Kasisto, a conversational and agentic AI provider for banks, and folded its platform and New York team into the Backbase Banking OS. Terms were not disclosed.

Automation Anywhere agreed to acquire Boost.ai, a Nordic Capital-owned conversational and voice AI company with customers in financial services, telecommunications and insurance, as reported by Dealroom News on 7 October 2026. Terms were not disclosed and closing was expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals.

categories.definition: Products that register a bank's own customers, sign them in to its digital channels, confirm it is still them when risk rises or money moves, and let them recover access, as distinct from identity products for the bank's staff.
categories.name: Customer identity and authentication
riskIssues: Account takeover through stolen passwords, phishing and intercepted one-time codes causes direct customer loss
Weak recovery and device-change processes let an attacker re-enrol as the customer
Sign-in friction and separate logins per channel push customers away from digital services and towards the call centre

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors' current material shows the category moving from passwords and one-time codes to passkeys and from sign-in alone to the whole customer journey. Okta's Auth0 documentation describes sign-in with passwords, social accounts or one-time codes, multi-factor authentication for sensitive data, single sign-on, user management and protection against credential attacks. Microsoft's Entra External ID lists self-service sign-up with custom attributes, email one-time passcodes, FIDO2 passkeys, self-service password reset, extra verification for sensitive actions after sign-in and extensions for a customer's own logic. Products aimed at banks add approval of payments: OneSpan describes passkeys whose approval is cryptographically bound to the amount and recipient, with device-bound credentials inside the banking app, and Transmit Security documents transaction signing with passkeys or mobile biometrics.

categories.definition: Products that hold a bank's security controls, cyber risks, policies and audit evidence in one system of record, map the controls to the regulations and frameworks the bank answers to, and test them from security tool data on a continuing basis instead of by periodic manual review.
categories.name: Cyber governance, risk and continuous controls monitoring
riskIssues: Control evidence is gathered by hand before each audit or examination, so it is out of date between reviews
The same control is documented and tested separately for every regulation and framework, in spreadsheets that disagree
Findings from security tools are not tied to the controls, risks and remediation actions that examiners ask about

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market describe the same core: a common control set mapped to many frameworks, risk assessments, control testing with evidence, policies and issue tracking on one platform. MetricStream, Archer and Hyperproof all present their products this way; MetricStream describes AI agents that test controls and gather evidence, and Hyperproof describes its modules as AI-powered. The difference being drawn is how controls are tested: RegScale positions continuous controls monitoring, fed by integrations with security tools and machine-readable formats such as NIST OSCAL, against periodic assessment, and Archer describes pulling control test results from automated systems alongside manual evidence. Money and sector bodies are following: SecurityWeek reported a Series B of more than US$30 million for RegScale in September 2025, and in February 2025 the Cyber Risk Institute said financial institutions want to move from point-in-time assessments to continuous control monitoring.

categories.definition: Products that keep protected copies of a bank's data, applications and identity systems, check those copies for signs of attack, and restore clean systems after ransomware, destructive attacks or outages.
categories.name: Backup and cyber recovery
riskIssues: Ransomware or a destructive attack encrypts or deletes production data and the backups with it
The bank restores from a copy that still contains the attacker's malware or changes, and is reinfected
Recovery plans are untested, so critical services cannot be restored within the bank's impact tolerances

trajectoryNotes.summary: Backup vendors now sell recovery from cyberattack, not only from failure. The product pages read describe the same pattern: copies that cannot be altered, scanning of backups for anomalies and known threats, recovery into an isolated or clean environment, and rehearsed recovery plans with reports. Commvault presents separate offerings for clean isolated recovery, cloud, SaaS and identity systems; Veeam describes immutable and vaulted copies, malware and indicator scanning, and orchestrated recovery with automated testing; Rubrik documents threat analytics, orchestrated application recovery and identity recovery in one cloud service. Two directions stand out: recovery of identity systems (Active Directory, Entra ID, Okta) is treated as the first step of any recovery, and vendors are adding recovery from damage done by AI agents. Rubrik's annual report names Commvault, Dell EMC, IBM, Veeam and Cohesity as competitors.

categories.definition: Products that build and prove the practical cyber capability of a bank's security staff, developers, executives and wider workforce through hands-on labs, team exercises on simulated networks and crisis simulations, and that measure the results as evidence of readiness.
categories.name: Cyber skills and readiness exercising
riskIssues: Security and incident teams have not practised against the attacks most likely to hit the bank, so response is slow or wrong when one happens
Executives and crisis teams meet their first major cyber incident without having rehearsed the decisions it demands
The bank cannot show its board and supervisors measured evidence that its people can detect, respond to and recover from a cyber attack

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market have moved from libraries of individual training labs to platforms that exercise whole teams and report a measure of readiness. Hack The Box sells labs, a threat range for incident drills, tabletop crisis exercises and a readiness index for each analyst, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK, NIST NICE and DORA. Cyberbit sells a cloud cyber range, team live-fire exercises, solo labs, an executive crisis simulation and its own readiness index. Immersive's product guide lists labs, cyber range exercises, live threat ranges, crisis simulations and peer benchmarking in one platform. SimSpace builds replicas of a customer's production environment for team rehearsal and for testing tools. The newest direction is testing AI agents alongside people: Hack The Box, Immersive and SimSpace each now describe assessing or validating AI agents on their ranges.

categories.definition: Products that find where sensitive data lives, who can reach it and how it moves, and that stop it leaving by routes it should not.
categories.name: Data security
riskIssues: The bank does not know where all copies of customer data are
Excessive access to sensitive data goes unnoticed
Data leaks through email, cloud storage or AI tools

trajectoryNotes.summary: Veeam, a data-resilience vendor owned by Insight Partners, agreed to buy data security company Securiti AI for $1.725 billion in cash and stock, with closing expected in the first week of December 2025.
Cyera raised $600 million at a $12 billion valuation in a round led by Evolution Equity Partners, taking its total funding above $2.3 billion.

Cyera agreed to acquire Oasis Security, a provider of non-human identity and agentic access governance, for about $1 billion, saying it would bring identity and data security into one platform as use of AI agents grows.

Proofpoint, owned by Thoma Bravo, agreed to acquire Varonis for $49.75 per share in cash, about $6.3 billion, with closing expected in the first half of 2027. SecurityWeek described it as the largest cybersecurity acquisition announced so far in 2026; Proofpoint plans to combine the two into a single data and AI security platform.

categories.definition: Services and appliances that sit in front of a bank's internet-facing networks, websites and APIs to absorb denial-of-service attacks and to block malicious requests, abusive automation and tampering with the pages customers load.
categories.name: DDoS, web application and API protection
riskIssues: Online banking, payment and API channels are taken offline or slowed by denial-of-service attacks
Web applications and APIs are exploited, or abused through their business logic, before flaws can be fixed
Automated traffic takes over customer accounts, scrapes data or commits fraud while looking like real customers

trajectoryNotes.summary: Products that were once bought separately are now sold as one cloud-delivered service. Cloudflare's documentation describes protection against network-layer and HTTP-layer denial-of-service attacks that is switched on by default, with rules that adapt to a site's normal traffic, and links its firewall to bot and client-side products. Akamai's App & API Protector page describes a web application firewall, API discovery, bot controls and application-layer DDoS defence in one product that tunes itself. F5's documentation describes a firewall with API security and API endpoint learning. Radware's 2025 annual report describes plans that add API discovery, bot management and client-side protection to a cloud firewall, names Akamai, Imperva, Netscout, Cloudflare, F5 and AWS as competitors, notes competition from security built into the public clouds, and reports new add-ons aimed at generative AI traffic.

categories.definition: Products that plant decoy systems, false credentials and other lures across a bank's networks, identity stores and cloud estate, so that any interaction with them gives an early, high-confidence signal that an intruder is present and a record of what the intruder did.
categories.name: Deception technology
riskIssues: An intruder who is already inside moves between systems for days or weeks before any control notices
Stolen or misused credentials look like legitimate activity to controls that rely on signatures or behaviour baselines
Security operations staff lose time to low-confidence alerts and cannot tell quickly which ones are real

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market describe the same core idea: decoys, lures and fake credentials that no legitimate user should touch, so that any contact is treated as a confirmed signal. Zscaler sells deception as part of its wider zero trust platform and Fortinet sells FortiDeceptor as part of its security operations platform, including a hosted version, while Acalvio and CounterCraft are specialists. In 2026 all four present deception as a defence against attacks run by AI agents, which probe many paths at once and so are likely to touch a decoy. The decoys themselves are spreading to AI infrastructure: Zscaler lists decoy chatbots and language-model interfaces, Acalvio announced decoys placed in AI agent workflows in July 2026, and CounterCraft describes AI agents that build and run the deception environment. Coverage of operational technology and of identity stores such as Active Directory is now common to the vendors read.

categories.definition: Products that detect AI-generated or manipulated voice, video, images and documents in onboarding, payment approval and contact-centre calls.
categories.name: Deepfake and synthetic media detection
riskIssues: Synthetic voice or video impersonates customers and executives
Checks designed for humans are defeated by generated media
Injected media bypasses a camera or microphone check

categories.definition: Products that watch the public internet outside the bank's own network for fake domains, accounts, apps and adverts that impersonate the bank, its staff or its products, and get them removed.
categories.name: Digital risk protection and impersonation takedown
riskIssues: Customers are defrauded through cloned login pages, fake apps and fake support accounts that use the bank's name
Impersonation of executives and advisers on social and messaging platforms is used to solicit payments or credentials
Fraud infrastructure stays live because removal is slow and handles one address at a time while the campaign behind it carries on

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market describe the same core job: monitor domains, social platforms, app stores, adverts and dark web sources for impersonation, then ask registrars, hosts and platforms to remove what is found. They differ in how much is automated. ZeroFox pairs automated correlation with analyst review and has widened into attack-surface, dark web and physical security intelligence. Netcraft stresses takedown speed and disrupting lookalike domains before an attack goes live. Doppel uses AI agents for detection and takedown with analysts for escalations, links related incidents in a threat graph, and has added phishing simulation, awareness training and email security. The common direction is from removing single addresses towards mapping and removing a whole campaign, with more of the work done by AI agents, and expansion into executive protection and neighbouring categories.

categories.definition: Products that answer or inspect an organisation's DNS lookups, block or redirect those that lead to malicious or unwanted destinations, and use DNS query data to find compromised devices and data leaving the network over DNS.
categories.name: Protective DNS and DNS security
riskIssues: Malware, phishing and ransomware reach their servers through DNS lookups that no other control inspects
Data is carried out of the bank inside DNS queries, which firewalls and proxies usually let through
The bank cannot tell which device or user made a suspicious lookup, so investigations stall

trajectoryNotes.summary: Government guidance treats this as a baseline control. The US agencies NSA and CISA published joint guidance in March 2021 on choosing a protective DNS service, describing it as a defence that blocks known-malicious domains and yields query logs for incident response, and CISA has run its own protective DNS resolver for federal civilian agencies since 2022. Commercial products do the same core job in different places. Akamai's service is a cloud DNS firewall with clients for devices off the network; Cloudflare applies DNS policies by user, location and category inside its zero-trust platform; BlueCat and Infoblox sell it alongside their DNS, DHCP and IP address management products, and Infoblox enforces policy on the resolvers the organisation already runs as well as in the cloud. The direction is from blocklists towards analysing query behaviour to catch tunnelling and algorithm-generated domains, blocking newly registered or suspicious domains before they are used, and feeding DNS evidence into security operations tools.

categories.definition: Products that read documents such as applications, statements and contracts and turn them into structured data for downstream processes.
categories.name: Document AI
riskIssues: Extraction errors flow into lending and onboarding decisions
Documents contain sensitive personal and financial data
Accuracy claims are hard to verify on the bank's own documents

trajectoryNotes.summary: Instabase raised a $100 million Series D led by the Qatar Investment Authority.

Reducto, a document-parsing startup that pairs OCR with vision-language models and sells through an API, raised a $75 million Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz, following a $24.5 million Series A in April 2025 and bringing total funding to $108 million.
Spend-management vendor Coupa announced it had acquired Rossum, an intelligent document processing provider, to extend document processing across its own products; terms were not disclosed.

categories.definition: Products that stop phishing, business email compromise and malware arriving by email and collaboration tools.
categories.name: Email security
riskIssues: Phishing remains the usual first step of an intrusion
Impersonation of executives and suppliers leads to fraudulent payments
Compromised internal mailboxes send trusted-looking attacks

trajectoryNotes.summary: Bitdefender agreed to acquire Mesh Security, an email security provider founded in 2020 that combines a gateway with API-based mailbox protection for managed service providers, and said it would build the technology into its XDR platform and MDR services. Terms were not disclosed.
Certificate authority DigiCert bought Valimail, a provider of DMARC email-authentication services, as reported by TechRadar; the price was not given.
Sublime Security raised a $150 million Series C led by Georgian, bringing its total funding to more than $240 million, for product development and international expansion.

Proofpoint completed its acquisition of Hornetsecurity, a German provider of Microsoft 365 security sold largely through managed service providers, in a transaction Proofpoint valued at $1.8 billion. Hornetsecurity is to run as a separate business unit serving managed service providers.

AegisAI, a startup founded by former Google security executives that uses AI agents to screen email for AI-generated spear phishing, raised a $36 million Series A led by Battery Ventures, bringing its total funding to $49 million.

categories.definition: Products that generate, store and control the cryptographic keys protecting a bank's data, including hardware security modules and services that let the bank hold keys for data in the cloud.
categories.name: Encryption and key management
riskIssues: Whoever holds the keys can read the data, including a cloud provider
Keys are scattered across systems with no central control
Hardware and algorithms must be replaced for the post-quantum transition

trajectoryNotes.summary: Utimaco sold its lawful interception unit, Utimaco Telecom Solutions, to investment firms INVISION and PINOVA; the sale completed on 30 September 2025 and the price was not disclosed. Utimaco said it would concentrate on its information and data security business.

Keyfactor, which sells tools for discovering cryptographic assets and managing machine identities, received an investment of more than $1 billion led by Summit Partners, with existing backers Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keeping significant stakes. Stated uses include product development, geographic expansion and possible acquisitions.

NIST's Cryptographic Module Validation Program states that US federal agencies could accept FIPS 140-2 validated modules for new systems only through 21 September 2026; after that date the programme moves those modules to its Historical list, where they may continue to be used in existing systems only.

Microsoft made external key management for Azure Key Vault Managed HSM generally available in all Azure public regions, according to an Azure Updates notice dated 16 October 2026. The feature lets Azure services that support customer-managed keys use key-encryption keys held in an HSM the customer operates outside Microsoft's infrastructure; access has to be enabled through the customer's Microsoft account team.

categories.definition: Products that keep an organisation's laptops, desktops and other endpoints inventoried, patched and correctly configured from a central console, and that can lock, repair or rebuild a device remotely when it is lost, misconfigured or knocked out of service.
categories.name: Endpoint management and resilience
riskIssues: Devices the bank cannot see or reach are left unpatched and outside its security controls
Security agents and required software are removed, disabled or broken on endpoints without anyone noticing
A faulty update or an attack leaves many staff devices unusable and they cannot be recovered without hands-on work

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market describe a common core: a live inventory of devices and software, operating-system and third-party patching, policy and compliance enforcement, software deployment and remote troubleshooting from one console. Ivanti and NinjaOne both add automation that corrects endpoint problems without an operator, Tanium presents autonomous remediation with governed, AI-assisted actions, and Microsoft Intune has added an AI assistant and agents for policy and remediation work. Recovery is the newer theme: Absolute Security sells firmware-embedded persistence that reinstalls its agent and can restore a device whose operating system will not start, and in October 2026 it announced the purchase of the FirmGuard firmware security business from Phoenix Technologies. Endpoint management, patching and vulnerability remediation are being sold together, so this category overlaps with vulnerability and exposure management.

categories.definition: Products that prevent, detect and respond to attacks on laptops, servers and other endpoints, and correlate that activity with signals from identity, network and cloud.
categories.name: Endpoint protection and XDR
riskIssues: Ransomware and hands-on-keyboard intrusions start on endpoints
A faulty security update can take down the bank's own machines
Detection signals are spread across tools and missed

trajectoryNotes.summary: Arctic Wolf agreed to buy the Cylance endpoint security business from BlackBerry for $160 million; BlackBerry had paid $1.4 billion for Cylance in 2018.

Sophos completed its $859 million all-cash acquisition of Secureworks, whose shares stopped trading on Nasdaq, and said it would combine Secureworks' Taegis XDR platform with its own managed detection and response services.

Microsoft said it would give some Microsoft Virus Initiative partners a private preview, from July 2025, of a Windows endpoint security platform that lets anti-malware and endpoint detection products run in user mode rather than in the kernel. The work is part of the Windows Resiliency Initiative that followed the July 2024 CrowdStrike update incident; vendors Microsoft said it worked with include CrowdStrike, Bitdefender, ESET, SentinelOne, Sophos, Trellix, Trend Micro and WithSecure.

Managed security services provider LevelBlue announced a proposed acquisition of XDR vendor Cybereason, with SoftBank becoming an investor in LevelBlue as part of the transaction; the price was not disclosed.

Palo Alto Networks signed a definitive agreement to acquire Koi, a startup securing AI agents and tools that run on endpoints, and said Koi's technology would be added to its Prisma AIRS platform and its Cortex XDR endpoint product. The price was not disclosed.

categories.definition: Assistants that answer staff questions and complete tasks by drawing on the organisation's own documents and systems.
categories.name: Enterprise AI assistants and search
riskIssues: The assistant reveals documents a user should not see
Answers are wrong but presented with confidence
Sensitive internal content is indexed by a third party

trajectoryNotes.summary: HubSpot agreed to acquire Dashworks, a workplace search assistant, and said the team would join its AI product group to improve search across business data in its Breeze assistant. Terms were not disclosed.
Glean raised a $150 million Series F led by Wellington Management at a $7.2 billion valuation.
Workday agreed to acquire Sana, a maker of enterprise knowledge, learning and agent tools, for about $1.1 billion, with closing expected in Workday's fiscal fourth quarter ending 31 January 2026.

ServiceNow completed its acquisition of Moveworks, an enterprise AI assistant and search vendor, a deal announced in March 2025 at $2.85 billion in cash and stock. ServiceNow said it would connect Moveworks' assistant and enterprise search to its own workflow platform.

categories.definition: Products that inspect and clean files at the points where they enter or move through a bank, by scanning them with several malware engines, rebuilding them without active content and analysing unknown ones, before the files reach users, applications or isolated networks.
categories.name: File and malware security
riskIssues: Files uploaded by customers, sent by third parties or carried in on removable media bring malware past controls that rely on one detection engine
Weaponised documents and archives that no engine yet recognises reach staff and back-office systems unchanged
The bank cannot show what was inspected, removed or blocked for each file that crossed into a sensitive or isolated network

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market combine prevention that does not depend on recognising a threat with conventional detection. Glasswall rebuilds files to a known-good structure and has added a machine-learning product that predicts unknown malware from file structure, plus redaction of sensitive content. Sasa Software's GateScanner line pairs content disarm and reconstruction with multi-engine scanning and sells it as removable-media kiosks, managed file transfer, email protection, an API and ICAP service and a data diode. OPSWAT's MetaDefender platform layers multi-engine scanning, content disarm, a sandbox and data-loss checks across similar delivery points. A July 2026 AV-Comparatives review, commissioned by OPSWAT, describes content disarm as a complement to antivirus and sandboxing that is deployed where files cross trust boundaries (email gateways, upload portals, file transfer, air-gapped and cross-domain systems), and included AI-assisted malicious content among its test scenarios. The direction is towards one policy engine serving every file entry point, with per-file reports of what was removed.

categories.definition: General-purpose AI models, offered through an API or for self-hosting, that other applications are built on.
categories.name: Foundation models
riskIssues: The bank's data is sent to a model provider and may be retained or used for training
Model behaviour changes when the provider updates or retires a version
Many of the bank's AI applications depend on the same few providers

trajectoryNotes.summary: The European Commission confirmed that the EU AI Act's obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models, covering transparency and copyright, apply from 2 August 2025, with further duties for models classed as posing systemic risk. Models already on the market before that date must comply by 2 August 2027.

OpenAI closed a $122 billion funding round at an $852 billion valuation, co-led by SoftBank with Amazon, Nvidia and Microsoft among the participants; about $3 billion came from individual investors through bank channels.
Anthropic raised a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation, led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital.
Mistral AI raised a EUR 3 billion Series D led by Samsung Electronics at a valuation above EUR 21 billion, nearly double the EUR 11.7 billion of its 2025 Series C led by ASML.

Cohere and Germany's Aleph Alpha signed a merger agreement, formalising a plan announced in April 2026; SiliconANGLE reported the combined company as worth about $20 billion. It is to operate under the Cohere name with headquarters in Toronto and Berlin once regulators clear the deal.

categories.definition: Products that detect payment fraud, account takeover, scams and money laundering in real time or in review, increasingly with machine learning.
categories.name: Fraud and financial crime
riskIssues: Authorised push payment scams and account takeover cause direct customer loss
Transaction monitoring generates more alerts than investigators can review
Model decisions must be explainable to customers and supervisors

trajectoryNotes.summary: Visa agreed to acquire Featurespace, a developer of real-time AI fraud and financial-crime detection for payments that grew out of Cambridge University's engineering department, with closing expected in Visa's fiscal year 2025; terms were not disclosed.

The UK Payment Systems Regulator's reimbursement protections for victims of authorised push payment scams took effect for Faster Payments and CHAPS payments made on or after 7 October 2024. The standard protection covers up to GBP 85,000, and the regulator said most consumers can expect reimbursement within five business days of a claim.

European Parliament and Council negotiators reached a provisional deal on the EU Payment Services Regulation and PSD3. Under it, a payment service provider that fails to put appropriate fraud-prevention mechanisms in place is liable for customers' losses, providers must check that a payee's name matches the account identifier, and victims of bank-impersonation fraud must be refunded in full. The deal still needed formal adoption by both institutions.

Visa agreed to acquire behavioural-biometrics fraud vendor BioCatch for $2.4 billion in cash from funds advised by Permira and other shareholders, with closing expected by the end of Visa's fiscal second quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

NICE said on its third-quarter earnings call that the sale process for its Actimize financial-crime business was continuing and gave no update, as reported by Calcalist. Calcalist noted a September report that Brookfield had entered exclusive talks to buy Actimize for about $2 billion, which NICE has not confirmed.

categories.definition: Products that establish who a workforce user is, sign them in once across applications, and decide what they may reach, including the lifecycle of accounts as people join, move and leave.
categories.name: Identity and access management
riskIssues: Stolen or weak credentials are the most common way into a bank
Leavers and movers keep access they should have lost
The bank cannot show supervisors who had access to what, and why

trajectoryNotes.summary: SailPoint returned to the public markets, with shares starting to trade on Nasdaq on 13 February 2025 after an upsized offering that raised $1.38 billion for the company and owner Thoma Bravo and valued it at $12.8 billion. Thoma Bravo had taken SailPoint private in 2022 for $6.9 billion.

NIST published Revision 4 of SP 800-63, its Digital Identity Guidelines, superseding SP 800-63-3. It is the first major revision of the suite since 2017 and sets requirements for identity proofing, authentication and federation, with three companion volumes.

Identity governance vendor Saviynt raised $700 million in a Series B growth round led by KKR at a valuation of roughly $3 billion, with stated uses including product development and tools to move customers off legacy platforms.

Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of CyberArk, paying $45.00 in cash and 2.2005 Palo Alto Networks shares for each CyberArk share, and said identity security would become a core pillar of its platform, covering human, machine and AI-agent identities.

Okta signed an agreement to acquire Permiso Security, which detects identity threats across human, non-human and AI-agent identities, to add identity threat detection and response to its platform; an update to the announcement dated 26 August 2026 says the deal has closed. Terms were not disclosed.

categories.definition: Products that check that a customer is a real person and who they claim to be when opening an account or making a high-risk change, using documents, biometrics and data sources.
categories.name: Identity verification
riskIssues: Synthetic and stolen identities are used to open accounts
Deepfakes defeat selfie and video checks
Biometric data is highly sensitive and tightly regulated

trajectoryNotes.summary: Entrust, a payments, identity and data-security provider, completed its acquisition of identity verification company Onfido, as reported on 9 April 2024; terms were not disclosed.

FinCEN, a bureau of the US Treasury, issued alert FIN-2024-Alert004 on fraud schemes that use deepfake media made with generative AI. It reports a rise in suspicious activity reports describing fraudulent identity documents used to get past identity verification and authentication, lists red-flag indicators, and reminds financial institutions of their Bank Secrecy Act reporting duties.

Incode acquired Identiq, an Israeli startup whose cryptographic tools let institutions share fraud signals without sharing customer records; the price was not disclosed. SiliconANGLE reported it as Incode's third acquisition in two years, after identity verification rival MetaMap in 2024 and AuthenticID in 2025.

Amsterdam-based Fourthline and digital identity provider Veridas agreed to merge into one identity platform covering Europe and the Americas, with completion expected in the second half of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Veridas shareholders including BBVA are to keep stakes in the combined group.

Socure announced a $156 million investment led by Summit Partners at a reported $5.2 billion valuation, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Wells Fargo and Docusign also taking part, and on the same day announced the acquisition of Fravity AI, a startup building AI agents for case investigations, for an undisclosed price. SiliconANGLE reported Fravity as Socure's third acquisition, after Berbix in 2023 and Effectiv in 2024.

categories.definition: Products that passively analyse network traffic inside and between an organisation's data centres, offices and cloud environments to detect attacker behaviour, and that keep network evidence for investigation and response.
categories.name: Network detection and response
riskIssues: An attacker who is already inside moves between internal systems unseen, because perimeter and endpoint tools do not watch traffic between them
Unmanaged, legacy and operational devices that cannot run an endpoint agent go unmonitored
After an incident the bank cannot reconstruct what happened on the network because no traffic record or packets were kept

trajectoryNotes.summary: The product pages of four vendors in this market describe the same core: passive sensors on premises and in public cloud, behavioural or machine-learning detection alongside signatures and threat intelligence, a record of network activity for investigation, and hand-off to SIEM, SOAR and endpoint tools. They differ at the edges. ExtraHop decrypts traffic out of band and Darktrace says it analyses both encrypted and decrypted traffic, while Vectra AI describes analysing encrypted traffic by behaviour and metadata without reading payloads. Vectra AI adds identity and cloud log sources to network data, Corelight builds on the open-source Zeek and Suricata projects, and Darktrace describes containing threats itself as well as through other tools. All four now present AI-assisted or agent-driven triage and investigation, and Corelight and ExtraHop offer Model Context Protocol servers so that AI agents can query network evidence. Sensor speed is rising: ExtraHop announced a 400 Gbps sensor in August 2026.

categories.definition: Products that connect users to applications by identity and device posture and inspect traffic from the cloud, replacing the corporate perimeter and VPN.
categories.name: Zero-trust network access and SASE
riskIssues: VPNs give broad network access once a user is in
Traffic to cloud and AI services bypasses inspection
The security service itself becomes a single point of failure

trajectoryNotes.summary: CISA, with the FBI and the national cyber agencies of New Zealand and Canada, published guidance on modern approaches to network access security. It sets out the risks of traditional remote access and VPN deployments and encourages organisations of all sizes to move towards zero trust, security service edge (SSE) and secure access service edge (SASE).

Cato Networks raised $359 million in a Series G round at a $4.8 billion valuation, led by new investors Vitruvian Partners and ION Crossover Partners, as reported by Globes; its valuation at the previous round was $3 billion.

Cato Networks made its first acquisition, buying Aim Security, a company founded in 2022 to help organisations deploy generative-AI tools securely, for an undisclosed price, and extended its Series G to $409 million with a further $50 million from Acrew Capital. Cato said it planned to offer Aim's capabilities inside its SASE platform in early 2026.
Netskope went public: its final prospectus dated 17 September 2025 offered 47.8 million Class A shares at $19.00 each, listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol NTSK.

categories.definition: Products that map how workloads talk to each other and restrict that traffic, so an intruder cannot move freely once inside.
categories.name: Network segmentation
riskIssues: An intruder moves from one compromised system to many
Ransomware spreads faster than people can respond
Flat networks leave critical systems reachable from anywhere inside

categories.definition: Products that attack a bank's own systems, continuously or on demand, to prove which weaknesses can actually be exploited.
categories.name: Offensive security and exposure validation
riskIssues: Scanners list weaknesses but do not show which ones lead to a breach
Point-in-time penetration tests go stale between tests
AI-assisted attackers find and chain weaknesses faster than manual testing can

categories.definition: Products that find where an organisation uses cryptography, assess which uses are vulnerable to a future quantum computer, and help replace or wrap them with quantum-resistant algorithms without rebuilding every system.
categories.name: Post-quantum cryptography and crypto-agility
riskIssues: Encrypted data captured today may be decrypted later once quantum computers mature
The bank does not have an inventory of where and how it uses cryptography
Algorithms are hard-coded, so replacing them is slow and costly
Suppliers and counterparties migrate on different timetables

trajectoryNotes.summary: Keyfactor bought two cryptographic-discovery startups, Toronto-based InfoSec Global and CipherInsights (part of Quantum Xchange), as reported on 13 May 2025; terms were not disclosed.

The G7 Cyber Expert Group, chaired by the US Treasury and the Bank of England, released a roadmap for a coordinated financial-sector move to post-quantum cryptography, addressed to financial entities, authorities and suppliers. Treasury's release says the roadmap and its timeline are not prescriptive.

Keyfactor received a growth investment of more than $1 billion led by Summit Partners, with existing backers Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth keeping substantial stakes; stated uses include product development, international expansion and acquisitions.

IonQ announced an all-stock agreement to acquire zero-trust security company Elisity for up to $1.3 billion, including an earnout of up to $150 million, saying it will combine its post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution capabilities with Elisity's platform. The filing gave an expected close in the fourth quarter of 2026.

NIST published the final version of IR 8547, its plan for moving from quantum-vulnerable public-key cryptography to post-quantum standards. As reported by Help Net Security, NIST will deprecate quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms after 2030 and disallow them under its standards after 2035, and prioritised US federal systems must adopt quantum-resistant key establishment by 31 December 2030 and digital signatures by 31 December 2031.

categories.definition: Products that let a bank build and test models without exposing real customer data, by generating synthetic data, masking, or computing on protected data.
categories.name: Synthetic data and privacy-enhancing technology
riskIssues: Real customer data is copied into development and vendor environments
Synthetic data may still leak information about real people
Privacy claims are hard to verify

trajectoryNotes.summary: SAS acquired the principal software assets of UK synthetic data company Hazy and said it would build the technology into its SAS Data Maker product, with a preview expected in early 2025.

NIST published the final version of SP 800-226, Guidelines for Evaluating Differential Privacy Guarantees. It explains how to reason about differentially private software and describes the pitfalls, which it calls privacy hazards, that arise when the technique is implemented in practice.

TechCrunch, citing a Wired report, said Nvidia had acquired synthetic data startup Gretel for a nine-figure price above Gretel's last $320 million valuation. The terms were not disclosed and the article carried no confirmation from either company.

Syntho announced it had acquired the MOSTLY AI brand, which continues as "MOSTLY AI, powered by Syntho". Trending Topics had reported on 4 March 2026 that, according to MOSTLY AI's chief executive, the Vienna synthetic data company was ceasing operations; the outlet put its total funding at about $31 million and said attempts to sell the company in the second half of 2025 had not succeeded.

The UK's National Security Strategic Investment Fund made a strategic investment of undisclosed size in Duality Technologies, whose platform uses fully homomorphic encryption, confidential computing and federated analytics. Duality said it is moving the technology into production with national security and defence customers.

categories.definition: Products that control, broker and record the use of administrator and other high-privilege accounts and the secrets they depend on.
categories.name: Privileged access management
riskIssues: Compromise of one administrator account gives an attacker the estate
Shared and standing privileged credentials cannot be attributed to a person
Secrets are hard-coded in scripts and pipelines

trajectoryNotes.summary: IBM completed its acquisition of HashiCorp, maker of the Vault secrets-management product, for $35 per share in cash, an enterprise value of $6.4 billion.
Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire CyberArk for $45.00 in cash plus 2.2005 Palo Alto Networks shares per CyberArk share, an equity value of about $25 billion.

The final set of requirements under the New York Department of Financial Services' amended cybersecurity regulation (23 NYCRR Part 500) takes effect on 1 November 2025, as summarised by law firm Hogan Lovells on 22 October 2025: covered entities must require multi-factor authentication for any user accessing any information system, with a narrower rule for small businesses that still covers privileged accounts other than service accounts. The Department's requirements page lists privileged access management under section 500.7(c) as applying to Class A companies.
Palo Alto Networks completed its acquisition of CyberArk on the terms agreed in July 2025.

Delinea completed its acquisition of StrongDM, an access management company for engineering, DevOps and AI-driven environments, for an undisclosed price. Delinea said the deal adds just-in-time runtime authorisation to its privileged access products, including for actions taken by AI agents.

categories.definition: Products that train a bank's staff to recognise and report social engineering, test them with simulated phishing, voice, message and deepfake attacks, and measure where human risk is concentrated.
categories.name: Security awareness and human risk management
riskIssues: Staff are deceived by phishing, voice, message or deepfake impersonation into moving money or giving up credentials
Generic annual training does not prepare staff for personalised, AI-generated attacks
The bank cannot show auditors and supervisors who was trained, how staff performed, or where human risk is concentrated

trajectoryNotes.summary: Vendors in this market now describe themselves as human risk management platforms and no longer only as training libraries. Hoxhunt simulates phishing by email, SMS, phone call and Microsoft Teams and generates training with AI; Proofpoint's ZenGuide scores risk for each user and enrols people in training automatically; SoSafe sells a human risk management tool and an AI chatbot beside its training and simulations. The market is also converging with email security: KnowBe4 lists inbound and outbound email security and AI agent products beside its awareness training, and Hoxhunt offers automated analysis of the emails staff report.

categories.definition: Platforms that collect security telemetry from across the organisation, detect threats in it, support investigation, and keep the record that auditors and regulators ask for.
categories.name: SIEM and security analytics
riskIssues: Attacks go unnoticed because logs are not collected or correlated
Log volume makes the monitoring bill unpredictable
The bank cannot reconstruct events for a regulator after an incident

trajectoryNotes.summary: Cisco completed its acquisition of Splunk for $157 per share in cash, about $28 billion in equity value.
Exabeam and LogRhythm completed their merger; the combined company kept the Exabeam name.

Palo Alto Networks closed its acquisition of IBM's QRadar software-as-a-service assets. The two companies said QRadar SaaS customers would be helped to move to Palo Alto's Cortex XSIAM, with no-cost migration services from IBM Consulting for eligible customers, while on-premises QRadar customers continue to get IBM support.

CISA, with the Australian Signals Directorate's Australian Cyber Security Centre and other partners, published guidance for organisations procuring and implementing SIEM and SOAR platforms: separate documents for executives and practitioners, plus practitioner guidance on which logs to prioritise for SIEM ingestion.

Telemetry company Cribl bought detection-engineering vendor CardinalOps, taking its intellectual property and about 20 security engineers, for an undisclosed price. TechTarget reported it as Cribl's first move beyond data routing into detection content, which Cribl described as SIEM-like rather than a full SIEM replacement.

categories.definition: Products that assess and monitor the security and resilience of a bank's suppliers, through questionnaires, evidence collection and outside-in ratings.
categories.name: Third-party risk management
riskIssues: A supplier's breach or outage becomes the bank's incident
Supervisors expect a complete register of third-party arrangements
Assessments are point-in-time and go stale

trajectoryNotes.summary: The OCC, the Federal Reserve Board and the FDIC issued joint guidance on managing risk in third-party relationships (OCC Bulletin 2023-17). It sets out principles for each stage of the third-party risk management life cycle, aligns supervisory expectations across the three agencies, and rescinds OCC Bulletin 2013-29 and its 2020 FAQ.

The Bank of England, PRA and FCA published final rules for critical third parties to the UK financial sector (PS16/24), taking effect on 1 January 2025 and applying to a provider once HM Treasury's designation order for it comes into force; none had been designated at publication. The regulators state that the regime does not reduce firms' own responsibility for managing risks from their third-party arrangements.
Bitsight, a cyber risk management company, is buying Israeli dark-web threat intelligence firm Cybersixgill for $115 million, as reported by TechCrunch on 14 November 2024.

The three European Supervisory Authorities (EBA, EIOPA and ESMA) designated critical ICT third-party providers under the Digital Operational Resilience Act, drawing on data from financial entities' registers of information. The designated providers come under direct ESA oversight of their risk management and governance.

SecurityScorecard acquired UK internet-scanning and threat intelligence startup Driftnet for an undisclosed price, as reported by SiliconANGLE, which noted the company had earlier bought vendor security review automation firm HyperComply.

categories.definition: Products that map the adversary behaviour relevant to a bank onto the security controls it already runs, to show which attack techniques are covered, which are not, and what to change first.
categories.name: Threat-informed defence and control coverage
riskIssues: The bank cannot show which attacker techniques its existing tools actually detect or block
Security spend goes to overlapping tools while gaps against relevant threat groups stay open
Threat intelligence is read but not turned into detection and control changes

trajectoryNotes.summary: MITRE's Center for Threat-Informed Defense describes the practice as using known adversary behaviour relevant to an organisation's threat model to assess and improve its defences, and publishes free mappings from security controls to ATT&CK techniques. Commercial products apply this to a customer's own tools: Tidal Cyber overlays a defensive stack on a threat profile and takes in results from attack-simulation tools; CardinalOps measures detection coverage against adversary behaviour and finds broken rules; Reach Security looks for misconfigured or underused controls and recommends changes. The market is converging with neighbours: Cribl announced in July 2026 that it is acquiring CardinalOps, and vendors here are adding vulnerability and asset context and AI assistance.

categories.definition: Services and platforms that collect information about adversaries, their tools and their infrastructure from open, technical and criminal-underground sources, analyse it, and deliver it to a bank's security teams and tools so that threats can be anticipated, prioritised and detected.
categories.name: Threat intelligence
riskIssues: The bank learns that it or its sector is being targeted only once an attack is under way
Stolen credentials, planned attacks or data offered for sale in criminal forums go unseen because the bank has no view of those sources
Analysts cannot tell which of thousands of indicators and alerts matter, so effort goes to noise while relevant threats wait

trajectoryNotes.summary: Providers in this market describe a common core: collection from closed criminal forums, marketplaces and messaging channels alongside open and technical sources, analyst-written reporting, alerting tailored to the customer, and delivery into security tools. Flashpoint and Intel 471 both add AI assistance for summarising and reporting; Intel 471 ties collection to the customer's stated intelligence requirements and generates ready-to-run queries for detection tools. Vendors are moving from supplying intelligence to acting on it: Recorded Future launched Autonomous Threat Operations in October 2025 to run threat hunting continuously across a customer's security tools. Ownership is consolidating into larger groups: Mastercard reported acquiring Recorded Future in December 2024 and launching a payment-focused threat intelligence service built on it in 2025.

categories.definition: Products that find weaknesses across a bank's technology and attack surface and rank them by how likely they are to be exploited.
categories.name: Vulnerability and exposure management
riskIssues: Known vulnerabilities stay unpatched because there are too many to rank
Internet-facing assets exist that the bank does not know about
Remediation cannot be evidenced to supervisors

trajectoryNotes.summary: Tenable completed its acquisition of Vulcan Cyber, an exposure management company, saying Vulcan's capabilities would add visibility, prioritisation and remediation to its exposure management platform; the announcement did not state the price.

ENISA, the EU's cybersecurity agency, put the European Vulnerability Database into operation, as required by the NIS2 Directive. It aggregates vulnerability information from CSIRTs, vendors and existing databases, including mitigation measures and exploitation status.
ServiceNow completed its acquisition of Armis, a cyber exposure management company covering operational technology, IoT and medical devices, for about $7.75 billion in cash.

CrowdStrike agreed to acquire the intellectual property of XM Cyber, a Schwarz Digits company, including more than 45 patents and source code but not its customers or revenue; the price was not disclosed. After closing, XM Cyber is to continue as a standalone business under an IP licence from CrowdStrike.

Reporting obligations under the EU Cyber Resilience Act apply from 11 September 2026, according to the European Commission: manufacturers of products with digital elements must give an early warning of an actively exploited vulnerability or severe incident within 24 hours and a full notification within 72 hours, through the single reporting platform operated by ENISA.

capabilities.description: Lets teams define agents, tools and workflows.
capabilities.name: Agent building tools

capabilities.description: Requires human approval for defined actions.
capabilities.name: Human approval steps

capabilities.description: Gives agents their own identity and scoped permissions.
capabilities.name: Agent identity and permissions

capabilities.description: Records every action an agent takes.
capabilities.name: Action audit trail

capabilities.description: Supports open standards for connecting agents to tools and each other.
capabilities.name: Open agent protocols

capabilities.description: Tests agent behaviour before and after release.
capabilities.name: Agent evaluation and testing

capabilities.description: Suggests and explains code in the editor.
capabilities.name: Code completion and chat

capabilities.description: Carries out multi-step changes with limited supervision.
capabilities.name: Autonomous coding agents

capabilities.description: Commits to not training on or retaining customer code.
