capability.rationale: Anchor 3: vendor pages cover four of six listed capabilities in full, with data loss prevention and masking partial. Anchor 4 needs all or nearly all capabilities, and blocking of data leaving by email, web or endpoint is not described.

maturity.rationale: Anchor 3: customer stories name E*TRADE, Nasdaq and Aflac and the changelog shows frequent releases. Anchor 4 needs more than three years of general availability. The earliest dated evidence of this platform on sale is its May 2025 FedRAMP listing, and the dossier does not show that the company has sold it since 2005.

observability.rationale: Anchor 2: an activity audit trail and API export of events and audit data are documented, which goes beyond manual export, but no named SIEM integration was found (only syslog alert routing), so anchor 3 is not fully met.

risk_country.rationale: Anchor 3 applied under the vendor-claim cap. Ownership is disclosed in SEC filings (US-listed, with a pending sale to Thoma Bravo-owned Proofpoint), and vendor documents show customers choosing a hosting region in the US, EU, UK or Canada and list group entities by country, which would meet anchor 4. The region evidence is vendor-published, and restriction of support access by jurisdiction was not found.

scalability.rationale: Anchor 4: customer stories name regulated enterprises including Nasdaq, E*TRADE and Aflac, and hosting is offered in nine customer-chosen geographies. SAML single sign-on and role-based access are also documented. Anchor 5 needs a regulated deployment confirmed by a source other than the vendor or independently published performance.

standards_alignment.rationale: Anchor 3: two current third-party attestations name the product. One is registry-confirmed: the FedRAMP Marketplace lists 'Varonis Data Security Platform' as FedRAMP Certified (Class C, Moderate, since 2025-05-14). The other is vendor-stated: a SOC 2 Type II report for the SaaS Data Security Platform dated 2025-12-24. Because the second rests on the vendor's statement, the basis is vendor-claimed. The ISO 27001, ISO 27701 and PCI DSS scopes are not public and the CSA STAR entry is a self-assessment. Anchor 4 needs published control mappings to category frameworks, which were not found.

viability.rationale: Anchor 4: audited public financials show US$623.5 million revenue and about US$921 million in cash and short-term investments for 2025. Net losses in each of the last three years rule out anchor 5. Confidence is medium because an acquisition by Proofpoint is pending and the self-hosted product is being retired.

capability.rationale: Anchor 4: all seven listed capabilities are shown in the vendor's public technical documentation: workload coverage, immutable repositories with single-use credentials, entropy and file-activity analysis of backups, scanning that finds the last clean restore point, isolated virtual labs and a clean-room scenario, orchestrated and tested recovery plans with reports, and recovery of Active Directory forests and Microsoft Entra ID. Limits are noted: Microsoft 365 and Salesforce are separate products, orchestration needs the Premium edition, and lab testing is documented for VMware vSphere and Hyper-V. Anchor 5 needs capability confirmed by a source other than the vendor; a 2022 TechTarget report describes one bank using isolated labs to check restores, which does not confirm the capability list as a whole, and no independent test was read.

maturity.rationale: Anchor 4: generally available for well over three years (the lifecycle policy dates version 11 to February 2021 and version 12 to February 2023; version 13.1 shipped in July 2026), with adoption shown by named regulated customers: Veeam's customer stories for Rabobank and Kasikornbank carry statements from named staff of each bank. Support and lifecycle policies are published. Anchor 5 also needs bank customers in production confirmed by a source other than the vendor: one independent report was read, a May 2022 TechTarget article saying Kasikornbank uses Veeam Backup & Replication, based on remarks at the vendor's conference. A single bank in an article more than four years old is not taken as meeting that anchor.

observability.rationale: Anchor 3: audit logs and approval records are documented, events can be streamed to a syslog server in RFC 5424 format and read by API, and the vendor describes integrations with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks. Anchor 4 is not met: no account of how a malware detection is explained was read, configurable retention of audit records is not described, and tamper evidence is limited to the option of storing file-restore audit logs on write-once storage.

risk_country.rationale: Anchor 4: ownership is disclosed (a US-headquartered private company controlled by Insight Partners, with TPG, Temasek and Neuberger Berman named as investors, though the size of each holding is not published), and the customer chooses where processing happens because the software and its backup repositories run on the customer's own infrastructure. Anchor 5 needs support access restricted to chosen jurisdictions and no sanctions exposure found: support engineer locations were not found, a restricted line is described only for US Federal customers, and sanctions screening has not been run.

scalability.rationale: Anchor 4: adoption at large-enterprise scale is shown in documentation and press (regression-tested maximums of 20,000 virtual machines per backup server and 100 backup servers under one monitoring server; a customer story describing 12,500 virtual machines at Rabobank; TechTarget reporting 2 petabytes at Kasikornbank), together with dedicated deployment, since the software runs only on the customer's own infrastructure. SAML single sign-on with eight tested identity providers and role-based access are documented. Anchor 5 needs a deployment at a bank confirmed by a source other than the vendor: the one independent report is from 2022, is a short passage based on a conference talk and gives no detail of the deployment, so it is not relied on for the top level.

standards_alignment.rationale: Anchor 2: one current third-party attestation was confirmed in a registry, a FIPS 140-3 validation (CMVP certificate 5156) that names a Veeam cryptographic module and not the product. The trust centre lists SOC 2 Type 2 and several ISO certificates, but the documents are behind a sign-in portal and their scope is not stated publicly; the CSA STAR entry covers Veeam Data Cloud, a different product. Anchor 3 needs two or more attestations whose scope covers the product; a bank that obtains the gated reports may be able to confirm that.

viability.rationale: Anchor 3: revenue-backed with no distress signals found. Anchor 4 needs audited or publicly reported financials: the company is privately held, the figures are its own statements relayed by the press, and its debt is not disclosed. Workforce reductions reported in 2023 and January 2024 are more than two years old.

capability.rationale: Anchor 4: documentation covers six of seven listed capabilities, with secrets detection partial because it appears only within container and infrastructure-as-code scanning, and none absent. events.headline: 1Kosmos announces FedRAMP High authorization through FedHIVE
events.summary: 1Kosmos announced on 2025-06-03 that its platform had achieved FedRAMP High authorization and is offered as part of FedHIVE's FedRAMP High offerings. The sponsoring agency and assessor were not named, and the FedRAMP Marketplace entry was not read.

events.headline: 1Kosmos raises US$57M Series B
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-08-12 that 1Kosmos had raised a US$57 million Series B led by Forgepoint Capital, Oquirrh Ventures and Origami Capital, including a US$10 million credit line from Bridge Bank, taking the total raised to US$72 million.

events.headline: ABBYY completes investment from Marlin Equity Partners, which becomes its largest shareholder
events.summary: ABBYY announced that it had completed an investment from Marlin Equity Partners, under which Marlin would become its largest shareholder and a Marlin managing director would join the board. No amount or percentage was given.

events.headline: ABBYY launches Vantage 3.0 with direct LLM integration
events.summary: ABBYY announced Vantage 3.0 with prompt-based extraction through a connection to Azure OpenAI, a rebuilt technology stack, an analytics dashboard, redaction tools and more pre-configured models. Release notes date general availability to February 2026.

events.headline: ABBYY discloses that a breach at supplier Klue exposed Salesforce data
events.summary: ABBYY disclosed on its trust centre on 2026-06-25 that a breach at Klue, a competitive-intelligence platform it had used, affected Salesforce data accessed through Klue's integration. ABBYY stated that its network, products and technology were not affected and that it revoked credentials, disabled the integration and stopped using Klue.

events.headline: ABBYY discloses possible exposure of CI/CD credentials from the Trivy supply-chain compromise
events.summary: ABBYY disclosed on its trust centre on 2026-09-02 a potential exposure of internal credentials for its CI/CD and artifact-management tooling arising from the March 2026 Trivy supply-chain compromise. ABBYY stated that it found no evidence of unauthorised use, that the credentials expired about 60 hours after issue and that it rotated them.

events.headline: Abnormal Security rebrands as Abnormal AI
events.summary: The company announced it had renamed itself Abnormal AI, the name it used after its 2018 founding, changed its legal name from Abnormal Security Corporation to Abnormal AI, Inc., and moved to the abnormal.ai domain.

events.headline: Abnormal AI appoints chief legal officer and two vice presidents
events.summary: Abnormal AI announced the appointments of John Slavitt as chief legal officer, Stephen Harrison as vice president of product for new products, and Noah Rolff as vice president of customer success.

events.headline: Anthropic files trademark and unfair competition suit against Abnormal AI over its logo
events.summary: Abnormal AI disclosed on 2026-07-07 that Anthropic filed a lawsuit against it on 2026-07-01 claiming trademark infringement and unfair competition over Abnormal's logo. Reported by BankInfoSecurity on 2026-07-08: the complaint was filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California and alleges that Abnormal's April 2025 rebrand moved its branding closer to Anthropic's. Abnormal denies the allegations and said the suit creates no security risk for customers. No ruling or settlement was found as of 2026-11-20.

events.headline: Abnormal AI says it is pursuing FedRAMP High, having held Moderate since April 2025
events.summary: Abnormal AI announced it is pursuing FedRAMP Class D (High) for its Abnormal Gov environment, with the Tennessee Valley Authority as sponsoring agency, and stated it has held FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) since April 2025. The High authorisation had not been granted at the time of the announcement.

events.headline: Abnormal AI and OpenAI announce partnership
events.summary: Abnormal AI announced a partnership with OpenAI under which it will expand its internal use of OpenAI models, join OpenAI's cyber partner programme and explore joint security tooling. The release says core detection products remain powered by Abnormal's own behavioural models.

events.headline: Abnormal AI adds Control Center, Email DLP Rules and AI Phishing Coach upgrades
events.summary: Abnormal AI announced Control Center (custom detection models and rules), Email DLP Rules for outbound mail, and adaptive phishing-simulation training in AI Phishing Coach. Custom AI models and the Phishing Coach features were stated as generally available from 31 August 2026; custom rules and Email DLP Rules were in early access.

events.headline: Absolute Software completes the purchase of NetMotion
events.summary: Absolute Software Corporation stated in a release filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it completed the acquisition of NetMotion Software from The Carlyle Group on 2021-07-01 for about US$340 million in cash, financed with about US$65 million of its own cash and a US$275 million term loan. NetMotion's remote access products became Absolute Secure Access.

events.headline: Crosspoint Capital Partners takes Absolute Software private
events.summary: Absolute's investors page states that the company became a wholly owned subsidiary of Crosspoint Capital Partners, L.P. on 2023-07-27 and that its shares no longer trade on the Toronto Stock Exchange or Nasdaq. SecurityWeek reported on 2023-05-16 that the agreed price was US$11.50 a share, an enterprise value of about US$870 million including debt.

events.headline: Absolute Software renames itself Absolute Security
events.summary: The company announced that it had changed its name from Absolute Software to Absolute Security; SecurityBrief reported the change on 2024-04-18. The date recorded is that of the press report, because the vendor's release as now published carries no date. The legal entities keep the Absolute Software name.

events.headline: Absolute Security acquires Syxsense
events.summary: Absolute Security announced the acquisition of Syxsense, a patch, vulnerability and endpoint management company founded in 2012, for an undisclosed price, reported by SiliconANGLE on 2024-09-05. Its patching, vulnerability remediation and workflow automation now form the Resilience for Security and Resilience for Automation editions of Secure Endpoint.

events.headline: Absolute Secure Endpoint reaches FedRAMP Moderate
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists the Absolute Secure Endpoint Product Suite as certified at Class C (Moderate) since 2025-03-04. Absolute announced the authorisation on 2025-03-06 and named Kratos as assessor.

events.headline: Absolute Resilience offered in the CrowdStrike Marketplace
events.summary: Absolute Security announced an expanded partnership with CrowdStrike under which its resilience products, including Rehydrate and application self-healing, can be bought through the CrowdStrike Marketplace.

events.headline: Absolute releases Rehydrate remote device recovery
events.summary: Absolute Security announced that Rehydrate, which runs recovery playbooks from device firmware to restore Windows PCs whose operating system has failed or been compromised, was generally available in the Resilience editions of Secure Endpoint.

events.headline: Absolute links Secure Endpoint device checks to Secure Access
events.summary: Absolute Security announced that Secure Endpoint and Secure Access were integrated on one platform, so that an enrolled device can be checked against security policy before it connects to networks and applications. No availability date was given.

events.headline: Absolute Secure Endpoint verified as GovRAMP Authorized
events.summary: Absolute Security announced on 2026-05-14 that Secure Endpoint had achieved GovRAMP Authorized verification at Moderate level for US state, local and education agencies. The GovRAMP register was not checked.

events.headline: Absolute publishes fixes in Secure Access 14.57
events.summary: Absolute disclosed in its vulnerability archive on 2026-08-12 that Secure Access 14.57 fixed flaws that could allow denial of service by an attacker who controlled an authentication session or sat between client and server. The entry read lists no CVE identifiers and does not state that the flaws were exploited.

events.headline: Absolute Security acquires FirmGuard from Phoenix Technologies
events.summary: Absolute Security announced the acquisition of FirmGuard, a firmware security and management service for UEFI BIOS, from Phoenix Technologies for an undisclosed price, to add firmware integrity checking, posture management and patching to its platform.

events.headline: Absolute Secure Endpoint adds Linux support
events.summary: Absolute Security announced that the Secure Endpoint agent supports Ubuntu and Red Hat Enterprise Linux workstations, with inventory and device freeze available at once and patching and automation in selected editions. The release also announced self-hosted Secure Access deployments for US federal and state organisations.

events.headline: ShadowPlex Platform listed as FedRAMP Ready at Moderate impact level
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace data file lists Acalvio's ShadowPlex Platform, a software-as-a-service offering, with the status FedRAMP Ready at the Moderate impact level and a ready date of 30 June 2025, with ControlCase as independent assessor. FedRAMP Ready is a readiness designation and not an authorisation; the same entry shows no agency authorisation. Acalvio first announced a FedRAMP Ready designation in October 2021.

events.headline: Acalvio launches 360 Deception for the ShadowPlex platform
events.summary: Acalvio announced 360 Deception on 17 March 2026, describing it as the next generation of its deception platform, aimed at attacks automated with AI. The company says it adjusts decoys and honeytokens dynamically, makes real assets appear deceptive as well as making decoys look real, and steers intruders into controlled false paths.

events.headline: Acalvio launches Deception Guardrails for AI agents
events.summary: Acalvio announced Deception Guardrails on 30 July 2026, a capability of the ShadowPlex platform that places decoys and tripwires in AI agent workflows and around AI infrastructure to detect agents that have been hijacked or are misbehaving. The company describes it as patent pending. SecurityBrief UK reported the launch the next day.

events.headline: Acalvio launches ShadowPlex AI Agent in the Gemini Enterprise agent marketplace
events.summary: Acalvio announced on 29 September 2026 an AI agent, listed in the Gemini Enterprise agent marketplace and working with Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise, that turns a security objective written in plain language into a deception playbook for deployment through the ShadowPlex platform.

events.headline: Adaptive Security raises US$43 million Series A co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and the OpenAI Startup Fund
events.summary: Adaptive Security announced on 2 April 2025 a US$43 million Series A co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and the OpenAI Startup Fund. TechCrunch reported that OpenAI confirmed it was its first investment in a cybersecurity company. SecurityWeek named Abstract Ventures, Eniac Ventures, CrossBeam Ventures and K5 as further investors. The company later said the OpenAI Startup Fund led a US$12 million follow-on in September 2025.

events.headline: Adaptive Security raises US$81 million Series B led by Bain Capital Ventures
events.summary: Adaptive Security announced on 16 December 2025 an US$81 million Series B led by Bain Capital Ventures, with NVentures (NVIDIA's venture arm), the OpenAI Startup Fund, Andreessen Horowitz, Abstract Ventures, Capital One Ventures and Citi Ventures taking part. The company and SecurityWeek put total funding at US$146.5 million; BankInfoSecurity reported US$136 million. BankInfoSecurity reported that the money would go to product, design and engineering teams in New York.

events.headline: Adaptive Security launches Adaptive Email Security in beta
events.summary: In a product update dated 16 April 2026 the company launched Adaptive Email Security in beta. The update describes a read-only API connection to Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 with no change to mail routing. In August 2026 the company said hundreds of customers were using the product.

events.headline: Adaptive Security launches AI Governance in beta
events.summary: In a product update dated 23 April 2026 the company launched Adaptive AI Governance in beta, describing real-time visibility of the AI tools and unsanctioned applications employees use.

events.headline: AegisAI launches with US$13 million in seed funding
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-09-11 that AegisAI, an email security startup founded by two former Google Safe Browsing and reCAPTCHA leaders, launched with US$13 million in seed funding backed by Accel and Foundation Capital. The product connects to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace and uses AI agents to examine attachments, links, metadata and QR codes.

events.headline: AegisAI raises US$36 million Series A led by Battery Ventures
events.summary: TechCrunch reported that AegisAI raised a US$36 million Series A led by Battery Ventures, with existing backers Accel and Foundation Capital, taking total funding to US$49 million. The company said it had dozens of customers and named Mesh, LangChain and Lokker.

events.headline: Aikido announces that code review start-up Trag has joined it
events.summary: Aikido said on 2025-08-21 that Trag, which uses language models to review code with whole-repository context, was now part of Aikido and that its team had joined earlier that summer. The technology became Aikido Code Quality. Terms were not disclosed. The event is dated to the announcement.

events.headline: Allseek and Haicker join Aikido to build AI penetration testing
events.summary: Aikido announced on 2025-09-24 that the teams of Allseek and Haicker, two start-ups building autonomous penetration-testing agents, were joining it to build Aikido Attack. The post does not call the deals acquisitions or give terms; SiliconANGLE later described Aikido as having acquired Allseek BV and Haicker SA in 2025.

events.headline: Aikido Security raises US$60M Series B led by DST Global at a US$1B valuation
events.summary: Aikido announced a US$60 million Series B on 2026-01-14, led by DST Global with PSG Equity, Notion Capital and Singular, at a US$1 billion valuation. SecurityWeek reported total funding of more than US$84 million.

events.headline: Aikido acquires Root, which patches open-source vulnerabilities in place
events.summary: Aikido announced on 2026-06-30 that it had acquired Root (Root.io Inc., founded in 2020 as Slim.AI), whose AI agents build patches for open-source vulnerabilities at the versions customers already run. The capability is offered as Aikido Libraries and Aikido Images. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Aikido announces ISO/IEC 42001 certification for its AI features
events.summary: Aikido said on 2026-08-26 that it had been certified to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, with a scope covering the AI-enabled features of its platform, including AutoFix, AutoTriage, AI pentesting and code review. The post does not name the certification body or the certificate date; the event is dated to the announcement.

events.headline: Aikido says its government edition is FedRAMP Moderate authorised through Knox Systems
events.summary: Aikido's changelog of 2026-10-22 announced FedRAMP Moderate status. Its FedRAMP page says the separate Aikido for Government edition has been authorised since October 2026 inside Knox Systems' FedRAMP boundary on AWS GovCloud. The FedRAMP Marketplace data file read on 2026-11-23 lists Knox Systems as FedRAMP Authorized at Moderate and does not name Aikido.

events.headline: Akamai completes acquisition of Guardicore
events.summary: Akamai announced on 2021-10-21 that it had completed its acquisition of Guardicore, a micro-segmentation company based in Tel Aviv, Israel, for approximately US$600 million, as first announced on 2021-09-29. The products became Akamai Guardicore Segmentation.

events.headline: Akamai acquires Fermyon Technologies
events.summary: Akamai's Form 10-K for 2025 records the acquisition in November 2025 of Fermyon Technologies, a serverless WebAssembly company. The filing sections read give the month only; the event is dated to the first of the month.

events.headline: Akamai issues US$3.5 billion of zero-coupon convertible senior notes
events.summary: Akamai's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 shows convertible senior notes due 2030 (US$1,750 million) and due 2032 (US$1,750 million) issued in May 2026, taking total convertible note principal to US$7,640 million. The filing sections read give the month only; the event is dated to the first of the month.

events.headline: Akamai acquires LayerX Security
events.summary: Akamai's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 records the acquisition in July 2026 of LayerX Security Ltd., a browser security company, for US$192.9 million in cash. The filing gives the month only; the event is dated to the first of the month.

events.headline: Akamai closes US$2.5 billion offering of convertible senior notes
events.summary: Akamai announced on 2026-11-12 that it had closed a private offering of US$2.5 billion of 1.00% convertible senior notes in two US$1.25 billion series, due 2028 and 2031, including the initial purchasers' full option. Akamai put net proceeds at about US$2.46 billion and said it would use them for note hedge transactions, to repay part of its convertible notes due September 2027, for capital expenditure in its cloud infrastructure business and for general corporate purposes.

events.headline: Akamai and Microsoft bring Akamai Workforce Protector to Edge for Business on mobile
events.summary: Akamai announced on 2026-11-18 a collaboration with Microsoft under which organisations can deploy the Akamai Workforce Protector extension (formerly LayerX) in Microsoft Edge for Business on managed iOS and Android devices, using Microsoft's deployment tools. The release does not concern Akamai Guardicore Segmentation.

events.headline: US Department of Defense designates Alibaba Group Holding Limited a Chinese military company
events.summary: The US Department of Defense published a notice in the Federal Register on 10 June 2026 under Section 1260H of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act that lists Alibaba Group Holding Limited as a Chinese military company, stating that it is indirectly affiliated with China's state assets regulator and is a military-civil fusion contributor through affiliation with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Alibaba's annual report filed on 20 May 2026 disclosed that an earlier listing in February 2026 had been withdrawn and stated that the designation mainly prohibits the Department of Defense from dealing with listed entities and does not trigger blocking sanctions.

events.headline: US court grants Alibaba a preliminary injunction limited to a lobbying restriction; designation stands
events.summary: Reported by the South China Morning Post on 29 October 2026: a judge of the US District Court for the Northern District of California granted Alibaba a preliminary injunction against a lobbying restriction tied to its Section 1260H designation, in a lawsuit Alibaba filed on 23 June 2026, and did not decide Alibaba's challenge to the designation itself, which remains in place. The Next Web reported on 5 July 2026, citing Bloomberg, that the court had earlier granted temporary relief on the same restriction.

events.headline: Anaconda files copyright case naming Alibaba Group and Alibaba Cloud in Delaware federal court
events.summary: According to the federal docket index published by CourtListener, Anaconda, Inc. filed a copyright case against Alibaba Group Holding Limited in the US District Court for the District of Delaware on 2026-11-13 (No. 1:26-cv-01466), with Alibaba Cloud listed among the parties. The claims and any response were not reviewed.

events.headline: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max flagship model
events.summary: Alibaba announced Qwen4-Max on 2026-11-16, describing it as the most capable Qwen model so far, with native vision and a one-million-token context window, available through QwenCloud's Token Plan and API. A follow-up Alibaba Cloud post on 2026-11-17 presented the model to enterprise teams. Neither post named Model Studio as a launch channel, and Alibaba said smaller open-weight Qwen4 models would follow without giving a date.

events.headline: Anthropic raises US$65 billion Series H at US$965 billion valuation
events.summary: Anthropic announced a US$65 billion Series H at a US$965 billion post-money valuation, led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital. Crunchbase News reported the total includes US$15 billion of previously committed investment from Amazon and Google.

events.headline: Court gives final approval to US$1.5 billion authors' copyright settlement with Anthropic
events.summary: Reported by Bloomberg Law on 2026-07-20 and The Next Web on 2026-07-21: a federal court granted final approval of a US$1.5 billion settlement in the authors' class action Bartz v. Anthropic over the downloading of pirated books used for model training.

events.headline: District judge rules Pentagon's supply chain risk designation of Anthropic unlawful
events.summary: Reported by Al Jazeera on 2026-08-28, and noted by the Associated Press on 2026-09-25: a federal district judge in California ruled that the US Defense Department acted unlawfully in designating Anthropic a supply chain risk earlier in 2026. The government was expected to contest the ruling.

events.headline: Appeals court lets Pentagon keep supply chain risk label on Anthropic
events.summary: Reported by the Associated Press on 2026-09-25, following Al Jazeera's report of the earlier district ruling: a federal appeals court in Washington ruled 2-1 against Anthropic's challenge to the Defense Department's supply chain risk designation in a parallel case. AP reported Anthropic said it disagreed and was considering further review.

events.headline: Anthropic exposes Claude Code source code through an npm packaging error
events.summary: Reported by TechRadar on 2026-04-01 and Notebookcheck on 2026-04-07: on 2026-03-31 a source map published with a Claude Code npm package exposed a large part of the tool's source code, which was quickly mirrored. TechRadar reported that Anthropic said no sensitive customer data or credentials were involved and called it a packaging error caused by human error, not a security breach. Notebookcheck reported that researchers then found a permission-rule flaw later fixed in an update.

events.headline: Anthropic announces 28 security and compliance integrations for its Compliance API
events.summary: Anthropic announced 28 partner integrations for the Compliance API, which exposes Claude Enterprise conversation content and activity events across Claude Enterprise and Claude Platform. Named partners include Splunk, Elastic, Datadog, Sumo Logic, CrowdStrike, Microsoft Purview, Zscaler and Proofpoint; a later update to the post says the list has passed 100.

events.headline: US export-control directive leads Anthropic to suspend Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all customers
events.summary: Reported by Il Sole 24 Ore on 2026-06-13: Anthropic disabled its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for all customers after a US government directive, issued under export-control rules on national-security grounds, required it to suspend access for foreign nationals; Anthropic said the action did not meet the standard of a transparent and fair process. Reported by The Regulatory Review on 2026-06-19: the order came from the US Department of Commerce and cited a cybersecurity concern. The two reports differ on whose access the order covered, and later status was not established.

events.headline: Reservoir Media Management files copyright case against Anthropic in California federal court
events.summary: According to the federal docket index published by CourtListener, Reservoir Media Management, Inc. filed a copyright case against Anthropic PBC in the US District Court for the Northern District of California on 2026-10-21 (No. 5:26-cv-12308). The index lists further copyright, trademark, patent and antitrust-coded cases filed against Anthropic between September and November 2026. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Anthropic lists on Nasdaq as ANT; IPO raises about US$93.5 billion gross
events.summary: Anthropic announced on 2026-11-18 that it had priced its initial public offering at US$83.00 per Class A share, and its shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT on 2026-11-19. In a release dated 2026-11-20, Anthropic said the offering closed with 1,127,000,000 shares sold, including the underwriters' full option, for gross proceeds of about US$93.5 billion, of which about US$91.6 billion went to the company, and that a concurrent private placement to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA and TSMC Partners raised about US$26.0 billion more. Al Jazeera reported on 2026-11-19 that the shares first traded at US$111.50 and closed at US$97.17.

events.headline: Anthropic status page records two periods of elevated errors across claude.ai, the API and Claude Code
events.summary: According to Anthropic's status page, two incidents on 2026-11-13 caused elevated errors. The first, described as an authentication issue affecting claude.ai and Claude Cowork, ran from about 09:58 to 11:58 UTC; the second, affecting claude.ai, the API, Claude Code, connectors and other services, ran from about 13:09 to 15:38 UTC. The status entries did not give a root cause for either incident.

events.headline: Anvilogic and Databricks announce detection engineering partnership
events.summary: Anvilogic announced a partnership with Databricks that integrates its detection engineering platform with the Databricks lakehouse, so that detections can be built and run on security data held there.

events.headline: Anvilogic launches Blueprints workflow automation
events.summary: Anvilogic announced Blueprints, a capability that lets analysts describe a security operations procedure in natural language and have AI agents run it across data onboarding, detection engineering, threat hunting and investigation.

events.headline: Anvilogic makes Blueprints generally available and adds search over cloud storage
events.summary: Anvilogic announced general availability of Blueprints, with scheduling, customer-configured connectors, sharing across teams and daily AI budget controls, and a new federated search that reaches data left in Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage and Google Cloud Storage without moving it.

events.headline: SpaceX completes acquisition of Cursor maker Anysphere

quote.text: Cursor has officially been acquired by SpaceX.

events.summary: Cursor announced on 2026-08-14 that its acquisition by SpaceX was complete, following a partnership with SpaceXAI announced in April 2026. The Next Web reported the same day that the deal was valued at $60bn, that a binding agreement had been announced in June 2026, and that SpaceX confirmed completion in a regulatory filing. The vendor's post gives no price. The Cursor name and the Anysphere, Inc. legal entity continue to appear on the vendor's site.

events.headline: Cursor raises $2.3bn Series D at $29.3bn post-money valuation
events.summary: Cursor announced a $2.3bn Series D at a $29.3bn post-money valuation, with existing investors Accel, Thrive and Andreessen Horowitz and new investors Coatue, NVIDIA and Google. The post said annualised revenue had passed $1bn and the team numbered over 300.

events.headline: Cursor buys code-review company Graphite
events.summary: The Next Web reported on 2026-08-14 that Cursor bought Graphite in December 2025. The exact date and terms were not found; the date recorded is the first day of the reported month.

events.headline: Firetiger team joins Cursor
events.summary: Cursor announced that the team of Firetiger, a 2024-founded company building agents that monitor software in production, was joining Cursor. No terms were given.

events.headline: Cursor launches Self-Hosted Machines for cloud agents
events.summary: Cursor announced that cloud agents can run tool execution on worker machines inside the customer's network, connected outbound to Cursor. The agent loop and model inference stay with Cursor, and tool outputs that may contain code are sent to Cursor.

events.headline: Cursor discloses data exposure via a provider key and tampered marketplace extension

quote.text: Uninstalling the extension alone may not be enough.

events.summary: Disclosed by Cursor on 2026-10-29 and updated on 2026-11-13: an attacker used an access key Cursor had issued to inference provider Fireworks to copy a storage bucket holding mostly 2025 coding-agent traces from sessions without Privacy Mode, some containing credentials. Cursor stated that those credentials gave access to internal tools and that tampered builds of the Claude Code extension (2.1.312 and 2.1.313) were served from its extension marketplace cache for about 11 hours on 2026-10-29 to at most 5,000 users. Cursor stated that agent traces were exposed for fewer than 0.05% of users, API credentials for fewer than 0.01% of customers, that customer code repositories and Privacy Mode data were not affected, and that it moved inference off Fireworks, rotated credentials and rebuilt the marketplace.

events.headline: Cursor adds multiplayer support to Projects, in beta for all users
events.summary: Cursor announced on its blog on 2026-11-10 that Projects, its workspace for directing several agents through a coordinator, now lets teammates join a shared Project with shared context, a shared task board and coordination between teammates' agents. Cursor said the feature is rolling out in beta to all users from that date.

events.headline: 1Password acquires Apono
events.summary: 1Password announced on 2026-06-15 that it had acquired Apono and would combine its just-in-time access capabilities with 1Password Unified Access and a new credential broker. Terms were not disclosed; SecurityWeek reported on 2026-06-17 that Calcalist put the price at $250 million to $300 million. The announcement does not say whether Apono continues as a standalone product; Apono's site describes it as now part of 1Password.

events.headline: Apono raises $34 million Series B
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-11-18 that Apono had raised a $34 million Series B led by USVP with 33N, Swisscom Ventures, Vertex Ventures and earlier investors, taking total funding to more than $54 million, and named Intel, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Workday as customers.

events.headline: AppViewX receives $30 million from Brighton Park Capital
events.summary: AppViewX announced $30 million of growth funding from Brighton Park Capital, with three new board members. Recorded although older than 24 months because it is the last financing with a disclosed amount and brought in the investor that later sold to Haveli Investments.

events.headline: Haveli Investments completes majority acquisition of AppViewX
events.summary: Haveli Investments, a private-equity firm based in Austin, Texas, completed its acquisition of AppViewX, announced on 21 November 2024 as a majority investment. Terms were not disclosed. AppViewX continues to trade under its own name.

events.headline: AppViewX appoints Dino DiMarino chief executive; Gregory Webb becomes chairman
events.summary: AppViewX named Dino DiMarino, formerly chief revenue officer of Qualys, as chief executive. Gregory Webb, chief executive since November 2019, moved to chairman. A new chief financial officer and chief revenue officer were named at the same time.

events.headline: AppViewX announces a post-quantum cryptography assessment tool
events.summary: AppViewX announced an assessment tool that scans code, dependencies, configurations and certificates and produces a cryptographic bill of materials and a readiness score. The tool is now documented as part of Quantum Trust Hub.

events.headline: AppViewX introduces Quantum Trust Hub as an add-on to its CLM product
events.summary: AppViewX introduced Quantum Trust Hub, a module for assessing quantum-vulnerable cryptography and planning migration, sold as an add-on to its certificate lifecycle management product under an additional licence, with a free readiness scan for existing customers.

events.headline: AppViewX acquires Eos, a maker of identity controls for AI agents
events.summary: AppViewX announced it had acquired Eos, which builds identity governance and access control for AI agents and autonomous workloads. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Archit Lohokare of Eos becomes AppViewX chief executive; Dino DiMarino steps down
events.summary: With the Eos acquisition, AppViewX appointed Eos co-founder Archit Lohokare as chief executive, succeeding Dino DiMarino, who the company said had stepped down to pursue other opportunities. Eos co-founder Kashyap Ivaturi became chief technology officer.

events.headline: AppViewX offers Quantum Trust Hub as a standalone product and adds Qualys discovery
events.summary: AppViewX announced that Quantum Trust Hub is available as a standalone solution, with discovery from existing Qualys scan data alongside Tenable, upload of third-party bills of materials, business-context risk ranking and ServiceNow remediation tickets.

events.headline: Aqua Security co-founders step back; Mike Dube named chief executive
events.summary: Aqua announced that co-founders Dror Davidoff and Amir Jerbi were stepping back from the chief executive and chief technology officer roles to become strategic advisers. Mike Dube, previously president and chief revenue officer, became chief executive, and Nir Makowski became chief product and technology officer.

events.headline: Aqua's open-source Trivy scanner and GitHub Actions compromised in supply chain attack
events.summary: Aqua disclosed that attackers who had obtained a privileged token from Trivy's GitHub Actions environment in late February 2026 published a malicious Trivy v0.69.4 release on 2026-03-19 and redirected version tags of the trivy-action and setup-trivy GitHub Actions to code containing an infostealer. Malicious Docker Hub images followed on 2026-03-22 and internal repositories were made public. Aqua said an earlier credential rotation had been incomplete, that it engaged Sygnia for forensics, and that it had no indication its commercial products were affected. The advisory is rated critical (CVE-2026-33634).

events.headline: Cinven completes acquisition of Archer from Clearlake and STG
events.summary: Clearlake Capital Group and Symphony Technology Group announced on 2023-07-10 that the sale of Archer Technologies to the private equity firm Cinven had completed; terms were not disclosed. Cinven's announcement of 2023-04-13 described Archer as a carve-out from RSA Security.

events.headline: Archer introduces Archer Evolv
events.summary: Archer announced Archer Evolv, described as its next-generation SaaS offering, with Evolv for Compliance available at launch and Evolv for Risk to follow.

events.headline: Archer launches Evolv Foundation and Evolv Workplace AI agents
events.summary: TechIntelPro reported on 2026-09-15 that Archer launched Archer Evolv Foundation and Archer Evolv Workplace, a governed set of AI agents (Operators) working inside its GRC system, including in third-party risk.

events.headline: Dynatrace completes its acquisition of Arize AI
events.summary: Dynatrace announced on 2026-10-01 that it had completed its acquisition of Arize. The definitive agreement, reported by ITPro on 2026-08-14, was a cash and stock transaction valued at US$915 million. Dynatrace said Arize will keep supporting both Arize AX and the open-source Phoenix project, and that Arize capabilities will be integrated into the Dynatrace platform over time. According to diginomica, the founders joined Dynatrace and Arize's chief executive continues to lead the Arize team. Dynatrace is not a tracked vendor in this dataset, so the record stays under Arize AI.

events.headline: Arize AI raises US$70M Series C led by Adams Street Partners
events.summary: Arize AI announced a US$70 million Series C led by Adams Street Partners, with M12, Sinewave Ventures, OMERS Ventures, Datadog, PagerDuty, Industry Ventures and Archerman Capital, and existing investors Foundation Capital, Battery Ventures, TCV and Swift VC. TechCrunch reported that the round took total funding to more than US$130 million.

events.headline: Armadin launches publicly with US$189.9 million in seed and Series A funding
events.summary: Armadin, founded by former Mandiant chief executive Kevin Mandia with Travis Lanham, Evan Peña and David Slater, announced its public launch with US$189.9 million in combined seed and Series A funding led by Accel, with GV, Kleiner Perkins, Menlo Ventures, In-Q-Tel, 8VC and Ballistic Ventures. SecurityWeek noted an earlier US$24 million seed announced quietly in late 2025 and did not say whether it is included in the total. The company described a platform of AI agents that carries out red-team attacks continuously.

events.headline: CrowdStrike chief executive George Kurtz joins Armadin's board
events.summary: Armadin announced that George Kurtz, founder and chief executive of CrowdStrike, had joined its board as an independent director with immediate effect. The copy of the release read is dated 28 April 2026; other republished copies give dates a day either side. Two days later Armadin announced a distribution partnership with CrowdStrike.

events.headline: Armadin and CrowdStrike announce partnership; Armadin Red offered through CrowdStrike
events.summary: Armadin announced that its Armadin Red assessment would be offered through CrowdStrike's Project QuiltWorks coalition, CrowdStrike's field organisation and its systems-integrator partners. Armadin supplies continuous offensive testing of infrastructure, identity and endpoints; CrowdStrike and its partners prioritise the results and carry out remediation. The release says the attacker integrates with the Falcon platform without giving detail.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 adds an external assessment built on Armadin
events.summary: Armadin and Palo Alto Networks announced that Unit 42's Frontier AI Defense service would include an External AI Hyperattack Assessment run by Armadin's agents: passive discovery of internet-facing assets, cloud resources and exposed secrets, then parallel reconnaissance and exploitation, with each attack chain logged as evidence that Unit 42 uses to give remediation guidance.

events.headline: Armadin raises US$255.5 million Series B at a valuation above US$2.5 billion
events.summary: Armadin announced a US$255.5 million Series B co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, with new investors Bain Capital Ventures and Redpoint and existing investors 8VC, Ballistic Ventures, GV, In-Q-Tel, Kleiner Perkins and Menlo Ventures. The company put its valuation above US$2.5 billion and total funding at about US$445 million, and said it was running attack campaigns in production for Fortune 500 and government customers.

events.headline: ServiceNow agrees to acquire Armis for US$7.75 billion
events.summary: Reuters and TechCrunch reported that ServiceNow agreed to buy Armis for US$7.75 billion in cash, ServiceNow's largest deal, with closing expected in the second half of 2026. Armis had been valued at US$6.1 billion in a US$435 million funding round in November 2025 and had been preparing for a public offering. ServiceNow put Armis's annual recurring revenue above US$340 million.

events.headline: ServiceNow completes acquisition of Armis
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2026-04-20 that it had completed its purchase of Armis for about US$7.75 billion in cash, funded from cash and debt. Its release says Armis Centrix remains available as a standalone solution and is also integrated with the ServiceNow AI Platform, and that Armis employees are joining ServiceNow.

events.headline: Atlassian agrees to acquire engineering-intelligence company DX
events.summary: Atlassian announced on 2025-09-18 a definitive agreement to acquire DX, which measures developer productivity and AI adoption for more than 350 enterprises. The Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 records that the acquisition closed in the quarter ended 2025-12-31 for total consideration of US$720.4 million.

events.headline: Atlassian acquires The Browser Company of New York
events.summary: Atlassian's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 records the acquisition on 2025-10-20 of The Browser Company of New York, maker of the Dia and Arc browsers, for a total purchase price of US$488.3 million.

events.headline: Atlassian cuts about 10% of its workforce
events.summary: Reported by The Register on 2026-03-11: Atlassian said it would cut about 1,600 jobs, 10% of staff, with its chief executive citing the effect of AI on the roles needed and a wish to fund AI and enterprise sales. Atlassian's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 states that a restructuring plan begun in its third fiscal quarter eliminated roles affecting approximately 10% of the workforce, with severance and termination benefits of US$203.9 million.

events.headline: AWS US-EAST-1 disruption traced to a DynamoDB DNS automation fault
events.summary: AWS stated in its post-event summary that a service disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region ran from 11:48 PM PDT on 19 October 2025 to 2:20 PM PDT on 20 October 2025. AWS attributed it to a latent race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management that left the regional endpoint with an empty DNS record, with knock-on effects on EC2 instance launches, Network Load Balancer, Lambda, ECS, EKS, Fargate, Amazon Connect, STS, console sign-in and Redshift. Amazon Bedrock is not named among the affected services. AWS said it disabled the DNS automation worldwide pending a fix and would add safeguards.

events.headline: Amazon announces about 14,000 corporate role cuts
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2025-10-28: Amazon said it would cut about 14,000 corporate roles to reduce layers of management and shift spending towards AI. Amazon disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K estimated severance costs of about US$2.7 billion for planned role eliminations in 2025, affecting all segments. Neither source gives a figure for AWS alone.

events.headline: Amazon announces a further 16,000 role cuts
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch and Retail Dive on 2026-01-28: Amazon said it would eliminate about 16,000 more roles across the company, following the October 2025 reduction, according to a memo from senior vice president Beth Galetti. TechCrunch reported that a meeting invitation referring to the cuts was sent in error to AWS employees. The share of the cuts falling on AWS was not stated.

events.headline: OpenAI models, Codex and Managed Agents come to Amazon Bedrock in limited preview
events.summary: Amazon announced on 28 April 2026 that OpenAI models, Codex and Amazon Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI were available on Amazon Bedrock in limited preview. The same page, updated on 8 September 2026, says the GPT-5.6 family became generally available on Bedrock on 9 July 2026 and GPT-6 Astra on 8 September 2026.

events.headline: AWS launches the Amazon Nova foundation models on Amazon Bedrock
events.summary: AWS announced on 2024-12-03 that Amazon Nova Micro, Lite and Pro, with the Nova Canvas image model and Nova Reel video model, were available in Amazon Bedrock, initially in US East (N. Virginia) with cross-Region inference from two other US Regions for the text models.

events.headline: AWS announces Amazon Nova 2 models, Nova Forge and the Nova Act service
events.summary: AWS announced on 2025-12-02 that Amazon Nova 2 Lite was available in Amazon Bedrock and Nova 2 Pro was in preview with early access for Nova Forge customers, both through global cross-Region inference. Amazon also announced Nova 2 Sonic, Nova 2 Omni, the Nova Forge service for building custom models from Nova checkpoints, and Nova Act for browser agents.

events.headline: AWS launches Amazon Quick Suite, with QuickSight folded in
events.summary: CIO Dive reported on 2025-10-09 that AWS made Quick Suite generally available as an agentic workspace for research, business intelligence and automation, with Amazon QuickSight becoming a component and existing QuickSight customers being upgraded. AWS's documentation now calls the product AWS Quick; its compliance pages list it as Amazon Quick, formerly Amazon Quick Suite.

events.headline: Kiro reaches general availability with a CLI and team plans
events.summary: The Kiro team announced general availability on 2025-11-17, after a preview that began in July 2025. The release added property-based testing against specs, checkpoints, multi-root workspaces, the Kiro CLI and team plans managed through AWS IAM Identity Center.

events.headline: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore becomes generally available in nine Regions
events.summary: AWS announced on 2025-10-13 that Amazon Bedrock AgentCore was generally available in nine AWS Regions, adding VPC, AWS PrivateLink, CloudFormation and tagging support across its services and Agent-to-Agent protocol support in AgentCore Runtime. Constellation Research reported the same day that AWS cited more than one million downloads of the AgentCore SDK.

events.headline: Amazon S3 Vectors becomes generally available with 2 billion vectors per index
events.summary: AWS announced on 2025-12-02 that Amazon S3 Vectors was generally available in 14 Regions, up from five in preview, with up to 2 billion vectors per index and 10,000 indexes per vector bucket. InfoQ reported on 2026-01-02 that the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Amazon OpenSearch integrations also became generally available and that more than 40 billion vectors had been ingested during the preview.

events.headline: Amazon disputes a report that a Kiro agent caused a December 2025 Cost Explorer interruption
events.summary: Reported by The Register on 2026-02-20 and TechTarget on 2026-02-23, both citing the Financial Times: a Kiro agent used by AWS engineers was said to have deleted and recreated an environment, interrupting a service for about 13 hours in December 2025. Amazon stated on 2026-02-20 that the event was a brief interruption to AWS Cost Explorer in one Region, caused by user error in the form of misconfigured access controls and not by AI, that it received no customer inquiries about it, and that it had since added safeguards including mandatory peer review for production access. The press accounts rest on one original report with unnamed sources; Amazon's statement does not say whether Kiro was in use.

events.headline: AWS discloses CVE-2026-12530 in the Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK
events.summary: AWS disclosed in security bulletin 2026-044-AWS on 2026-06-17 that the install_packages() method of the Code Interpreter client in the bedrock-agentcore Python SDK, versions 1.1.3 up to but not including 1.6.1, sanitised package names with an incomplete blocklist, so crafted arguments could redirect package resolution to a third-party server or expose sandbox files. AWS said version 1.6.1 fixes it. The bulletin does not state whether exploitation is known.

events.headline: AWS discloses CVE-2026-16796 in the Bedrock AgentCore Python SDK
events.summary: AWS disclosed in security bulletin 2026-065-AWS on 2026-07-23 that a second flaw in the install_packages() method of the bedrock-agentcore Python SDK, in versions before 1.18.1, could let a remote authenticated user run arbitrary commands in the Code Interpreter sandbox through crafted package-name arguments. AWS credited an individual researcher and BeyondTrust Phantom Labs and said version 1.18.1 fixes it. The bulletin does not state whether exploitation is known.

events.headline: AWS connectivity incident in US-EAST-1 disrupts IAM Identity Center sign-in and new sign-ups
events.summary: Reported by Dr. Web on 2026-11-15 and by Pasquale Pillitteri on 2026-11-16: AWS posted a notice of connectivity issues in its US-EAST-1 (Northern Virginia) region on 2026-11-15, with IAM Identity Center sign-in, new account sign-ups and Kiro among the services named. UptimeRobot's copy of the AWS status updates also lists Amazon OpenSearch Service and puts the incident at a little over two hours, with a subset of Network Load Balancers in one availability zone recovering last; the reports differ on exact start and end times. The reports say AWS gave no cause.

events.headline: AWS Quick adds enterprise guardrails in preview
events.summary: AWS announced on 2026-11-20 a preview of enterprise guardrails for AWS Quick, letting administrators apply content filters, denied topics, blocked words, prompt-attack detection and controls for selected personal data types to user prompts, by user, identity-provider group or account default, with a detect-only mode. AWS said the preview is open to select customers on the Professional and Enterprise plans.

events.headline: Axonius acquires medical device security firm Cynerio
events.summary: Axonius announced it had acquired Cynerio, which secures medical devices in healthcare settings, for more than US$100M in cash and stock, planning to combine it with its asset platform. CTech later reported the price as US$180M with further milestone payments.

events.headline: Axonius reported to cut about 100 staff, roughly 11% of its workforce
events.summary: Reported by CTech on 2025-11-06 and by GovInfoSecurity on 2025-11-13: Axonius laid off about 100 of roughly 900 employees. A company spokesperson was quoted describing it as a strategic decision to sharpen focus for future growth.

events.headline: Axonius co-founder Dean Sysman steps down as chief executive; Joe Diamond named interim CEO
events.summary: CTech reported on 2026-02-15 that co-founder Dean Sysman moved from chief executive to executive chairman, citing a family medical matter, and that Joe Diamond became interim chief executive. CTech reported in November 2026 that Diamond was confirmed as chief executive in May 2026.

events.headline: Axonius launches AI Workforce of virtual workers
events.summary: Axonius announced general availability of AI Workforce, more than 50 types of virtual workers that monitor environments, flag exposures and carry out remediation with configurable human approval and logged actions, alongside its AI Companion and MCP Server.

events.headline: BeyondTrust discloses compromise of Remote Support SaaS instances; US Treasury affected
events.summary: Disclosed by BeyondTrust on 2024-12-08 and updated to 2025-01-28: a compromised infrastructure API key was used to reset local application passwords and reach Remote Support SaaS instances of 17 customers. The company said the attacker first exploited a zero-day in a third-party application to reach an asset in a BeyondTrust AWS account, that no other products and no FedRAMP instances were affected, and that its forensic investigation ended on 2025-01-17. Reported by TechTarget and The Register on 2024-12-31: the US Treasury told lawmakers that the stolen key let an attacker, which it attributed to a China state-sponsored group, reach some workstations and unclassified documents.

events.headline: BeyondTrust reported among companies affected by Salesloft Drift data theft
events.summary: Reported by TechTarget on 2025-09-12 and by BleepingComputer on 2025-09-14: BeyondTrust was among the companies affected by the campaign that used stolen Salesloft Drift tokens to take data from customers' Salesforce environments. UpGuard's tracker says BeyondTrust was alerted by Salesforce on 22 August 2025 and confirmed it was affected; none of the three sources says what data was taken.

events.headline: Critical flaw in BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access exploited in the wild
events.summary: Disclosed by BeyondTrust on 2026-02-06 as advisory BT26-02 (CVE-2026-1731, CVSS 9.9): remote code execution in Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access. Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-02-20: SaaS instances were patched on 2 February, exploitation was detected from 31 January, CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 13 February with a three-day deadline for federal agencies, and later marked it as used in ransomware campaigns. Self-hosted customers had to apply the patch themselves.

events.headline: BeyondTrust announces availability of AI Agent Security
events.summary: BeyondTrust's press listing carries a release dated 21 October 2026 announcing that AI Agent Security is available. The product page describes discovery and inventory of AI agents, just-in-time scoped access, protection of the credentials agents use, and runtime policy enforcement, as part of the Pathfinder platform.

events.headline: Critical BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw (CVE-2026-102764) exploited as a zero-day since late August
events.summary: Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-10-16 and by CSO Online on 2026-10-16: BeyondTrust warned customers that a critical authentication bypass in Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier (CVE-2026-102764, advisory BT26-05, CVSS 4.0 score 9.3 per CSO Online) had been exploited in the wild before a fix existed, with exploitation dated to 29 August 2026 in BeyondTrust's timeline. Both outlets say a patch was released on 8 October, that hosted (SaaS) instances were patched by BeyondTrust and self-hosted appliances must be patched by the customer, and that Mandiant attributes the activity to a suspected China-linked espionage group it tracks as Armory Castle. CSO Online reports two confirmed intrusions, one BeyondTrust-hosted instance and one self-hosted customer appliance, found on 28 September; neither company has said whether other customers were compromised. Privileged Remote Access shares the affected code and was patched as a precaution, although BeyondTrust said it found no way to exploit it there.

events.headline: BigID launches DSPM as a Snowflake Native App
events.summary: BigID announced a DSPM application on the Snowflake Marketplace that discovers and classifies sensitive data inside a customer's Snowflake environment without moving it.

events.headline: BigID lays off about a fifth of its workforce

quote.text: AI is the biggest technological change of our careers

events.summary: Reported by Globes and CTech on 2026-05-26: BigID laid off about 20% of its staff. Globes put the number at about 150 of roughly 650 employees, CTech gave a workforce of around 600, and both said staff at the Tel Aviv development centre were affected. Both quote the company linking the cuts to a move to an AI-first approach in software development and operations.

events.headline: DataHub releases connector bringing BigID classifications into its catalog
events.summary: DataHub announced in a Business Wire release on 2026-11-12 a partnership with BigID and a connector that copies BigID's data classification and sensitivity findings onto the matching tables and columns in the DataHub catalog. DataHub said the connector is available in its open-source and cloud editions, reads from BigID on a schedule, and that the two companies are exploring two-way synchronisation.

events.headline: Visa agrees to acquire BioCatch for US$2.4 billion in cash
events.summary: Visa announced a definitive agreement to acquire BioCatch from funds advised by Permira and other shareholders for US$2.4 billion in cash. Closing is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and is expected by the end of Visa's fiscal second quarter of 2027. As of 2026-11-20 no completion announcement was found, so BioCatch is recorded as still independent.

events.headline: BioCatch announces New Zealand banks will launch an intelligence-sharing network
events.summary: BioCatch's news index lists a release dated 2026-11-18 stating that New Zealand banks are to launch an intelligence-sharing network to combat fraud and scams. A release the same day reported results from BioCatch Trust Australia, which launched in November 2024 with five banks.

events.headline: BioCatch launches AiRE to detect AI agents in digital banking sessions
events.summary: BioCatch announced on 2026-11-10 the launch of BioCatch AiRE (Agentic AI Risk Essentials), which it says detects AI agents interacting with digital banking platforms in real time and gives institutions indicators of potentially risky agent activity. BioCatch said the capability is offered through existing customer integrations.

events.headline: Moody's invests US$250M in Bitsight at a reported US$2.4B valuation
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported that Moody's invested US$250 million in Bitsight, valuing the company at US$2.4 billion. TechCrunch later described Moody's as the largest shareholder following this investment.

events.headline: Bitsight agrees to acquire threat intelligence firm Cybersixgill for US$115M
events.summary: TechCrunch and SecurityWeek reported that Bitsight agreed to buy Cybersixgill, an Israeli dark-web threat intelligence provider, for US$115 million. Sixgill entities now appear on Bitsight's subprocessor list.

events.headline: Bitsight appoints John Clancy as chief executive
events.summary: Bitsight announced that John Clancy became chief executive with immediate effect, succeeding Steve Harvey, who stepped down after six years and remains an advisor to the board.

events.headline: Bitsight makes Beacon vendor monitoring generally available and adds MCP access
events.summary: Bitsight announced general availability of Bitsight Beacon, which monitors critical vendors for exposure, malicious activity and compromise, together with Model Context Protocol and agent access to its risk dataset.

events.headline: Clearlake and Francisco Partners complete purchase of Synopsys software security unit, renamed Black Duck
events.summary: Clearlake Capital Group and Francisco Partners completed the purchase of the Synopsys Software Integrity Group for up to US$2.1 billion, including up to US$475 million contingent on the buyers' returns. The business became an independent company named Black Duck Software, Inc. Synopsys's annual report for fiscal 2024 records the divestiture.

events.headline: Black Duck names new CIO and promotes CISO
events.summary: Black Duck appointed Ishpreet Singh as chief information officer and promoted Bruce Jenkins to chief information security officer, following the hire of a chief revenue officer in November 2024. ITPro reported the appointments on 2024-12-24.

events.headline: Black Duck launches Signal agentic AI application security product
events.summary: Black Duck's newsroom lists the launch of Black Duck Signal, described as agentic AI application security, on 2025-12-10, with a further release on securing AI-generated code on 2026-03-23.

events.headline: Black Duck appoints Dom Glavach as CISO
events.summary: Black Duck announced Dom Glavach as chief information security officer on 2026-04-09. The leadership page retrieved on 2026-11-20 also lists Greg Hughes as chief executive in place of Jason Schmitt; no announcement of that change was found.

events.headline: Black Duck joins Anthropic's Project Glasswing
events.summary: Black Duck announced on 2026-09-08 that it had been selected to join Anthropic's Project Glasswing, a week after making its Signal product available on the Claude Directory.

events.headline: Polaris listed on FedRAMP Marketplace as in process; not yet authorised
events.summary: Black Duck announced that the Polaris Platform is listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace in the initial implementation phase and that it is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Class C certification with an assessment against the Rev5 Moderate baseline. The product is not yet authorised.

events.headline: NormShield renames itself Black Kite and moves headquarters to Boston
events.summary: The cyber risk ratings company NormShield announced its new name, Black Kite, and the move of its headquarters from Vienna, Virginia to Boston. It said the platform was unchanged and was used by 160 customers, and that it had raised US$7.5M in Series A funding in 2020.

events.headline: Bitsight's patent suit against Black Kite ends in the District of Massachusetts
events.summary: According to the federal docket indexed by CourtListener, BitSight Technologies, Inc. v. NormShield Inc. (D. Mass., 1:23-cv-12055), a patent infringement suit filed on 2023-09-05, was terminated on 2025-02-13. Black Kite stated on 2024-09-23 that the court had dismissed the patent claims on 2024-09-20 after ruling the asserted claims of five patents invalid, with non-patent claims then still pending. The terms on which the case ended were not read from a court document.

events.headline: Black Kite releases Black Kite AI Agent
events.summary: Black Kite released an AI agent embedded across its platform that investigates vendor findings, produces reports and benchmarks prospective vendors. SecurityBrief reported the launch and repeated the vendor's figure of more than 3,000 customers.

events.headline: Black Kite releases an MCP server for its platform
events.summary: Black Kite released a Model Context Protocol server that lets customers and service providers connect their own AI agents and tools to its third-party cyber risk platform and data.

events.headline: Black Kite's offering is listed as FedRAMP Ready at Moderate
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists the Third-Party Risk Intelligence System of NormShield, Inc. DBA Black Kite as FedRAMP Ready at the Moderate level from 2026-03-25, assessed by Linford & Company. Ready is a pre-authorisation status; no agency authorisation is listed. The vendor announced the status in a release.

events.headline: Black Kite announces GovRAMP status for its third-party risk intelligence product
events.summary: Black Kite announced a GovRAMP status for its Third-Party Cyber Risk Intelligence product. The release's title says Ready while its body says Authorization; the GovRAMP participants list read on 2026-11-22 shows the product as Ready at Moderate.

events.headline: Black Kite announces integration with CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM
events.summary: Black Kite announced an integration that delivers its third-party vendor risk intelligence into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM for use in security operations workflows.

events.headline: Bolster appoints Rod Schultz as chief executive, succeeding co-founder Abhishek Dubey
events.summary: In a release dated 4 November 2024, Bolster announced Rod Schultz as chief executive and described co-founder Abhishek Dubey as the former chief executive. The release said Schultz had most recently been a senior vice-president at Dust Identity. The event is a little older than the usual 24-month window and is recorded because the company's leadership changed.

events.headline: Bolster AI launches Signals, an intelligence and benchmarking layer on its platform
events.summary: In a release dated 29 October 2025, Bolster AI announced Signals, which lets customers query their threat data in plain language and compare their exposure with anonymised industry benchmarks. The release said it was available to all platform customers.

events.headline: Bolster AI says its technology powers Akamai's Brand Guardian
events.summary: In a release dated 25 March 2026, Bolster AI said it had partnered with a global cybersecurity and cloud company to power a new product called Brand Guardian; the release did not name the partner, and Bolster AI's blog post of the same day named Akamai. Akamai's own release announcing Brand Guardian that day does not mention Bolster AI. The partnership is therefore recorded on Bolster AI's account only.

events.headline: Bolster AI adds marketplace monitoring and takedowns to its platform
events.summary: In a release dated 4 May 2026, Bolster AI announced monitoring of online marketplaces for counterfeit listings, unauthorised sellers and fraudulent digital goods, with takedown requests and tracking of re-listings. The release said it was available at once as part of the platform.

events.headline: Bolster AI adds fraudulent advert monitoring and takedowns to its platform
events.summary: In a release dated 21 July 2026, Bolster AI announced detection of paid search and social adverts that impersonate a customer's brand, with takedown requests and monitoring for reappearance. The release said it was available at once as part of the platform; a knowledge-base article describes how the findings appear in the Web and Social Media modules.

events.headline: Bolster AI introduces Threat Graph for linking related findings into campaigns
events.summary: In a blog post dated 20 October 2026, Bolster AI introduced Threat Graph, a view inside Signals that connects related URLs, domains, hosting providers, phone numbers, emails and social accounts so a campaign can be investigated together. A knowledge-base article updated the same day documents it.

events.headline: Braintrust raises US$80M Series B led by Iconiq
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-02-17 that Braintrust raised a US$80 million Series B led by Iconiq, with Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock, basecase capital and Elad Gil participating, at a valuation of US$800 million. The company said the money would go to engineering and go-to-market hiring, new observability tools and expansion into new regions.

events.headline: Braintrust reports unauthorised access to an AWS account holding customer AI-provider keys
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2026-05-06 and SecurityWeek on 2026-05-08: Braintrust told customers it had found unauthorised access to one of its Amazon Web Services accounts, which held the AI-provider API keys that customers store with Braintrust at organisation level. SecurityWeek reported that the incident was discovered on 2026-05-04 after a report of suspicious behaviour, that customers were emailed on 2026-05-05, that at least one customer was affected and three others reported unusual spikes in AI-provider usage. Braintrust said it had locked down the account, rotated internal secrets and recommended that all customers rotate stored provider keys; TechCrunch reported the company's statement that it had confirmed a security incident but had no evidence of a breach at that time. The cause had not been published in either report.

events.headline: Braintrust releases a Terraform provider for managing its configuration as code
events.summary: Braintrust announced on its blog on 2026-11-10 a Terraform provider that manages access control, project setup and shared configuration such as AI secrets and automations as code, plus a command-line tool that exports an existing organisation's resources. Braintrust said the provider is published on the Terraform and OpenTofu registries.

events.headline: Cato Networks raises US$359M Series G at US$4.8B valuation
events.summary: Globes reported that Cato Networks raised US$359M in a Series G round led by Vitruvian Partners and ION Crossover Partners, with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Acrew Capital and Adams Street Partners, at a valuation of US$4.8B, taking total funding above US$1B.

events.headline: Cato Networks acquires Aim Security and extends Series G to US$409M
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported that Cato Networks announced its first acquisition, AI security company Aim Security, for an undisclosed price, to add AI security to its SASE platform from early 2026. Cato also said it had passed US$300M in annual recurring revenue and added US$50M from Acrew Capital to its Series G.

events.headline: Cato Networks announces AgentSense runtime guardrail for AI agents
events.summary: Cato Networks announced on 2026-11-17, in a release distributed by PR Newswire, a capability called AgentSense that assesses AI agents while they run and aims to block unsafe actions, including those steered by untrusted content. Cato said it is integrated in the Cato platform and included at no extra charge in Cato AI Usage licences; a drift detection function was described as still to come.

events.headline: Censys raises $40 million Series D and $30 million of debt
events.summary: Censys announced $70 million of funding: a $40 million Series D led by Morgan Stanley Expansion Capital, with Decibel Partners, Greylock Partners, GV and Intel Capital, and $30 million of debt financing. SecurityWeek put total venture funding at more than $149 million. The company said the money would go to AI-driven security operations products and international expansion.

events.headline: Censys appoints Jeff Hackett as chief financial officer
events.summary: Censys's newsroom lists a release dated 6 October 2026 announcing Jeff Hackett as chief financial officer; he appears in that role on the leadership page.

events.headline: Cerebras Systems lists on Nasdaq, raising US$5.5 billion
events.summary: Cerebras priced its initial public offering of 30 million Class A shares at US$185 on 2026-05-13 and began trading on Nasdaq as CBRS on 2026-05-14, according to TechCrunch and the prospectus. The Form 10-Q for the third quarter states the offering completed on 2026-05-15 with 34.5 million shares sold including the over-allotment and net proceeds of about US$6.2 billion.

events.headline: OpenAI commits to 750 MW of Cerebras inference capacity
events.summary: Cerebras's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 describes a December 2025 agreement under which OpenAI is committed to 750 MW of inference capacity, with an option for up to 2 GW in total. The filing gives the month but not the day; the first of the month is recorded. The prospectus describes the multi-year deal as worth more than US$20 billion.

events.headline: Cerebras announces six new inference data centres in North America and Europe
events.summary: Cerebras announced on 2025-03-11 an expansion of its inference capacity to sites in Minneapolis, Oklahoma City, Montreal, a further US location and Europe, adding to existing sites in Santa Clara, Stockton and Dallas. It said the Oklahoma City and Montreal hardware would be owned and operated by Cerebras and the other sites operated jointly with G42.

events.headline: Cerebras puts disaggregated inference into production, pairing GPUs with its CS-3 systems
events.summary: Cerebras announced on its blog on 2026-11-17 that it is running disaggregated inference in production, with AMD Instinct GPUs handling prompt processing and its CS-3 systems generating responses. Cerebras said it measured five times the throughput per megawatt of a CS-3-only setup, is using the approach on its Inference Cloud, and has given early access to partners including Amazon Web Services and Fireworks AI.

events.headline: Nadav Zafrir becomes Check Point chief executive; founder Gil Shwed moves to executive chairman
events.summary: The 2025 Form 20-F states that Nadav Zafrir became chief executive officer in December 2024 and that founder Gil Shwed moved to the role of executive chairman. The filing gives the month only; the first day of the month is recorded here.

events.headline: Check Point settles Israeli tax dispute for 2016-2020
events.summary: Disclosed in Check Point's 2025 Form 20-F: on 15 July 2025 the company and the Israeli Tax Authority settled tax assessments for 2016 to 2020 for NIS 223.2 million (about $66 million), ratified by the Tel Aviv District Court on 16 July 2025 and paid on 31 July 2025. The authority had originally demanded NIS 536 million for 2016-2019 and NIS 94 million for 2020.

events.headline: Check Point agrees to acquire AI security company Lakera
events.summary: Check Point announced on 16 September 2025 an agreement to acquire Lakera, a company founded in 2021 with research centres in Zurich and San Francisco whose products were Lakera Guard (runtime protection for AI applications and agents) and Lakera Red (pre-deployment testing), and which ran the Gandalf prompt-injection game. Check Point said the products would become Check Point AI Agent Security and Check Point AI Red Teaming. The price was not disclosed; Globes estimated $300 million.
