BankInfoSecurity reported that Lakera had raised $30 million and had about 60 employees. Lakera is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Check Point completes acquisition of Lakera
events.summary: The 2025 Form 20-F states that Check Point acquired 100% of the share capital of Lakera AI AG, a Swiss company, in October 2025; the day is not given, so the first day of the month is recorded here. Check Point's fourth-quarter results release put the net cash consideration at about $190 million. Lakera's runtime product is now sold as Check Point AI Agent Security, with its runtime layer named AI Guardrails.

events.headline: Check Point acquires AI agent discovery company Cyata
events.summary: The 2025 Form 20-F states that Check Point acquired 100% of the share capital of Cyata Security Ltd., an Israeli company specialising in discovering and governing autonomous AI agents, in February 2026; the day is not given, so the first day of the month is recorded here. The fourth-quarter 2025 results release said Cyata adds AI agent discovery across endpoints and SaaS. Consideration was not disclosed in the sections read.

events.headline: Check Point launches AI Defense Plane
events.summary: Check Point announced the AI Defense Plane on 23 March 2026 as a control plane for AI security drawing on technology from the Lakera and Cyata acquisitions. It listed Workforce AI Security and AI Application and Agent Security as available immediately and AI Red Teaming as in limited release.

events.headline: Check Point AI Agent Security adds agent discovery and risk assessment in early access
events.summary: A documentation changelog entry dated 1 June 2026 announced early access to Check Point AI Agent Security, which extends the AI Guardrails runtime layer with agent discovery and per-agent risk assessment mapped to OWASP and MITRE ATLAS, and added an Agent Behavior Defense category with an off-task action detector and a tool allow/deny list.

events.headline: Check Point says its WAF has been added to its FedRAMP-certified government platform
events.summary: Check Point announced on 2026-11-12 that its web application and API security product, Check Point WAF, has achieved FedRAMP certification and is included in its FedRAMP Marketplace listing. The release does not state the impact level or a sponsoring agency, and it does not concern Check Point's email security or AI agent security products.

events.headline: Check Point expands Microsoft collaboration to run its SASE platform on Azure
events.summary: Check Point announced on 2026-11-18 an expanded collaboration with Microsoft to deploy Check Point SASE on Microsoft Azure, citing 48 additional Azure points of presence and integration with Microsoft Entra. Check Point said it expects the service to be available through Microsoft Marketplace in the first half of 2027.

events.headline: Hellman & Friedman to acquire Checkmarx from Insight Partners
events.summary: Checkmarx announced on 2020-03-16 that Hellman & Friedman would acquire it from Insight Partners at a US$1.15 billion valuation, with Insight retaining a substantial minority interest. Wikipedia records completion in April 2020 with TPG as co-investor. Dated to the announcement.

events.headline: Checkmarx acquires AI security-agent startup Tromzo
events.summary: Checkmarx announced on 2025-12-09 that it had acquired Tromzo, whose agents triage findings and recommend fixes, to power its Assist agents from early 2026. Terms were not disclosed. ISMG reported that Tromzo was founded in 2021 and had about 10 employees.

events.headline: Checkmarx GitHub Actions and extensions compromised in supply-chain attack
events.summary: Checkmarx disclosed that attackers gained access to its GitHub repositories on 2026-03-19 through the Trivy supply-chain attack and published malicious versions of two GitHub Actions and two Open VSX extensions on 2026-03-23, a KICS Docker image, a GitHub Action and VS Code extensions on 2026-04-22, and a Jenkins plugin on 2026-05-09. It said data taken from its GitHub repositories on 2026-03-30 was published on the dark web on 2026-04-25. Its update of 2026-07-06 stated that Mandiant's investigation was complete, that the incident was contained, and that the AWS production environment and the Checkmarx One SaaS environment were not accessed. The Hacker News reported the first wave on 2026-03-24 and attributed it to the TeamPCP group.

events.headline: Checkmarx One for Government announced as FedRAMP Moderate
events.summary: Checkmarx announced on 2026-07-13 that Checkmarx One for Government had achieved FedRAMP Moderate status and was listed in the FedRAMP Marketplace. The listing was not checked in this session.

events.headline: Checkmarx appoints Kobi Sivilya as chief information security officer
events.summary: Checkmarx announced on 2026-11-05 the appointment of Kobi Sivilya to oversee security, IT and business applications. The release quotes chief executive Sandeep Johri.

events.headline: Cisco completes acquisition of AI security startup Robust Intelligence
events.summary: Cisco announced on 2024-08-26 that it intended to acquire Robust Intelligence, a privately held company whose platform tests and protects AI models from development to production, and added an update dated 2024-09-24 stating that the acquisition had been completed. Terms were not disclosed. Cisco said the technology would be integrated into Cisco Security Cloud. Robust Intelligence is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Cisco announces AI Defense for discovering, validating and protecting enterprise AI
events.summary: Cisco announced AI Defense on 2025-01-15, covering discovery of AI assets, automated model validation (algorithmic red teaming), run-time guardrails, and visibility and access control for employee use of third-party AI tools. The release said the product would be available in March 2025 and is built into Cisco Security Cloud.

events.headline: Cisco discloses voice-phishing incident exposing Cisco.com user profile data in a third-party CRM
events.summary: Disclosed by Cisco on 2025-08-01 (updated 2025-10-03): Cisco stated that on 2025-07-24 it became aware that an attacker had used voice phishing against a Cisco representative to access and export a subset of basic profile information from one instance of a third-party cloud CRM system. Cisco stated the data was mainly account profile information of Cisco.com registrants (name, organisation, address, user ID, email, phone, account metadata), that no passwords or customers' confidential information were obtained, and that it identified no impact to its products or services. The incident is not specific to AI Defense.

events.headline: Cisco adds AI BOM, MCP Catalog and agentic guardrails to AI Defense
events.summary: At Cisco Live EMEA on 2026-02-10 Cisco announced additions to AI Defense: an AI bill of materials, an MCP Catalog for discovering and managing risk in MCP servers, adaptive multi-turn algorithmic red teaming, real-time guardrails for agent interactions, and an integration with NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails. The release gave no availability dates and noted some features were still in development.

events.headline: Cisco launches self-serve AI Defense: Explorer Edition and an Agent Runtime SDK
events.summary: At RSA Conference on 2026-03-23 Cisco announced AI Defense: Explorer Edition, a self-serve red-teaming tool that Cisco says uses the same validation engine as AI Defense, along with an Agent Runtime SDK and an LLM security leaderboard. Role-based access control requires the enterprise edition, according to the release.

events.headline: Cisco says it will add Anthropic's Claude Mythos to AI Defense adaptive red teaming
events.summary: In a release dated 2026-11-09 Cisco said it is adding Anthropic's Claude Mythos model to the adaptive red-teaming framework in AI Defense, restricted to registered targets and authenticated operators, and described it as coming soon for select enterprises. The same release said AI Defense has been used by hundreds of customers since its January 2025 launch; no customers were named.

events.headline: Cisco completes its acquisition of Splunk for about $28 billion
events.summary: Cisco announced on 2024-03-18 that it had completed the purchase of Splunk for $157 per share in cash, about $28 billion in equity value. Splunk's shares stopped trading on Nasdaq that day. Splunk Enterprise Security has been a Cisco product since.

events.headline: Cisco introduces Essentials and Premier editions of Splunk Enterprise Security
events.summary: At Splunk's .conf25 event Cisco announced two editions of Splunk Enterprise Security. Essentials was stated to be available in all regions and Premier, which adds SOAR and user and entity behaviour analytics, was in early access. A Triage Agent and other AI features were announced for 2026.

events.headline: Splunk Enterprise Security Premier becomes generally available
events.summary: Splunk stated on 2026-02-10 that the Premier edition was generally available on Splunk Cloud, with availability for customer-managed environments from 18 February. The same post described the AI Triage Agent as being at alpha stage in the first half of 2026.

events.headline: Cisco completes its acquisition of Duo Security for US$2.35 billion
events.summary: Cisco announced on 2018-10-01 that it had completed the acquisition of Duo Security, a privately held provider of multi-factor authentication and access security based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, for US$2.35 billion in cash and assumed equity awards. Duo's team joined Cisco's networking and security business. Recorded because it changed ownership of the product; Duo Security is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Cisco announces Duo Agentic Identity for registering and governing AI agents
events.summary: Cisco's Duo business announced Duo Agentic Identity, under which AI agents are registered in Duo Directory as non-human identities mapped to a human owner, discovered through Cisco Identity Intelligence, and governed through an MCP gateway that checks each tool call against Duo's authorisation policy. The announcement does not state whether the features were generally available.

events.headline: Cisco completes acquisition of non-human identity specialist Astrix Security
events.summary: Cisco announced on 2026-05-04 that it intended to acquire Astrix Security, an Israeli company whose platform inventories AI agents, MCP servers and non-human identities and manages their access and lifecycle, and added an update dated 2026-06-29 stating that the acquisition had been completed. Cisco did not disclose the price; Calcalist reported about US$400 million and SiliconANGLE cited an earlier estimate of about US$300 million. Cisco said Astrix's capabilities would be integrated into Cisco Identity Intelligence and extended to Duo and Secure Access, and that existing Astrix customers should keep using their current support process. The Astrix website now redirects to Cisco Identity Intelligence. Astrix Security is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Cisco Secure Access Dubai data centre incident forces customers to move to India regions
events.summary: Disclosed by Cisco on its Secure Access status page and in a support note: an incident at its Dubai data centre began on 2026-03-02. Resource connectors in the region showed as disconnected and remote access VPN clients could fail to connect. Cisco redirected roaming traffic to Mumbai and told customers to deploy new connectors and move VPN profiles and network tunnels to its India regions; web gateway and zero-trust clients moved to the next closest data centre automatically. Cisco gave no cause in the pages read, and its status page still showed the Middle East (UAE) region as degraded on 2026-11-21.

events.headline: Cisco says Secure Access for Government has reached FedRAMP Class D (High)
events.summary: Cisco stated in a post dated 2026-08-11 that Secure Access for Government, which received FedRAMP Class C (Moderate) in August 2025, had achieved FedRAMP Certified Class D (High), applied to existing subscriptions without customer action. The date is that of the post; the certification date was not given, and a FedRAMP Marketplace entry for the offering was not located on 2026-11-21.

events.headline: Cloudflare discloses Salesforce support-case data taken via Salesloft Drift
events.summary: Cloudflare disclosed on 2025-09-02 that an attacker using the compromised Salesloft Drift integration accessed its Salesforce tenant from 12 to 17 August 2025 and took support case text and customer contact details. Cloudflare stated that it rotated 104 API tokens found in that data, saw no suspicious activity, and that its services and infrastructure were not compromised.

events.headline: Cloudflare network outage disrupts services including Access for several hours
events.summary: Cloudflare reported that on 2025-11-18 a database permissions change produced an oversized bot-management configuration file that made its core proxy fail from 11:20 UTC, with the main impact resolved at 14:30 and all systems normal at 17:06 UTC. Access had widespread authentication failures until 13:05 UTC. Cloudflare stated it was not an attack; its annual report cites the event as widespread service unavailability.

events.headline: Second Cloudflare outage in three weeks affects about 28% of HTTP traffic
events.summary: Cloudflare reported that on 2025-12-05, from 08:47 to 09:12 UTC, a configuration change made to mitigate a React Server Components vulnerability triggered errors on about 28% of the HTTP traffic it serves. Cloudflare stated it was not an attack and committed to staged rollouts with rollback and fail-open error handling.

events.headline: Cloudflare chief legal officer Doug Kramer to step down; Alissa Starzak to succeed
events.summary: Cloudflare reported in a Form 8-K that Doug Kramer gave notice on 6 February 2026 of his resignation as chief legal officer effective 31 March 2026, staying on as a senior adviser, and that deputy chief legal officer Alissa Starzak is expected to succeed him.

events.headline: Cloudflare announces plan reducing about 20% of its workforce
events.summary: Cloudflare reported in its Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 that a plan announced on 2026-05-07 reduced approximately 20% of its workforce, with restructuring charges estimated at up to US$165M, and that the plan was substantially complete by the end of September 2026.

events.headline: Italian regulator AGCOM fines Cloudflare about EUR 14.2 million over Piracy Shield; Cloudflare appeals
events.summary: Cloudflare disclosed in its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026 that an Italian regulator issued an administrative fine of about EUR 14.2 million against it in December 2025 for alleged failure to comply with a regulatory scheme, which it is challenging. Cloudflare stated in a March 2026 blog post that AGCOM moved to issue the fine on 2025-12-29 in connection with the Piracy Shield site-blocking system and that it appealed on 2026-03-08.

events.headline: Cogent Security launches from stealth with US$11 million
events.summary: Cogent Security announced its launch from stealth with US$11 million led by Greylock Partners, with Lockstep and angel investors, and a set of AI agents for vulnerability management covering context gathering, prioritisation, fixes and reporting. The release quoted the chief information security officer of Alteryx.

events.headline: Cogent Security raises US$42 million Series A led by Bain Capital
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Cogent raised US$42 million in a Series A led by Bain Capital, with Greylock Partners, Definition Capital and individual investors, bringing total funding to US$53 million. The company named Upwind, Alteryx and CSC Generation as customers and said it worked with dozens of Fortune 1000 companies.

events.headline: Cogent launches Zero Day Response and Autonomous Remediation
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Cogent introduced Zero Day Response, which checks new advisories and pre-CVE disclosures against a customer's software inventory within minutes, and Autonomous Remediation, which builds a fix plan for each asset, checks business impact before acting and verifies the fix, under autonomy levels the customer sets. Whether the features were generally available was not stated.

events.headline: Cogent agrees to acquire Specular
events.summary: Pulse 2.0 reported on 2026-11-11 that Cogent had announced an agreement to acquire Specular, a company whose AI agents probe an organisation from the internet to find exposed assets and test how they could be exploited. Terms were not disclosed. Specular's founder is to lead offensive security at Cogent, and the external testing is to be combined with Cogent's remediation tools. Cogent's newsroom dates the announcement 2026-11-10.

events.headline: Cogent introduces DefenseOS with Agent Policies and Agent Automations
events.summary: Cogent announced on its blog on 2026-11-17 DefenseOS, which it describes as the context engine and agent harness at the core of its platform, together with Agent Policies for encoding an organisation's rules and Agent Automations for scheduled or event-triggered security work. The post does not give pricing or a general availability date.

events.headline: NICE completes its acquisition of Cognigy, valued at about US$955M
events.summary: NICE Ltd. announced on 2025-09-08 that it had closed its acquisition of Cognigy after regulatory approvals. The deal, announced on 2025-07-28, valued Cognigy at about US$955M. Cognigy became the NiCE Cognigy business unit, led by co-founder Philipp Heltewig as general manager and NICE's chief AI officer, and remains available both standalone and within NICE's CXone Mpower platform.

events.headline: NICE launches a next generation of NiCE Cognigy with reusable skills and decision tracing
events.summary: NICE announced a new generation of NiCE Cognigy with a redesigned builder, agents assembled from reusable skills, tools and personas, an AI assistant for building and testing, tracing of each step an agent takes, and native speech-to-speech models. Existing deployments continue unchanged; default models are included in the conversation price and premium third-party models are billed on usage.

events.headline: Cognition signs agreement to acquire Windsurf
events.summary: Cognition announced a definitive agreement to acquire Windsurf's intellectual property, agentic IDE product, trademark, brand and team. No price was given. The announcement cited $82M of annual recurring revenue and more than 350 enterprise customers for Windsurf. SiliconANGLE later reported that the deal followed a collapsed OpenAI bid and Google's hiring of Windsurf's founders.

events.headline: Cognition reported to lay off 30 staff and offer buyouts after Windsurf deal
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2025-08-05, citing The Information: Cognition laid off 30 employees about three weeks after acquiring Windsurf and offered the roughly 200 remaining Windsurf employees a buyout of nine months' salary. SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-09-08 that roughly 200 employees remained after the August 2025 layoff of 30 staff.

events.headline: Cognition raises more than $1bn Series D at $26bn valuation
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Cognition raised more than $1bn at a $26bn valuation in May 2026, when run-rate revenue was $492M. The vendor's blog lists the Series D post on 2026-05-27.

events.headline: Windsurf editor becomes Devin Desktop
events.summary: Cognition introduced Devin Desktop on 2026-06-02. Its July 2026 anniversary post says the company unified into one brand with that launch, and its FedRAMP post refers to 'Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)'.

events.headline: Cognition says Devin platform is FedRAMP High in process; Devin Desktop and CLI authorized
events.summary: Cognition announced that its full platform, including Devin Cloud, is listed as FedRAMP Class D (High) In-Process, and stated that Devin Desktop and CLI are FedRAMP High authorized. The listing was not confirmed on the FedRAMP Marketplace in this session.

events.headline: Cognition raises more than $2bn Series E at $48bn valuation
events.summary: Cognition announced a Series E of more than $2bn at a $48bn valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz and Accel, with Founders Fund, General Catalyst and Avenir returning. It said run-rate revenue had grown from $492M in May to almost $900M and named Citi among Devin customers.

events.headline: Cognition introduces Devin Bots, persistent agents that manage teams of Devin agents
events.summary: Fortune reported on 17 November 2026 that Cognition launched Devin Bots, persistent agents that split up work, assign it to Devin agents and keep context over projects lasting days or weeks. According to the article, dozens of customers have early access; it does not state general availability or pricing.

events.headline: RBC and Cohere partner on generative AI platform for financial services
events.summary: The Canadian Press reported on 2025-01-09 that RBC and Cohere would jointly develop generative AI products for financial services, with Cohere building a finance-specific version of its North workspace.

events.headline: Judge denies Cohere's motion to dismiss news publishers' copyright suit
events.summary: Reported by Bloomberg Law and Press Gazette on 2025-11-14: a federal judge in the Southern District of New York denied Cohere's motion to dismiss the copyright and trademark claims brought by news and magazine publishers in Advance Local Media LLC et al. v. Cohere Inc.

events.headline: Cohere announces plan to combine with Germany's Aleph Alpha
events.summary: Cohere announced on 2026-04-24 a plan to combine with Aleph Alpha, with Cohere leading the combined company. TechCrunch reported that Schwarz Group would provide EUR 500 million of structured financing and lead Cohere's planned Series E, and that the deal needed regulatory and shareholder approval.

events.headline: Cohere and Aleph Alpha sign definitive merger agreement
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Cohere and Aleph Alpha signed a merger agreement on 2026-09-16, with the combined company reportedly valued at US$20 billion, operating under the Cohere brand with dual headquarters in Berlin and Toronto. The deal was subject to regulatory clearance and had not closed.

events.headline: Cohere makes its North workspace widely available
events.summary: Cohere moved North from an early-access programme begun in January 2025 to wide availability on 2025-08-06. BetaKit and TechCrunch reported private deployment options including on-premises and air-gapped environments, and early customers including RBC, Bell, Dell and LG CNS.

events.headline: Cohere releases North 2 with agent memory, skills and admin cost controls
events.summary: Cohere announced North 2 on 2026-10-05, adding a new agent harness, reusable skills, shared libraries, memory across sessions, per-agent guardrails, administrator quotas and spending caps, new connectors and the option to use models other than Cohere's, as also reported by Techzine.

events.headline: Cohere completes initial close of Series E at a CAD 35.7 billion valuation
events.summary: Light Reading reported on 2026-10-29 that Cohere had completed the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to CAD 7 billion at a valuation of CAD 35.7 billion, led by Schwarz Group, with Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital and the Government of Canada as new investors and Inovia Capital, NVIDIA and Prosperity7 Ventures returning. The amount raised at the initial close was not given. The report said annual recurring revenue had grown 165% year on year at the end of the third quarter of 2026 and the company had 300 customers.

events.headline: Cohere completes acquisition of AISLE and brings in the team behind code-review firm cubic
events.summary: In a company blog post dated 13 November 2026, Cohere said it had completed its acquisition of AISLE, a developer of autonomous vulnerability discovery and remediation systems, and that the team behind cubic, an AI code-review platform, was joining Cohere. Cohere said it is forming a cybersecurity business, Cohere Cyber, around AISLE and a secure coding unit led by cubic's founder. No deal values were disclosed, and the post does not state how the cubic transaction is structured.

events.headline: Cohere names Jaya Baloo as its first chief information security officer
events.summary: Cohere announced in a blog post dated 12 November 2026 that Jaya Baloo had joined as its first chief information security officer. The post describes her as a co-founder of AISLE and a former security chief at Rapid7, Avast and KPN Telecom.

events.headline: Cohere adds a Crunchbase connector to North
events.summary: Cohere said in a blog post dated 17 November 2026 that North now has a Crunchbase connector giving access to private-company data such as funding and acquisition history. According to the post, it is available to North customers who hold their own Crunchbase licence and have single sign-on enabled, and figures drawn from Crunchbase carry citations.

events.headline: Concentric AI raises US$45 million Series B
events.summary: Concentric AI announced a US$45 million Series B led by Top Tier Capital Partners and HarbourVest Partners, with CyberFuture, Ballistic Ventures, Engineering Capital, Clear Ventures and Citi Ventures, taking total funding to about US$67 million. A Top Tier partner joined the board.

events.headline: Concentric AI adds Private Scan Manager for processing in the customer's environment
events.summary: Concentric AI announced Private Scan Manager, which lets Semantic Intelligence scans be processed inside the customer's own environment, together with support for NetApp ONTAP and MongoDB.

events.headline: Concentric AI acquires Swift Security and Acante
events.summary: Concentric AI announced it had bought two Silicon Valley start-ups: Swift Security, for data-in-motion controls on use of public AI tools, and Acante, for governing data used by in-house AI workloads. BankInfoSecurity reported that they employed about 20 and 10 people. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Concentric AI announces TX-RAMP certification
events.summary: Concentric AI said its Semantic Intelligence platform had achieved certification under the Texas Risk and Authorization Management Program, which lets it sell to Texas state agencies and public universities. The state's list was not checked.

events.headline: Private Scan Manager extended to Microsoft Azure
events.summary: Concentric AI announced that Semantic Intelligence scans can be processed in a customer's own Microsoft Azure environment, following AWS earlier in the year. Support for AWS GovCloud (US) was announced on 2026-01-13.

events.headline: Semantic DLP integrates with the Anthropic Compliance API
events.summary: Concentric AI announced that Semantic DLP can audit activity on the Claude platform, including prompts, responses and policy violations, through Anthropic's Compliance API.

events.headline: Concentric AI appoints a chief revenue officer
events.summary: Concentric AI announced the appointment of Gary Olson as chief revenue officer and Will Saso as vice-president of sales for the Americas.

events.headline: Concentric AI announces an endpoint agent for Semantic DLP
events.summary: Concentric AI announced the Semantic DLP Agent, extending its controls from the browser to desktop AI applications, coding agents and locally run models, with analysis of whether a prompt fits the user's role.

events.headline: CoreWeave completes initial public offering on Nasdaq at US$40 per share
events.summary: CoreWeave's 10-K states that in March 2025 it completed its IPO, selling about 37 million Class A shares at US$40.00 for net proceeds of about US$1.4B. The day of the month is not given in the source; the event is dated to the first of the month.

events.headline: OpenAI commits up to about US$6.5B more to CoreWeave under existing master agreement
events.summary: CoreWeave's filings state that in September 2025 it entered an order form under its May 2025 master services agreement with OpenAI, under which OpenAI committed to pay up to about US$6.5B through May 2031. The day is not given in the source.

events.headline: CoreWeave's proposed all-stock acquisition of Core Scientific is terminated
events.summary: CoreWeave announced on 7 July 2025 an agreement to acquire data centre operator Core Scientific in an all-stock deal valued at about US$9.0B. On 30 October 2025 it announced the agreement was terminated after Core Scientific stockholders did not approve it; the commercial relationship continues.

events.headline: Securities class action filed against CoreWeave in the District of New Jersey
events.summary: Disclosed in CoreWeave's 10-Q filed 2026-11-12: a putative class action, Masaitis v. CoreWeave, Inc. et al, was filed on 12 January 2026 alleging false and misleading statements under the Securities Exchange Act. Derivative actions followed and are stayed. The company states the claims are without merit.

events.headline: NVIDIA buys US$2.0B of CoreWeave Class A shares in a private placement
events.summary: CoreWeave's 10-Q states that in January 2026 it agreed to sell about 23 million Class A shares to NVIDIA Corporation at US$87.20 per share for gross proceeds of US$2.0B. The day is not given in the source.

events.headline: Meta commits up to about US$21.0B to CoreWeave for computing capacity
events.summary: CoreWeave's 10-Q states that in March 2026 Meta Platforms entered an order form initially committing up to about US$21.0B for capacity through 2032. The day is not given in the source.

events.headline: Jane Street commits about US$6.0B to use CoreWeave's platform
events.summary: CoreWeave's 10-Q states that in April 2026 it announced that trading firm Jane Street had committed about US$6.0B to use its AI cloud platform. The day is not given in the source.

events.headline: Credo AI launches global partner programme
events.summary: Channel Insider reported on 2025-07-17 that Credo AI formalised alliances with more than 30 technology and consulting firms, naming Microsoft, IBM, Databricks, Booz Allen Hamilton and McKinsey. The date is the article date; the launch was announced that week.

events.headline: Carahsoft to distribute Credo AI to US public sector
events.summary: Carahsoft was named Credo AI's master government aggregator, making the platform available through contract vehicles including NASA SEWP V, ITES-SW2 and NASPO ValuePoint.

events.headline: G42 and Credo AI sign responsible AI agreement
events.summary: At the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, Abu Dhabi group G42 and Credo AI unveiled a preliminary agreement covering risk-monitoring tools, policy design and education programmes for governments and enterprises.

events.headline: Credo AI joins Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program
events.summary: Credo AI announced acceptance into Microsoft's invite-only Pegasus programme, extending an existing Azure AI Foundry integration and a co-sell relationship.

events.headline: CERT/CC publishes four vulnerabilities in the CrewAI framework
events.summary: CERT/CC published vulnerability note VU#221883 on 2026-03-30, reporting four vulnerabilities in the open-source CrewAI framework (CVE-2026-2275, -2285, -2286 and -2287) covering code execution through the code interpreter tool's sandbox fallback, server-side request forgery in RAG search tools and local file reads in the JSON loader. SecurityWeek reported on 2026-03-31, and GBHackers on 2026-04-01, that no complete patch was available at publication. The note as revised on 2026-05-20 carries a vendor statement that the code interpreter tool was removed, path and URL validation were added, and all issues are fixed in current releases. This is a product vulnerability disclosure, not a reported breach of the vendor's systems.

events.headline: Cribl announces the acquisition of detection-coverage firm CardinalOps
events.summary: Cribl announced on 14 July 2026 that it was acquiring CardinalOps, a company founded in 2020 whose platform measured an organisation's detection coverage against adversary behaviour and found and repaired broken or noisy detection rules in other vendors' SIEM and EDR tools. Terms were not disclosed. BankInfoSecurity reported that CardinalOps had 35 staff and had raised US$24 million; TechTarget reported Cribl's chief executive saying about 20 security engineers and the intellectual property would move to Cribl. Cribl said it would open a Tel Aviv office for the team. No separate statement that the transaction had closed was found; a Cribl release of 19 August 2026 refers to it as an acquisition made in July, and when checked for this record cardinalops.com redirected permanently to cribl.io. The technology was then built into Cribl Detect.

events.headline: Cribl buys Radiant Security's AI security-operations technology assets
events.summary: Cribl announced on 19 August 2026 that it had bought technology assets, including intellectual property for automated alert triage and investigation, from Radiant Security. It described this as its second security technology acquisition of the year after CardinalOps. Terms were not disclosed. The release describes a purchase of assets, not of the company.

events.headline: Cribl launches Cribl Detect, a SIEM that includes detection posture management
events.summary: Cribl announced Cribl Detect on 29 September 2026 and said it was available to Cribl.Cloud customers. The release lists detection posture management, which maps existing detections to MITRE ATT&CK and shows coverage gaps, broken or noisy rules and missing telemetry, alongside in-stream detections, federated investigation and AI-assisted triage. TechTarget reported that the product combines technology from the CardinalOps and Radiant Security deals and is not yet supported on premises or in self-managed environments. Cribl's documentation labels every Cribl Detect page as Preview and says the feature is not recommended for production environments.

events.headline: CrowdStrike content update crashes Windows hosts running the Falcon sensor
events.summary: Disclosed by CrowdStrike in its incident reports of 2024-07-24 and 2024-08-06 and in its fiscal 2026 Form 10-K: a Rapid Response Content update released at 04:09 UTC on 19 July 2024 caused Windows hosts running sensor 7.11 and later to crash; the update was reverted at 05:27 UTC. CrowdStrike attributed the crash to a mismatch between the 21 input fields supplied and the 20 the sensor expected, which a Content Validator logic error let through, and said about 99% of Windows sensors were back online by 29 July 2024. Recorded although older than 24 months because it is the defining update incident for this category.

events.headline: CrowdStrike announces plan to cut about 500 roles, 5% of its workforce
events.summary: Filed by CrowdStrike with the SEC on 2025-05-07 (Form 8-K, Item 2.05): on 6 May 2025 the company announced a strategic plan eliminating about 500 positions, around 5% of its global workforce, with expected charges of US$36 million to US$53 million, while continuing to hire in strategic areas.

events.headline: Georgia court lets Delta's suit against CrowdStrike over the July 2024 outage proceed in part
events.summary: Reported by ITPro on 2025-05-20 and The Register on 2025-05-21: Judge Kelly Lee Ellerbe of Fulton County Superior Court allowed Delta Air Lines' negligence and computer trespass claims over the July 2024 outage to proceed and dismissed a fraud-based claim. Delta has put its losses at about US$500 million; CrowdStrike's counsel said the company expects any liability to be capped by contract at single-digit millions.

events.headline: CrowdStrike says it terminated an insider who shared screen images with a hacking group
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2025-11-21 and SecurityWeek on 2025-11-24: after the Scattered Lapsus$ Hunters group posted screenshots of internal CrowdStrike dashboards, CrowdStrike said it had identified and terminated a suspicious insider the previous month who shared pictures of his screen externally, that its systems were never compromised, and that it had referred the matter to law enforcement.

events.headline: CrowdStrike completes acquisition of Seraphic Algorithms
events.summary: CrowdStrike's fiscal 2026 Form 10-K reports that it signed an agreement to acquire Seraphic Algorithms Ltd. on 12 January 2026 and closed on 3 February 2026 for US$327.4 million in cash, net of cash acquired, plus replacement equity awards.

events.headline: CrowdStrike completes acquisition of SGNL.AI
events.summary: CrowdStrike's fiscal 2026 Form 10-K reports that it signed an agreement to acquire SGNL.AI, Inc. on 7 January 2026 and closed on 20 February 2026 for US$627.9 million in cash, net of cash acquired, plus replacement equity awards.

events.headline: CrowdStrike acquires Onum Technology and Pangea Cyber in fiscal 2026
events.summary: CrowdStrike's fiscal 2026 Form 10-K reports the acquisitions of Onum Technology Inc. and Pangea Cyber Corporation during the fiscal year, with US$382.3 million of cash paid for business acquisitions net of cash acquired. The filing's data tags date the two acquisitions 12 and 26 September 2025.

events.headline: CrowdStrike makes Falcon AI Detection and Response (AIDR) generally available
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced general availability of Falcon AI Detection and Response, which inspects AI prompts, responses and agent actions for prompt injection, unsafe content and sensitive data and applies report, redact or block policies. Its documentation changelog of the same date lists browser, application, agentic, gateway, cloud and OpenTelemetry collectors and integration with Falcon Next-Gen SIEM. SecurityWeek had reported on 2025-09-16 that CrowdStrike would buy Pangea to build the product.

events.headline: CrowdStrike introduces Falcon Guardian as the successor to Falcon AIDR
events.summary: At its Fal.Con 2026 conference CrowdStrike introduced Falcon Guardian, which it called the evolution of Falcon AIDR. It adds discovery of AI agents on endpoints, tracing of agent activity against endpoint telemetry, and controls over which agents may run. An AI gateway and a managed service for Guardian were described as still to come. The AIDR documentation states that AIDR reaches end of support on 2026-11-30 and that its capabilities continue in Falcon Guardian.

events.headline: CrowdStrike adds network vulnerability assessment to Falcon Exposure Management
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced that Network Vulnerability Assessment was generally available in Falcon Exposure Management. It uses existing Falcon sensors to scan network devices such as routers, switches and firewalls without separate scanners. Existing customers were offered free scanning for up to 10% of licensed assets, capped at 10,000.

events.headline: CrowdStrike says Falcon Exposure Management is authorised at FedRAMP Moderate
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced that Falcon Exposure Management was available to organisations requiring FedRAMP Moderate authorisation, in the Falcon platform's GovCloud environment. The FedRAMP Marketplace lists the Falcon platform for government without enumerating modules, so the module-level statement rests on the vendor's release.

events.headline: CrowdStrike signs definitive agreement to acquire Fiddler AI; deal not yet closed
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced in a press release dated 2026-11-03 that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, an AI observability vendor. CrowdStrike said Fiddler's product will be sold within the Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, with general availability expected in its fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, that the price will be paid mostly in cash with a portion in stock subject to vesting, and that closing is expected in the same quarter subject to customary conditions. No price was disclosed. The same agreement is also recorded from Fiddler's side as fiddler-ai-evt-2026-11-crowdstrike-agreement.

events.headline: CrowdStrike signs definitive agreement to acquire AI security testing company Dreadnode; deal not yet closed
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced in a press release dated 2026-11-03 that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Dreadnode, which builds automated security testing for AI models, applications and agents. CrowdStrike said the technology will become an Automated AI Security Testing capability on the Falcon platform, planned for general availability in its fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, with test findings feeding Falcon Guardian as policy recommendations. The price was not disclosed; it is to be paid mostly in cash with a portion in stock subject to vesting, and closing is expected in the same quarter subject to customary conditions.

events.headline: Crusoe raises US$3.9 billion Series F at a US$30.9 billion valuation
events.summary: Crusoe announced on 2026-09-17 the initial closing of a Series F of US$3.9 billion at a post-money valuation of US$30.9 billion, co-led by Atreides Management, Mubadala Capital and Valor Equity Partners, with participants including Founders Fund, GIC, NVIDIA, Qatar Investment Authority, Salesforce Ventures and TPG. TechCrunch reported the same figures.

events.headline: Crusoe adds three directors to its board
events.summary: Crusoe announced on 2026-09-17 that Thomas Seifert, chief financial officer of Cloudflare, Bill Stein, former chief executive of Digital Realty, and JB Straubel, founder of Redwood Materials, had joined its board. TechCrunch also reported the appointments.

events.headline: Crusoe and Neuberger Specialty Finance announce a US$700 million facility
events.summary: Crusoe's newsroom lists an announcement dated 2026-10-22 of a US$700 million facility with Neuberger Specialty Finance to finance power infrastructure. Only the newsroom listing was read; the terms were not.

events.headline: Crusoe reports ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification for Crusoe Cloud and Managed Inference
events.summary: Crusoe stated on its trust centre on 2026-02-03 that Schellman had awarded it ISO 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 certificates covering its cloud platform and Managed Inference services.

events.headline: Crusoe Cloud renews SOC 2 Type II, extending scope to Managed Inference
events.summary: Crusoe stated on its trust centre on 2026-06-17 that Crusoe Cloud had renewed its SOC 2 Type II attestation for the period 2025-05-01 to 2026-04-30, covering infrastructure and managed AI services including Managed Inference.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks agrees to acquire CyberArk for about $25 billion
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 30 July 2025 an agreement to acquire CyberArk for $45.00 in cash and 2.2005 Palo Alto Networks shares per CyberArk share, which the release valued at about $25 billion of equity. Both boards approved the deal, which was subject to regulatory clearance and a CyberArk shareholder vote.

events.headline: CyberArk reported among companies affected by Salesloft Drift data theft
events.summary: Reported by TechTarget on 2025-09-12 and by BleepingComputer on 2025-09-14: CyberArk was among the companies affected by the campaign that used stolen Salesloft Drift tokens to take data from customers' Salesforce environments. UpGuard's tracker dates CyberArk's confirmation to 4 September 2025 and says the exposure was limited to business contact details and account and conversation metadata in its CRM. CyberArk's own notice is no longer reachable at its original address, which now redirects to a Palo Alto Networks blog index.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks completes acquisition of CyberArk
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 11 February 2026 that it had completed the acquisition of CyberArk, exchanging each CyberArk share for $45.00 in cash and 2.2005 Palo Alto Networks shares. The release said CyberArk's products would stay available as a standalone platform while being integrated. The acquirer's FY2026 Form 10-K records the same completion date, about 4,223 employees added, and a guarantee of CyberArk's $1.25 billion convertible notes due 2030. ITPro reported the deal value as about $25 billion.

events.headline: Job cuts at CyberArk reported the day after acquisition closes
events.summary: Reported by CTech on 2026-02-12 and by Globes on 2026-02-17: hundreds of CyberArk employees were told their roles would end, one day after the acquisition closed. CTech reported more than 10% of about 4,000 staff; Globes reported about 700 people worldwide, mainly in support and head-office functions and not in research and development. Palo Alto Networks gave no number and said the changes affected a small part of the combined workforce in overlapping roles.

events.headline: CyberArk products relaunched as Idira under the Palo Alto Networks brand
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Idira on 12 May 2026 as its identity security platform, generally available that day, built on CyberArk's privileged access technology and extended to machine and AI-agent identities. Existing CyberArk SaaS customers get upgrade paths that depend on their licence tier. The cyberark.com site now redirects to Idira pages on paloaltonetworks.com, and the documentation and status sites carry the Idira name.

events.headline: Malicious update published to Cyberhaven's Chrome extension
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2024-12-27 and TechTarget on 2025-01-02: an attacker who had phished a Cyberhaven employee's Chrome Web Store access published a malicious version of the company's browser extension on 2024-12-25. Cyberhaven said it removed the package within about an hour of detecting it and advised customers to rotate credentials. TechTarget reported that dozens of other extensions were compromised in the same campaign.

events.headline: Cyberhaven raises US$100 million Series D at US$1 billion valuation
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-04-02 that Cyberhaven raised US$100 million in a Series D led by StepStone with Schroders and Industry Ventures, valuing it at US$1 billion and taking total funding to US$250 million.

events.headline: Howard Ting steps down as Cyberhaven chief executive; Nishant Doshi named interim
events.summary: BankInfoSecurity reported on 2025-05-13 that chief executive Howard Ting had resigned, citing family reasons, and that chief product and development officer Nishant Doshi became interim chief executive, with Ting staying on the board. Later company releases describe Doshi as chief executive.

events.headline: Cyberhaven introduces Flow platform
events.summary: Cyberhaven announced Flow, its platform combining data lineage, loss prevention, insider risk management and controls for AI agents, saying it would be available in the following quarter with an upgrade path for existing customers.

events.headline: Cyberhaven names Todd Rotger president and adds three executives
events.summary: Cyberhaven announced Todd Rotger as president for go-to-market, Manish Kalia as chief product officer, Aaron Feigin as chief marketing officer and Andy Dobrov as senior vice-president of customer experience.

events.headline: Cyberhaven puts Agentic Data Security module on sale
events.summary: Cyberhaven announced that Agentic Data Security, a Flow module that finds AI agents, records their prompts, tool calls and file reads, and applies data policies to their actions, was available for purchase.

events.headline: Cycode launches Agentic Development Security Platform
events.summary: Cycode announced on 2026-03-23 that it was repositioning its platform as an Agentic Development Security Platform, adding Maestro agent orchestration, AI visibility and governance, and real-time guardrails for AI coding tools. The release does not say which features are generally available.

events.headline: Cycode adds persistent memory to its Maestro security agent
events.summary: A Cycode blog post dated 10 November 2026 introduced memory for Maestro, the agent within the Cycode platform. The post describes an always-on store for preferences, rules and team vocabulary and a recalled store for factual context, which users can view, change or delete. It does not say whether the feature is generally available or in preview.

events.headline: CyCognito announces new automation and visibility features for its external exposure platform
events.summary: CyCognito announced on 17 March 2025 additions to its platform including action rules for classifying assets, AI-assisted search, cross-asset relationship queries, an industry benchmarks dashboard, change monitoring, AWS and Cloudflare integrations and WordPress vulnerability testing. The release gave no general-availability date.

events.headline: CyCognito reports 2025 alliances with Wiz, Armis, NCC Group, DeepSeas and Picus
events.summary: In a release of 16 December 2025 CyCognito said it had formed cloud security, managed security and exposure testing alliances during 2025 with Wiz, Armis, NCC Group, DeepSeas and Picus across the EU, US and Asia-Pacific. It reported growing demand in financial services, manufacturing and the public sector without giving customer numbers. Picus lists CyCognito among its integrations.

events.headline: CyCognito announces Continuous AI Pentesting, running with select design partners
events.summary: CyCognito announced Continuous AI Pentesting on 16 June 2026: AI agents that test the external attack surface continuously and chain exposures across applications, APIs, cloud and AI services, alongside the platform's existing deterministic tests. The release said the capability was running with select design partners and gave no wider availability date.

events.headline: Cyera acquires non-human identity startup Otterize
events.summary: Cyera announced the acquisition of Otterize, which sets least-privilege access for cloud workloads, in a deal it described as estimated in the tens of millions of dollars. The release says it followed Cyera's acquisition of Shape AI and a US$540 million Series E at a US$6 billion valuation.

events.headline: Cyera raises US$600 million at a US$12 billion valuation
events.summary: Cyera announced a US$600 million round led by Evolution Equity Partners with Cyberstarts, Temasek and existing investors including Accel, AT&T Ventures, Blackstone, Coatue and Spark Capital. SecurityWeek reported total funding of more than US$2.3 billion and earlier rounds of US$540 million (June 2025, US$6 billion valuation) and US$400 million (January 2026, US$9 billion valuation).

events.headline: Cyera agrees to acquire Oasis Security for about US$1 billion
events.summary: Cyera announced a letter of intent to acquire Oasis Security, a non-human identity and agent access governance company, for about US$1 billion, mostly in cash with the rest in shares according to TechCrunch. SecurityBrief UK reported on 8 September 2026 that the deal had completed and that the Oasis technology now operates as Cyera Identity.

events.headline: Goldman Sachs Alternatives invests US$400 million in Cyera
events.summary: Cyera announced a US$400 million investment from the growth equity arm of Goldman Sachs Alternatives as an extension of its Series G, at a valuation of more than US$12 billion.

events.headline: Cyera's AI security platform listed in the Claude Marketplace
events.summary: Cyera announced that its AI security platform is available in the Claude Marketplace, according to a release listed in its newsroom. The body of the release was not reviewed.

events.headline: Cyera announces Cy Agents and Cyera Endpoint
events.summary: At its datasecAI 2026 event Cyera announced Cy Agents, a set of AI agents for detection, triage and investigation, and Cyera Endpoint, an on-device sensor that extends data loss prevention to laptops and workstations. The release does not say whether either is generally available.

events.headline: Varonis files trade-secrets case in Delaware federal court naming Cyera US as a defendant
events.summary: According to the federal docket published by CourtListener, Varonis Systems, Inc. filed a Defend Trade Secrets Act case in the US District Court for the District of Delaware on 2025-05-08 (No. 1:25-cv-00571) against two individuals and Cyera US Inc. The docket showed the case as active in November 2026, with a bench trial set for July 2029. The complaint was not read.

events.headline: Daon launches mobile driving licence support with MATTR
events.summary: Daon announced on 2025-10-28 support for mobile driving licences in its identity platform, built with MATTR and designed to the ISO/IEC 18013-5 and 18013-7 standards.

events.headline: Daon announces eIDAS certification for identity verification
events.summary: Daon's media center records a 2025-11-04 announcement of certification for high-assurance EU digital identity verification. Its compliance page states that xProof on TrustX was audited at the Extended (High) level against ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 and EN 319 401 and links a certificate; the certificate file was not read.

events.headline: Daon launches Workforce Identity Fraud Prevention
events.summary: Daon's media center records the launch on 2026-05-05 of Workforce Identity Fraud Prevention, a solution for verifying employees across the employment lifecycle.

events.headline: Daon announces ISO/IEC 42001 certification
events.summary: Daon announced on 2026-06-16 that it had been certified to ISO/IEC 42001 for its AI management system after an independent audit, covering its digital identity and fraud prevention solutions across operations in the United States, Ireland, Serbia, Australia and the United Kingdom. The certification body was not named.

events.headline: Thoma Bravo completes US$5.3 billion acquisition of Darktrace
events.summary: Private equity firm Thoma Bravo completed its all-cash acquisition of Darktrace plc at US$7.75 per share, about US$5.3 billion. Darktrace's shares stopped trading on the London Stock Exchange. Darktrace continues to trade under its own brand.

events.headline: Darktrace / EMAIL adds behavioural DLP, BIMI support and service-desk integrations
events.summary: Darktrace announced label-free data loss prevention for outbound email, BIMI support in its DMARC component, automatic Jira and ServiceNow ticket creation and an email analysis agent for Microsoft Security Copilot.

events.headline: Jill Popelka to step down as Darktrace CEO; chairman named interim CEO
events.summary: Darktrace announced that chief executive Jill Popelka would step down and that board chairman Charles Goodman would act as interim chief executive.

events.headline: Darktrace appoints Ed Jennings as President and CEO
events.summary: Darktrace announced the appointment of Ed Jennings, formerly chief executive of Quickbase and chief operating officer of Mimecast, as President and CEO from 2026-03-23.

events.headline: Databricks signs Series K term sheet at a valuation above US$100 billion
events.summary: Databricks announced on 19 August 2025 that it had signed a term sheet for a Series K round valuing the company at more than US$100 billion, to fund Agent Bricks, its Lakebase database and acquisitions. TechCrunch later described the round as US$1 billion closed in September 2025.

events.headline: Databricks reports US$5 billion Series L at US$134 billion valuation plus US$2 billion debt capacity
events.summary: Databricks announced on 9 February 2026 more than US$7 billion of new financing: about US$5 billion of equity in a Series L round at a US$134 billion valuation and about US$2 billion of added debt capacity. Named investors included JPMorganChase, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Microsoft, Morgan Stanley and Qatar Investment Authority. It also reported a revenue run-rate above US$5.4 billion.

events.headline: Databricks closes US$5 billion round at US$190 billion valuation
events.summary: Databricks announced on 13 August 2026 a US$5 billion strategic round at a US$190 billion valuation led by Coatue with Blackstone, MGX, T. Rowe Price and Sixth Street Growth, after announcing a term sheet at US$188 billion on 16 July 2026. It reported a revenue run-rate above US$7 billion. The Next Web reported that the company intends to stay private for now.

events.headline: Databricks acquires spreadsheet company Row Zero
events.summary: Databricks announced on 24 September 2026 that it had acquired Row Zero, whose spreadsheet connects to governed data, to add a spreadsheet interface to its Genie assistant. Terms were not given in the release.

events.headline: Judge denies Databricks' motion to dismiss authors' AI-training copyright class action
events.summary: Reported by Bloomberg Government on 2026-04-23: Judge Charles Breyer of the US District Court for the Northern District of California denied Databricks' bid to dismiss a proposed class action by authors who allege it trained a large language model on their books without permission. The federal docket index published by CourtListener lists the case as In re Mosaic LLM Litigation, No. 3:24-cv-01451, filed 2024-03-08.

events.headline: Datadog notifies customers of unauthorised access to source code repositories
events.summary: Datadog disclosed in its Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 2026-02-18) that in April 2025 it notified customers that an unauthorised third party had accessed a number of its source code repositories through compromised employee account credentials, and that it revoked the credentials and terminated the access. The filing gives the month only; the first of the month is used as a placeholder date.

events.headline: Datadog acquires data observability startup Metaplane
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2025-04-23 that Datadog had acquired Metaplane, a Boston-based data observability startup, for undisclosed terms, and that it was Datadog's second acquisition of 2025.

events.headline: Datadog acquires experimentation platform Eppo
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2025-05-05 that Datadog had acquired Eppo, a feature-flagging and experimentation platform, for undisclosed terms; the article cited a report that the price was about US$220M. Datadog said the deal would help teams compare AI models.

events.headline: Datadog adds AI Agent Monitoring and LLM Experiments to LLM Observability
events.summary: Datadog announced on 2025-06-10 at its DASH conference that AI Agent Monitoring, which maps each agent's decision path, was generally available, and that LLM Experiments and an AI Agents Console were in preview.

events.headline: Datadog renames LLM Observability to Agent Observability and moves to per-span pricing
events.summary: A third-party pricing tracker recorded that Datadog's pricing page changed the product name from LLM Observability to Agent Observability in the week of 2026-06-08, replacing per-request pricing with a free tier and a Pro tier billed per LLM span. Datadog's own HIPAA eligible-services list, updated 2026-07-23, refers to 'Agent Observability (formerly LLM Observability)'. No dated vendor announcement of the rename was found; the date used is the tracker's.

events.headline: DataRobot acquires Agnostiq and its Covalent compute orchestration platform
events.summary: DataRobot announced on 10 February 2025 that it had acquired Agnostiq, maker of the open-source distributed computing platform Covalent, to add compute orchestration across cloud, on-premises and hybrid environments for agentic AI applications. Terms were not given in the release.

events.headline: DataRobot announces Agent Workforce Platform built with NVIDIA
events.summary: DataRobot's press index lists a release dated 31 July 2025 announcing its Agent Workforce Platform, built with NVIDIA. The company's home page now presents the Agent Workforce Platform as its main offering.

events.headline: DataRobot promotes on-premises, air-gapped and VPC deployment of its agent platform
events.summary: DataRobot announced on 22 July 2026 that its Agent Workforce Platform runs fully outside the public cloud, on premises, air-gapped or in a virtual private cloud, with the same governance and monitoring in each, and positioned this for regulated sectors including financial services. NVIDIA, Dell and Nebius are named as infrastructure partners.

events.headline: DataRobot and Dell Technologies offer on-premises agentic AI blueprint for Middle East enterprises
events.summary: DataRobot said in a press release dated 17 November 2026 that it is working with Dell Technologies to combine the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA and the DataRobot Agent Workforce Platform for Middle East customers running on-premises, private or hybrid environments. The release says a DataRobot blueprint is offered through the Dell Automation Platform, with financial services and logistics as initial focus sectors.

events.headline: Decagon raises US$250M Series D at a US$4.5B valuation
events.summary: Decagon announced a US$250M Series D led by Coatue and Index Ventures at a US$4.5B valuation, about three times its valuation in June 2025. It also announced a new version of its voice agent.

events.headline: Decagon introduces Alto, an in-house voice model for its voice agents
events.summary: Decagon said in a blog post dated 11 November 2026 that it had introduced Alto, a voice model that governs turn-taking and responses in its voice agents and is already handling live customer calls. The company claims an average response time of about 700 milliseconds and a resolution-rate gain of more than five points; these are vendor figures. The post gives no release-stage label.

events.headline: Decagon introduces Missions for multi-step customer outcomes spanning several conversations
events.summary: Decagon announced Missions in a blog post dated 12 November 2026. The post describes it as a way for agents to pursue a stated goal across multiple conversations, parties and systems over days or weeks, keeping a case record and customer memory. It does not say whether the feature is generally available or in beta.

events.headline: Italian data protection authority orders limitation of DeepSeek's processing of Italian users' data
events.summary: The Garante per la protezione dei dati personali announced on 30 January 2025 that it had urgently ordered Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence and Beijing DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence to limit processing of Italian users' data, with immediate effect, and had opened an investigation. The authority stated that the companies' reply, which said they did not operate in Italy and that European law did not apply to them, was wholly insufficient.

events.headline: Researchers report a publicly accessible DeepSeek database containing chat histories and API keys
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch and The Register on 30 January 2025, citing research published by Wiz on 29 January 2025: an unauthenticated ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek was reachable from the internet and held more than a million log entries including chat history, API keys and backend details. Wiz stated that DeepSeek secured the database promptly after being notified. TechCrunch reported that it was not known whether anyone else had accessed it and that DeepSeek did not respond to a request for comment.

events.headline: Canada restricts DeepSeek chatbot on some federal government devices
events.summary: Reported by Global News on 7 February 2025: an email from the chief information officer of the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat said the DeepSeek application was restricted on government mobile devices managed by Shared Services Canada as a precaution, citing serious privacy concerns about collection and retention of personal information, and recommended that other departments consider blocking the application and website. The Canadian Press, carried by CTV News the same day, reported the restriction on some government phones. The memo itself was not found on a government site.

events.headline: Berlin data protection commissioner notifies Apple and Google of DeepSeek app as illegal content
events.summary: The Berlin Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information published a press release in June 2025 stating that it had notified Apple and Google in Germany of the DeepSeek app as illegal content. Reuters reported in a factbox dated 7 January 2026 that the German commissioner had asked the two companies to remove the app from their stores over data safety concerns. Only the title of the regulator's PDF could be read in this session; the legal reasoning was not reviewed.

events.headline: DeepSeek releases V4 models on its API and sets retirement date for legacy model names
events.summary: DeepSeek's API change log records the release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro and V4-Flash on 24 April 2026 through OpenAI-format and Anthropic-format interfaces, with the legacy names deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner to be discontinued three months later.

events.headline: DeepSeek's first external funding round reported at about 50 billion yuan
events.summary: Caixin Global reported on 17 July 2026, citing a regulatory filing by a listed company that invested indirectly, that DeepSeek raised about 50 billion yuan in its first external round at a post-money valuation above 350 billion yuan, with Tencent and CATL among the investors. The Next Web, citing Reuters, reported on 16 June 2026 that founder Liang Wenfeng was to contribute the largest share. DeepSeek did not announce the round on the pages reviewed.

events.headline: US DHS orders DeepSeek products excluded and removed from federal civilian agency systems
events.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security published in the Federal Register on 20 October 2026 notice of Exclusion and Removal Order #2026-01, dated 24 July 2026 and issued under the Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act. The order directs federal civilian executive agencies to exclude Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd and affiliated entities from procurements and to remove DeepSeek products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from their information technology, with exceptions available on request. The order states that DeepSeek's servers are located in China and that use could result in transfer of sensitive data there. It does not apply to private companies.

events.headline: US agencies' advisory alleges model distillation campaigns by DeepSeek, Alibaba and four other firms
events.summary: CISA, the NSA and the FBI published advisory AA26-251A on 8 September 2026, which stated that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI had conducted high-volume distillation of US AI companies' models since at least late 2024 in breach of the providers' terms of use. The advisory stated that DeepSeek used the outputs to train its R1 and V3 models and that Alibaba used them to improve its Qwen models. These are the agencies' allegations; no response from either company was found in this session.

events.headline: DeepSeek adds built-in web search, file input, URL reading and safety checks to its API
events.summary: DeepSeek's API documentation, in a news post and change log entry dated 13 November 2026, says the deepseek-flash model now supports built-in web search, file input, URL reading and an optional safety check across its Messages, Responses and Chat Completions interfaces. Search, fetch, OCR, speech recognition and text-to-speech are also offered as standalone APIs, and the post says tool usage fees apply on top of token charges.

events.headline: Thycotic and Centrify complete merger under TPG Capital ownership
events.summary: The companies announced on 13 April 2021 that Thycotic and Centrify had completed their merger and would operate for the time being as ThycoticCentrify, led by Art Gilliland and backed by TPG Capital, with Insight Partners, Thoma Bravo and PSP Investments holding minority stakes. SiliconANGLE later reported that TPG had bought Thycotic from Insight Partners and Centrify from Thoma Bravo in March 2021.

events.headline: ThycoticCentrify renamed Delinea
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 1 February 2022 that TPG Capital had renamed ThycoticCentrify as Delinea Inc., a new brand for the combined company.

events.headline: Delinea completes acquisition of StrongDM
events.summary: Delinea announced on 5 March 2026 that it had completed its acquisition of StrongDM, an access management company, adding just-in-time runtime authorisation across infrastructure, applications and cloud to its privileged access products. Financial terms were not disclosed. StrongDM is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset; Delinea now publishes a separate sub-processor list for it.

events.headline: Delinea releases a Microsoft Sentinel solution for Delinea Platform privileged access events
events.summary: Delinea announced on 18 November 2026 a Microsoft Sentinel solution that sends Delinea Platform audit events, including secret access, authentication, session activity and configuration changes, into Sentinel with analytic rules, hunting queries and workbooks. The company says it is available in the Microsoft Marketplace and the Sentinel Content Hub.

events.headline: DigiCert previews Quantum Central for post-quantum readiness
events.summary: DigiCert announced a free, self-service preview of Quantum Central, a new part of DigiCert ONE for cataloguing cryptographic assets, flagging quantum-vulnerable systems and planning migration, with Jira integration.

events.headline: DigiCert Quantum Central becomes generally available
events.summary: DigiCert announced general availability of Quantum Central, adding policy evaluation, remediation tracking, CBOM export, an AI assistant and links to Trust Lifecycle Manager. Quantum Computing Report covered the release the next day.

events.headline: Doppel raises US$35 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners
events.summary: Doppel announced on 2 May 2025 a US$35 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with 9Yards Capital and Sozo Ventures joining earlier investors. SecurityWeek reported the round, a valuation of US$205 million and total funding of US$54.4 million.

events.headline: Doppel launches Simulation, a phishing simulation product using AI agents
events.summary: In a release dated 20 August 2025 Doppel launched Doppel Simulation for security awareness training and social engineering testing. The release describes it as using autonomous AI phishing agents and campaigns informed by current threats.

events.headline: Doppel raises US$70 million Series C at a valuation above US$600 million
events.summary: Fortune reported on 19 November 2025, and SecurityWeek the next day, that Doppel had raised a US$70 million Series C led by Bessemer Venture Partners at a valuation of more than US$600 million, taking total funding to US$124 million. New investors included George Kurtz and NTT DOCOMO Ventures.

events.headline: Doppel announces ISO/IEC 42001, 27001 and 27701 certification
events.summary: In a release dated 13 April 2026 Doppel said it had earned ISO/IEC 42001, 27001 and 27701 certification, adding to its SOC 2 Type II report, and named Mastermind as the certifier. The release does not state the certificate scope, and no registry entry was read.

events.headline: Doppel announces Email Security
events.summary: In a release dated 27 May 2026 Doppel announced Email Security, joining its digital risk protection and human risk management products, to investigate inbox threats using its threat graph and request takedown of the infrastructure behind phishing campaigns.

events.headline: Doppel Email Security becomes generally available
events.summary: Doppel announced general availability of Email Security on 30 July 2026, in the Americas and Asia-Pacific regions, together with an AI managed service for its human risk management product. SecurityBrief UK reported the launch on 31 July 2026.

events.headline: MUFG Innovation Partners invests in Doppel
events.summary: Doppel announced on 24 September 2026 that MUFG Innovation Partners, the corporate venture arm of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, had become a strategic investor. The investor's own notice, dated 25 September 2026, says the investment was made through its No. 3 investment partnership. Neither gave an amount.

events.headline: Doppel acquires PropRise and adds its founders to its engineering team
events.summary: Doppel announced on 4 November 2026 that it had acquired PropRise, a Y Combinator-backed company founded in 2023, and that its two founders would join Doppel's engineering organisation. Pulse 2.0 reported the deal on 7 November 2026. No price was given.

events.headline: Dropzone AI raises US$37 million Series B
events.summary: Dropzone AI announced a US$37 million Series B led by Theory Ventures with Madrona, Decibel, Pioneer Square Labs and IQT. SecurityWeek, reporting on 2025-07-29, put total funding at more than US$57 million.

events.headline: Dropzone AI says its AI SOC Analyst is FedRAMP High (Class D) certified through Second Front's platform
events.summary: Dropzone AI said in a press release published on 2026-11-20 that its AI SOC Analyst had obtained FedRAMP High (Class D) certification through Second Front's 2F Game Warden platform, making it available to US federal agencies for production use. The release points to Second Front's FedRAMP Marketplace listing (FR2410866384) and names no authorising agency. That listing, checked on 2026-11-22, shows 2F Game Warden as FedRAMP Certified at Class D (High) since 2025-08-12 but does not name Dropzone AI, so the certification runs through Second Front's platform and Dropzone's inclusion rests on its own statement.

events.headline: Oracle and Duality announce privacy-first AI for government and defence customers
events.summary: Duality's news page links an Oracle announcement dated 2025-10-13 on delivering privacy-first AI to government and defence customers with Duality. The Oracle page itself could not be retrieved, so details are limited to the headline.

events.headline: Duality releases version 4.6 of its platform with data harmonisation
events.summary: Duality's news page lists the release of Duality 4.6 on 2026-06-14, described as adding data harmonisation for analytics and AI across several organisations.

events.headline: Duality and Red Hat partner on AI for sovereign and regulated environments
events.summary: Duality announced a partnership with Red Hat to let governments and regulated enterprises run AI and analytics on sensitive data using trusted execution environments on infrastructure they control, naming defence, public sector, healthcare and financial services as targets.

events.headline: UK's National Security Strategic Investment Fund invests in Duality
events.summary: NSSIF announced a strategic investment in Duality, saying the vendor's privacy-enhancing technology is in production with national security and defence customers. The amount was not disclosed. The date is that of the vendor's blog post.

events.headline: Eigen Technologies Ltd enters administration
events.summary: According to Companies House filings, Eigen Technologies Ltd, the UK company behind the Eigen document AI platform, entered administration on 5 June 2024, the day before Sirion announced it had acquired Eigen. The company was renamed ETL Realisations 2024 Limited on 17 June 2024, the administration ended on 2 June 2026 with a move to dissolution, and the company was dissolved on 2 September 2026. The filings reviewed do not describe the terms on which the business passed to Sirion.

events.headline: Sirion announces acquisition of Eigen Technologies
events.summary: Sirion, a contract lifecycle management software company, announced it had acquired Eigen Technologies, a London document AI provider serving financial services and insurance. Terms were not disclosed. Sirion said Eigen's technology would be combined with its extraction agent and that Eigen's researchers would form a London AI research centre; TechCrunch reported that Eigen's co-founder would become Sirion's chief AI officer.

events.headline: Haveli Investments completes majority investment in Sirion
events.summary: Sirion announced that Haveli Investments, an Austin-based private equity firm, had completed a majority investment in the company, following an agreement announced on 8 January 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed. Sirion continues to trade under its own name.

events.headline: Sirion completes an IRAP assessment at OFFICIAL: Sensitive level in Australia
events.summary: Sirion announced that an independent assessor had completed an Infosec Registered Assessors Program assessment of its platform at the OFFICIAL: Sensitive level under the Australian Government Information Security Manual.

events.headline: Elastic commits to plan reducing its workforce by about 7%
events.summary: Disclosed by Elastic in a Form 8-K filed on 2026-06-24: on 2026-06-23 the company committed to a plan to reduce its workforce by approximately 7%, with non-recurring cash charges of about US$22 million to US$25 million, mostly severance, and reductions substantially complete by the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2027. The company said it would keep hiring in priority areas and expected total headcount to grow over the fiscal year. The chief executive's message to staff, published the same day, cited AI and automation changing how work is done.

events.headline: Elastic chief product officer Ken Exner resigns; engineering leaders report to the CEO
events.summary: Elastic's Form 8-K filed on 2026-06-24 reported that chief product officer Ken Exner gave notice on 2026-06-18, with a last day of 2026-07-17, to pursue another opportunity and not because of any disagreement. Senior engineering leaders, including the head of the Observability and Security group, now report directly to the chief executive. No successor was named.

events.headline: Elastic Cloud's AWS Bahrain region becomes unavailable; still unresolved in November 2026
events.summary: Disclosed by Elastic on its status page: a connectivity disruption in the AWS Bahrain (me-south-1) region was first posted on 2026-03-02, citing localised power issues. An update on 2026-09-21 stated that the region had been removed from selection for new deployments, that existing deployments there were inaccessible because of an AWS infrastructure disruption with no recovery timeline, and that customers should assume the region is unavailable for the foreseeable future. The incident was still open on 2026-11-20. Other regions were shown as operational.

events.headline: Elastic announces AlertZero AI agents for Elastic Security in technical preview
events.summary: Elastic announced AlertZero, a layer of specialised AI agents in Elastic Security organised into triage, hunt, detection and forensics 'Watches', with analysts setting how much each may do without approval. It is a technical preview for Elastic Cloud, self-managed and air-gapped deployments and works with a model of the customer's choice. No pricing was given.

events.headline: Securities suit filed against Elastic N.V. in the Eastern District of New York
events.summary: According to the CourtListener federal docket index, searched on 2026-11-20, Lucid Alternative Fund, LP v. Elastic N.V.
