(1:25-cv-00785) was filed in the Eastern District of New York on 11 February 2025 under the Securities Exchange Act, and no termination date is shown. The claims were not retrieved. In its fiscal 2026 annual report Elastic states that it is not party to any legal proceeding that would have a material adverse effect on it.

events.headline: Elastic completes acquisition of embedding-model developer Jina AI
events.summary: Elastic announced on 2025-10-09 that it had completed the acquisition of Jina AI, a developer of open-source multilingual and multimodal embedding models, rerankers and small language models. Elastic said the models would be offered through the Elastic Inference Service on Elastic Cloud alongside its vector database and would continue to be published openly. The release did not disclose the price.

events.headline: Elastic signs agreement to acquire agent observability firm HoneyHive
events.summary: Elastic said in a blog post dated 19 November 2026, and in its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results released the same day, that it has entered into an agreement to acquire HoneyHive, an AI agent observability and evaluation company. Elastic plans to bring HoneyHive's tracing and evaluation features into Elastic Observability. The deal had not closed at the time of the announcement and no terms were disclosed.

events.headline: Elastic makes Jina embeddings v5 text and omni models available in Microsoft Foundry
events.summary: Elastic announced in a press release dated 18 November 2026 that its Jina embeddings v5 text and omni models are in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog, where customers can deploy them as dedicated endpoints in their own Azure environments. The release says the omni models cover image, audio and video in one vector space.

events.headline: Endor Labs raises US$93 million Series B led by DFJ Growth
events.summary: Endor Labs raised a US$93 million Series B led by DFJ Growth, with Salesforce Ventures, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Coatue, Dell Technologies Capital, Section 32 and Citi Ventures taking part. The company said it would use the money to extend its platform to reviewing and governing AI-generated code.

events.headline: Endor Labs acquires Autonomous Plane
events.summary: Endor Labs announced the acquisition of Autonomous Plane, a container and cloud-native application security company founded by the creator of DockerSlim, to combine dependency findings with container image analysis. Terms were not disclosed. The date is that of the published announcement.

events.headline: Endor Labs launches AURI with a free developer tier
events.summary: SecurityBrief UK reported on 2026-03-06 that Endor Labs had launched AURI, a security platform for teams using AI coding assistants and agents, with a free developer tier delivered through an MCP server, a command-line tool and editor integrations. The date is that of the report.

events.headline: Endor Labs integrates with OpenAI's Daybreak Defense Factory and Codex Security
events.summary: Endor Labs said in a blog post dated 12 November 2026 that OpenAI had announced an integration between Endor Labs and its Daybreak Defense Factory. According to the post, Endor Labs findings and reachability evidence are passed to Codex Security, which implements and tests fixes that Endor Labs then checks against customer policy before human review. The post says the integration is live.

events.headline: Ent emerges from stealth with a US$100 million seed round
events.summary: Ent announced a US$100 million seed round led by Decibel, with Sequoia, Crosspoint Capital Partners, Craft Ventures, Shield Capital, Felicis and In-Q-Tel, and said its endpoint platform was generally available on Windows, macOS, Linux and browsers.

events.headline: Ent adds AI tool visibility, endpoint data classification and application control
events.summary: Ent announced a view of AI tools and agents in use on endpoints with policy control over them, an on-device small language model that classifies sensitive data, and application control aimed at tools attackers commonly abuse.

events.headline: Ent appoints Kevin Arsenault as chief revenue officer
events.summary: Ent named Kevin Arsenault, previously a sales executive at CrowdStrike and Proofpoint, as its chief revenue officer.

events.headline: Ent joins Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program and lists on Microsoft Marketplace
events.summary: Ent said it had joined the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program, was available on Microsoft Marketplace, and had integrations with Microsoft Defender XDR, Sentinel, Purview, Entra ID, Intune and Security Copilot.

events.headline: Ent appoints Sam Hahm as Vice President of Global Channel Sales
events.summary: Ent announced in a press release dated 10 November 2026 that Sam Hahm had been appointed Vice President of Global Channel Sales to lead its partner and reseller expansion. The release says he previously held leadership roles at Oasis Security and Armorblox.

events.headline: Datacard Group completes purchase of Entrust, Inc. from Thoma Bravo
events.summary: Datacard Group, a privately held maker of card-issuance systems based near Minneapolis, completed its purchase of Dallas-based Entrust, Inc. from private-equity firm Thoma Bravo on 2013-12-31. Terms were not disclosed by the companies; Twin Cities Business cited a Bloomberg report of about $500 million. The combined business is the present-day Entrust. Recorded as an ownership change older than 24 months.

events.headline: Entrust announces the Cryptographic Security Platform
events.summary: Entrust announced a platform unifying management of keys, secrets and certificates with PKI, compliance management and HSM support, offered on-premises or as a managed service, with availability stated for May 2025.

events.headline: Entrust names Tony Ball to succeed Todd Wilkinson as CEO from 31 March 2026
events.summary: Entrust announced that Tony Ball, head of its payments and identity business, would become chief executive on 2026-03-31 on the planned retirement of Todd Wilkinson, chief executive since 2008. Whether the handover took place on that date was not verified.

events.headline: Entrust says nShield HSM post-quantum algorithms passed NIST algorithm validation
events.summary: Entrust announced that the ML-DSA, ML-KEM and SLH-DSA implementations in nShield HSM firmware 13.8.0 had been validated under NIST's Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program, and that the firmware had been submitted for FIPS 140-3 Level 3 module validation. Algorithm validation is not module validation.

events.headline: Sectigo reports completing migration of Entrust's public certificate business
events.summary: Sectigo, which acquired Entrust's public certificate business, announced that more than 500,000 certificates had been moved from Entrust Certificate Services to its own platform. Entrust is the seller in this transaction; the Cryptographic Security Platform is not part of it.

events.headline: Entrust offers the Cryptographic Security Platform as a cloud service
events.summary: SecurityBrief UK reported on 2026-03-11 that the platform had become available as a SaaS product alongside on-premises and hybrid deployment, covering PKI, certificate lifecycle management, key management and compliance management. The date recorded is the date of the report.

events.headline: Entrust and IBM Consulting announce joint quantum-safe services
events.summary: SecurityBrief UK reported on 2026-04-30 that IBM Consulting will deploy and operate the Cryptographic Security Platform as the control layer in quantum-safe transformation work covering discovery, policy enforcement, lifecycle management and migration planning. The date recorded is the date of the report.

events.headline: NIST lists new FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certificate #5329 for the nShield 5s HSM
events.summary: The NIST CMVP registry shows certificate #5329 for the Entrust nShield 5s Hardware Security Module, FIPS 140-3 overall Level 3, initially validated on 2026-06-15 and replacing certificate #4765. Its approved-algorithm list does not include ML-KEM, ML-DSA or SLH-DSA.

events.headline: Entrust adds CBOM import and export to the Cryptographic Security Platform
events.summary: Entrust announced CBOM import and export, Ansible-based certificate automation, expanded composite-algorithm support and SPIRE-based identities for non-human workloads, available as a service or on-premises.

events.headline: Entrust completes its acquisition of identity verification company Onfido
events.summary: FF News reported on 2024-04-09 that Entrust had completed its purchase of Onfido, a London-founded identity verification company established in 2012. Terms were not disclosed. Onfido was described as having more than 500 employees and over 1,200 customers before the deal. Its documentation now presents the product as Entrust Identity Verification.

events.headline: Exabeam and LogRhythm complete merger; combined company keeps the Exabeam name
events.summary: Exabeam and LogRhythm announced completion of their merger on 17 July 2024. The combined company kept the Exabeam name, with former LogRhythm chief executive Chris O'Malley as CEO and Broomfield, Colorado as its base. LogRhythm SIEM continues as the self-hosted product alongside the cloud-native New-Scale platform. The Register reported that Exabeam described the deal as a private transaction and would not disclose its value or structure. Thoma Bravo, which invested in LogRhythm in 2018, lists the merged Exabeam as a portfolio company.

events.headline: Exabeam appoints Pete Harteveld as CEO; Chris O'Malley retires
events.summary: Exabeam announced that chief revenue officer Pete Harteveld became chief executive, succeeding Chris O'Malley, who retired and stayed on through the fourth quarter of 2025 to support the transition. The release cited double-digit bookings growth over the prior two quarters.

events.headline: Exabeam extends Nova AI across New-Scale and adds AI features to LogRhythm SIEM
events.summary: Exabeam announced that its Nova AI agent now works across the New-Scale platform as a persistent investigator, with related-case grouping, an executive digest and a deeper integration for monitoring Claude Enterprise activity, plus a plugin for AI command-line tools. The self-hosted LogRhythm SIEM gained collectors for generative AI services and a community MCP server. The release gave no availability dates or pricing.

events.headline: Proposed settlement notified in stockholder class action over Exabeam and LogRhythm merger
events.summary: According to the settlement website for Mihovilovic v. Exabeam, Inc. (Delaware Court of Chancery, C.A. No. 2024-0976-PAF), a proposed US$7,000,000 cash settlement of a stockholder class action over Exabeam's 2024 merger with LogRhythm awaits a court hearing in December 2026. A claims-notice site, ClaimDepot, published a notice on 15 October 2026 describing the fund as US$20.5M including equity and saying the defendants deny wrongdoing. The date recorded is that of the ClaimDepot notice; the date the settlement was agreed was not sourced.

events.headline: Exaforce raises US$125 million Series B
events.summary: Exaforce announced a US$125 million Series B with HarbourVest, Peak XV, Mayfield, Khosla Ventures, Seligman Ventures and AICONIC, taking total funding to US$200 million a year after a US$75 million Series A.

events.headline: Exaforce announces US$75 million Series A
events.summary: Exaforce's newsroom records its announcement on 2025-04-17 of a US$75 million Series A; Help Net Security later described the round as raised a year before the 2026 Series B.

events.headline: Exaforce introduces ExaU for building custom security AI agents
events.summary: Exaforce said in a blog post dated 16 November 2026 that ExaU lets security teams create their own AI agents, which it calls Exabots, with defined roles, persistent memory, scheduled routines and permission boundaries. The post says actions that change data need the user's approval and that ExaU is included in the Exaforce platform and available now; it gives no pricing.

events.headline: Exaforce introduces Force ER emergency incident response service
events.summary: Exaforce said in a blog post dated 14 November 2026 that it is introducing Force ER, an emergency incident response service open to organisations that are not existing customers and that needs no retainer. The post says a responder answers within 15 minutes and that Exaforce's managed detection and response team then works the incident on the Exaforce platform; it gives no pricing.

events.headline: Extend announces $17 million in seed and Series A funding led by Innovation Endeavors
events.summary: SiliconANGLE and Fintech Finance News reported on 17 June 2025 that Extend had raised $17 million across a seed round and a Series A, led by Innovation Endeavors with Y Combinator, Homebrew and Character among the investors and angels including Scott Belsky and Guillermo Rauch. Fintech Finance News named Brex, Square, Checkr and Flatiron Health as customers.

events.headline: Bain Capital Private Equity and Crosspoint Capital Partners agree to acquire ExtraHop for US$900 million
events.summary: On 8 June 2021 ExtraHop said it had agreed to be acquired by Bain Capital Private Equity and Crosspoint Capital Partners in a transaction valued at US$900 million, expected to close that summer. The acquirers' release said the co-founders would stay in their roles and remain significant investors. GeekWire reported the company had raised US$61.6 million before the deal and would keep operating under its own brand. Later press reports describe the company as owned by the two firms.

events.headline: ExtraHop names Rob Greer chief executive; Greg Clark becomes executive chairman
events.summary: ExtraHop announced on 14 January 2025 that Rob Greer, previously general manager of Broadcom's Enterprise Security Group, had joined as chief executive, with Greg Clark moving to executive chairman. GeekWire reported that Greer was the third chief executive since February 2022 and that he is also an operating partner at Crosspoint Capital, one of the owners. In the same release the company said it took more than US$300 million of bookings in 2024.

events.headline: ExtraHop RevealX Federal receives FedRAMP authorisation at Moderate impact
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists ExtraHop RevealX Federal as FedRAMP Authorized at Moderate impact, with an agency authorisation dated 15 September 2025 and Schellman Compliance as assessor. The entry describes it as a SaaS offering hosted in AWS US-East regions. ExtraHop announced the authorisation on 7 October 2025.

events.headline: ExtraHop announces a 400 Gbps sensor for RevealX
events.summary: On 25 August 2026 ExtraHop announced a sensor for RevealX that it says analyses data-centre traffic at 400 Gbps at line rate, with general availability expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The throughput figure is the company's own; no independent measurement was found.

events.headline: F5 completes acquisition of AI security company CalypsoAI
events.summary: F5 announced on 2025-09-11 that it would acquire CalypsoAI, a privately held AI security company with major operations in Dublin, Ireland, for $180 million in purchase consideration. F5's fiscal 2025 annual report records the closing date as 2025-09-26 and cash consideration of $145.2 million, with CalypsoAI becoming a wholly owned subsidiary. The two figures are stated on different bases and the sources retrieved do not reconcile them. CalypsoAI is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: F5 introduces F5 AI Guardrails and F5 AI Red Team, built on CalypsoAI technology
events.summary: On 2025-09-29 F5 said it had completed the CalypsoAI acquisition and introduced two products based on it: F5 AI Guardrails for run-time protection of AI models and agents, and F5 AI Red Team for automated adversarial testing. F5's privacy statement gives the former product names as Inference Defend and Red Team.

events.headline: F5 discloses long-term nation-state intrusion and theft of BIG-IP source code
events.summary: Disclosed by F5 in a Form 8-K filed on 2025-10-15: F5 stated that on 2025-08-09 it learned a highly sophisticated nation-state threat actor had maintained long-term access to certain systems, including the BIG-IP product development environment and an engineering knowledge management platform, and had exfiltrated files containing portions of BIG-IP source code and information about undisclosed vulnerabilities. F5 stated it had no evidence of modification to its software supply chain or of access to CRM, financial, support case or iHealth systems, that some files held configuration or implementation information for a small percentage of customers, and that the U.S. Department of Justice had permitted a delay in disclosure. F5's fiscal 2026 annual report stated that governmental authorities had made inquiries and reported $28.0 million of related professional services and other expenses. The incident predates the close of the CalypsoAI acquisition and the filings do not mention AI Guardrails.

events.headline: F5 director Michael Montoya leaves board to become Chief Technology Operations Officer
events.summary: F5's Form 8-K of 2025-10-15 reported that Michael Montoya resigned from the board effective 2025-10-09 and was appointed Chief Technology Operations Officer effective 2025-10-13, reporting to the chief executive and leading enterprise-wide strategy and execution with a focus on security. The board was reduced from eleven to ten members.

events.headline: F5 acquires SurePath AI for network-based AI discovery and shadow AI detection
events.summary: F5 announced on 2026-06-22 that it had acquired SurePath AI, which provides network-based AI discovery, intent classification and shadow AI detection. Terms were not disclosed in the release. F5's fiscal 2026 annual report says the acquisition completed in June 2026 and is expected to be integrated into the F5 AI Security Platform.

events.headline: F5 launches AI Security Platform combining governance, discovery, testing and run-time protection
events.summary: On 2026-06-22 F5 introduced the F5 AI Security Platform, which groups AI governance, discovery, security testing (F5 AI Red Team), run-time protection (F5 AI Guardrails) and observability, deployable on premises, air-gapped, in private or public cloud, or hybrid. The release gave no general availability dates.

events.headline: F5 reports fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 restructuring plan with workforce-reduction charges
events.summary: F5 disclosed in its Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2026-09-30 a restructuring plan in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 with $7.4 million in workforce-reduction charges, following plans in the first and fourth quarters of fiscal 2025 with charges of $11.3 million and $14.3 million. The number of employees affected was not stated in the text retrieved. The date shown is the fiscal year end, not the date of the reductions.

events.headline: Securities class action filed against F5 after its October 2025 breach disclosure
events.summary: According to the complaint, Smith v. F5, Inc. (2:25-cv-02619) was filed in the Western District of Washington on 19 December 2025 as a putative securities class action alleging misleading statements about F5's security while the intrusion disclosed in October 2025 was under way. A shareholder derivative complaint, Kelly v. Locoh-Donou (2:26-cv-00435), followed on 5 February 2026 with F5 as nominal defendant. The federal docket index showed neither case terminated on 2026-11-20. The allegations are unproven.

events.headline: Fable Security leaves stealth with US$31 million from Greylock Partners and Redpoint Ventures
events.summary: Fable Security announced its public launch on 28 July 2025 with US$31 million in funding: a seed round of about US$6.5 million led by Greylock Partners, in whose venture studio the company was started, and a Series A of about US$24.5 million led by Redpoint Ventures. SecurityWeek, BetaNews and Tech Funding News reported the launch. Form D notices filed on 25 November 2025 give 10 April 2024 and 30 May 2025 as the dates of first sale of the two offerings.

events.headline: Fable Security releases a human risk reporting dashboard for security leaders and service providers
events.summary: MSSP Alert reported on 22 October 2025 that Fable Security had that week released a reporting dashboard giving a single risk score for the organisation, with the behavioural factors behind it at organisation, department and individual level, and a view across customers for managed-service providers.

events.headline: Fable Security launches Briefing Agent to turn threat reports and policies into employee briefings
events.summary: Enterprise Security Tech reported on 17 September 2026 that Fable Security had launched Briefing Agent, an AI tool that drafts targeted security briefings from emerging threats and company policies. An administrator must approve the script, audience and delivery channel before a briefing is sent, and the tool keeps source material, prompts and revision history. It was made available to existing customers within their subscriptions.

events.headline: Fable Security makes AI voice-phishing simulations generally available
events.summary: Fable Security announced on 29 October 2026 the general availability of voice-phishing simulations: AI voice calls to employees and shared lines using pretexts such as password and MFA resets, vendor payment changes and executive impersonation, with coaching after the call and results fed into each person's risk profile. The pricing page lists it as an add-on sold separately.

events.headline: Fastly completes acquisition of Signal Sciences, maker of the product now sold as Fastly Next-Gen WAF
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K that on 1 October 2020 it completed the acquisition of Signal Sciences Corp. under an agreement dated 26 August 2020, with Signal Sciences becoming a wholly owned subsidiary. The filing says Signal Sciences' shares, options and warrants were exchanged for 6,367,709 shares of Fastly Class A common stock, among other consideration. Fastly's product documentation says the Fastly Next-Gen WAF is the new name for the Signal Sciences Cloud WAF and Signal Sciences Next-Gen WAF and still runs on Signal Sciences technology. Recorded because it changed the ownership of the product.

events.headline: Fastly chief executive Todd Nightingale resigns; Kip Compton appointed
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K that Todd Nightingale resigned as chief executive officer, president and director with effect from 16 June 2025 to pursue another opportunity, and that the resignation was not due to any disagreement with the company. Charles (Kip) Compton, chief product officer since January 2024, was appointed chief executive officer and a director from the same date.

events.headline: Fastly appoints Richard Wong as chief financial officer and Scott Lovett as president, go to market
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K dated 6 August 2025 that Richard Wong would become chief financial officer on 11 August 2025, replacing Ronald Kisling, who stayed as an adviser until 15 September 2025, and that Scott Lovett, chief revenue officer since August 2024, became president, go to market. The filing says Mr Kisling's departure was not due to any disagreement with the company.

events.headline: Fastly issues US$180 million of 0% convertible senior notes due 2030 and retires 2026 notes
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K that on 9 December 2025 it issued US$160 million of 0% convertible senior notes due 15 December 2030, with an option for the initial purchasers to take a further US$20 million. Its annual report for 2025 gives the total issued as US$180 million and says that on the same date it repurchased US$150 million of its 2026 notes for US$148.9 million in cash. The quarterly report for September 2026 says the remaining US$38.6 million of 2026 notes was repaid in 2026.

events.headline: Court lets part of the securities class action against Fastly proceed
events.summary: Reported by Fastly in its Form 10-Q filed on 4 November 2026: a putative securities class action filed on 24 May 2024 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (case 4:24-cv-03170) names the company and certain officers, alleges violations of sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act on behalf of purchasers of Fastly securities between 15 November 2023 and 7 August 2024, and seeks unspecified damages. On 10 August 2026 the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss the second amended complaint, and the defendants filed an answer on 27 October 2026. The filing says six related stockholder derivative complaints have been filed and are stayed or subject to negotiated stays. No outcome has been decided.

events.headline: Fastly increases its revolving credit facility from US$60 million to US$100 million
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K that on 17 August 2026 it amended its credit agreement with Silicon Valley Bank, a division of First-Citizens Bank, raising the senior secured revolving facility from US$60 million to US$100 million, extending its scheduled maturity to 17 August 2029 subject to conditions tied to the 2028 convertible notes, and lowering the interest margin by 0.25%. The quarterly report for September 2026 says nothing was drawn on the facility.

events.headline: Fastly's president, go to market, Scott Lovett to retire in 2027
events.summary: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K filed on 4 November 2026 that Scott Lovett notified the company on 30 October 2026 of his planned retirement as president, go to market, on a date to be set during 2027. He stays in the role while a new chief revenue officer is recruited and will then act as a senior adviser until at least 30 June 2027.

events.headline: Visa announces agreement to acquire Featurespace
events.summary: Visa announced a definitive agreement to acquire Featurespace. BankInfoSecurity reported on 2024-09-26 that terms were not disclosed, that investor IP Group expected US$149.8 million for its stake, and that Featurespace had 419 employees and more than 80 direct customers including HSBC and NatWest.

events.headline: Visa completes acquisition of Featurespace
events.summary: Visa announced completion of the acquisition and said Featurespace would become part of its Risk and Identity Solutions business unit, with the Featurespace product portfolio integrated into Visa's fraud prevention offerings over the following months. Companies House records Visa Inc. as a person with significant control of Featurespace Limited from 2024-12-19.

events.headline: Featurespace's Scam Detect becomes part of Visa A2A Protect
events.summary: A Featurespace article dated 2026-02-03 introduced Visa A2A Protect, a risk-scoring product for account-to-account payments that combines Featurespace's Scam Detect with Visa network-level intelligence. The date is that shown on the article, which may not be the launch date.

events.headline: Feedzai announces about US$75M round at US$2B valuation and ECB digital euro selection
events.summary: Feedzai announced a new investment round of about US$75 million at a stated US$2 billion valuation, naming Lince Capital, Iberis Capital and Explorer Investments as new investors and Oxy Capital and Buenavista Equity Partners as returning ones. In the same release it said the European Central Bank had selected it, with PwC as subcontractor, under a framework agreement for digital euro fraud and risk management with an estimated value of EUR 79.1 million and a maximum of EUR 237.3 million.

events.headline: Feedzai acquires Demyst and its Zonic data orchestration platform
events.summary: Feedzai announced the acquisition of Demyst, including its Zonic data workflow orchestration platform and data-integration capabilities. Terms were not disclosed. Demyst's chief executive and key staff were to join Feedzai.

events.headline: Feedzai makes Feedzai IQ Score available, including on AWS Marketplace
events.summary: Feedzai announced availability of Feedzai IQ Score, a fraud risk score delivered by API and derived from signals across its customer network using what it describes as federated learning that shares aggregated, anonymised risk signals rather than raw customer data. The release says the score is available on AWS Marketplace.

events.headline: Feedzai launches Farol, an AI agent embedded in RiskOps Studio
events.summary: Feedzai announced Farol, an AI agent inside RiskOps Studio that summarises alerts, analyses rule performance, answers product questions and helps draft suspicious activity reports. The release does not name the underlying model providers.

events.headline: Feedzai appoints Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer
events.summary: Feedzai's press-release index lists a release dated 2026-11-10 announcing Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer; the leadership page shows him in that role.

events.headline: Feedzai expands Digital Trust to detect AI agents accessing bank accounts
events.summary: Feedzai announced in a press release dated 12 November 2026 that it has expanded its Digital Trust solution so banks can detect AI agents signing in to customer accounts. The release describes persistent device fingerprinting, a risk score drawing on shared intelligence, and cryptographic device binding that can also serve as a possession factor in place of SMS one-time passcodes. It states no availability date or pricing, and the performance figures in it are Feedzai's own.

events.headline: FICO eliminates about 15% of positions in fiscal fourth quarter
events.summary: According to FICO's Form 10-K filed on 2026-11-06, the company incurred US$27.3 million in employee separation costs in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 from eliminating approximately 15% of positions across the company. The filing gives the quarter, not a date; the quarter ended on 2026-09-30. A year earlier it eliminated 226 positions.

events.headline: FICO agrees term sheet to settle FICO Score antitrust class actions for US$65M
events.summary: According to FICO's Form 10-K filed on 2026-11-06, FICO and the plaintiffs in consolidated putative class actions in the Northern District of Illinois, which allege antitrust claims over the distribution of FICO Scores, entered into a term sheet on 2026-09-29 for a proposed settlement: a US$65.0 million cash payment and compliance undertakings, with no admission of wrongdoing. The settlement needs court approval. The matter concerns the Scores business, not Falcon Fraud Manager.

events.headline: Fiddler AI raises US$30M Series C led by RPS Ventures
events.summary: Fiddler AI announced a US$30 million Series C led by RPS Ventures, with existing investors Lightspeed Venture Partners, Lux Capital, Insight Partners, Capgemini Ventures, Dallas VC, Dentsu Ventures and Mozilla Ventures and new investors LG Technology Ventures, Benhamou Global Ventures and LDV Partners. The company said the round brought total funding to US$100 million.

events.headline: CrowdStrike signs definitive agreement to acquire Fiddler AI; deal not yet closed
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced on 2026-11-03 that it had signed a definitive agreement to acquire Fiddler AI. CrowdStrike said Fiddler will be sold as part of its Falcon platform under the name Falcon Observe, that the price is to be paid predominantly in cash with a portion in stock subject to vesting, and that closing is expected in its fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 subject to customary conditions. Financial terms were not disclosed. No completion announcement was found as of 2026-11-20, so Fiddler is recorded as still independent. CrowdStrike is not yet a tracked vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Fiddler AI introduces Agent Registry, an inventory of AI agents in its control plane
events.summary: Fiddler AI said in a blog post dated 10 November 2026 that it is introducing Agent Registry, a central inventory in the Fiddler AI Control Plane that lists each agent with its model, tools and deployment context alongside alerts and token usage. The post does not say whether the feature is generally available or in preview.

events.headline: Fiddler AI and AMD describe joint approach to running monitored AI agents on AMD hardware
events.summary: A post on Fiddler AI's blog dated 16 November 2026, which says it first appeared on AMD's blog, describes a technical collaboration in which AMD supplies accelerated computing and open software and Fiddler supplies evaluation, observability and guardrails for agents running on it. The post mentions no investment or commercial terms.

events.headline: Fireworks AI raises US$250M Series C at US$4B valuation
events.summary: Fireworks AI announced a US$250M Series C, including primary and secondary funding, led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Index Ventures and Evantic at a US$4B valuation, bringing stated total funding to US$327M.

events.headline: Fireworks AI raises US$1.505B Series D at US$17.5B valuation
events.summary: Fireworks AI announced a US$1.505B Series D led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV with NVIDIA and others participating, and said its annualised revenue run rate had passed US$1B. SiliconANGLE reported the round the same day.

events.headline: Two civil suits filed against Fireworks AI in the Northern District of California
events.summary: According to the CourtListener federal docket index, searched on 2026-11-20, Komorski v. Fireworks AI, Inc. (3:26-cv-13987) was filed on 17 November 2026 and Brethelette v. Fireworks.AI, Inc. (3:26-cv-14080) on 18 November 2026, both in the Northern District of California. The complaints were not retrieved, so what the suits allege is not established.

events.headline: Fireworks AI discloses unauthorised access to customer secrets, models and datasets
events.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed in security bulletins from 2026-10-10 that between 3 August and 7 October 2026 an intruder used stolen credentials and a vulnerability in one of its services to reach secrets, model files and datasets belonging to a small number of customers. The company said that investigation was complete. The event is dated to the first bulletin.

events.headline: Fireworks AI discloses a second intrusion that reached account and billing information
events.summary: Fireworks AI disclosed in bulletins of 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17 a second, separate incident between 23 and 30 October 2026. It said an intruder entered through development machines at a third-party cloud provider that had itself been breached and reached part of production, accessing account and billing information for all accounts created before 30 October and datasets, models or secrets for a small number of customers. It said it does not store card numbers and that the investigation was still open. UiPath, which uses Fireworks AI as a sub-processor, said on its trust centre that it found no indication its customers' data was affected and rotated keys as a precaution.

events.headline: Audax Private Equity takes a majority stake in Flashpoint
events.summary: Flashpoint announced on 21 July 2021 that Audax Private Equity had made a majority growth investment in the company; Help Net Security reported the deal two days later. Terms were not disclosed. The company said many of its earlier venture investors rolled part of their proceeds into the business and that it would use the capital for product development and acquisitions. Flashpoint continues to trade under its own name. Audax is not a vendor tracked in this dataset.

events.headline: David Lemon joins Flashpoint as president
events.summary: Flashpoint said on 7 January 2025 that David Lemon, previously chief revenue officer at Archer Integrated Risk Management, had joined as president. Co-founder Josh Lefkowitz remains chief executive.

events.headline: Flashpoint adds analyst posts, entity profiles and natural-language image search to Ignite
events.summary: Help Net Security reported on 28 April 2025 that Flashpoint had added four features to Ignite: short analyst-validated posts called Sparks, structured profiles for IP addresses, domains and card BINs, image search by plain-language description, and a form for customers to request collection from Telegram channels.

events.headline: Flashpoint makes its MCP server generally available
events.summary: Flashpoint said on 25 June 2026 that its MCP server was generally available. It lets AI assistants that support the Model Context Protocol query Flashpoint data, including finished reports, technical indicators, ransomware activity and compromised credentials, under the customer's existing entitlements. The first release is read-only and connects by OAuth or an API token.

events.headline: Flashpoint announces an agentic AI offering for Ignite, due in early 2027
events.summary: Flashpoint announced on 10 November 2026 an offering called Flashpoint Agentic AI: a hub in Ignite combining chat-driven investigations with agents for intelligence briefings, alert set-up, alert triage and drafting intelligence requirements. The company said it would be available in early 2027 as a separate offering from the AI features already included with product licences.

events.headline: Francisco Partners completes acquisition of Forcepoint from Raytheon Technologies
events.summary: Francisco Partners completed its purchase of Forcepoint from Raytheon Technologies on 11 January 2021, having agreed the deal in October 2020. Manny Rivelo was appointed chief executive on closing. No price was given in the release or by SecurityWeek.

events.headline: TPG completes purchase of Forcepoint's government business
events.summary: TPG completed its acquisition of Forcepoint's Global Governments and Critical Infrastructure business on 2 October 2023, making it a separate company. Forcepoint's release said Francisco Partners kept a minority stake in that business and continued to own Forcepoint's commercial business. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Forcepoint completes acquisition of Getvisibility
events.summary: Forcepoint announced on 7 April 2025 that it had completed the acquisition of Getvisibility, a provider of AI-based data security posture management and data detection and response, after a partnership of more than two years. The price was not disclosed. Getvisibility's co-founders joined Forcepoint.

events.headline: Forcepoint launches Data Security Cloud
events.summary: Forcepoint launched Data Security Cloud on 29 April 2025, a cloud-delivered platform combining DSPM, DDR, enterprise DLP, SaaS, web and email security, using its AI Mesh classification.

events.headline: Forcepoint appoints Matt Derdeyn chief financial officer
events.summary: Forcepoint's company page records that Matt Derdeyn was appointed chief financial officer on 2 June 2025.

events.headline: Forcepoint extends DSPM to databases and data lakes
events.summary: Forcepoint announced on 7 October 2025 that its DSPM and AI Mesh classification now cover structured data in Microsoft SQL, Oracle, MySQL, Databricks and Snowflake as well as files. General availability dates were not stated.

events.headline: Forcepoint announces ARIA assistant and new endpoint agent
events.summary: Forcepoint announced on 4 March 2026 an assistant called ARIA, embedded in Data Security Cloud, that drafts policies from natural-language requests, and a new endpoint agent that inspects data on devices without a proxy. Availability dates and the underlying model were not stated.

events.headline: Forcepoint launches AI Data Security platform
events.summary: Forcepoint launched AI Data Security on 22 July 2026, adding governance of AI agents, an AI agent gateway, real-time prompt and response controls and AI detection and response to its data security products. It said the platform was available through partners, with the gateway, detection and shadow-AI controls rolling out over the following quarter.

events.headline: Forcepoint and BeyondTrust integrate DSPM with identity risk insights
events.summary: Forcepoint announced on 8 October 2026 an integration between Forcepoint DSPM and BeyondTrust Identity Security Insights, so that teams can see which sensitive data a risky identity can reach and revoke that identity's access.

events.headline: Fortanix DSM Appliance validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3
events.summary: The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program registry lists the Fortanix DSM Appliance under certificate #5555, validated to FIPS 140-3 overall Level 3 on 2026-10-19 with a sunset date of 2031-10-18. The approved algorithms include the LMS hash-based signature scheme but not ML-KEM or ML-DSA.

events.headline: Fortanix adds multi-sourced quantum entropy to Data Security Manager
events.summary: Fortanix announced that Data Security Manager can draw key-generation randomness from external quantum random number generators supplied by Qrypt and Quantum Dice, in addition to its internal entropy sources.

events.headline: Fortanix promotes Patrick Conte to chief revenue officer
events.summary: Fortanix announced that Patrick Conte, previously head of Americas sales and channels, became chief revenue officer, and that Ron Longo stepped down from that role and remained as an adviser.

events.headline: Rafay and Fortanix announce joint confidential AI as a service offering
events.summary: Rafay Systems and Fortanix announced that the Rafay platform orchestrates workloads on CNCF Confidential Containers using Fortanix Confidential AI. In the joint design Data Security Manager releases encryption keys only to environments attested by Fortanix Confidential Computing Manager.

events.headline: Fortinet completes acquisition of cloud security firm Lacework
events.summary: Fortinet announced on 2 August 2024 that it had completed its acquisition of Lacework, a cloud-native application protection platform company, effective 1 August 2024. The price was not disclosed in the release. The Lacework platform is now sold as FortiCNAPP. Recorded because it changed the product's ownership.

events.headline: Securities class action filed against Fortinet over FortiGate refresh-cycle statements
events.summary: Disclosed in Fortinet's Form 10-Q filed 2026-10-30, whose litigation data labels name Oklahoma Firefighters Pension and Retirement System v. Fortinet Inc. et al. Plaintiff counsel's case page says the complaint was filed on 22 September 2025 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (case 25-cv-08037), covers purchases from 8 November 2024 to 6 August 2025, and alleges misleading statements about the 2025-2026 FortiGate refresh cycle; a consolidated complaint is dated 24 April 2026. The allegations are untested and no ruling was found. The text of Fortinet's own litigation note could not be read.

events.headline: Fortinet discloses exploited FortiCloud SSO authentication bypass, CVE-2026-24858
events.summary: Disclosed by Fortinet on 2026-01-27 in advisory FG-IR-26-060: a critical authentication bypass in FortiCloud single sign-on let an attacker with a FortiCloud account log in to devices registered to other accounts where that sign-on was enabled, and was exploited in the wild by two malicious FortiCloud accounts, which Fortinet locked on 22 January. Fortinet disabled FortiCloud SSO on 26 January and restored it the next day with vulnerable versions blocked. Affected products are FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiProxy, FortiSwitchManager, FortiWeb and FortiNAC-F; FortiSASE is not listed and the advisory says FortiGate Cloud, FortiManager Cloud and FortiAnalyzer Cloud were not affected. CSO Online reported on 2026-01-28 that customers had seen administrator accounts created on fully patched devices and that the US cybersecurity agency added the flaw to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue.

events.headline: Fortinet discloses two critical routing-daemon flaws affecting FortiOS and FortiSASE
events.summary: According to Fortinet PSIRT advisories FG-IR-26-267 and FG-IR-26-268, published on 10 November 2026, FortiOS and FortiSASE are affected by CVE-2026-126253, an authentication bypass in the OSPF daemon rated CVSS 9.3, and CVE-2026-126254, a numeric truncation error in the BGP daemon rated CVSS 9.6 that an authenticated iBGP neighbour could use to cause denial of service. The advisories say FortiSASE 26.3.1 was remediated in 26.3.2 with no customer action, list FortiSASE 25.1 to 26.2 as needing migration to a fixed release, and mark both flaws as not known to be exploited.

events.headline: Futurex opens Middle East office and data centres in Dubai and Abu Dhabi
events.summary: Futurex announced a Middle East regional office and two data centres in the United Arab Emirates, in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, for its cloud HSM and key-management services. The colocation operators were not named.

events.headline: Futurex adds Melbourne data centre, its sixteenth site
events.summary: Futurex announced a Melbourne data centre alongside its existing Sydney site, bringing its cloud HSM footprint to 16 sites, and said the services there are built on the CryptoHub platform. The operator was not named.

events.headline: Futurex says German Banking Industry Committee approved its HSMs and cloud service for girocard
events.summary: Futurex announced that the German Banking Industry Committee confirmed that its Excrypt HSMs, and its VirtuCrypt cloud payment HSM service including European data centres, meet the committee's security requirements for the girocard scheme, following independent evaluation. The approval was not checked against a registry.

events.headline: CryptoHub receives Veeam Ready Security qualification for key management
events.summary: Futurex announced that CryptoHub was qualified under Veeam's key management system compatibility category for Veeam Backup & Replication, integrating through KMIP.

events.headline: Cisco completes acquisition of Galileo; product becomes Splunk Agent Observability
events.summary: Cisco announced on 2026-04-09 its intent to acquire Galileo Technologies, Inc., an AI evaluation and observability company, and added an update dated 2026-05-22 stating that the acquisition had been completed. Terms were not disclosed. Galileo's product is now sold as Splunk Agent Observability within Cisco's Splunk Observability portfolio, and the galileo.ai website redirects to splunk.com.

events.headline: Salesforce and ServiceNow commit US$1.5B to Genesys
events.summary: Genesys announced US$1.5B in investment commitments from Salesforce and ServiceNow in equal amounts. Proceeds were to be used to repurchase shares from existing holders, with Hellman & Friedman and Permira remaining majority owners. Closing was expected by the end of Genesys's fiscal year 2026; completion was not verified in this session.

events.headline: Class action alleges Genesys recorded domestic violence hotline conversations without consent
events.summary: Reported by CX Today on 2025-04-15: a proposed class action in the US District Court for the Northern District of California alleged that Genesys recorded and analysed calls, texts and chats to the National Domestic Violence Hotline without consent, citing federal wiretap law and the California Invasion of Privacy Act. Customer Experience Magazine reported on 2026-07-22 that Genesys agreed to pay US$2.5M to settle, without admitting wrongdoing, subject to court approval. A settlement notice site gives the case as A.B. v. Genesys Cloud Services, Inc., 3:25-cv-03276-EMC, with preliminary approval on 2026-10-16 and a final hearing on 2027-03-04.

events.headline: Genesys discloses unauthorised access to internal learning and CRM systems
events.summary: Genesys disclosed that on 2026-10-16 it became aware that an unauthorised third party had accessed internal business systems, including a learning management system and a customer relationship management platform, and that business contact and account information was accessed or downloaded. Genesys stated that the Genesys Cloud and Genesys Engage platforms and the customer data in them were not affected, and said on 2026-10-23 that the incident was contained with review continuing. Reported by SecurityWeek on 2026-10-26: a group calling itself ScarlettGroup claimed the attack.

events.headline: Genesys launches Standalone AI Agents and Genesys Arena
events.summary: Genesys announced Standalone AI Agents, which let an organisation deploy the Genesys Cloud Agentic Virtual Agent without moving its contact centre to Genesys Cloud, together with Genesys Arena, a set of prebuilt agent kits, and an effort-based pricing model.

events.headline: GetReal Labs trades as GetReal Security
events.summary: The company launched from stealth in June 2024 as GetReal Labs. Its press releases of 2025-03-26 use the name GetReal Security, and a September 2025 release describes it as formerly GetReal Labs. The exact date of the change was not found; 2025-03-26 is the earliest dated use of the new name read.

events.headline: GetReal Security raises US$17.5M Series A led by Forgepoint Capital
events.summary: GetReal Security announced a US$17.5M Series A led by Forgepoint Capital, with Ballistic Ventures, Evolution Equity and K2 Access Fund and strategic investors In-Q-Tel, Cisco Investments and Capital One Ventures. Reported by TechCrunch and SecurityWeek.

events.headline: GetReal Security launches its forensic analysis platform
events.summary: The company launched a cloud platform with a web interface, an API and integrations, bringing together GetReal Inspect for files, GetReal Protect for real-time audio and video streams, and the Prepare and Respond services. TechCrunch reported the launch alongside the funding round.

events.headline: Doppel and GetReal Security announce partnership on deepfakes targeting brands and executives
events.summary: Doppel and GetReal Security announced a partnership combining Doppel's monitoring for online impersonation with GetReal's analysis of whether images, audio and video are authentic.

events.headline: GetReal Protect extends real-time deepfake detection to Microsoft Teams and Cisco Webex
events.summary: GetReal Security announced real-time deepfake protection in GetReal Protect for Microsoft Teams and Cisco Webex meetings, with Zoom to follow, together with SIEM and SOAR integrations and a graph of affected identities and meetings. Reported by Biometric Update.

events.headline: GetReal Protect adds continuous identity verification, generally available
events.summary: GetReal Security announced general availability of continuous identity verification in GetReal Protect, which checks consenting, enrolled participants' face and voice throughout a meeting, alongside deepfake and impersonation detection for Microsoft Teams, Cisco Webex, Zoom and voice systems.

events.headline: GetReal Protect for Microsoft Teams listed in Microsoft Marketplace
events.summary: GetReal Security said on 2026-11-19 that its Microsoft Teams integration is available in Microsoft Marketplace and that it is taking part in Microsoft's programme for certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection in Teams, with certification in progress.

events.headline: GitGuardian raises US$50M Series C led by Insight Partners
events.summary: SecurityWeek and SiliconANGLE (2026-02-11) and BankInfoSecurity (2026-02-17) reported a US$50 million Series C led by Insight Partners with Quadrille Capital and existing investors Balderton, BPI, Eurazeo, Fly Ventures and Sapphire Ventures, bringing total funding to US$106 million. The vendor said the money would go to AI agent security and management of non-human identities, and to hiring in the US and Europe.

events.headline: Researcher discloses that a ggshield option turned off TLS certificate verification entirely
events.summary: An independent researcher reported on the oss-security mailing list on 2025-11-17 that the --allow-self-signed option of ggshield, GitGuardian's command-line scanner, disabled all TLS certificate verification in versions up to 1.43.0, which could expose scanned content and API credentials to interception; no CVE was assigned and no exploitation was reported. The post says the vendor at first called the behaviour intentional. GitGuardian's release notes for ggshield 1.44.1 stated that the old option name was misleading, added an explicit --insecure option with warnings, and deprecated the old name. The two sources give different dates for that release.

events.headline: GitGuardian patches self-hosted Embedded Cluster installs against nginx HTTP/2 flaws
events.summary: GitGuardian announced in a customer notice dated 2026-11-19 that Embedded Cluster installations of its self-hosted edition on releases 2025.1.0 to 2026.11.0 were exposed to two nginx HTTP/2 vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, reachable on port 443, and that release 2026.11.1 turns HTTP/2 off in the bundled ingress. Helm and KOTS installations on an existing cluster and the hosted service were not listed as affected. The notice does not say whether the flaws were exploited.

events.headline: Microsoft completes acquisition of GitHub for US$7.5 billion in stock
events.summary: Microsoft's annual report for fiscal 2019 states that it acquired GitHub, Inc. on 2018-10-25 in a US$7.5 billion stock transaction, including US$1.3 billion of cash payments for vested GitHub equity awards and an indemnity escrow, and that GitHub is reported in its Intelligent Cloud segment.

events.headline: GitHub Advanced Security split into GitHub Secret Protection and GitHub Code Security
events.summary: GitHub announced on 2025-03-04 that from 2025-04-01 GitHub Advanced Security would be sold as two standalone products, GitHub Secret Protection at US$19 and GitHub Code Security at US$30 per active committer per month, and that both would be available to GitHub Team customers for the first time.

events.headline: GitHub chief executive Thomas Dohmke announces departure; GitHub continues within Microsoft CoreAI
events.summary: GitHub's chief executive Thomas Dohmke announced on 2025-08-11 that he would leave by the end of 2025 and that GitHub and its leadership team would continue as part of Microsoft's CoreAI organisation. ITPro reported on 2026-01-09 that GitHub's leadership team now reports into CoreAI, led by Jay Parikh.

events.headline: GitHub discloses theft of about 3,800 internal repositories via poisoned VS Code extension
events.summary: GitHub disclosed on 2026-05-20 that it had detected on 2026-05-18 the compromise of an employee device through a poisoned third-party VS Code extension, and that an attacker's claim to have taken about 3,800 GitHub-internal repositories was directionally consistent with its investigation. GitHub stated it had no evidence of impact on customer information outside those repositories, some of which hold customer information such as support excerpts, and that it rotated secrets including the Enterprise Server signing key. Reported also by SecurityWeek on 2026-05-20 and BleepingComputer on 2026-05-21. GitHub's update of 2026-05-26 said the investigation was continuing.

events.headline: GitHub Copilot moves from premium requests to token-metered AI Credits
events.summary: GitHub announced on 2026-04-27 that from 2026-06-01 Copilot premium request units would be replaced by GitHub AI Credits consumed by token usage at each model's published rate, with pooled credits and budget controls for organisations. Seat prices were unchanged at US$19 for Copilot Business and US$39 for Copilot Enterprise; code completions stay unmetered.

events.headline: Ninth Circuit affirms dismissal of DMCA claim against GitHub, Microsoft and OpenAI over Copilot
events.summary: Reported by The Next Web on 2026-09-18 and PPC Land on 2026-09-20: in Doe v. GitHub (No. 24-7700) a Ninth Circuit panel on 2026-09-16 affirmed dismissal of the programmers' Digital Millennium Copyright Act claim that GitHub Copilot and OpenAI's Codex model removed copyright management information, holding that the tools generate new output. Both outlets reported that two breach-of-contract claims remain pending in the Northern District of California.

events.headline: GitHub puts on-demand secret scanning in Copilot's security review into public preview
events.summary: GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says Copilot's security review now runs GitHub's secret scanning detectors on code changes before merge, in public preview, across Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, Copilot SDK integrations and Copilot code review. The entry says the feature is off by default, is not yet in VS Code, and that scans consume AI credits under the Secret Protection AI Credit SKU.

events.headline: GitHub Copilot app adds GA support for GitHub Enterprise Server; browser use enters preview
events.summary: GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says the GitHub Copilot app's support for GitHub Enterprise Server accounts is now generally available, and that Azure DevOps repository support and browser use, in which Copilot operates a Chromium-based browser in an isolated tab group, are in public preview. The entry says browser use is off by default and states no plan or pricing changes.

events.headline: GitHub reports roughly six-hour degradation of pull requests, Actions and Git operations
events.summary: According to GitHub's status page, an incident on 16 November 2026 degraded pull requests, GitHub Actions and Git push and fetch latency, with impact from about 09:30 to 15:55 UTC. GitHub's post-incident summary attributes it to storage servers holding Git repository data reaching disk read bandwidth limits during a planned repository migration, made worse by a disk configuration setting, and says the same cause produced a shorter event on 13 November.

events.headline: Glean raises US$150 million Series F at a US$7.2 billion valuation
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2025-06-10 that Glean raised a US$150 million Series F led by Wellington Management at a US$7.2 billion valuation, with new investors including Khosla Ventures, Bicycle Capital, Geodesic Capital and Archerman Capital and existing investors including Sequoia Capital, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed, General Catalyst, ICONIQ, Capital One Ventures and Citi. The report said Glean had raised US$610 million since early 2024.

events.headline: Glean adds voice, canvas, more than 100 actions and an agent sandbox to Glean Assistant
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-02-17 that Glean added real-time voice, branded document and image creation, a canvas for working with the assistant, more than 100 actions across applications such as Salesforce, Jira and GitHub, and a sandbox for agents.

events.headline: Glean announces Glean Intelligence, AI usage controls, AI Gateway and independent agents
events.summary: Glean's announcement post, last updated 2026-08-26, lists Glean Intelligence (model choice across more than 40 models) and AI usage controls as generally available, AI Gateway, auto routing and independent agents as beta, and the Tau desktop app and context-aware threat detection in Glean Protect as coming soon. The post advises basing purchase decisions on generally available features.

events.headline: Trademark suit filed against Glean Technologies in the Northern District of California
events.summary: According to the CourtListener federal docket index, searched on 2026-11-20, Glean IP Holdings Inc. v. Glean Technologies, Inc. (3:25-cv-08536) was filed in the Northern District of California on 6 October 2025 as a trademark infringement action, and no termination date is shown. The claims were not retrieved.

events.headline: Glia announces contractual guarantee against AI hallucinations
events.summary: Glia announced a contractual guarantee to its bank and credit union customers against hallucinated answers and prompt-injection attacks in its customer-facing AI, which it attributes to an approvals framework that does not generate answers freely.

events.headline: Glia launches Glia Banker and Glia CoPilot
events.summary: destinationCRM reported on 2026-03-30 that Glia had introduced Glia CoPilot, a knowledge assistant for staff, and Glia Banker, the next generation of Glia Virtual Assistant for automating customer and member interactions.

events.headline: Glow appoints Patti Degnan as chief information security officer
events.summary: SecurityInfoWatch reported on 2026-08-31, from a company announcement, that Glow had named Patti Degnan, formerly chief information security officer of Notion, as its chief information security officer, leading security, IT, privacy and customer trust.

events.headline: Glow leaves stealth with US$180M Series A at a US$1.2B valuation
events.summary: TechCrunch and SecurityWeek reported on 2026-07-22 that Glow, an endpoint security company founded in 2025, had left stealth with a US$180 million Series A at a US$1.2 billion valuation, led by Sequoia Capital, Cyberstarts, Greenoaks and Redpoint Ventures, with Index Ventures, Swish Ventures, Lux Capital, Holly Ventures and Operator Collective. The company said it already had paying customers in financial services, healthcare and retail.

events.headline: Google Cloud APIs disrupted worldwide by a Service Control policy fault

quote.text: We deeply apologize for the impact this outage has had.

events.summary: Google stated in its incident report that from 10:51 to 18:18 US/Pacific on 12 June 2025 many Google Cloud products were disrupted across regions. Google attributed it to a quota-policy change containing blank fields that crashed its Service Control API management binary through a code path, added on 29 May 2025, that had not been exercised during rollout; Google said recovery began within about 40 minutes but took up to about 2 hours 40 minutes in us-central1 because restarting tasks overloaded the underlying infrastructure. The Vertex Gemini API, Agent Platform Online Inference and Agent Search are listed among the affected products. Google said it froze changes to the system and would make it fail open.

events.headline: Google discloses intrusion into a corporate Salesforce instance
events.summary: Reported by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer on 2025-08-06: Google disclosed on 5 August 2025, in an update to a threat-intelligence post, that one of its corporate Salesforce instances was accessed in June 2025 by a group it tracks as UNC6040, which uses voice phishing. Google said the data taken was contact information and related notes for small and medium businesses, largely public business details, retrieved during a short window before access was cut off. The reports do not link the incident to Google Cloud customer workloads or to the products tracked here.

events.headline: Gemini made generally available on Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped
events.summary: Google announced general availability of Gemini on Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped and a preview on GDC connected, naming Gemini 2.5 Flash and Pro, for organisations that need models to run in their own or a partner's data centre.

events.headline: European Commission fines Google EUR 3.0 billion over advertising technology
events.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that in September 2025 the European Commission decided Google had infringed competition law through self-preferencing in its advertising technology business, imposed a EUR 3.0 billion fine and ordered the conduct to stop. Alphabet recognised a US$3.5 billion charge in the third quarter of 2025, placed bank guarantees in place of payment and appealed in November 2025. The matter concerns advertising technology, not the enterprise AI products tracked here. The filing gives the month only; the day recorded here is the first of that month.

events.headline: Google Agentspace becomes Gemini Enterprise
events.summary: Google's release notes for 9 October 2025 state that the Google Agentspace experience and its resources and documentation are now referred to as Gemini Enterprise. TechCrunch reported the launch the same day, with Standard and Plus editions from US$30 per seat per month and a Business edition at US$21, and named customers including Macquarie Bank and Klarna.

events.headline: Alphabet finalises US$1.4 billion settlement of privacy matters
events.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that in October 2025 it finalised a US$1.4 billion settlement of certain privacy matters, and that it remains party to privacy investigations and lawsuits in the US and EU concerning location information, user choices and advertising practices. The filing does not connect the settlement to Google Cloud services. The filing gives the month only; the day recorded here is the first of that month.

events.headline: Final judgment entered in US Department of Justice search case against Google
events.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that a final judgment was entered in December 2025 in the search case brought by the US Department of Justice and state attorneys general, restricting how Google distributes its services and requiring it to share certain search data and offer syndication to some competitors. Google appealed in January 2026 and the plaintiffs appealed in February 2026; the Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026 says the appeals remain pending. The filing gives the month only; the day recorded here is the first of that month.

events.headline: European Commission opens antitrust investigation into Google's use of content for AI
events.summary: Reported by Computerworld and the Irish Examiner on 2025-12-09: the European Commission opened an antitrust investigation into whether Google used web publishers' content and YouTube videos for its AI models and AI search features without appropriate compensation or a way to refuse, and whether this disadvantages rival AI developers. The reports say there is no deadline for the investigation. No outcome was found.

events.headline: Vertex AI becomes part of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
events.summary: Google's release notes for 22 April 2026 record the initial release of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and state that Vertex AI is now part of it, with a table of renamed services (for example Vertex AI Model Registry to Agent Platform Model Registry). Google's product page also uses the name 'Gemini platform'. Service level agreements and some compliance pages still use the Vertex AI name.

events.headline: Google Cloud job cuts reported, including Mandiant and threat intelligence teams
events.summary: Reported by Business Today and The Free Press Journal on 2026-06-05, both citing Business Insider: Google cut jobs across its Cloud division over about two weeks, including staff in the Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant. Neither report gives a number. A Google spokesperson is quoted as saying the company regularly evaluates its internal structures. Alphabet's total headcount, per its filings, rose from 190,820 at the end of 2025 to 204,757 at 30 September 2026.

events.headline: European Commission fines Google EUR 890 million under the Digital Markets Act
events.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026 that in July 2026 the European Commission issued Digital Markets Act non-compliance decisions with fines of EUR 430 million relating to Google Play and EUR 460 million relating to Search. Alphabet recognised a US$1.0 billion charge and appealed both decisions in October 2026. The same filing says the EUR 4.1 billion Android fine became final in July 2026 and was paid with interest (US$5.2 billion). The filing gives the month only; the day recorded here is the first of that month.

events.headline: Google Cloud launches Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services in preview
events.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini Enterprise for Financial Services, initially in preview for capital markets and corporate banking, with a Google-managed financial research agent, more than 50 financial skills and connectors to licensed data sources including FactSet, LSEG, Moody's, MSCI and S&P Global. The release names CME Group as a user and Deutsche Bank as a design partner that will deploy the research agent in its corporate bank.

events.headline: US court denies divestiture in Google advertising technology case, orders behavioural remedies
events.summary: Alphabet disclosed in its Form 10-Q for the third quarter of 2026 that in September 2026 the US District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia issued its remedies decision in the Department of Justice advertising technology case, denying structural divestitures and ordering behavioural remedies on interoperability, data access and auction conduct. Alphabet said it plans to appeal the adverse part of the April 2025 liability decision once final judgment is entered. The filing gives the month only; the day recorded here is the first of that month.

events.headline: Google releases the Gemini 4 model family
events.summary: Google's deprecations schedule lists the release of Gemini 4 Argon on 13 October 2026, followed by Gemini 4 Carbon on 10 November, Gemini 4 Hydrogen on 12 November and Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November 2026. Google describes Carbon as its strongest reasoning model, with a 1M-token context window, and published a model card for it on 10 November 2026. Introductory pricing for Carbon runs to 30 November 2026.

events.headline: Google launches Antigravity agentic development platform in public preview
events.summary: SD Times reported on 18 November 2025 that Google announced Antigravity alongside Gemini 3, free in public preview, with support for Gemini 3, Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5 and OpenAI's GPT-OSS. Google's developer blog of 20 November 2025 describes an AI-powered editor and a manager surface for running several agents, on macOS, Windows and Linux.

events.headline: Google Cloud announces Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience
events.summary: Google Cloud announced Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience at the NRF 2026 retail conference: a shopping agent, Customer Experience Agent Studio for building support agents, and an enhanced food-ordering agent. The release names Kroger, Lowe's, Woolworths and Papa Johns. CMSWire reported on 14 January 2026 that Google's chief executive described it as available in preview.

events.headline: Google's seventh-generation TPU becomes generally available on Google Cloud
events.summary: Cloud TPU release notes record that TPU7x, the first release in the Ironwood family and Google Cloud's seventh-generation TPU, became generally available on 31 March 2026, after a preview from 24 November 2025. On 1 June 2026 Compute Engine gained general support for creating TPU VMs through its instance APIs.

events.headline: Anthropic agrees multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity with Google and Broadcom
events.summary: Anthropic announced an agreement with Google and Broadcom for multiple gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity, expected to come online from 2027 and sited mostly in the United States. Anthropic said it trains and runs Claude on AWS Trainium, Google TPUs and Nvidia GPUs, and that Amazon remains its primary cloud provider.

events.headline: Google releases Antigravity 2.0 and folds Gemini CLI and Gemini Code Assist into it
events.summary: InfoWorld reported on 20 May 2026 that Google launched Antigravity 2.0 at Google I/O, with a desktop app, the Antigravity CLI and expanded SDK, and said Gemini CLI and the Gemini Code Assist IDE extensions would stop serving free and consumer-plan users on 18 June 2026. Customers with Gemini Code Assist Standard or Enterprise licences keep support, with no end date given. The article gives the launch day as the Tuesday before its dateline.

events.headline: Google Security Operations SIEM and SOAR added to Google's FedRAMP certified services
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace entry for Google Services lists Google Security Operations SIEM and Google Security Operations SOAR as certified services with an availability date of 8 June 2026; Google Kubernetes Engine carries the same date. Google's documentation says the product supports FedRAMP High and Moderate and that its Triage and Investigation Agent is not covered.

events.headline: Google Cloud makes Deferred tier generally available at 50% below Standard pay-as-you-go rates
events.summary: Google Cloud's weekly news roundup, dated 19 November 2026, lists under the week of 16 to 20 November that the Deferred service tier is generally available on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for the Interactions API, Agent Development Kit and Deep Research. The roundup and Google's documentation say deferred turns are billed at 50% below Standard pay-as-you-go rates; the documentation adds a 24-hour completion target with no credit-backed latency SLA and support on the global endpoint only. The exact launch day within that week is not stated.

events.headline: Groq licenses its inference technology to NVIDIA; founder and president join NVIDIA
events.summary: Groq announced on 24 December 2025 a non-exclusive licence of its inference technology to NVIDIA, under which founder Jonathan Ross, president Sunny Madra and other staff joined NVIDIA while Groq continued as an independent company operating GroqCloud. Groq did not state the price; TechCrunch and SiliconANGLE later described it as a US$20 billion deal, and TechCrunch reported that the proceeds were paid out to Groq's investors.

events.headline: Groq names a new chief executive after its founder joins NVIDIA
events.summary: Groq announced on 24 December 2025 that Simon Edwards would become chief executive as founder Jonathan Ross left for NVIDIA. The Next Web reported on 23 June 2026 that Adam Winter was by then chief executive, with Alex Davis of the investor Disruptive as chairman and further executive appointments; the date of that second change was not found.

events.headline: Groq raises US$650 million led by Disruptive and Infinitum
events.summary: Groq announced on 22 June 2026 that it had raised US$650 million to expand its inference cloud. SiliconANGLE and The Next Web reported that Disruptive and Infinitum led the round and that existing investors took part; no valuation was disclosed.

events.headline: Groq becomes an NVIDIA Cloud Partner
events.summary: Groq's newsroom lists an announcement dated 12 August 2026 that it had become an NVIDIA Cloud Partner; its Series A release describes this as certification to design, deploy and operate NVIDIA accelerated computing to NVIDIA's reference architecture.

events.headline: Groq announces US$350 million Series A at a US$3.5 billion valuation
events.summary: Groq announced on 17 August 2026 a US$350 million Series A led by Disruptive with planned participation from NVIDIA, valuing the company at US$3.5 billion and subject to customary closing conditions. TechCrunch noted that the valuation was below the US$6.9 billion of September 2025 and that the company described it as a new valuation for the business after the NVIDIA licensing deal.

events.headline: Former Groq shareholders sue former board and chief executive over NVIDIA deal
events.summary: Reported by Bloomberg Law and Crypto Briefing on 5 October 2026: two former Groq shareholders sued Groq's former board and former chief executive in the Delaware Court of Chancery, alleging breaches of fiduciary duty in the December 2025 agreement with NVIDIA. The complaint was unsealed on 5 October 2026; the filing date was not sourced. The allegations are unproven.

events.headline: Battery Ventures buys a majority stake in Guardsquare for US$29 million
events.summary: Guardsquare announced a US$29 million investment from Battery Ventures, its first institutional financing, with two Battery partners joining the board. Tech.eu and Unquote reported that Battery took a majority stake. The company said it then served more than 650 customers in over 70 countries.

events.headline: Guardsquare adds server-side mobile app attestation
events.summary: Guardsquare announced a mobile app attestation service that checks, on the server side, that an app calling a customer's APIs is genuine and running in a trusted environment, returning a signed short-lived token with a verdict. Policies can be changed without republishing the app.

events.headline: Verdane announces an investment in Guardsquare
events.summary: The growth investor Verdane announced an investment in Guardsquare, following earlier investment by Battery Ventures, to fund organic growth and acquisitions. Completion was subject to regulatory approvals. The amount and the size of the stake were not disclosed; SecurityBrief reported that Battery Ventures continued its involvement.

events.headline: Guardsquare completes purchase of Verimatrix's XTD application protection assets
events.summary: Guardsquare and Verimatrix each announced completion of the sale of Verimatrix's Extended Threat Defense (XTD) assets, including patents and a team, to Guardsquare after regulatory approval. CSI Magazine reported at signing in December 2025 an initial price of US$8.5 million, to be adjusted at closing; the final price was not found. Guardsquare said XTD customers and partners would continue to be served without disruption.

events.headline: Guardsquare announces acquisitions of Runway and Bugfender
events.summary: Guardsquare announced that it had acquired Runway, a mobile release management platform, and Bugfender, a remote logging and crash-reporting provider, adding release management and crash analytics to its mobile security products. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: H2O.ai discloses unauthorised access to a development environment
events.summary: Disclosed by H2O.ai in security bulletins dated 2025-02-21 and 2025-03-31, and in a notice filed with the Maryland Attorney General: an unauthorised actor accessed certain H2O.ai systems at various times between 2024-12-20 and 2025-01-29. H2O.ai said the activity was limited to one development environment, that production systems and environments holding sensitive customer data were not accessed, and that the files affected were mainly internal business records, including customer agreements, purchase orders and support tickets. The filing states that payroll and employee files containing personal information of current and former employees were accessed and may have been taken. H2O.ai said a forensic investigation with CrowdStrike was complete by 2025-03-31.

events.headline: H2O.ai launches model risk management framework for generative AI
events.summary: H2O.ai announced a model risk management framework for generative AI as part of Enterprise h2oGPTe, covering automated test generation, human-calibrated evaluation, robustness testing and guardrail-based mitigation, for air-gapped and on-premises deployments.

events.headline: H2O.ai's government cloud offering listed as FedRAMP High
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists 'H2O.AI for Government' (package FR2521554684) at the High impact level through the agency path, dated 2026-04-16. H2O.ai announced the listing for H2O.ai Cloud for Government on 2026-05-20.

events.headline: AT&T adds H2O AI Super Agent to its Ask AT&T platform
events.summary: H2O.ai announced that AT&T is using H2O AI Super Agent in the expansion of its internal Ask AT&T platform, for uses including customer experience, fraud prevention and field operations.

events.headline: H2O.ai completes IRAP assessment of H2O AI Cloud at PROTECTED level
