events.summary: H2O.ai announced that H2O AI Cloud had been assessed under the Australian Information Security Registered Assessors Program at the PROTECTED level, against the March 2026 Information Security Manual. The assessor was not named in the announcement.

events.headline: H2O.ai appoints a chief financial officer
events.summary: H2O.ai announced the appointment of Steven Vattuone, previously chief financial officer of ON24, as its chief financial officer.

events.headline: H2O.ai makes TimeH2O and TabH2O foundation models generally available on H2O AI Cloud
events.summary: H2O.ai announced in a press release dated 17 November 2026 that TimeH2O, a time-series foundation model, and TabH2O, a tabular foundation model, are generally available on H2O AI Cloud for production use and fine-tuning. The release says TimeH2O-v1 open weights are published for research under a non-commercial licence, with production use needing a licence from H2O.ai. The benchmark rankings it cites are reported by H2O.ai itself.

events.headline: IBM completes acquisition of HashiCorp
events.summary: IBM announced it had completed its acquisition of HashiCorp at US$35 per share in cash, an enterprise value of US$6.4 billion, placing HashiCorp's products including Vault in IBM Software. IBM's annual report for 2025 dates the acquisition to 27 February 2025. ITPro reported that the close followed UK and US regulatory review.

events.headline: HashiCorp business operations transition to IBM
events.summary: HashiCorp told customers on 5 August 2025 that all its business operations would transition to IBM on 1 September 2025, with IBM taking over billing, support systems aligning with IBM Support and some product editions being renamed.

events.headline: IBM publishes security bulletins for three medium-severity HashiCorp Vault flaws fixed in 2.2.2
events.summary: According to IBM security bulletins published on 12 and 13 November 2026, Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise are affected by CVE-2026-92735, a server-side request forgery in the integrated storage join process that could expose server-environment credentials from an uninitialised node (CVSS 5.9), and by two ACL deny-rule bypasses, CVE-2026-93335 and CVE-2026-128100 (CVSS 6.5 each). The bulletins list fixes in Vault 2.2.2 and in Vault Enterprise 1.21.14 and 1.19.25, and do not mention exploitation.

events.headline: Hawk AI begins trading as Hawk
events.summary: The company's press releases used the name Hawk AI up to 2024-02-14 and Hawk from 2024-06-11; its about page says it was originally known as HAWK:AI. No announcement of the change was found, so the date recorded is that of the first release under the new name. The legal entity remains Hawk AI GmbH.

events.headline: Hawk raises US$56 million Series C led by One Peak
events.summary: Hawk announced a US$56 million Series C led by One Peak with existing investors Macquarie Capital, Rabobank, BlackFin Capital Partners, Sands Capital, DN Capital, Picus and Coalition. The company said it had more than 80 customers and would use the money for product development and expansion, particularly in the US.

events.headline: Hawk AI GmbH issued ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certificate valid to November 2028
events.summary: TUV SUD Management Service GmbH issued certificate 12 310 64806 TMS to Hawk AI GmbH for an information security management system covering development, operation and maintenance of its sanctions screening, anti-money laundering and fraud prevention platform, valid from 2025-10-20 to 2028-11-03.

events.headline: Hawk appoints Eric Larsson as chief financial officer
events.summary: Hawk announced Eric Larsson, formerly in finance leadership at NICE Actimize, as chief financial officer, based in New York. The press centre also lists a president and chief revenue officer appointment in July 2026 and a chief customer officer appointment in May 2026.

events.headline: SAS acquires the principal software assets of Hazy

quote.text: Hazy is a pioneer in bringing synthetic data to market as a viable enterprise product

events.summary: SAS announced that it had acquired the principal software assets of Hazy, a London synthetic data company founded in 2017, for undisclosed terms. The purchase covered Hazy's software and intellectual property, not the company. SAS said the technology would be built into SAS Data Maker, then in private preview.

events.headline: Hazy Limited enters members' voluntary liquidation
events.summary: According to Companies House filings, Hazy Limited, the UK company that had developed the Hazy synthetic data software, began a members' voluntary liquidation on 17 February 2025, after a declaration of solvency sworn on 29 January 2025, and liquidators were appointed the same day. The company's status is shown as in liquidation. This followed the sale of its principal software assets to SAS in November 2024.

events.headline: SAS Data Maker becomes generally available on Microsoft Marketplace
events.summary: SAS announced general availability of SAS Data Maker, its synthetic data generator incorporating Hazy's technology, through Microsoft Marketplace, after a private preview. SAS listed support for multi-table and time-series source data and differential privacy, and said it planned to support other cloud providers and integrate the product into SAS Viya.

events.headline: HiddenLayer and Cohere announce collaboration on securing agentic AI
events.summary: HiddenLayer announced on 29 June 2026 a collaboration with Cohere under which its AI Security Platform secures agents, models, prompts and integrations at runtime on Cohere's North platform. HiddenLayer said it had evaluated North against its own security standards and deployed it internally.

events.headline: HiddenLayer joins Databricks Unity AI Gateway ecosystem
events.summary: HiddenLayer's newsroom lists a 17 June 2026 announcement that it joined the Databricks Unity AI Gateway ecosystem to bring its security controls to enterprise AI workloads on Databricks. The announcement itself was not retrieved; the date and title are from the newsroom listing.

events.headline: HiddenLayer launches Agent Harness Security for AI coding agents
events.summary: HiddenLayer announced Agent Harness Security on 3 August 2026, a runtime control for AI coding agents that monitors prompts, tool calls, shell commands and file edits and can redact secrets or block risky actions. It extends the platform's AI Runtime Security module and was described as available as a stand-alone solution; Zivian Health was quoted as a user.

events.headline: HiddenLayer appoints Mike Gesnaldo as chief revenue officer
events.summary: HiddenLayer announced on 12 August 2026 the appointment of Mike Gesnaldo, previously at CrowdStrike, Tanium and Dazz, as chief revenue officer leading its go-to-market organisation.

events.headline: HiddenLayer selected to support US Department of Energy Prometheus initiative
events.summary: HiddenLayer announced on 18 August 2026 that it had been selected, as a partner of Idaho National Laboratory, to support Prometheus, a US Department of Energy initiative on AI for nuclear reactor design and operation with $60 million of Phase II funding over three years, subject to appropriations. HiddenLayer's own share of the funding was not stated.

events.headline: HiddenLayer raises $100 million Series B led by Delta-v Capital
events.summary: HiddenLayer announced a $100 million Series B on 2 September 2026, led by Delta-v Capital with participation from Ten Eleven Ventures, Morgan Stanley, Microsoft's M12 and Booz Allen Ventures. SiliconANGLE reported this brought total funding to about $156 million, including a $6 million seed round and a $50 million Series A in September 2023. The company said annual recurring revenue had grown more than tenfold and that it had signed more than 50 new platform customers.

events.headline: Patent infringement suit filed against HiddenLayer in the Western District of Texas
events.summary: According to the CourtListener federal docket index, searched on 2026-11-20, Congruent Media Resourcing LLC v. HiddenLayer, Inc. (7:26-cv-00229) was filed in the Western District of Texas on 10 June 2026 as a patent infringement action, and no termination date is shown. The claims were not retrieved.

events.headline: Holistic AI launches LLM Decision Hub
events.summary: Holistic AI released a free online resource comparing more than 20 large language models on performance, safety, jailbreak resistance and cost, combining public benchmarks with its own red-teaming tests.

events.headline: Holistic AI reports ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification
events.summary: The vendor's trust centre states that ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification was achieved in February 2026 after a stage 2 audit, with a scope covering development and deployment of the platform. Only the month is given; the certification body is not named.

events.headline: Vahé Torossian joins Holistic AI board
events.summary: Holistic AI appointed Vahé Torossian, a former Microsoft executive and a venture partner at Tola Capital, to its board of directors.

events.headline: Holistic AI releases Agentic Red Teaming 2.0
events.summary: A platform update adds agent profiling, adaptive attacks and tests for data extraction, tool abuse, bias and sycophancy, with evidence, severity and a recommended fix for each finding.

events.headline: Horizon3.ai raises US$100M Series D led by NEA
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-06-11 that Horizon3.ai raised a US$100M Series D led by NEA with 9Yards Capital, Craft Ventures and SignalFire, bringing total funding to US$178.5M. The company's own post also names Qualcomm Ventures.

events.headline: Horizon3 raises US$250M Series E at a valuation above US$2 billion
events.summary: Horizon3 announced a US$250M Series E co-led by NightDragon and NEA, with new investors including EDBI, PSG, SAIC and Sapphire Ventures. The company put the valuation above US$2 billion; TechCrunch reported the round the same day.

events.headline: Horizon3 announces Impact Level 4 authorisation for NodeZero for Defense
events.summary: Horizon3 announced that NodeZero for Defense, covering internal pentesting with risk-based exposure management, is included in an Impact Level 4 authorisation and is available to US defence customers. The release does not name the authorising body.

events.headline: Horizon3 reports CMMC Final Level 2 (Self) status for its federal environment
events.summary: Horizon3 announced in a press release dated 19 November 2026 that it has reached CMMC Final Level 2 (Self) status. The release describes a self-assessment against the 110 requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, submitted and affirmed in the Supplier Performance Risk System, covering its federal product and sales environment; it names no third-party assessor. The release links the status to NodeZero for Government.

events.headline: Horizon3 launches Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab research unit
events.summary: Horizon3 announced in a press release dated 12 November 2026 that it has set up the Adversarial Intelligence Frontier Lab, a research unit directed by Purdue University associate professor Z. Berkay Celik, to study AI-enabled attacks, adaptive defence and safe autonomy for security agents using evidence from NodeZero tests. The release announces no new NodeZero features or pricing.

events.headline: Hyperscience announces FedRAMP High authorization through Palantir FedStart
events.summary: Hyperscience announced that its Hypercell platform is offered at the FedRAMP High impact level through Palantir's FedStart programme. The FedRAMP Marketplace lists Hyperscience Hypercell among the software delivered in Palantir's authorised PFCS Supporting Services offering; the authorization is held by Palantir.

events.headline: Hyperscience releases Hypercell Fall 2026 with ORCA 2 vision-language model framework
events.summary: Hyperscience announced the Fall 2026 release of Hypercell for SaaS and on-premises customers, adding the ORCA 2 vision-language model framework with zero-shot table extraction, redaction and masking, address validation, document translation and auto-labelling.

events.headline: IBM releases watsonx.governance 2.1
events.summary: IBM announced general availability of watsonx.governance 2.1 features, including an Amazon SageMaker integration, Evaluation Studio, guardrails for generative AI, risk-assessment support for the EU AI Act and an integration with Guardium AI Security. The announcement page does not display its date; 11 December 2024 is the date shown for it in search listings.

events.headline: Banco do Brasil adopts watsonx.governance for AI governance
events.summary: Brazilian trade publication Convergencia Digital reported on 13 June 2025 that Banco do Brasil had built its AI governance framework on IBM watsonx.governance. An IBM case study describes the bank operating under a unified AI governance model designed with EY, with generative AI integration still being tested.

events.headline: IBM links watsonx.governance with Guardium AI Security and adds Compliance Accelerators
events.summary: Verdict reported on 19 June 2025 that IBM was combining watsonx.governance with Guardium AI Security so that detected AI use cases can start governance workflows, and that a Compliance Accelerators add-on would ship pre-loaded with regulations and standards including the EU AI Act, SR 11-7, ISO/IEC 42001 and the NIST AI RMF.

events.headline: IBM unveils Guardium Cryptography Manager
events.summary: The Quantum Insider reported on 8 October 2025 that IBM had introduced Guardium Cryptography Manager for inventory, lifecycle management and remediation of keys and certificates, building on the earlier Guardium Quantum Safe assessment tool, with certificate lifecycle management and database encryption support due from November 2025.

events.headline: IBM announces agreement to acquire Confluent
events.summary: IBM's 2025 annual report says that on 8 December 2025 it announced its intent to acquire Confluent for $31 per share in cash, about $11 billion in enterprise value, that Confluent stockholders approved the merger on 12 February 2026, and that closing was expected by mid-2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Completion was not verified in this session.

events.headline: watsonx.governance 2.3 becomes generally available
events.summary: IBM's product lifecycle page gives 15 December 2025 as the general availability date of watsonx.governance 2.3.x, under a support policy of two years plus a one-year critical-fix extension.

events.headline: IBM launches IBM Quantum Safe suite for post-quantum migration
events.summary: IBM announced IBM Quantum Safe on 27 October 2026 according to an analyst commentary published the next day; Quantum Computing Report says it was released commercially at IBM's TechXchange conference. The suite groups Quantum Safe Cryptography Manager, Quantum Safe Explorer and Quantum Safe Proxy and builds on Guardium Cryptography Manager from 2025.

events.headline: IBM announces agent-building tools and an Agent Catalog for watsonx Orchestrate
events.summary: At its Think 2025 conference IBM announced new agent capabilities for watsonx Orchestrate: tools for building agents, prebuilt agents for HR, sales and procurement, connections to more than 80 enterprise applications, multi-agent orchestration and an Agent Catalog of more than 150 agents and tools from IBM and partners, as reported by TechTarget on 2025-05-06.

events.headline: IBM Verify for Government listed as a FedRAMP certified service
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace entry for IBM Platform Services for Government (FedRAMP Certified, Class C) lists IBM Verify for Government among its certified services, with an availability date of 4 June 2025.

events.headline: IBM Security Verify renamed IBM Verify
events.summary: An IBM support note dated 4 August 2025 states that the product name changed from IBM Security Verify to IBM Verify. The same note lists deprecations, including features dependent on IBM X-Force and version 1.0 certification-campaign APIs. The date is that of the note; the exact day of the rename was not found.

events.headline: IBM releases Granite 4.0 models
events.summary: IBM released the Granite 4.0 language models (H-Small, H-Tiny, H-Micro and Micro) under the Apache 2.0 licence, available on watsonx.ai and through partners including Hugging Face, Docker Hub, NVIDIA NIM and Ollama. IBM said the checkpoints are cryptographically signed and that it runs a bug bounty with HackerOne.

events.headline: IBM Data Services for Government, including watsonx services, listed as FedRAMP Certified
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists IBM Data Services for Government as FedRAMP Certified (Rev5, Agency path, Class C) with a certification date of 10 February 2026. The listing's description names watsonx.ai, watsonx.data, watsonx.governance and watsonx Orchestrate for Government.

events.headline: IBM introduces the Agentic Control Plane in watsonx Orchestrate
events.summary: IBM announced an Agentic Control Plane for watsonx Orchestrate on AWS and IBM Cloud, with an operations dashboard, agent analytics, runtime policy management, credential health monitoring, an overview of which agents can reach which integrations, content guardrails and a shared Agent Catalog. The announcement is dated 2 July 2026 and says the release arrived in June 2026.

events.headline: IBM releases Granite 4.2 reasoning models
events.summary: IBM released Granite 4.2 language models in 3B, 8B and 30B sizes under the Apache 2.0 licence, with selectable thinking modes and tool calling; the model card gives a release date of 25 August 2026. The Decoder reported the release on 2026-08-26 and noted that the performance claims are IBM's own.

events.headline: IBM and Microsoft announce Imagine Enterprise, an industry-focused AI agent platform
events.summary: IBM and Microsoft announced in a press release dated 10 November 2026 a platform called Imagine Enterprise for building, running and governing AI agents for industry-specific processes, starting with financial services, insurance and retail. The release says IBM Consulting contributes pre-built agents and assets from IBM Consulting Advantage and Microsoft supplies the AI, data, cloud and security foundation. It does not mention watsonx or Granite.

events.headline: Illumio joins World Wide Technology's ARMOR framework for AI risk
events.summary: Illumio announced on 2026-11-10 that it will be featured in World Wide Technology's AI Readiness Model for Operational Resilience (ARMOR), naming Illumio Insights and Illumio Segmentation.

events.headline: Immersive Labs renames itself Immersive and its platform Immersive One
events.summary: On 12 February 2025 the company announced that it was dropping Labs from its trading name and renaming its platform Immersive One, which it described as a single platform of hands-on labs, simulations, cyber drills and ranges for technical and non-technical staff. The legal entities kept the Immersive Labs name.

events.headline: Immersive names Mark Schmitz chief executive; founder James Hadley becomes chief innovation officer
events.summary: The company announced on 11 March 2025 that Mark Schmitz, previously president of Collibra and interim chief executive of Citrix, would join as chief executive on 17 March 2025. Founder James Hadley moved to chief innovation officer and stayed on the board. BusinessCloud reported the appointment the next day, and the group's 2025 accounts record the change.

events.headline: Immersive and Cycode announce a partnership on secure software development
events.summary: In a release dated 11 September 2025 the two companies said they would combine Immersive's developer security training with Cycode's code scanning results, so that findings can direct targeted training. The combined offering was described as due in the following months.

events.headline: Immersive appoints a chief product officer and a chief technology officer
events.summary: On 16 September 2025 the company named Aniket Menon, formerly a vice-president of product at Rapid7, as chief product officer and confirmed Thanos Karpouzis, previously its vice-president of engineering, as chief technology officer.

events.headline: Immersive launches Dynamic Threat Range for live-fire team exercises
events.summary: The company announced general availability of Dynamic Threat Range within Immersive One on 19 November 2025. The release says it runs full attack chains in supported enterprise environments, initially with Elastic and Splunk, and measures time to detect and respond. Microsoft Sentinel support and custom exercise creation were described as planned for early 2026.

events.headline: Immersive One adds AI security labs, vendor-specific exercises and framework heat maps
events.summary: On 17 March 2026 the company announced additions to Immersive One: hands-on labs on agentic AI and prompt injection, exercises using CrowdStrike Falcon, Google Security Operations, Splunk, IBM QRadar and Microsoft Sentinel, enhanced after-action reporting for crisis simulations, and heat maps aligned to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST NICE and MITRE frameworks. No availability date was given.

events.headline: Immersive announces Immersive AI Security in early access
events.summary: On 18 November 2026 the company announced a new product family, Immersive AI Security, with two products: AI Govern & Control, which monitors and controls how staff use AI tools in the browser, and AI Observe & Assess, an on-premises appliance that maps and tests internally built AI agents. Both link findings to training in Immersive One. They are in an early-access programme, with general availability planned for early 2027.

events.headline: Immuta launches Immuta AI and Copilot
events.summary: Immuta's newsroom lists trade-press coverage dated 3 to 5 March 2025 of the launch of Immuta AI and a Copilot assistant for its data governance platform.

events.headline: Immuta and Alation announce data access partnership
events.summary: Immuta's newsroom lists coverage dated 2 September 2025 of a partnership with data catalogue vendor Alation aimed at closing gaps between finding data and getting access to it.

events.headline: Immuta launches data provisioning for AI agents
events.summary: Immuta's newsroom lists a CRN article dated 3 April 2026 on the launch of a data provisioning system for AI agents. The vendor's platform page describes per-agent identities and short-lived, policy-scoped roles.

events.headline: ALTR Solutions files federal suit against Immuta in Delaware
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, ALTR Solutions, Inc. filed suit against Immuta Inc. in the US District Court for the District of Delaware on 2025-12-31 (1:25-cv-01586). The listing shows no nature of suit. Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: Incode acquires AuthenticID
events.summary: Biometric Update reported on 2025-08-19 that Incode had acquired AuthenticID, a Seattle-based identity verification company. The price was not disclosed and no closing date was given.

events.headline: Incode announces FedRAMP Ready status at the High baseline
events.summary: Incode announced on 2025-11-14 that it had reached FedRAMP Ready status at the High baseline after a readiness assessment by an accredited assessor, and said its next step was to work with a sponsoring agency toward an authorization. FedRAMP Ready is a readiness designation, not an authorization.

events.headline: Incode launches Deepsight deepfake and injection defence
events.summary: Incode's press index records the launch of Deepsight on 2025-12-02. The product page describes it as a layer that checks for deepfakes, camera injection, device tampering and scripted behaviour during verification.

events.headline: Incode reports passing iBeta Level 3 liveness testing on iOS and Android
events.summary: Incode announced on 2026-03-02 that its passive liveness passed iBeta Level 3 presentation attack detection testing on both iOS and Android, reporting 900 attacks with none accepted. The iBeta confirmation letter was not read.

events.headline: Incode acquires Identiq
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-06-25 that Incode had acquired Identiq Protocol, an Israeli company whose cryptographic method lets institutions share fraud signals without sharing customer records. The price was not disclosed. Incode described the deal as part of a US$100 million commitment to privacy-preserving identity infrastructure, and it was reported as its third acquisition in two years after MetaMap (2024) and AuthenticID (2025).

events.headline: Incode launches TrustGraph fraud-signal network
events.summary: Incode's press index records the launch of TrustGraph on 2026-10-14, described by the vendor as a privacy-preserving network that flags repeat fraud across participating organisations without pooling raw data.

events.headline: Incode launches Know Your Agent, tying AI agents to a verified person
events.summary: Incode announced on 2026-11-17 a product called Incode Know Your Agent. According to the company's release, it detects AI agents in a business's traffic, checks the person behind an agent with a live face match against a government record, lets that person set limits on what the agent may do, and logs agent actions against those limits. Incode says it is available now; the release names no customers or partners.

events.headline: Infisical raises US$40M Series B at a reported US$600M valuation
events.summary: Infisical announced a US$40 million Series B led by Elad Gil with Y Combinator and Gradient Ventures participating. SecurityWeek reported the valuation as US$600 million and total funding as nearly US$60 million, and said the money would go to product development, hiring and AI agent security.

events.headline: Vista Equity Partners agrees to buy Infoblox for about US$1.6 billion
events.summary: Fortune reported on 19 September 2016 that the private-equity firm Vista Equity Partners had agreed to buy Infoblox, then a listed company trading under the ticker BLOX, for about US$1.6 billion, or US$26.50 a share in cash. The completion date was not sourced in this research.

events.headline: Warburg Pincus invests in Infoblox and takes joint control with Vista Equity Partners
events.summary: The European Commission cleared on 9 November 2020 the acquisition of joint control of Infoblox by Warburg Pincus and Vista Equity Partners Management, noting that Vista had held sole control. Infoblox announced on 1 December 2020 that the transaction had closed, with Vista continuing as an investor and equal partner. The amount was not disclosed.

events.headline: Infoblox announces ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification
events.summary: In a blog post dated 19 May 2025 Infoblox said it had achieved ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification, validated by an independent body it did not name. The post gives no scope, certificate number or dates.

events.headline: Patent holder files Unified Patent Court action against Infoblox over NIOS products
events.summary: Reported by ip fray on 2026-02-01: Nixu FL IP Protection LLC filed a patent infringement action on 30 January 2026 in the Hamburg Local Division of the Unified Patent Court against Infoblox Inc., Infoblox Germany GmbH and a German reseller, over European patent EP2005696, seeking an injunction in respect of products running NIOS or NIOS-X. In a procedural order published on 8 June 2026 (UPC_CFI_360/2026) the court dismissed the case against Infoblox Inc. as inadmissible for the United Kingdom part of the patent and rejected the rest of its jurisdiction objection. No decision on the merits was found.

events.headline: Two vulnerabilities in Infoblox NIOS through 9.0.7 published
events.summary: According to the US National Vulnerability Database, CVE-2025-61880 and CVE-2025-61879 were published on 12 February 2026. The first describes insecure deserialisation in Infoblox NIOS through version 9.0.7 that can lead to remote code execution (CVSS 3.1 base score 8.8 in the record); the second describes an arbitrary file write by a high-privileged user (7.7). The records were not checked for evidence of exploitation. NIOS is not one of the products evaluated here.

events.headline: Infoblox completes acquisition of Axur and launches Digital Risk Protection Services
events.summary: Infoblox announced on 14 January 2026 an agreement to acquire Axur, a provider of external threat discovery and takedown, and on 5 May 2026 that the acquisition had completed. Terms were not disclosed. It introduced Digital Risk Protection Services as the first part of a new product, Infoblox Exposure Management, with findings feeding Infoblox Threat Defense, and said further integration would follow.

events.headline: Infoblox adds external attack surface management and supplier monitoring to Exposure Management
events.summary: In a release dated 28 July 2026 Infoblox announced External Attack Surface Management and Supply Chain Intelligence as additions to Infoblox Exposure Management alongside Digital Risk Protection Services. The release mentions an early access programme and gives no general availability date.

events.headline: Infoblox completes acquisition of network observability company Kentik
events.summary: Network World reported on 8 July 2026 that Infoblox had agreed to acquire Kentik, a network observability company, on undisclosed terms. Infoblox's release of 6 August 2026 says the acquisition has completed and that Kentik's capabilities will be integrated into its platform over time.

events.headline: Infoblox investigates data exposure through a compromised third-party vendor
events.summary: Reported by The Register on 2026-11-16 and by Cyber Daily on 2026-11-17: Infoblox said it was investigating unauthorised access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor. The Register, citing sources and an email from the chief executive, reported that the intruders used the vendor's access to Infoblox's SharePoint and that the data included personal and payroll details of employees and their dependants and saved configuration snapshots of some customers' NIOS deployments. A company spokesperson told both outlets there was no indication that Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Infoblox did not say how many customers or employees were affected.

events.headline: Instabase raises US$100M Series D led by Qatar Investment Authority
events.summary: TechCrunch reported that Instabase raised a US$100M Series D led by the Qatar Investment Authority with Andreessen Horowitz, Greylock Partners, Index Ventures and NEA participating, and cited a Bloomberg report putting the valuation at US$1.24 billion, against US$2 billion at its 2023 round.

events.headline: Instabase says the BreezeML team is joining the company
events.summary: Instabase announced that the team of BreezeML, which builds agents to analyse and stress-test AI applications, is joining Instabase. The post does not say whether the company or its assets were acquired and gives no terms.

events.headline: Instabase renames itself SuperApp and launches a collaboration product; AI Hub continues
events.summary: Instabase, Inc. announced it is becoming SuperApp, Inc. and launched SuperApp, a new product for shared conversations between people and multiple AI models. The company stated that Instabase AI Hub remains fully supported for existing customers; SiliconANGLE reported that AI Hub will use SuperApp technology under the hood.

events.headline: Thoma Bravo completes a strategic investment in Intel 471
events.summary: Thoma Bravo announced on 8 September 2021 that it had agreed to make a strategic growth investment in Intel 471, and on 27 September 2021 that the investment was complete. Financial terms were not disclosed; debt financing came from Antares Capital. The co-founders were to keep leading the company and to retain a significant ownership position. Whether Thoma Bravo holds control is not stated.

events.headline: Intel 471 launches Verity471, its next-generation intelligence platform
events.summary: Intel 471 announced Verity471, a platform that brings its Cyber Threat Intelligence, Cyber Threat Exposure and Threat Hunting portfolios into one interface, together with two new exposure modules for the external attack surface and for third parties. Help Net Security reported the launch the same day.

events.headline: Intel 471 names a Chief Revenue Officer and a Chief Technology Officer
events.summary: Intel 471 announced that Amy Minyard-Bishop, previously Chief Customer Officer, had become Chief Revenue Officer and that Steve Micallef, founder of SpiderFoot, had become Chief Technology Officer.

events.headline: Intel 471 appoints Michael DeBolt as President
events.summary: Intel 471 announced that Michael DeBolt, its Chief Intelligence Officer, had also been appointed President. Jason Passwaters remains Chief Executive.

events.headline: Intel 471 bundles its three exposure modules on Verity471
events.summary: Intel 471 announced the Cyber Threat Exposure Bundle, which combines the Attack Surface Exposure, Third-Party Exposure and Brand Exposure modules of Verity471 in one offering. Help Net Security reported it the same day. The bundle is a separate portfolio from the intelligence product evaluated here.

events.headline: Intel 471 adds Retroactive Threat Detection to Verity471
events.summary: Intel 471 announced Retroactive Threat Detection, which turns the indicators in an intelligence report into ready-to-run queries for a customer's SIEM and endpoint detection tools so that a team can check whether it was affected. It is available to Verity471 customers with certain intelligence subscriptions.

events.headline: Intel 471 adds an AI agent and an MCP connector to Verity471
events.summary: Intel 471 announced Agent471, an AI agent inside Verity471 that answers questions across a customer's subscribed intelligence with citations, and MCP471, a Model Context Protocol connector that brings the intelligence into AI tools the customer already runs. Help Net Security reported the announcement the same day.

events.headline: interface.ai raises US$30M in its first outside funding, led by Avataar Venture Partners
events.summary: TechCrunch reported that interface.ai raised US$30M, made up of US$20M in equity and US$10M in debt, in a round led by Avataar Venture Partners. It was the company's first outside capital after being bootstrapped. The chief executive told TechCrunch the company had a 120-person team, more than 100 financial-institution customers and annual recurring revenue in the tens of millions of dollars.

events.headline: interface.ai reports completing its annual SOC 2 Type 2 and CSA STAR Level 2 attestation
events.summary: interface.ai's trust centre announced on 25 June 2025 that its SOC 2 Type 2 annual attestation and CSA STAR Level 2 attestation were complete, with the report available on request. The CSA STAR registry lists the company's intelligent virtual assistants at Level 1 and Level 2.

events.headline: interface.ai announces a partnership with Telarus for its contact centre and agentic AI offering
events.summary: interface.ai's newsroom lists an 18 February 2026 announcement of a strategic partnership with Telarus tied to its combined contact centre and agentic AI offering for community banking.

events.headline: interface.ai launches Smart Collections, a collections AI agent for credit unions and community banks
events.summary: interface.ai's newsroom lists a 19 February 2026 launch of Smart Collections, a multi-channel collections AI agent. The vendor's site labels its collections product as beta or early access.

events.headline: interface.ai launches Nexus, an agentic contact centre platform
events.summary: interface.ai announced Nexus, a contact-centre-as-a-service platform for credit unions and community banks in which AI handles the conversation and routes selected requests to human agents. The release says it is available for pilots and phased rollouts; the product page labels it beta.

events.headline: IRONSCALES launches three AI agents and outbound email encryption in Winter 2026 release
events.summary: IRONSCALES announced a Red Teaming Agent, a Phishing SOC Agent and a Phishing Simulation Agent, integrated outbound email encryption and enhancements to deepfake protection for Microsoft Teams. The release also named a new chief strategy officer and a senior vice president of research and development.

events.headline: IRONSCALES says it is verified under Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program
events.summary: IRONSCALES announced it had been verified under Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program, which it says gives it access to frontier AI for adversarial simulation and stress-testing of its detection models. The vendor page shows no date; the date is taken from the linked wire-service release.

events.headline: IRONSCALES appoints Steve McKenzie as chief operating officer
events.summary: IRONSCALES announced that Steve McKenzie, previously chief customer and revenue officer at LinkSquares and formerly at Mimecast, joined as chief operating officer overseeing go-to-market, customer success and revenue operations. The vendor page shows no date; the date is taken from the linked wire-service release.

events.headline: ISARA and Carahsoft announce US public-sector distribution partnership
events.summary: ISARA and Carahsoft Technology announced that Carahsoft will act as ISARA's public-sector distributor, making its cryptographic inventory, posture-management and post-quantum offerings available through Carahsoft's resellers and contract vehicles such as NASA SEWP V and ITES-SW2.

events.headline: Island raises US$400M Series F at a US$6.4B valuation
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2026-09-24 that Island raised a US$400 million Series F led by Evolution Equity Partners at a US$6.4 billion valuation, taking total funding to well over US$1 billion. The vendor's about page gives the same round and valuation.

events.headline: Island raises US$250M Series E at a US$4.8B valuation
events.summary: BankInfoSecurity reported on 2025-03-27 that Island raised a US$250 million Series E led by Coatue Management at a US$4.8 billion valuation, bringing the total raised to US$730 million.

events.headline: Island launches Enterprise Platform extending browser controls to other browsers, desktop apps and networks
events.summary: Island announced the Island Enterprise Platform: the Enterprise Browser, an extension for consumer browsers, a desktop component for native applications, and shared services for AI, network, data, identity and endpoint, all under one management console and policy set.

events.headline: Island announces ISO/IEC 27001 certification for the Enterprise Browser
events.summary: Island said in a post dated 2025-05-20 that its Enterprise Browser had recently been certified against ISO/IEC 27001. The post does not give the certificate dates or the certification boundary.

events.headline: Jazz emerges from stealth with US$61M in seed and Series A funding
events.summary: Jazz announced its public launch with US$61 million in combined seed and Series A funding led by Glilot Capital Partners and Team8, with Ten Eleven Ventures, Merlin Ventures, Encoded Ventures and MassMutual Ventures taking part. SecurityWeek and BankInfoSecurity reported the launch the same day.

events.headline: Jazz appoints six senior leaders
events.summary: Jazz announced six senior appointments or promotions: heads of sales, revenue operations, marketing, human resources and research and development, and a chief operating officer.

events.headline: Jazz's Melody investigator released as an app on CrowdStrike Foundry
events.summary: Jazz said its agentic investigator, Melody, is available as an app in the CrowdStrike Foundry catalogue. Data protection signals already collected by the Falcon sensor feed Melody's investigations and findings are returned to the Falcon record, with no new agent needed to start.

events.headline: JetBrains discloses breach of its Cadence cloud service through an unpatched TeamCity server
events.summary: JetBrains disclosed on 2026-08-28, with updates to 2026-09-03, that attackers had gained unauthorised access to Cadence, a JetBrains-hosted compute service used from PyCharm. Reported by The Hacker News on 2026-09-05: the intruders exploited TeamCity flaw CVE-2026-63077 on a server JetBrains had not patched, were active from 2026-08-08 to 2026-08-24, and exposed user names, email addresses, a 2024 server backup with credentials, and AWS credentials. The affected server was taken offline. The reports do not say that JetBrains AI or the IDEs were affected.

events.headline: Centana Growth Partners buys Jumio's assets out of Chapter 11
events.summary: Jumio announced that a Delaware bankruptcy court approved the sale of substantially all its assets to an acquisition vehicle of Centana Growth Partners after a court-supervised auction. TechCrunch later reported the price as US$850,000 and that the business continued under the Jumio name as a new company.

events.headline: Jumio names Bala Kumar president and interim chief executive
events.summary: Biometric Update reported that Robert Prigge, chief executive since 2016, was replaced by Bala Kumar, previously chief product and technology officer, as president and interim chief executive while a permanent successor was sought.

events.headline: Jumio appoints Mark Lorion as chief executive
events.summary: Jumio announced Mark Lorion, formerly chief executive of Tempo Software, as chief executive. Bala Kumar remained president and chief product and technology officer.

events.headline: Jumio appoints Matt DeLauro as chief revenue officer
events.summary: Jumio announced Matt DeLauro, most recently president of SEON Technologies, as chief revenue officer.

events.headline: Jumio completes worldwide rollout of selfie.DONE reusable identity
events.summary: Jumio announced availability of selfie.DONE in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, completing a rollout that began in Latin America and continued in North America and Asia-Pacific during 2026.

events.headline: JumpCloud acquires identity threat detection company Breez
events.summary: JumpCloud announced it had acquired Breez, described as an identity threat detection, investigation and response platform, to enhance its identity threat detection and response capabilities. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: JumpCloud acquires Brazilian managed service provider MacSolution
events.summary: JumpCloud announced the acquisition of MacSolution, which it described as its largest managed service provider in the Americas, to build a go-to-market hub in São Paulo. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Backbase acquires Kasisto and folds its agentic AI platform into the Backbase Banking OS
events.summary: Backbase announced on 2026-06-23 that it had acquired Kasisto. Kasisto's agentic AI platform, financial-services intelligence and New York-based team became part of Backbase and its Banking OS. The price was not disclosed. A Backbase blog post of 2026-07-13 states that Kasisto is no longer a separate company, and kasisto.com now redirects to backbase.com.

events.headline: Backbase names separate CTOs for digital banking and agentic banking
events.summary: Backbase, which acquired Kasisto in June 2026, announced on 2026-11-10 that Greg Fahy becomes Chief Technology Officer for Digital Banking and Deepak Pandey becomes Chief Technology Officer for Agentic Banking. The release says Pandey's organisation is responsible for Conversational Banking, which Backbase says became generally available in October and runs in production at more than 10 banks.

events.headline: KeeperPAM made available to all customers
events.summary: Keeper's Admin Console 17.1.0 release notes of 2025-02-13 state that KeeperPAM is available for all customers. The vendor's July 2026 blog gives February 2025 as the launch of KeeperPAM.

events.headline: Keeper's government platform listed as FedRAMP Certified at the High level
events.summary: The FedRAMP Marketplace lists 'Keeper ICAM & Identity Security Platform for Government' (package FR2116544598A) as FedRAMP Certified, Rev5 type, Agency path, Class D (High), certified since 2025-12-18, with eight authorisation letters on record when read on 2026-11-21.

events.headline: Keeper launches an emergency breach response service built around KeeperPAM
events.summary: Keeper Security announced on 2026-11-18 a global emergency service for organisations under active attack. According to the company, requests go through an emergency portal to its solution engineering team, which helps deploy KeeperPAM to revoke standing privileges and rotate compromised credentials. Keeper does not publish pricing and says commercial terms are discussed after containment.

events.headline: Keycard leaves stealth with $38 million in seed and Series A funding
events.summary: Keycard announced on 2025-10-21 that it had raised $38 million and opened early access to its identity and access platform for AI agents. SecurityWeek reported on 2025-10-22 that the total comprised an $8 million seed round co-led by Andreessen Horowitz and Boldstart Ventures and a $30 million Series A led by Acrew Capital.

events.headline: Keycard acquires Runebook
events.summary: Keycard announced on 2025-11-20 that it had acquired Runebook, whose Tome product connects Model Context Protocol servers, and that the team was joining to extend Keycard's integrations and SDKs. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Keycard acquires Anchor.dev
events.summary: Keycard announced on 2026-02-10 that it had acquired Anchor.dev, a developer-infrastructure company working on certificate automation, and that its two founders were joining. SiliconANGLE reported the deal the same day. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Keycard launches Keycard for Multi-Agent Apps
events.summary: Keycard's blog lists the announcement of Keycard for Multi-Agent Apps on 2026-05-13. Help Net Security reported on 2026-05-15 that it extends the platform to session-based, delegated access among autonomous agents, with Python and TypeScript SDKs, and quoted a product manager at Chime saying its engineers had agents running against production systems within days.

events.headline: Keycard introduces an integration for Temporal's Python SDK
events.summary: In a blog post dated 2026-11-10, Keycard introduced Keycard for Temporal, an integration for Temporal's Python SDK that the company says lets AI agents be authorised inside Temporal activities without access tokens being stored in workflow history. The post is mainly a how-to guide and does not describe a formal partnership with Temporal.

events.headline: Sixth Street Growth takes significant minority stake in Keyfactor at about $1.3B valuation
events.summary: Keyfactor announced a minority investment from Sixth Street Growth at an enterprise value of roughly $1.3 billion, with Insight Partners remaining an investor and two Sixth Street representatives joining the board. The amount invested was not disclosed. Recorded because it changed the ownership structure.

events.headline: Keyfactor acquires InfoSec Global and the CipherInsights product from Quantum Xchange
events.summary: Keyfactor announced it had bought Toronto-based InfoSec Global, maker of the AgileSec cryptographic discovery and agility products, and CipherInsights, a passive network sensor for cryptographic discovery, from Quantum Xchange. Terms were not disclosed. BankInfoSecurity reported InfoSec Global had 46 employees and that deeper product integration was planned over the following 12 months.

events.headline: Keyfactor announces FedRAMP Moderate authorisation for its government certificate lifecycle service
events.summary: Keyfactor announced that Keyfactor for Government Certificate Lifecycle Automation as a Service received FedRAMP Moderate authorisation. The announcement does not mention AgileSec, so it is not evidence about that product.

events.headline: Keyfactor announces $1B+ growth investment led by Summit Partners
events.summary: Keyfactor announced a strategic growth investment of more than $1 billion led by Summit Partners. Existing investors Insight Partners and Sixth Street Growth are to keep significant ownership, and two Summit managing directors are to join the board on closing. Valuation and stake sizes were not disclosed.

events.headline: Keyfactor releases AgileSec 3.6 with CBOM export and GCP KMS discovery
events.summary: Keyfactor announced AgileSec 3.6. Listed changes include CBOM export, a Google Cloud KMS sensor, improved detection of TLS 1.3 key exchange and post-quantum algorithms, a Tanium integration, SAML role-mapping improvements and unified Helm charts for Amazon EKS and Microsoft AKS.

events.headline: Keygraph's open-source pentester reaches version 3.0
events.summary: TestingCatalog reported on 2026-09-07, in an article labelled sponsored, that Keygraph had released Shannon 3.0, the open-source pentester whose engine underlies the commercial platform, with a GitHub Action, a GitLab CI/CD component and SARIF output. Keygraph's site lists Shannon 3.0 as the current major version. The date is that of the article; the release date itself was not confirmed.

events.headline: Vista Equity Partners completes acquisition of KnowBe4
events.summary: Vista Equity Partners completed its acquisition of KnowBe4 at US$24.90 per share in cash. KnowBe4's shares stopped trading and were removed from the Nasdaq Global Select Market. KnowBe4 continues to trade under its own brand.

events.headline: KnowBe4 completes acquisition of Egress
events.summary: KnowBe4 completed its acquisition of cloud email security provider Egress, agreed on 2024-04-24, for an undisclosed price. The Egress products Defend, Prevent and Protect now form KnowBe4 Cloud Email Security.

events.headline: Kore.ai announces growth investment led by AllianceBernstein
events.summary: Kore.ai announced a strategic growth investment led by AllianceBernstein Private Credit Investors, with existing investors Vistara Growth, Beedie Capital and Sweetwater Private Equity taking part. The amount was not disclosed.

events.headline: Kore.ai launches the Artemis edition of its Agent Platform
events.summary: Kore.ai launched the Artemis edition of the Kore.ai Agent Platform, first on Microsoft Azure, with a declarative agent language, an AI architect agent and platform-level governance. VentureBeat reported that new customers start on Artemis and existing customers were planning migrations.

events.headline: LangChain raises US$125 million Series B at US$1.25 billion valuation
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2025-10-21: LangChain raised US$125 million at a US$1.25 billion valuation in a round led by IVP, with new investors CapitalG and Sapphire Ventures and existing investors Sequoia, Benchmark and Amplify.

events.headline: LangChain announces US$300 million Series C at US$3 billion valuation
events.summary: LangChain announced on 2026-11-13 a US$300 million Series C at a US$3 billion valuation led by existing investor CapitalG, with new investors including GIC and DFJ Growth. It said more than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith.

events.headline: LangChain announces ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification
events.summary: LangChain told customers through its trust centre on 2026-10-19 that it had achieved ISO/IEC 42001:2023 certification. Its FAQ gives the scope as the systems, teams and assets supporting generally available AI features in LangSmith for which LangChain manages the model.

events.headline: LangChain reorganises LangSmith around a per-agent record and announces the LangSmith Agent Platform
events.summary: LangChain announced on 2026-11-16 that LangSmith has been rebuilt around an agent record: each agent gets an owner, an immutable ID and a type, with environments and traces grouped under it. The company says agents on any OpenTelemetry-compatible platform can be registered alongside those built in LangSmith, and that the new version is available in cloud, bring-your-own-cloud and self-hosted deployments. No pricing change is mentioned.

events.headline: LangSmith adds access controls for trace inputs and outputs on Enterprise plans
events.summary: LangChain announced on 2026-11-17 three access controls for LangSmith: restricting who can see trace inputs and outputs, user groups with per-workspace permissions, and policies that decide trace visibility from run metadata such as a customer ID. The company says the controls are available on LangSmith Enterprise plans and that traces are still stored in full.

events.headline: LangChain puts LangSmith Tool Gateway into public beta
events.summary: LangChain announced on 2026-11-19 a public beta of LangSmith Tool Gateway, a managed layer between agents and their tools that handles credentials, identity and access for each tool call and traces the calls in LangSmith. According to the post, deny policies and the audit log require contacting LangChain, and the audit log is an Enterprise plan feature.

events.headline: ClickHouse acquires Langfuse alongside a US$400M Series D
events.summary: ClickHouse announced on 2026-01-16 that it had acquired Langfuse; terms were not disclosed. Langfuse said its whole team joined ClickHouse, that the product stays open source and self-hostable with no planned licensing changes, and that Langfuse Cloud continues with the same endpoints, contracts and support. SiliconANGLE reported the acquisition together with ClickHouse's US$400 million Series D at a US$15 billion valuation. ClickHouse is not a tracked vendor in this dataset, so the record stays under Langfuse.

events.headline: Lasso Security raises $30 million in round led by ClearSky
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-09-02, and SecurityBrief on 2026-09-08, that Lasso Security raised $30 million in a round led by ClearSky, with Entrée Capital (which led the 2023 seed round), iAngels, Singtel Innov8, Mindset and Swish Data. Neither report named the stage. SiliconANGLE put total funding at more than $37 million. The company said revenue had grown more than 500% in twelve months, without giving a figure.

events.headline: Lasso Security launches LEAP, a guardrail engine that runs on CPUs
events.summary: Alongside its funding round, Lasso launched LEAP, a guardrail engine that the company says runs on ordinary server CPUs and returns a verdict in under five milliseconds. It works with RAPID, a self-hosted model that handles the decisions needing judgement against a plain-language policy. Performance figures are the company's own and were not independently tested in the reports retrieved.

events.headline: Lema AI emerges from stealth with US$24M in funding
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2026-02-09 that Lema AI emerged from stealth with US$24 million raised across seed and Series A rounds from Team8, F2 Venture Capital and Salesforce Ventures. Ynetnews reported that Team8 led the Series A and F2 led the seed.

events.headline: Lema releases Outreach Campaigns for sending one questionnaire to many vendors
events.summary: Lema's blog, in a post its blog index dates 2026-11-12, announced Outreach Campaigns, a feature for sending a single questionnaire to many vendors at once and tracking the responses outside regular assessments, aimed at urgent situations such as a newly disclosed vulnerability. The company says it is available to all Lema customers.

events.headline: LexisNexis Risk Solutions data taken from its GitHub account; about 364,000 people notified
events.summary: Reported by SecurityWeek and The Record on 2025-05-28: an unauthorised party acquired LexisNexis Risk Solutions data from a third-party software development platform, which the company confirmed was its GitHub account, on 2024-12-25; the company learned of it on 2025-04-01. A Maine attorney general filing put the number of people affected at 364,333. The data included names, contact details, Social Security numbers, driver's licence numbers and dates of birth. The company said its own systems, infrastructure and products were not compromised. The reports do not mention ThreatMetrix.

events.headline: LexisNexis Risk Solutions adds AI-agent detection for government agencies in ThreatMetrix and BehavioSec
events.summary: LexisNexis Risk Solutions announced on 2026-11-10 what it calls Know Your Agent intelligence for government agencies: signals meant to show when an AI agent, rather than a person or a conventional bot, is interacting with a digital government system. The release says the capability is available with LexisNexis ThreatMetrix and LexisNexis BehavioSec; it gives no pricing.

events.headline: Magnitude emerges from stealth with US$10M seed round
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2026-06-16 that Magnitude emerged from stealth with US$10 million in seed funding led by Ballistic Ventures, offering AI agents for third-party risk management.

events.headline: PAM360 build 8551 fixes an authentication bypass and a SQL injection flaw
events.summary: According to ManageEngine's PAM360 release notes, build 8551 of 2026-06-09 fixed CVE-2026-12263, an authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-11840, a SQL injection flaw. Earlier 2026 builds fixed CVE-2026-5785 (SQL injection, 2 April), CVE-2026-6213 (remote code execution in a third-party package, 7 April) and CVE-2026-8326 (path traversal in a third-party library, 22 May). The release notes read do not say whether any was exploited.

events.headline: PAM360 hotfix build 8601 fixes a remote code execution flaw
events.summary: According to ManageEngine's PAM360 release notes, hotfix build 8601 of 2026-07-30 fixed CVE-2026-18199, a remote code execution vulnerability, and build 8561 of 2026-07-07 fixed CVE-2026-14828, a SQL injection flaw. The release notes read do not say whether either was exploited.

events.headline: Microsoft selects Marvell LiquidSecurity HSMs for Azure Cloud HSM
events.summary: Marvell announced that Microsoft chose its LiquidSecurity hardware security modules for Azure Cloud HSM, a single-tenant service, in addition to Azure Key Vault and Managed HSM, which already ran on them. Microsoft's own overview of the service points to a NIST certificate held by Marvell.

events.headline: LS2 HSM module validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3 with ML-KEM and ML-DSA
events.summary: The NIST register shows certificate #5588 for the LS2 HSM Family module, validated on 2026-11-16 at FIPS 140-3 overall Level 3, with the post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA among its approved algorithms. The certificate runs to 2031-11-15.

events.headline: Marvell sells its automotive ethernet business to Infineon for US$2.5B
events.summary: Marvell's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 records the sale of its automotive ethernet business to Infineon Technologies AG on 2025-08-14 for US$2.5 billion in cash, with a pre-tax gain of US$1.8 billion.

events.headline: Marvell completes acquisition of Celestial AI
events.summary: Marvell's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 reports, as an event after the year end, that the acquisition of Celestial AI was completed on 2026-02-02. The business is unrelated to the hardware security module line.

events.headline: Marvell completes acquisition of XConn Technologies
events.summary: Marvell's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 reports, as an event after the year end, that the acquisition of XConn Technologies was completed on 2026-02-10. The business is unrelated to the hardware security module line.

events.headline: Marvell adds three independent directors, expanding its board from seven to ten
events.summary: Marvell announced on 2026-11-12 that Donna C. Morris of Walmart, Douglas R. Bettinger of Lam Research and Sasan K. Goodarzi of Intuit joined its board as independent directors, effective the same day. The release says the board grows from seven to ten members and mentions no departures.

events.headline: Marvell and Lumentum sign definitive agreement to combine in an all-stock deal; not yet closed
events.summary: Marvell announced in a press release dated 2026-11-02 that it and Lumentum had signed a definitive agreement, approved by both boards, under which Marvell will acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction: each Lumentum share converts into 4.500 Marvell shares, which Marvell put at an implied enterprise value of US$115 billion for Lumentum. Existing Marvell stockholders would own about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum stockholders about 33%, and Matt Murphy would remain chairman and chief executive. Marvell expects closing in the first half of calendar 2028, subject to approval by both companies' stockholders, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.

events.headline: Memcyco announces a new version of its impersonation protection that swaps stolen data for decoys
events.summary: Memcyco announced what it called its next-generation digital impersonation protection, adding replacement of credentials and card data entered on fake sites with decoy data, optional warnings to users on impersonating sites and real-time attack reports. The release gave no version number or availability date.

events.headline: Memcyco raises US$37 million Series A, bringing total funding to US$47 million
events.summary: Memcyco announced a US$37 million Series A led by NAventures (the venture arm of National Bank of Canada), E. León Jimenes and PagsGroup, with earlier investors Capri Ventures and Venture Guides taking part. SecurityWeek and SiliconANGLE reported total funding of US$47 million. The company said the money would fund expansion, including in Latin America.

events.headline: Trident Digital Tech Holdings and Memcyco agree an Asia-Pacific partnership
events.summary: Singapore-based Trident Digital Tech Holdings and Memcyco announced a partnership to integrate Memcyco's account takeover prevention into Trident's Tridentity identity platform for Asia-Pacific enterprises, with joint offerings expected to be sold from the third quarter of 2026.

events.headline: Memcyco publishes ISO/IEC 27001, 27017 and 27018 certificate and states SOC 2 Type II
events.summary: On 10 April 2026 Memcyco published an article and a Standards Institution of Israel certificate, marked year 2026, issued to Memcyco Ltd for ISO/IEC 27001:2022 with ISO/IEC 27017 and 27018. The article also states a SOC 2 Type II report. The date is that of the article; issue dates, scope and the SOC 2 period are not published.

events.headline: Memcyco joins Candescent's digital banking marketplace
events.summary: Memcyco announced it had become a certified marketplace partner of Candescent, a digital banking platform that says it serves more than 1,300 financial institutions, with its scam and account takeover detection to be integrated into Candescent's platform. Tech Times reported the partnership on 25 May 2026.

events.headline: Memcyco releases PoSA v1.11 with Attack Overview and a Risk API
events.summary: Memcyco released version 1.11 of PoSA, adding earlier identification of attacker devices, an Attack Overview that links events affecting the same user, and a Risk API that returns user and device risk scores with their underlying signals before access is granted. SecurityBrief reported the release on 13 October 2026.

events.headline: Memcyco appoints IBI Group as reseller in India
events.summary: Memcyco and Mumbai-based security firm IBI Group announced a partnership under which IBI Group will resell and co-market Memcyco's services in India, starting with banking and financial services, fintech, e-commerce and critical infrastructure.

events.headline: Meta opens Muse Spark 1.1 to US developers through a paid Meta Model API preview
events.summary: Reuters reported on 2026-07-09 that Meta released developer access to Muse Spark 1.1 in public preview through the Meta Model API for developers in the United States, at US$1.25 per million input tokens and US$4.25 per million output tokens. The report said the original Muse Spark, from the superintelligence team Meta formed in 2025, debuted in April 2026 and was expected to replace the Llama models in Meta's own apps.

events.headline: Meta releases Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model under Apache 2.0
events.summary: BetaNews reported on 2026-08-10 that Meta had released Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter open-weight model distilled from Muse Spark 1.2 under the Apache 2.0 licence, downloadable from Hugging Face, and that Mark Zuckerberg said the weights of Muse Spark 1.2 would also be released. The date shown is the report's date; the report places the release within the preceding day.

events.headline: Meta releases open weights for Muse Spark Open under the Muse Model License
events.summary: Meta announced on 2026-10-15 the open-weight Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter model with a one-million-token context window, under its Muse Model License. Weights are on Hugging Face, Amazon SageMaker AI, Google Cloud Model Garden and Microsoft Foundry, with hosted inference from providers including Together AI and Fireworks AI. The model card says offering the model as a paid service needs a separate agreement with Meta above US$20 million of revenue in 12 months.

events.headline: Meta cuts about 8,000 jobs, roughly 10% of its workforce
events.summary: Reported by NPR on 2026-04-23 and Al Jazeera on 2026-05-20: Meta told staff it would cut about 8,000 jobs, roughly 10% of its workforce, with effect from 20 May 2026, and would not fill about 6,000 open roles, as it increased spending on AI. NPR said a Meta spokesperson confirmed an internal memo first published by Bloomberg. Al Jazeera reported that about 7,000 employees were being moved into AI-related roles.

events.headline: Court rules for Meta in FTC antitrust case; FTC appeals in January 2026
events.summary: Meta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that on 2025-11-18 the court granted judgment in its favour in the antitrust case the US Federal Trade Commission filed in December 2020 over the Instagram and WhatsApp acquisitions, after a trial from 14 April to 27 May 2025, and that the FTC filed a notice of appeal on 2026-01-20.

events.headline: Spanish court awards about EUR 542 million against Meta Ireland in publishers' case
events.summary: Meta disclosed in its 2025 Form 10-K that on 2025-11-19 a Spanish court, in a case brought by the media association AMI against Meta Ireland, found no abuse of dominance but upheld an unfair-competition claim and awarded damages of about EUR 542 million. Meta said it has appealed.

events.headline: Microsoft Sentinel data lake reaches general availability
events.summary: Microsoft's release notes for September 2025 list the Microsoft Sentinel data lake as generally available, alongside previews of Sentinel graph and a Model Context Protocol server, and describe Sentinel as evolving from a SIEM into a security platform. The notes give the month but not the day; the last day of the month is used here.

events.headline: ACCC starts Federal Court proceedings over Microsoft 365 consumer plans with Copilot
events.summary: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission announced on 2025-10-27 that it had commenced Federal Court proceedings against Microsoft Australia and Microsoft Corporation. It alleges that about 2.7 million Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscribers were misled about their options when Copilot was integrated and prices rose, because a cheaper Classic plan without Copilot was not disclosed. The matter concerns consumer plans, not the enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. No outcome was found.

events.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI sign new definitive agreement after OpenAI recapitalisation
events.summary: Microsoft announced a new definitive agreement with OpenAI on 2025-10-28. Microsoft said it held about 27% of OpenAI Group PBC on an as-converted diluted basis, that its IP rights to OpenAI models and products ran to 2032, and that OpenAI remained its frontier model partner. Microsoft's fiscal 2026 Form 10-K describes the interest as approximately 25% and records a dilution gain from the recapitalisation.

events.headline: Azure Front Door incident disrupts Azure and Microsoft services for about eight hours
events.summary: Microsoft stated in its post-incident review that between 15:41 UTC on 29 October and 00:05 UTC on 30 October 2025 customers and Microsoft services using Azure Front Door and Azure CDN had connection timeouts and DNS resolution failures. Microsoft listed Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID (identity and access management, user management and mobility management policy services), Microsoft Sentinel threat intelligence, Microsoft Purview and the Azure portal among the services affected, and said a specific sequence of valid customer configuration changes produced incompatible metadata that exposed a latent bug in the Front Door data plane.

events.headline: Azure AI Foundry is renamed Microsoft Foundry
events.summary: Microsoft's Ignite announcement of 2025-11-18 presents its AI development platform as Microsoft Foundry. Microsoft's documentation lists Azure AI Studio and Azure AI Foundry as the previous brand names and Azure AI Services as the previous name of Foundry Tools. The same announcement said Foundry Models had added models from Anthropic and Cohere.

events.headline: Microsoft, NVIDIA and Anthropic announce partnerships; Claude models come to Foundry
events.summary: Microsoft announced on 2025-11-18 that Anthropic had committed to buy US$30 billion of Azure compute capacity, that Claude models would be available to Microsoft Foundry customers and would continue to be offered in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and that Microsoft would invest up to US$5 billion and NVIDIA up to US$10 billion in Anthropic.

events.headline: Microsoft Ireland Operations named a critical ICT third-party provider under DORA
events.summary: Microsoft stated that on 2025-11-18 the European Supervisory Authorities published their list of critical ICT third-party providers under the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act and that Microsoft Ireland Operations Limited is on it, making it subject to the ESAs' oversight mechanism. This is a supervisory designation, not an enforcement action. Microsoft said it would cooperate with the oversight.

events.headline: Microsoft and OpenAI amend agreement; Microsoft's licence to OpenAI IP becomes non-exclusive
events.summary: Microsoft announced on 2026-04-27 an amended agreement with OpenAI. Microsoft said it remains OpenAI's primary cloud partner, that OpenAI can now serve its products on any cloud, that Microsoft's licence to OpenAI IP runs to 2032 and is now non-exclusive, that Microsoft will stop paying a revenue share to OpenAI, and that OpenAI's revenue share payments to Microsoft continue to 2030 subject to a cap. The Register reported the change the same day.

events.headline: UK CMA opens strategic market status investigation into Microsoft business software
events.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority published on 2026-05-14 that it had opened an investigation into whether to designate Microsoft as having strategic market status in respect of its business software ecosystem under Part 1 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. The CMA case page lists the case as open.

events.headline: OpenAI added to Microsoft's Online Services subprocessor list
events.summary: Microsoft's documentation states that OpenAI was added to the Microsoft Online Services Subprocessors List on 2026-06-23 and that OpenAI-operated models became available in Copilot experiences from 2026-07-09, in addition to OpenAI models that Microsoft operates in Azure. Microsoft says its Product Terms and Data Protection Addendum apply, that these models are excluded from in-country processing commitments and that they are not available in government clouds.

events.headline: Microsoft cuts about 4,800 roles, around 2.1% of its workforce
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch and by Reuters (carried by KSL.com) on 2026-07-06: Microsoft cut about 4,800 roles, about 2.1% of its global workforce, with Xbox and commercial sales most affected. TechCrunch reported that the chief people officer's memo said the roles were not being replaced by AI. Neither report names the security, identity or AI platform teams as affected.

events.headline: Microsoft discloses and fixes CVSS 10.0 remote code execution flaw in Entra ID
events.summary: Reported by Help Net Security on 2026-08-21 and by The Hacker News: Microsoft published CVE-2026-69836, a deserialisation flaw in Microsoft Entra ID rated CVSS 10.0 that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code over a network. Microsoft said it had already fixed the service and that customers needed to take no action. Both outlets reported that the advisory first marked the flaw as exploited and that Microsoft then changed this and said it had not been exploited in the wild.

events.headline: Azure OpenAI and Foundry services degraded in Sweden Central for about six hours
events.summary: Microsoft stated in a post-incident review that between 10:03 and 15:58 UTC on 29 September 2026 Azure OpenAI Service, Foundry Agent Service, Foundry Models and Azure AI services in the Sweden Central region returned intermittent failures, higher latency and HTTP 500 and 503 errors. Microsoft attributed this to a planned deployment that cleared internal caches at peak time and, with two caching defects, sent about 20 times normal traffic to a regional backend service.

events.headline: UK CMA proposes to designate Microsoft with strategic market status in business software
events.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority published on 2026-10-16 a proposed decision to designate Microsoft as having strategic market status in respect of its business software ecosystem, with a roadmap of possible interventions, and opened a consultation. The decision is provisional; no final designation was found.

events.headline: Worldwide Microsoft 365 outage lasts nearly 24 hours; Copilot among services affected
events.summary: Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-11-16 and by ITPro: an outage that began on 12 November 2026 disrupted Microsoft 365 services worldwide for nearly 24 hours, including Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams and Copilot. Both reported Microsoft's preliminary account that a latent software defect, extra load after a Teams failover and reduced server capacity caused a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive. A final post-incident report had not been published when this was recorded.

events.headline: Microsoft announces MAI-Thinking-1, its first in-house reasoning model, at Build 2026
events.summary: Reported by Thurrott.com on 2026-06-02: at Build 2026 Microsoft released models built by its in-house AI team, including MAI-Thinking-1, described as its first reasoning model and offered in private preview on Microsoft Foundry, together with MAI-Image-2.5, MAI-Transcribe-1.5, MAI-Voice-2 and MAI-Code-1. The report said Microsoft planned to make the models available on Fireworks AI, Baseten and OpenRouter.

events.headline: MAI-Thinking-1 enters public preview in Microsoft Foundry
events.summary: Microsoft AI stated on 2026-08-12 that MAI-Thinking-1 was available in public preview through the Microsoft Foundry model catalogue and a browser playground, describing it as a sparse mixture-of-experts model with a 256,000-token context window trained without distillation from third-party models. Microsoft's documentation of the same date lists it for global standard deployment only, without a service-level agreement while in preview.

events.headline: Microsoft AI announces MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7, MAI Cyber 2 Flash and other models at Ignite
events.summary: Microsoft AI announced on 2026-11-17 a set of new in-house models: MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, MAI Image 2.7 and 2.7 Flash, MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Realtime 1, a transcription model built on MAI Transcribe 2 and Decision 1.1. It also described MAI Licensed Weights, under which a customer customises an MAI model with its own data and runs it in its own Azure environment, initially through Microsoft's own engagement teams. Availability differs by model; MAI Code 2 Flash was described as a limited-access preview in Foundry.

events.headline: Microsoft's Ignite 2026 keynote: unified Copilot experience, more models for Foundry, Cobalt 200 VMs generally available
events.summary: Microsoft published an edited version of Satya Nadella's Ignite keynote on 2026-11-17. It describes a unified Copilot experience spanning Chat, Cowork, Code and Autopilot, says GPT 6.2 and Meta's latest models are coming to Foundry, and says Cobalt 200 virtual machines are generally available. Microsoft also claims its Maia 300 chip delivers 40% more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. The post gives no prices and, for most items, no availability dates.

events.headline: Microsoft makes Perception security agents generally available and folds Sentinel SIEM features into Defender
events.summary: In a Microsoft Security blog post dated 2026-11-17, Microsoft said Perception, a system that coordinates attack-simulation, detection and remediation agents, is generally available. It also said the core of an Integrated Security Operations Center in Defender is generally available, giving eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers Sentinel SIEM features and 90-day default retention for Defender data. Entra dynamic permissions and Conditional Access controls are in limited preview, and several Purview data-protection features for Copilot are due in preview or general availability in January 2027. No prices are listed.

events.headline: Microsoft discloses a critical Azure OpenAI elevation-of-privilege flaw, already mitigated in the service
events.summary: According to the Microsoft Security Response Center entry released on 2026-11-10, CVE-2026-119990 is a missing-authentication flaw in Azure OpenAI that could let an unauthenticated attacker elevate privileges over a network; Microsoft scores it CVSS 9.8. Microsoft says the issue has been fully mitigated in the service, that customers need take no action, and that it was not exploited or publicly disclosed beforehand. Qualys lists it among the critical issues in its review of the November updates.

events.headline: Microsoft patches a remote code execution flaw in Microsoft Defender rated CVSS 8.8
events.summary: According to the Microsoft Security Response Center entry released on 2026-11-10, CVE-2026-122194 is a null pointer dereference in Microsoft Defender that could let an unauthenticated attacker run code over a network, with user interaction required; Microsoft scores it CVSS 8.8 and says customer action is required. Microsoft reports no exploitation or prior public disclosure and rates exploitation as less likely. The entry does not say which Defender products are affected.

events.headline: Malicious versions of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package published on PyPI
events.summary: Reported by The Hacker News and BleepingComputer on 2026-11-18: attackers published two malicious versions (1.26.1 and 1.26.2) of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI on 2026-11-17.
