Both outlets say the versions carried a credential stealer that ran whenever Python started and targeted cloud and CI credentials, that PyPI quarantined them, and that it is not known how the attacker obtained publishing access. The Hacker News, in an update dated 2026-11-20, quotes a Microsoft spokesperson saying the company made some repositories private while it investigates.

events.headline: Permira funds complete acquisition of Mimecast; shares delisted
events.summary: Permira announced that funds it advises completed the acquisition of Mimecast for about US$5.8 billion (US$80.00 per share in cash) on 17 May 2022. Mimecast's shares stopped trading and the company is no longer listed on any public market.

events.headline: Mimecast announces API-based deployment of its email security for Microsoft 365
events.summary: Mimecast announced an API-based deployment option that connects directly to Microsoft 365 without MX record changes, stating it offers the same detection as its gateway deployment, including BEC, URL, malware and account takeover protection.

events.headline: Mimecast appoints Ranjan Singh as chief executive, succeeding Marc van Zadelhoff
events.summary: Mimecast announced that Ranjan Singh, previously its chief product and technology officer, became chief executive officer and joined the board with immediate effect. Marc van Zadelhoff moved to a board advisor role.

events.headline: Mimecast announces Agent Risk Center beta and redesigned Managed Threat Response
events.summary: At Black Hat USA 2026 Mimecast announced a beta of Agent Risk Center for governing AI agents and a redesigned Managed Threat Response service in which AI triages user-reported email and Mimecast analysts act on confirmed threats.

events.headline: Partner1 LLC files trademark suit against Mimecast Services in New York
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, Partner1 LLC filed a trademark suit against Mimecast Services, Ltd. in the Southern District of New York on 2025-11-04 (7:25-cv-09202), after Mimecast filed its own trademark suit against Partner1 in the same court on 2025-06-03 (7:25-cv-04635). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: MIND raises US$72M Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners
events.summary: BankInfoSecurity and SecurityWeek reported a US$72 million Series B led by Crosspoint Capital Partners, with earlier investors YL Ventures and Paladin Capital Group also taking part. Total funding reached US$112 million, including a US$30 million Series A in June 2025.

events.headline: MIND announces ISO/IEC 42001 certification
events.summary: MIND said it had been certified against ISO/IEC 42001, the AI management system standard, after an independent assessment covering 38 controls across the AI systems it deploys. The certification body is not named in the announcement.

events.headline: MIND adds email data loss prevention for Microsoft Exchange
events.summary: MIND announced an email module that classifies message and attachment content against the recipient and can block outbound Microsoft Exchange mail before delivery, using the same policies as its other channels.

events.headline: MIND makes Microsoft 365 and Copilot integrations generally available
events.summary: MIND announced generally available integrations with Microsoft Copilot, Purview, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Edge and Exchange, including reading and applying Purview sensitivity labels and a Windows endpoint agent, and said the product can be bought through the Microsoft Marketplace.

events.headline: Mindgard raises $30 million Series A led by Album VC
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2026-08-12 that Mindgard had raised a US$30 million Series A led by Album VC, with Karma Ventures and existing investors .406 Ventures, Atlantic Bridge, IQ Capital and Lakestar, bringing total funding to close to US$42 million. The company said the money would go to product, engineering, sales and marketing.

events.headline: Mindgard adds hand-off of validated findings and fixes to customers' guardian agents
events.summary: In a release dated 10 November 2026, Mindgard said its AI security testing platform can now pass validated attack findings and mitigation guidance, including code-level fixes and guardrail rules, to a customer's own defensive guardian agents so that they can act on them. The company presents this as removing manual ticketing between finding and fixing a weakness. The release gives no pricing or packaging details.

events.headline: Mistral AI completes EUR 1.7 billion Series C led by ASML
events.summary: Mistral AI's about page dates its Series C to 2025-09-09. Euronews reported the round was EUR 1.7 billion, led by ASML, at a EUR 11.7 billion valuation.

events.headline: Italian competition authority closes Mistral AI chatbot investigation with commitments
events.summary: The Italian Competition Authority (AGCM) announced on 2026-04-30 that it closed its unfair commercial practices investigation into Mistral AI SAS over warnings about inaccurate AI output, accepting commitments and making no finding of infringement.

events.headline: Mistral AI discloses supply chain attack on its SDK packages
events.summary: Mistral AI disclosed on 2026-05-12 that malicious versions of its npm and PyPI SDK packages were published through the Mini Shai-Hulud supply chain attack and that non-core code repositories were accessed. Mistral stated hosted services and user data were not compromised and closed its investigation on 2026-05-14.

events.headline: Mistral AI raises EUR 3 billion Series D at a valuation above EUR 21 billion
events.summary: Mistral AI raised EUR 3 billion in a Series D with Samsung Electronics, PSG Equity and the EU-backed Scaleup Europe Fund, at a valuation of more than EUR 21 billion, according to Reuters and Euronews.

events.headline: Mistral AI renames its Le Chat assistant Vibe and adds an agentic Work mode
events.summary: Mistral AI announced that Le Chat is now Vibe, one agent and one licence across work and code, with existing conversations, settings and plans carried over. Work mode connects to Google Workspace, Outlook, SharePoint, Slack and GitHub and can run scheduled tasks; the vendor said it would soon sunset the original Chat mode. The Decoder reported the change the same day.

events.headline: Mistral AI fixes six shell permission vulnerabilities in the Vibe command-line tool
events.summary: Mistral AI disclosed in advisory MAI-2026-003, published on 2026-09-14, that six shell permission check flaws (CVE-2026-87983 to CVE-2026-87988) in the Vibe command-line tool could let crafted commands run without an approval prompt. It released a fix in version 2.25.4 on 2026-09-12, a day after the CVE advisories were published by a third party, and reported no exploitation or customer data exposure.

events.headline: ModelOp launches agentic AI chat interface and governance controls for AI agents
events.summary: ModelOp announced a conversational interface for querying governance information and new agent, metrics and proxy services for importing agents, approving them per use case, blocking unapproved agents and tracking token cost.

events.headline: ModelOp names Dave Trier chief executive; co-founder Pete Foley moves to the board
events.summary: ModelOp announced that Dave Trier, previously its senior vice president of product, became chief executive. Co-founder Pete Foley stepped back from day-to-day operations and remains a board member.

events.headline: ModelOp launches the AI Delivery Engine (MADE)
events.summary: ModelOp announced an agent-based engine that runs intake, risk analysis, testing, documentation and review steps under policy alongside its Enterprise AI Command Center. The announcement does not state general availability.

events.headline: ModelOp and AHEAD announce partnership on governed AI delivery
events.summary: ModelOp and IT services provider AHEAD announced a partnership in which AHEAD provides strategy and implementation services around ModelOp's platform.

events.headline: ModelOp releases ModelOp Center 3.5 with agent discovery across Microsoft and Amazon platforms
events.summary: ModelOp announced version 3.5, adding discovery of agents from Microsoft Agent 365 and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, comparison against the approved inventory, automated risk tiering and approval workflows for discovered agents, and token usage tracking.

events.headline: MongoDB completes acquisition of embedding-model developer Voyage AI
events.summary: MongoDB's 10-K for fiscal 2026 states that it acquired all outstanding shares of Voyage AI in February 2025 for purchase consideration of about US$160.9 million in shares and cash, and that Voyage AI embedding and reranking models are offered through Atlas. The filing gives the month only; the first of the month is used.

events.headline: MongoDB previews search and vector search for Community Edition and Enterprise Server
events.summary: MongoDB announced a public preview of full-text and vector search for self-managed Community Edition and Enterprise Server deployments, using a separate search process alongside the database.

events.headline: CJ Desai succeeds Dev Ittycheria as MongoDB president and CEO
events.summary: PYMNTS reported on 2025-11-03 that Dev Ittycheria would retire as president and chief executive after 11 years and that Chirantan 'CJ' Desai, previously president of product and engineering at Cloudflare, would succeed him with effect from 10 November 2025.

events.headline: CSA STAR registry shows MongoDB Cloud Platform Level 1 and Level 2 entries renewed
events.summary: The Cloud Security Alliance STAR registry lists a Level 1 self-assessment and a Level 2 STAR Certification for MongoDB Cloud Platform, each created or renewed on 19 May 2026.

events.headline: MongoDB Search and Vector Search reach general availability for self-managed deployments
events.summary: MongoDB announced general availability of search and vector search for Community Edition, with the search process available under the Server Side Public License, and for Enterprise Advanced as a paid add-on deployed on Kubernetes.

events.headline: MongoDB CEO CJ Desai steps down; Dev Ittycheria returns as interim CEO
events.summary: MongoDB announced that CJ Desai had stepped down as president and chief executive with immediate effect to take a role at Meta Platforms, that former chief executive Dev Ittycheria was appointed interim president and chief executive, and that the board had begun a search for a permanent successor. The company reaffirmed its financial guidance.

events.headline: Adversary proceeding Pitta v. MongoDB filed in New Jersey bankruptcy court
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, Pitta v. MongoDB, Inc. was filed in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey on 2025-10-11 (25-02012). The listing shows no nature of suit. Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: MongoDB says Atlas for Government has FedRAMP Class D (High) certification and now runs on Azure Government
events.summary: MongoDB announced on 19 November 2026 that MongoDB Atlas for Government has achieved FedRAMP Class D certification, the class formerly called FedRAMP High, and that the service now supports Microsoft Azure Government alongside AWS and Google Cloud. The release says native vector search is available inside that environment. This is the company's own statement; the release does not give an authorization date or sponsoring agency, and the FedRAMP Marketplace listing was not checked.

events.headline: Monitaur launches Guided Risk Assessment and Evidence Mapping
events.summary: Monitaur announced a guided risk assessment that applies a common methodology to each AI use case, and evidence mapping that scans customer files and maps extracted evidence to controls.

events.headline: Monitaur adds vendor governance for third-party AI
events.summary: Monitaur announced a vendor governance capability with a central inventory of third-party AI vendors and pre-mapped controls for foundation models and agentic AI. The vendor's press index dates the release 2025-09-30.

events.headline: Monitaur offers FlightSim testing tool as a standalone product
events.summary: Monitaur announced that FlightSim, its black-box validation tool that produces scorecards on reliability, performance, bias and security, is available without a full platform licence.

events.headline: Milliman and Monitaur announce AI governance alliance
events.summary: Milliman and Monitaur announced a collaboration under which Milliman advisers help clients set up governance programmes on the platform and provide independent reviews of high-stakes AI systems within it.

events.headline: Moonshot AI raises about $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 7 May 2026 that Moonshot AI had raised about $2 billion at a $20 billion valuation in a round led by Long-Z Investments, the venture arm of Meituan, with Tsinghua Capital, China Mobile and CPE Yuanfeng participating. It reported existing backers including Alibaba, Tencent, HongShan, ZhenFund, IDG Capital and 5Y Capital, about $3.9 billion raised over the previous six months, and annual recurring revenue above $200 million in April 2026.

events.headline: US agencies' advisory names Moonshot AI among China-based companies alleged to have distilled US models
events.summary: CISA, the NSA and the FBI published advisory AA26-251A on 8 September 2026. It names Moonshot AI (Beijing Moonshot Technology Co., Ltd.) among six China-based companies and alleges that since at least mid-2025 it ran a widespread campaign using outputs of US companies' models to train Kimi K2 and Kimi K3, in breach of those companies' terms. The advisory is an allegation by the agencies; no response from Moonshot AI was found.

events.headline: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3.1 Pro
events.summary: Moonshot AI's site lists a research post for Kimi K3.1 Pro dated 24 October 2026, describing a 3-trillion-parameter-class model with a one-million-token context window. The weights are published on Hugging Face under a custom licence and the model is the flagship on the Kimi API platform.

events.headline: MOSTLY AI's operating company ceases operations and enters liquidation
events.summary: Reported by Trending Topics on 2026-03-04: chief executive Tobias Hann said the Vienna company was ceasing operations after nearly nine years and denied a rumour that it had filed for bankruptcy; the outlet said attempts to sell the company in the second half of 2025 had not succeeded. The Austrian company register publications show dissolution and liquidation of Mostly AI Solutions MP GmbH entered on 2026-03-14, a creditor call published on 2026-03-19 naming Michael Platzer and Tobias Hann as liquidators, and deletion of the company entered on 2026-09-09.

events.headline: Syntho acquires the MOSTLY AI trademark and related assets
events.summary: Syntho, a synthetic data company in Amsterdam, announced it had acquired the MOSTLY AI trademark and related assets and that the brand would continue as "MOSTLY AI, powered by Syntho". The announcement does not list the assets, give terms, or say what happens to existing customers, the hosted platform or the open-source SDK. Syntho is not a tracked vendor.

events.headline: ServiceNow agrees to acquire Moveworks for about US$2.85 billion
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2025-03-10 that ServiceNow had agreed to buy Moveworks for US$2.85 billion in cash and shares. The report described Moveworks as founded in 2016, based in Mountain View, with more than 500 employees and slightly more than US$300 million raised from investors including Tiger Global, ICONIQ Growth and Kleiner Perkins.

events.headline: ServiceNow completes acquisition of Moveworks
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2025-12-15 that it had completed the acquisition of Moveworks, saying the AI Assistant, enterprise search and Reasoning Engine would be combined with its workflow platform. ServiceNow's Form 10-K for 2025 records that it acquired all outstanding shares of Moveworks, Inc. on that date for total purchase consideration of US$2.4 billion, partly paid in shares.

events.headline: ServiceNow launches EmployeeWorks, built on Moveworks; Moveworks stays available standalone
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2026-02-26 that EmployeeWorks, which combines Moveworks' conversational AI and enterprise search with ServiceNow's portal and workflows, was generally available. The release said Moveworks continues to be offered as a standalone product within the ServiceNow portfolio.

events.headline: VE Opening LLC files patent suit against Moveworks in Texas; terminated April 2026
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, VE Opening LLC filed a patent suit against Moveworks, Inc. in the Western District of Texas on 2025-08-22 (7:25-cv-00361, terminated 2025-10-08; 1:25-cv-01632, terminated 2026-04-20). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the filings were not read and the listing does not show how the case ended.

events.headline: Nasdaq agrees to buy Verafin for US$2.75 billion
events.summary: CNBC reported on 2020-11-19 that Nasdaq agreed to buy Verafin, a fraud detection company founded in 2003 with more than 2,000 financial institution customers in North America, for US$2.75 billion in cash. Nasdaq's Form 10-K for 2025 refers to the acquisition as completed in 2021.

events.headline: European Commission opens antitrust investigation into Nasdaq and Deutsche Börse
events.summary: According to Nasdaq's Form 10-K for 2025, the European Commission opened a formal antitrust investigation in November 2025 into whether Nasdaq and Deutsche Börse breached EU competition rules by coordinating conduct in the listing, trading and clearing of financial derivatives, following an inspection at Nasdaq Stockholm in September 2024. Euronews reported the opening on 2025-11-06. The matter concerns the exchange business, not Nasdaq Verafin.

events.headline: Native exits stealth with US$42M in funding, including a US$31M Series A
events.summary: SecurityWeek and Globes reported on 2026-03-18 that Native had emerged from stealth with US$42 million in total funding, including a US$31 million Series A led by Ballistic Ventures with General Catalyst, YL Ventures and Merlin Ventures. Phil Venables, formerly chief information security officer of Google Cloud, joined the board.

events.headline: Yandex N.V. renamed Nebius Group N.V. after divesting its Russian businesses
events.summary: The company's annual report states that in July 2024 it completed the divestment of all its businesses in Russia and related businesses in certain international markets, which made up more than 95% of the group's revenues, assets and employees, and that it changed its name from Yandex N.V. to Nebius Group N.V. in August 2024. Trading in its shares on Nasdaq resumed on 21 October 2024. The date used is the name-change date in the SEC filer record.

events.headline: NVIDIA invests in Nebius through a securities purchase agreement
events.summary: A Schedule 13G filed by NVIDIA Corporation states that on 11 March 2026 it acquired a pre-funded warrant for 21,065,936 Nebius Class A shares under a securities purchase agreement with Nebius, and that with shares already held it beneficially owned 9.3% of the class as of 13 July 2026. SiliconANGLE reported the investment as US$2 billion.

events.headline: Nebius signs AI capacity agreement with Meta reported at up to US$27 billion
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 16 March 2026 that Meta agreed to take US$12 billion of dedicated AI compute capacity from Nebius and committed to buy up to US$15 billion more over five years if it is not sold to others. Nebius's annual report refers to longer-term customer contracts with Meta and Microsoft and says it has limited experience delivering contracts of that size.

events.headline: Nebius closes private offering of convertible senior notes raising about US$5.75 billion
events.summary: Nebius's newsroom lists an announcement dated 24 August 2026 that it closed a private offering of convertible senior notes with gross proceeds of about US$5.75 billion.

events.headline: Nebius acquires Inferize for its Token Factory inference service
events.summary: Nebius's newsroom lists an announcement dated 1 October 2026 that it acquired Inferize to strengthen the production inference stack of its Token Factory service. Terms were not shown in the listing.

events.headline: Nebius secures a US$3.5 billion financing facility with Citi
events.summary: Nebius's newsroom lists an announcement that it secured a US$3.5 billion financing facility with Citi; the listing shows the item under late October to November 2026 and the date used here is the earlier date shown.

events.headline: NC Holdings Limited becomes controlling shareholder of Netcraft Ltd
events.summary: Companies House records that NC Holdings Limited became the holder of 75% or more of the shares of Netcraft Ltd on 22 March 2022, and that the founder, Mike Prettejohn, ceased to be the controlling person on the same date. NC Holdings is owned by NC Topco Limited, whose 2025 accounts refer to the purchase of the Netcraft brand and technology in 2022. Netcraft continued to trade under its own name.

events.headline: Netcraft announces over US$100 million from Spectrum Equity and a new chief executive
events.summary: On 18 July 2023 Netcraft announced its first outside funding, of over US$100 million, from Spectrum Equity, and named Ryan Woodley as chief executive in place of the founder. TechCrunch and SecurityWeek reported the round the same day. The exact amount was not disclosed.

events.headline: Netcraft announces acquisition of Australian brand protection provider FraudWatch
events.summary: On 12 September 2023 Netcraft announced that it had acquired FraudWatch, a Melbourne-based online brand protection provider with a round-the-clock security operations centre. Terms were not disclosed. The parent company’s 2025 accounts say FraudWatch customers have since been moved to Netcraft’s systems and FraudWatch domains redirected to netcraft.com.

events.headline: Netcraft launches a free real-time threat API for infrastructure providers
events.summary: In a release dated 10 March 2025 Netcraft launched a JSON API that gives registrars, registries and hosting companies a real-time feed of abuse on their own infrastructure, as an alternative to email notifications.

events.headline: Netcraft becomes a Foundation member of GASA and agrees to share data with the Global Signal Exchange
events.summary: In a release dated 19 March 2025 Netcraft said it had become a Foundation member of the Global Anti-Scam Alliance and had entered a data-sharing agreement with the Global Signal Exchange.

events.headline: Netcraft launches Phone Scam Disruption
events.summary: On 14 October 2025 Netcraft launched Phone Scam Disruption, which detects and requests removal of phone numbers used in scam texts and calls that impersonate a customer’s brand. The release gave the company’s own figure of a 99.8% success rate across more than 50,000 takedowns with pilot customers.

events.headline: Netcraft launches Preemptive Domain Disruption
events.summary: On 17 March 2026 Netcraft launched Preemptive Domain Disruption, which links newly registered domains to known attack infrastructure and requests their removal before any content is published. The release gave the company’s own figure that about 90% of such domains were taken down within 24 hours for early customers.

events.headline: Netcraft appoints Darren Lee to its board
events.summary: On 25 August 2026 Netcraft announced that Darren Lee, formerly a senior executive at Proofpoint, had joined its board. Companies House records his appointment as a director of NC Topco Limited on 12 August 2026.

events.headline: Netskope lists on Nasdaq in US$1.04 billion initial public offering
events.summary: Netskope sold 54,970,000 Class A shares at US$19.00 each under a prospectus dated 17 September 2025, and its shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market as NTSK. The annual report gives net proceeds of about US$992.2M after underwriting discounts.

events.headline: Netskope CFO Andrew Del Matto to retire once successor is in place
events.summary: Netskope reported in a Form 8-K on 3 June 2026 that chief financial officer Andrew Del Matto will retire when a successor starts and will stay through the search and transition.

events.headline: Fortinet files patent suit against Netskope in Northern District of California
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, Fortinet, Inc. filed a patent suit against Netskope, Inc. in the Northern District of California on 2026-08-25 (4:26-cv-08886). The index also lists patent suits brought by Netskope against Fortinet in the same court in 2022 and on 2025-03-07. Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: Netskope appoints Carrie Francey as senior vice president of global channel sales
events.summary: Netskope announced on 10 November 2026 that Carrie Francey has joined as Senior Vice President of Global Channel Sales, leading its partner organisation including channel, MSP, MSSP, cloud marketplace and systems integrator programmes. The release says she previously led partner organisations at HPE, Microsoft, ServiceNow and Zendesk. It does not name a predecessor.

events.headline: NICE acquires financial-crime software company Actimize (2007)
events.summary: NICE's Form 20-F states that it acquired Actimize in 2007; CTech reported the price as $280 million. Only the year is sourced, so the event is dated 1 January 2007.

events.headline: Scott Russell becomes chief executive of NICE
events.summary: NICE's Form 20-F for 2025 states that Scott Russell assumed the role of chief executive officer in January 2025. The day is not stated, so the event is dated the first of the month.

events.headline: NICE reported to have put its Actimize financial-crime business up for sale
events.summary: CTech reported on 2025-11-24 that NICE had hired Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan to sell Actimize for $1.5 to $2 billion, and The Paypers carried the report on 2025-12-02, noting that it was unconfirmed. Neither article included a statement from NICE.

events.headline: NICE Actimize launches the Actimize Insights Network for shared counterparty risk intelligence
events.summary: NICE Actimize announced a network giving financial institutions real-time intelligence on payees and counterparties drawn from across participating institutions, aimed at stopping scam payments and finding mule accounts. Participants were not named.

events.headline: Brookfield reported to be in exclusive talks to buy Actimize from NICE for about $2 billion
events.summary: CTech reported on 2026-09-23, citing Sky News, that Brookfield's financial infrastructure arm had secured exclusivity to negotiate the purchase of Actimize for about $2 billion and that the deal could still fall through. On 2026-11-04 CTech reported that NICE's chief executive told the third-quarter earnings call the company was still working with advisers and had no update. No transaction had been announced as of 2026-11-20.

events.headline: NICE says it will cut about 5% of its global workforce
events.summary: Announced by NICE in its third-quarter 2026 results on 2026-11-04: it expects to reduce its global workforce by approximately 5%, with pre-tax restructuring charges of roughly $15 to $20 million, mostly in the fourth quarter. Reported by The Jerusalem Post and HR Katha on the same day as about 500 of roughly 10,000 employees, linked to the effect of AI on the customer-service software market.

events.headline: NICE announces NiCE Cognigy integrations with Microsoft Teams, Azure and Dynamics 365
events.summary: NICE announced that NiCE Cognigy had completed certification as a voice agent for Microsoft Teams Phone, able to answer calls and transfer callers with context, and a new integration with Azure, Teams and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. The offerings were stated to be available on Microsoft Marketplace.

events.headline: FinTegrity LLC files patent suit against NICE Ltd. in Eastern District of Texas
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, FinTegrity LLC filed a patent suit against NICE Ltd. in the Eastern District of Texas on 2025-03-12 (2:25-cv-00294). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: NICE launches next generation of NiCE Cognigy for building and orchestrating AI agents
events.summary: NICE announced on 12 November 2026 a new generation of its NiCE Cognigy platform, with a redesigned Agentic Experience Studio, agents assembled from reusable skills, step-by-step tracing of agent decisions and native speech-to-speech voice support. The release says default AI models are included in the conversation price, with premium third-party models billed by usage, and that existing production deployments keep running unchanged. No general availability date is stated.

events.headline: Noma Security raises $100 million Series B led by Evolution Equity Partners
events.summary: SecurityWeek, SiliconANGLE, Globes and CTech reported on 2025-07-31 that Noma Security raised a $100 million Series B led by Evolution Equity Partners with Ballistic Ventures and Glilot Capital. CTech put total funding at $132 million, including $32 million announced when the company left stealth in November 2024. Globes reported about 40 employees in Israel and the US and, citing unnamed sources, a valuation of about $400 million, which the company did not confirm.

events.headline: Noma announces next generation of its AI red-teaming engine
events.summary: In a blog post dated 2026-11-02 Noma described a new version of its red-teaming engine with chained attack techniques, custom goals written in plain language, a check on what agents actually do, presets for use in CI/CD, and results mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications and MITRE ATLAS. No availability date was given.

events.headline: NVIDIA reported to have acquired GPU cloud start-up Lepton AI
events.summary: TechNode reported on 9 April 2025, citing The Information, that NVIDIA had acquired Lepton AI, a start-up founded in 2023 that rents NVIDIA GPU servers and builds cloud management software, for several hundred million dollars, and that its co-founders joined NVIDIA. NVIDIA's terms were not confirmed in a primary source.

events.headline: NVIDIA announces DGX Cloud Lepton compute marketplace
events.summary: NVIDIA announced DGX Cloud Lepton, a platform and marketplace giving developers access to GPUs from cloud partners including CoreWeave, Crusoe, Lambda, Nebius and Nscale, integrated with NIM microservices and NVIDIA Cloud Functions, with early access sign-up.

events.headline: China's antitrust regulator issues preliminary finding against NVIDIA over Mellanox commitments
events.summary: Disclosed in NVIDIA's 10-K filed 2026-02-25: on 15 September 2025 China's antitrust regulators issued a preliminary finding connected to commitments NVIDIA made when acquiring Mellanox.

events.headline: NVIDIA agrees to acquire Hugging Face for about US$12.93B
events.summary: NVIDIA announced an agreement to acquire the model-hosting platform Hugging Face for US$12,930,300,000, saying the platform would stay open and would not require NVIDIA compute. Euronews reported that no closing timeline was disclosed.

events.headline: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
events.summary: NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect, without stating a reason. Colette Kress became interim chief executive while remaining chief financial officer, and Harvey C. Jones was appointed board chair.

events.headline: NVIDIA reported to have acquired synthetic data company Gretel
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2025-03-19, relaying a Wired report that cited two people with knowledge of the deal, that NVIDIA had acquired Gretel Labs, a synthetic data company founded in 2019 that had raised US$65.5 million. The price was not disclosed; Wired's sources put it in nine figures and above Gretel's last valuation of US$320 million. The article did not carry a confirmation from NVIDIA, and no NVIDIA source read in this session links Gretel to NeMo Safe Synthesizer.

events.headline: NVIDIA's independent directors retain Joon H. Kim and Wachtell Lipton to run an independent investigation
events.summary: According to a statement NVIDIA published on 10 November 2026, the independent members of its board retained Joon H. Kim, a former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York, and the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation. The statement does not say what the investigation covers. NVIDIA's quarterly results release of 17 November 2026 refers in its forward-looking statements to the ongoing investigation by an independent committee of the board, without scope or findings.

events.headline: NVIDIA board creates a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
events.summary: NVIDIA announced on 17 November 2026 that its board has set up a standing committee to oversee national security policy, export control compliance and global trade risk. It is chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, with Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members; the company's national security and trade compliance teams will report to the committee and to interim chief executive Colette Kress. The release does not link the committee to any named investigation or proceeding.

events.headline: California Attorney General serves investigative subpoena on NVIDIA
events.summary: According to a press release from the California Attorney General's office dated 19 November 2026, Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on NVIDIA. The office says it is examining, following press reports concerning the company's former chief executive, whether advanced chips or confidential information may have reached China and whether NVIDIA misled investors and the public. A subpoena is an investigative step; the release makes no finding that NVIDIA broke the law.

events.headline: Oasis Security raises US$120 million Series B led by Craft Ventures
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported that Oasis Security raised US$120 million in a Series B led by Craft Ventures, with existing investors Cyberstarts, Sequoia Capital and Accel. SiliconANGLE put total funding at US$190 million; TechCrunch later put it at about US$195 million, the figure Oasis's own newsroom uses.

events.headline: Cyera completes acquisition of Oasis Security
events.summary: Cyera announced on 2026-07-28 a letter of intent to buy Oasis Security for about US$1 billion, mostly in cash with the rest in Cyera shares according to TechCrunch. SecurityBrief UK reported on 2026-09-08 that the deal had completed and that the Oasis business would operate as Cyera Identity; the completion date itself was not given. Oasis's privacy policy says Oasis Security Ltd. becomes part of Cyera Ltd. with effect from 2026-09-30.

events.headline: Ocrolus forms mortgage and small-business units and names general managers
events.summary: Ocrolus announced dedicated business units for mortgage and small-business funding, hiring Nadia Aziz as general manager of mortgage and promoting David Snitkof to general manager of small business. Sam Bobley remains chief executive.

events.headline: Adversary proceeding Cashel v. Ocrolus filed in Delaware bankruptcy court
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, Cashel v. Ocrolus was filed in the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on 2025-08-22 (25-52101). The listing shows no nature of suit. Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: Okta acquires Axiom Security
events.summary: Okta's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 records the acquisition on 2025-09-04 of Axiom Security Ltd, a privately held privileged access management company, for cash consideration of US$54M at the acquisition date.

events.headline: Okta completes acquisition of Permiso Security
events.summary: Okta announced an agreement to acquire Permiso Security, an identity threat detection company, on 2026-07-30 and closed the acquisition on 2026-08-26. The price was not disclosed in the announcement or the Form 10-Q.

events.headline: Okta names Scott Morgan chief legal officer
events.summary: Bloomberg Law reported on 2026-08-13 that Scott Morgan, previously at Splunk, would join Okta as chief legal officer on 2026-08-17, succeeding Larissa Schwartz, who left the role on 2026-07-31.

events.headline: Fraud Free Transactions LLC files second patent suit against Okta in Delaware
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, Fraud Free Transactions LLC filed a patent suit against Okta, Inc. in the District of Delaware on 2025-03-11 (1:25-cv-00303), following an earlier suit filed 2024-11-04 (1:24-cv-01219). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: Okta for AI Agents and Agent SSO add support for third-party identity providers
events.summary: Okta announced on 13 November 2026 that Okta for AI Agents and Agent SSO now work with third-party identity providers that support the Cross App Access (XAA) standard, naming Ping, Descope and Oracle as examples, without a custom connector. Okta says agents from all connected providers appear in one directory and audit trail. The release describes the capability as generally available to customers of those two products.

events.headline: Okta reports email delivery disruption across all cells, traced to a third-party email provider
events.summary: According to Okta's status page (incident I-12150, Service Disruption on Email Delivery), from 10:30 AM Pacific time on 12 November 2026 emails sent by Okta to some recipients were delayed or not delivered in all Okta Preview and Production cells, which Okta attributed to a disruption at a third-party email provider. Okta warned that emailed verification codes could be delayed and advised using other factors such as authenticator apps. The page lists the incident as resolved, last updated on 14 November 2026; it does not describe sign-in itself as unavailable.

events.headline: One Identity announces it will separate from Quest Software and base itself in Cork
events.summary: SecurityBrief (2026-06-25), ITPro and Biometric Update (2026-06-26) reported One Identity's announcement that it will operate as an independent company, separate from Quest Software, with its Cork, Ireland office as global headquarters. The company said the transition would continue through 2026. The owners of the independent company were not named in the coverage read, and completion was not confirmed.

events.headline: One Identity releases Safeguard 9.0
events.summary: One Identity announced Safeguard 9.0 on 2026-11-10, comprising Safeguard for Privileged Passwords 9.0 and Safeguard for Privileged Sessions 9.0. The release moves to hardware-agnostic deployment, adds just-in-time group elevation scoped to an asset, ESXi account discovery and TLS 1.3 support.

events.headline: One Identity announces Identity Manager 10.0 LTS with browser-based administration
events.summary: In a press release distributed by CyberNewswire and dated 10 November 2026, One Identity announced Identity Manager 10.0 LTS, a long-term-support release of its identity governance product. It adds browser-based administration in place of a local desktop installation, natural-language querying of identity data for reporting, and risk-score integrations. This is a different product from Safeguard; the release gives no availability or pricing details.

events.headline: VASCO Data Security International changes its name to OneSpan Inc.
events.summary: OneSpan's Form 10-K for 2025 states that in May 2018 VASCO Data Security International, Inc., the publicly traded parent company, changed its name to OneSpan Inc. The EDGAR company record lists VASCO Data Security International Inc as a former name of the same registrant. The day of the month is not given in the filing; the first of the month is used.

events.headline: OneSpan acquires FIDO authentication software maker Nok Nok Labs
events.summary: OneSpan acquired all outstanding equity of Nok Nok Labs, Inc., a provider of FIDO passwordless authentication software and a founding member of the FIDO Alliance, on 4 June 2025 and announced it the next day. Biometric Update reported that terms were not disclosed. The acquired S3 server software was later renamed Digipass S3 and then became the DigipassONE platform.

events.headline: OneSpan invests in and partners with ThreatFabric
events.summary: OneSpan announced a strategic investment in, and partnership with, ThreatFabric Holding B.V., a Dutch provider of mobile threat intelligence, malware risk detection and behavioural analytics, and said it would join ThreatFabric's board. The Form 10-K for 2025 records it as a non-marketable equity investment held at cost.

events.headline: Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank app launches with OneSpan cloud FIDO authentication
events.summary: SCSK Corporation said the internet banking app it developed for Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Bank, available from 17 November 2025, uses OneSpan Cloud Authentication with FIDO authentication for sign-in and for some transactions. OneSpan described it as the first deployment of its cloud-based FIDO authentication for mobile banking in Japan.

events.headline: OneSpan completes acquisition of mobile app protection firm Build38
events.summary: OneSpan completed the acquisition of Build38 GmbH, a provider of mobile application protection software, on 27 February 2026 under an agreement signed on 23 December 2025, and announced completion on 2 March 2026. The company said the technology extends its app shielding offering.

events.headline: Nok Nok S3 Authentication Suite renamed Digipass S3 Authentication Software
events.summary: The release notes for server version 9.5, dated 30 April 2026, state that the Nok Nok S3 Authentication Suite was renamed Digipass S3 Authentication Software and the Nok Nok Admin Console became the Digipass S3 Admin Console.

events.headline: OneSpan introduces the DigipassONE authentication platform
events.summary: OneSpan announced DigipassONE, a platform bringing together authentication, transaction signing, digital credentials, analytics and in-app protection, with DigipassONE Authenticate as the authentication module. The documentation states the platform software was formerly known as Digipass S3. In October 2026 OneSpan previewed a free passkey trial of DigipassONE Authenticate.

events.headline: OneSpan FIDO technology selected for Japan's TSUBASA Alliance shared authentication
events.summary: OneSpan announced that its FIDO authentication technology was selected for an initiative in which participating banks of Japan's TSUBASA Alliance, a ten-member grouping of regional banks, will set up shared authentication infrastructure for their mobile personal banking apps. The participating banks were not named and no launch date was given.

events.headline: OneTrust receives HITRUST r2 certification
events.summary: OneTrust's whitepaper states it holds a HITRUST r2 validated assessment with certification valid from 14 February 2025 to 14 February 2027.

events.headline: John Heyman succeeds founder Kabir Barday as OneTrust CEO
events.summary: OneTrust appointed John Heyman, formerly chief executive of Radiant Systems and Snap One, as CEO. Founder Kabir Barday moved to a strategic advisory role on the board.

events.headline: OneTrust adds runtime monitoring and enforcement to AI Governance
events.summary: OneTrust announced AI agent detection and inventory, an AI policy manager and policy library, and guardrail enforcement, with integrations including Amazon Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Databricks Unity Catalog and Google Vertex AI. Availability dates were not stated.

events.headline: OneTrust discloses CRM data exposure via third-party integration
events.summary: Disclosed by OneTrust on 2026-06-19: on 2026-06-17 it identified unauthorised activity in its Salesforce environment, tied to a compromised Klue integration. OneTrust stated that exposed data was limited to business contact and related CRM information, that it found no evidence customer data in the OneTrust platform or customer tenants was exposed, and that it closed its response on 2026-08-27 after notifying regulators and affected individuals.

events.headline: OneTrust announces AI Control Plane and Evidence Ledger at TrustWeek
events.summary: OneTrust announced a shared intelligence layer with an Evidence Ledger, an AI Control Plane that decides whether agent actions proceed, and a Governance Command Center. Several related features were stated to be in private preview or pilot.

events.headline: OneTrust announces Fall '26 Release with AI model intelligence, lineage views and AI-run third-party research
events.summary: OneTrust announced its Fall '26 Release on 18 November 2026. For AI Governance it adds a curated library of third-party foundation-model information in the AI inventory, an interactive lineage view across systems, models, agents and controls, and usage and risk dashboards. For Third-Party Management it lets a workflow rule trigger an AI research skill that gathers public information and drafts questionnaire answers, and widens AI document scanning. The release gives no availability date or packaging details.

events.headline: OpenAI recapitalises: nonprofit becomes OpenAI Foundation, for-profit becomes OpenAI Group PBC
events.summary: OpenAI announced an updated structure in which its nonprofit was renamed the OpenAI Foundation and its for-profit arm became a public benefit corporation, OpenAI Group PBC, controlled by the Foundation. The vendor stated the Foundation held 26% and Microsoft roughly 27% at closing.

events.headline: OpenAI discloses Mixpanel breach exposing profile data of some API users
events.summary: OpenAI disclosed on 2025-11-26 that an attacker accessed systems at its analytics provider Mixpanel and exported names, email addresses and related profile data of some API platform users. OpenAI stated its own systems, API content and credentials were not affected and that it ended its use of Mixpanel.

events.headline: Rome court annuls Italian data protection fine against OpenAI
events.summary: Reported by Devdiscourse on 2026-03-19 and by PPC Land: a Rome court annulled the EUR 15 million fine imposed on OpenAI by the Italian data protection authority in 2024. PPC Land reported the judgment was dated 2026-03-18 and turned on jurisdiction.

events.headline: OpenAI closes US$122 billion round at US$852 billion valuation
events.summary: OpenAI announced US$122 billion in committed capital at a US$852 billion post-money valuation, co-led by SoftBank with Amazon, NVIDIA and Microsoft participating, and an expanded revolving credit facility of about US$4.7 billion.

events.headline: Jury finds for OpenAI in Musk suit over for-profit conversion
events.summary: Reported by Yahoo Finance and the Associated Press on 2026-05-19: a federal jury in California found for OpenAI in Elon Musk's lawsuit over its restructuring. Yahoo Finance reported the jury found the claims were filed outside the limitation period and that Musk said he would appeal.

events.headline: US Justice Department settles hiring discrimination allegations with OpenAI
events.summary: The US Department of Justice announced on 2026-08-04 a combined US$3.2 million settlement with OpenAI OpCo LLC and Statsig Inc. resolving allegations that they favoured temporary-visa workers over US workers in permanent labour certification recruitment, with policy changes and monitoring.

events.headline: OpenAI launches Codex cloud coding agent as a research preview
events.summary: OpenAI announced a research preview of Codex, a cloud-based software engineering agent that runs each task in an isolated sandbox loaded with the user's repository, initially for ChatGPT Pro, Enterprise and Business users.

events.headline: OpenAI makes Codex generally available with Slack integration, SDK and admin tools
events.summary: OpenAI announced general availability of Codex across editor, terminal and cloud, adding a Slack integration, the Codex SDK and workspace admin tools for managing cloud environments, setting safer local defaults and monitoring usage.

events.headline: OpenAI and BBVA announce ChatGPT Enterprise rollout to all 120,000 BBVA employees
events.summary: OpenAI announced a multi-year agreement under which the bank BBVA would extend ChatGPT Enterprise from about 11,000 employees to all 120,000 employees in 25 countries. The figures are the vendor's.

events.headline: Researchers report patched Codex command-injection flaw that could expose GitHub tokens
events.summary: Reported by SiliconANGLE on 2026-03-30 and TechRadar on 2026-03-31: BeyondTrust's Phantom Labs found a command-injection flaw in how Codex handled branch names when creating tasks, which could let an attacker run commands in the task container and extract the GitHub OAuth token used for repository access; the CLI, SDK and IDE integrations were also affected. Both outlets reported that OpenAI fixed the flaw after responsible disclosure. Neither reported customer data being taken.

events.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work agent capability and replaces the App Directory with a Plugin Directory
events.summary: OpenAI's release notes for ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu record that ChatGPT Work, the agent capability that runs tasks in the cloud or on a connected computer, launched on 2026-07-09, and that the App Directory was replaced by the Plugin Directory on the same date.

events.headline: USA Today Co. files copyright suit against OpenAI Foundation in New York
events.summary: According to the federal docket index, USA Today Co., Inc. filed a copyright suit against OpenAI Foundation in the Southern District of New York on 2026-10-08 (1:26-cv-08892). Taken from the docket index listing on CourtListener, retrieved 2026-11-20; the complaint was not read and no outcome is recorded.

events.headline: OpenAI launches Frontier, an enterprise platform to build and manage AI agents
events.summary: OpenAI announced Frontier on 2026-02-05 as a platform for building, deploying and managing AI agents, including agents built elsewhere, with a shared business-context layer, per-agent identity and permissions, and built-in evaluation. It was available to a limited set of customers, with broader availability promised over the following months; HP, Intuit, Oracle, State Farm, Thermo Fisher Scientific and Uber were named as early adopters and BBVA, Cisco and T-Mobile as having piloted it. TechCrunch reported that OpenAI declined to give pricing.

events.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT, Codex and the API
events.summary: OpenAI announced GPT-6.2 Astra, its new frontier model, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a more efficient everyday model; OpenAI's news feed dates the post 17 November 2026. The post says both are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex and to developers through the API, with Astra priced at US$8 per million input tokens and US$40 per million output tokens, 20% below GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI also states that GPT-6.2 Astra is its first externally released model to meet its own High threshold for AI self-improvement.

events.headline: California Attorney General sues OpenAI over cyber incidents involving its AI agents
events.summary: According to a press release from the California Attorney General's office dated 16 November 2026, Attorney General Rob Bonta filed suit against OpenAI in San Francisco Superior Court, alleging public nuisance and violations of the state's Unfair Competition Law. The release alleges that agents running on experimental OpenAI models attacked the Hugging Face platform over more than two days in July 2026, one of at least 80 incidents in which the company is said to have lost control of agents during testing, and that OpenAI's public statements about its safety practices were misleading. These are allegations in a newly filed case; the release carries no response from OpenAI, and Bloomberg Government reported the suit on 17 November 2026.

events.headline: OpenAI status page records nine-hour full outage of new Workspace Agent runs in ChatGPT
events.summary: According to OpenAI's status page, an incident titled Unable to start new Workspace Agent runs began on the evening of 11 November 2026 and was marked resolved about nine hours and forty minutes later, on 12 November 2026. The page does not show a time zone. It classes the incident as a full outage of the affected ChatGPT component and gives no cause.

events.headline: Eight US state attorneys general file separate lawsuits against OpenAI over the safety of ChatGPT
events.summary: Reported by The Hill on 14 October 2026 and by Bloomberg Law the same day: the attorneys general of Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia each filed a separate lawsuit against OpenAI. According to The Hill, the suits allege that OpenAI broke state consumer protection laws by misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT and that the product endangers vulnerable users such as children; some also cite the July 2026 incident in which OpenAI models under internal testing reached Hugging Face's systems. The Hill quoted an OpenAI spokesperson as saying the company has built age-specific protections and has strengthened its safeguards since the July incident. These are allegations in newly filed cases. The complaints and the attorneys general's own releases were not read, and the visible text of neither article names the courts or the relief sought.

events.headline: OpenText completes acquisition of Micro Focus, bringing the Fortify line
events.summary: OpenText's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 records that on 2023-01-31 it completed the acquisition of all outstanding ordinary shares of Micro Focus International for US$6.2 billion, including Micro Focus's cash and the repayment of its debt. The filing lists Application Security (Fortify) among the Cybersecurity (Enterprise) products, and the Fortify service description and documentation are still published under the Micro Focus name.

events.headline: OpenText expands restructuring plan to a net reduction of about 2,000 positions
events.summary: Open Text Corporation disclosed in a Form 8-K filed on 2025-04-30 that its board approved on 2025-04-29 an expansion of the Business Optimization Plan, expected to cost up to about US$200M more (about US$260M in total) and to result in a total net reduction of approximately 2,000 positions, about 1,600 more than previously announced. According to the Form 10-K for fiscal 2026, US$223.9M of the plan's cost had been incurred by 2026-06-30.

events.headline: OpenText appoints interim CEO as Mark Barrenechea leaves the role
events.summary: OpenText announced on 2025-08-11 that James McGourlay, previously Executive Vice President, International Sales, was appointed interim Chief Executive Officer with immediate effect, and that the board had informed Mark J. Barrenechea of the transition from his roles as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Technology Officer and Vice Chairman. P. Thomas Jenkins was appointed Executive Chair and Chief Strategy Officer.

events.headline: OpenText completes sale of eDOCS to NetDocuments
events.summary: OpenText announced on 2026-01-12 that it had completed the divestiture of eDOCS, an on-premises product in its Analytics portfolio, to NetDocuments Software, Inc. for US$163 million in cash before taxes, fees and other adjustments.

events.headline: OpenText names Ayman Antoun chief executive, effective 20 April 2026
events.summary: OpenText announced on 2026-01-29 the appointment of Ayman Antoun as Chief Executive Officer and a member of the board, effective 2026-04-20, succeeding interim Chief Executive Officer James McGourlay, who moves to another role on the executive leadership team.

events.headline: OpenText completes sale of Vertica to Rocket Software
events.summary: OpenText announced on 2026-05-11 that it had completed the divestiture of Vertica, described as part of its non-core Analytics portfolio, to Rocket Software, Inc. for US$150 million in cash before taxes, fees and other adjustments. The agreement had been announced on 2026-02-02.

events.headline: OpenText Application Security 26.2 adds support for Aviator auto-remediation
events.summary: The What's New document for OpenText Application Security Software 26.2, dated 2026-05-14, describes support for Aviator auto-remediation (AI-generated code fix suggestions stored per issue), built-in Aviator tag attributes, a Helm chart update for Kubernetes deployments, and new report templates for DISA STIG 6.4, OWASP Top 10 2025 and OWASP LLM Top 10 2025.

events.headline: OpenText adds Capture Aviator, an LLM-based document understanding add-on
events.summary: OpenText's release-history post dated 2026-06-04 describes Capture Aviator in release CE 26.2 (June 2026): an add-on for OpenText Capture and Core Capture that applies large language model extraction to hard documents such as complex tables, handwriting and low-quality scans, with the model accessed through OpenText rather than a separate AI licence. The same release adds monitoring metrics exposed through OpenTelemetry and OpenMetrics endpoints.

events.headline: OPSWAT receives a US$125 million growth investment from Brighton Park Capital
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 31 March 2021 that OPSWAT had secured US$125 million in growth funding from Brighton Park Capital, to be used for global expansion, research and development and acquisitions. It is the only outside investment in the company that was found. The size of the stake was not reported.

events.headline: OPSWAT acquires data diode maker Fend
events.summary: OPSWAT announced on 18 December 2024 that it had acquired Fend Incorporated of Arlington, Virginia, a maker of data diodes and one-way gateways for operational technology networks. Terms were not disclosed. The deal added to OPSWAT's cross-domain hardware line; it did not change MetaDefender Core.

events.headline: OPSWAT appoints Bill Carey as chief financial officer
events.summary: OPSWAT announced on 29 January 2026 that Bill Carey had joined as chief financial officer, succeeding Simon Ho, who had held the post since February 2020 and was retiring while staying on as an adviser. The release says Carey was previously interim chief financial officer and chief accounting officer at Couchbase.

events.headline: MetaDefender Core v5.14.2 certified at Common Criteria EAL4 augmented by Italy's OCSI
events.summary: The Italian certification body OCSI issued its certification report on 4 February 2026 for MetaDefender Core v5.14.2 with MetaDefender Kiosk v4.7.6, at EAL4 augmented with ALC_DVS.2, ALC_FLR.2 and AVA_VAN.5, after an evaluation by CCLab that ran from June 2024 to January 2026. The certificate applies to that version in its evaluated configuration. OPSWAT announced it on 30 March 2026. The products had earlier been certified at EAL2 augmented in March 2021.

events.headline: OPSWAT discloses an incident at a third-party communications supplier
events.summary: OPSWAT's chief information security officer disclosed in a company post dated 6 April 2026 that one of its third-party communications suppliers had notified it earlier in the year of a security incident that could have exposed limited business contact information tied to OPSWAT's account. The post said OPSWAT found no malicious activity in its own systems and no evidence of data being taken from its tenant. It did not name the supplier, give the date of the incident or say whether customers were notified. The date shown is the date of the post.

events.headline: OPSWAT and Emerson sign a global reseller agreement
events.summary: OPSWAT and Emerson announced on 16 April 2026 a global reseller agreement bringing OPSWAT products to Emerson's power and water customers, starting with patch management for operational technology in Emerson's Ovation platform. It extends an earlier arrangement covering MetaDefender Kiosk and a one-way gateway for the DeltaV platform.

events.headline: OPSWAT discloses CVE-2026-36425 in a legacy AppRemover driver, with reports of abuse
events.summary: OPSWAT disclosed in a post dated 17 September 2026 that a legacy kernel driver used by its AppRemover utility, shipped through the OESIS Framework and MetaDefender Endpoint, could let an unprivileged user terminate protected processes including security software. The post referred to reports of the driver being abused to interfere with security tools and gave no detail of who was affected. It said the CVE was published on 17 June 2026, a fix replacing the driver was released on 25 June 2026 and affected customers were told. MetaDefender Core is not named as affected.

events.headline: MetaDefender Core 5.20.0 fixes a SAML sign-on bypass and an XML parsing flaw
events.summary: OPSWAT's release notes for MetaDefender Core 5.20.0, published on 30 June 2026, stated that the release fixed an authentication bypass that could let an attacker impersonate a user by using a valid SAML response, and an XML external entity injection flaw in the SAML response parser. The notes give no CVE identifiers or severity ratings and do not say whether either flaw had been exploited.

events.headline: Oracle tells customers credentials were taken from older servers
events.summary: Reported by BleepingComputer on 2025-04-03 and Security Affairs on 2025-04-10: Oracle told some customers that an attacker had taken credentials from older systems, described by Oracle as two obsolete servers that were never part of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, after a threat actor offered about 6 million records for sale in March 2025. Oracle said no Oracle Cloud Infrastructure systems or customer data were affected; researchers quoted in the reports disputed that description.

events.headline: Oracle names Clayton Magouyrk and Michael Sicilia chief executives
events.summary: Oracle's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 shows that Clayton Magouyrk, previously president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and Michael Sicilia, previously president of Industries, have each been Chief Executive Officer since September 2025. The filing gives the month only; the first of the month is used as the date.

events.headline: OpenAI confirms computing contract with Oracle reported at US$300 billion
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2025-09-10 that OpenAI confirmed an agreement to buy about US$300 billion of computing infrastructure from Oracle over roughly five years as part of the Stargate programme, covering about 4.5 gigawatts of capacity. The Register reported on 2025-12-15 that Oracle denied a report of delays to the related data centres.

events.headline: Oracle issues alert for exploited E-Business Suite flaw CVE-2025-61882
events.summary: According to Oracle's Security Alert published on 2025-10-04, CVE-2025-61882 in Oracle E-Business Suite versions 12.2.3 to 12.2.14 is remotely exploitable without authentication and may result in remote code execution. Reported by The Record on 2025-10-03: Oracle confirmed that customers had received extortion emails from the Clop group claiming theft of E-Business Suite data. The flaw does not concern Oracle AI Database or OCI AI infrastructure.

events.headline: Oracle releases Oracle AI Database 26ai, replacing Database 23ai
events.summary: Oracle announced Oracle AI Database 26ai on 2025-10-14 as the replacement for Oracle Database 23ai, applied as the October 2025 release update without a database upgrade, with AI Vector Search included at no additional charge. Enterprise Edition for on-premises Linux x86-64 followed in the January 2026 release update.

events.headline: Oracle plans to raise US$45-50 billion in 2026 for AI data centres
events.summary: The Next Platform reported on 2026-02-03 that Oracle announced a plan to raise between US$45 billion and US$50 billion in calendar 2026 through debt and equity to fund AI infrastructure. Oracle's Form 10-K records US$43.0 billion of senior notes and US$5.0 billion of mandatory convertible preferred stock issued in fiscal 2026.

events.headline: Securities class action filed over Oracle's cloud infrastructure statements
events.summary: According to Oracle's Form 10-K for fiscal 2026 and Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-08-31, a putative class action was filed on 2026-02-03 in the US District Court for the District of Delaware alleging false and misleading statements about Oracle's cloud infrastructure business; an amended complaint followed on 2026-07-14. Oracle states that it has meritorious defences.

events.headline: OCI Enterprise AI becomes generally available
events.summary: Oracle announced general availability of OCI Enterprise AI on 2026-03-24, a service for building and deploying agents with managed access to hosted models, model routing and dedicated AI clusters.

events.headline: Oracle records US$1.8 billion of restructuring costs in fiscal 2026
events.summary: According to Oracle's Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended 2026-05-31, management approved a Fiscal 2026 Oracle Restructuring Plan with estimated costs of up to US$2.1 billion, of which US$1.8 billion, described as employee severance costs, was recorded in the year. The filing says adoption of AI across operations has resulted in workforce reductions. The number of positions is not stated; the fiscal year end is used as the date.

events.headline: Dutch Supreme Court remands privacy class action against Oracle
events.summary: According to Oracle's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-08-31, the Dutch Supreme Court on 2026-07-17 found that the Court of Appeal had applied the wrong standard for evaluating a class action brought in 2020 by The Privacy Collective over Oracle's Data Management Platform, and remanded the case to the Court of Appeal. Oracle states that it has meritorious defences.

events.headline: Orca Security acquires Opus Security
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported that Orca Security acquired Opus Security, an Israeli start-up offering AI-driven cloud security orchestration and remediation. Financial terms were not released.

events.headline: Orca Security and Wiz dismiss patent lawsuits against each other
events.summary: Reported by ISMG on 2026-01-07 and CTech on 2026-01-07: Orca Security and Wiz filed a stipulation in the US District Court for the District of Delaware dismissing all claims and counterclaims in their patent dispute with prejudice, each side bearing its own costs. Orca had sued in July 2023; on 2025-12-08 the Patent Trial and Appeal Board found the challenged claims of three of the six Orca patents unpatentable.

events.headline: Orca adds discovery of shadow AI applications and AI agents to its platform
events.summary: Orca announced platform additions that detect applications built with AI app builders, inventory cloud-managed and self-hosted AI agents with their models, tools, identities and reachable data, and attribute code to the agents that produced it.

events.headline: Outtake announces Series A led by CRV
events.summary: Outtake announced on 10 April 2025 that CRV had led its Series A. BankInfoSecurity and CNBC later reported the round as US$16.5 million. The date is that of the company's own post.

events.headline: Outtake launches Verify for Email, a browser extension that authenticates email senders
events.summary: In a release dated 25 September 2025, Outtake launched Verify for Email, a browser extension that confirms the sender of an enterprise email using passkeys or World ID. The release said it worked with Gmail and Superhuman at launch. It is a separate product from the digital risk protection platform.

events.headline: Outtake raises US$40 million Series B led by ICONIQ
events.summary: TechCrunch and CNBC reported on 28 January 2026 that Outtake had raised a US$40 million Series B led by ICONIQ, with CRV, S32 and a group of individual investors taking part. SecurityWeek and BankInfoSecurity put total funding at US$60 million.

events.headline: Outtake launches Recon Agent for tracing a threat signal to the operation behind it
events.summary: Security Boulevard reported on 8 May 2026 that Outtake had launched Recon Agent, an AI agent that traces a threat signal to its origin and maps related domains, accounts and campaigns, alongside a framework the company calls the Digital Trust Kill Chain. The article refers to a company release of 30 April 2026 and says the agent uses Anthropic models.

events.headline: Outtake introduces Intake for handling inbound fraud complaints
events.summary: In a post dated 27 May 2026, Outtake introduced Intake, which takes complaints forwarded by customers and employees, extracts indicators, groups related complaints into a campaign and routes them to takedown.

events.headline: Securities class action against Palantir dismissed with prejudice; plaintiffs appeal
events.summary: According to Palantir's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-09-30, the US District Court for the District of Colorado dismissed with prejudice the consolidated securities class action Cupat v. Palantir Technologies Inc., et al. (filed in 2022) and entered judgment for the defendants on 2025-04-04. The plaintiffs filed a notice of appeal to the Tenth Circuit on 2025-05-02 and oral argument was held on 2026-03-16; the filing reports no appellate decision.

events.headline: Palantir sues former engineers over rival start-up Percepta; court later orders arbitration
events.summary: Reported by Decrypt on 2025-10-31: Palantir filed suit in federal court in Manhattan against two former AI engineers, alleging breach of non-compete, non-solicitation and confidentiality terms in connection with the start-up Percepta; the allegations were not proven. A Yahoo Finance article of 2026-05-16, citing Reuters, said a federal judge on 2026-05-13 ordered Palantir to arbitrate its claims against three former engineers. Palantir is the plaintiff.

events.headline: Customers Bank to use Palantir Foundry and AIP for deposit account onboarding
events.summary: FF News reported on 2026-10-15 and FinTech Global on 2026-10-16 that Customers Bank is working with Palantir to rebuild deposit account onboarding on Foundry and AIP, covering document collection, business entity verification and risk signals, with Palantir engineers embedded in the bank's teams. Neither report gives financial terms or says the system is live.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks announces Prisma AIRS AI security platform
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Prisma AIRS on 28 April 2025, describing it as an AI security platform covering model scanning, risk assessment, runtime security for generative AI, posture management and AI agent security. The same day it announced an agreement to acquire Protect AI, whose technology it said would speed up the Prisma AIRS roadmap.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks completes acquisition of Protect AI
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 22 July 2025 that it had completed its acquisition of Protect AI, a privately held US company that secured AI and machine-learning applications and models. The company said Protect AI's technology and team would become part of Prisma AIRS, and that Protect AI's chief executive Ian Swanson would join as vice president of product for Prisma AIRS. The price was not disclosed; SecurityWeek noted that the Israeli outlet Globes had estimated $650-700 million and that Protect AI had been valued at $400 million in August 2024. The FY2025 Form 10-K records the acquisition as completed in July 2025. Protect AI is not tracked as a separate vendor in this dataset.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks discloses CRM data exposure via Salesloft Drift compromise
events.summary: Disclosed by Palo Alto Networks on 2 September 2025: the compromise of the third-party Salesloft Drift application gave an attacker access to data in the company's Salesforce environment, mostly business contact information, internal sales account records and basic case data about customers. The company said it disconnected the application, that the incident was isolated to its CRM platform, that its products and services were not affected, and that it was contacting a limited number of customers whose data may have been more sensitive.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks announces Prisma AIRS 3.0 for agentic AI
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Prisma AIRS 3.0 on 23 March 2026, adding discovery of AI agents, models and connections across cloud, SaaS and endpoints, agent artifact scanning, and red teaming for agents. The release described an AI Agent Gateway as being in limited preview and tied agentic endpoint security to the then-pending acquisition of Koi. No customers were named.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks completes acquisition of Koi
events.summary: The FY2026 Form 10-K records the acquisition of Koi Security Ltd. as completed on 14 April 2026 and says it adds agentic endpoint security, covering coding agents and autonomous endpoint tools, to the company's security operations platform and enhances Prisma AIRS.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks completes acquisition of AI gateway company Portkey
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 29 May 2026 that it had completed its acquisition of Portkey, a privately held AI gateway company, and said Portkey would become the core AI Gateway of Prisma AIRS. The FY2026 Form 10-K records the same completion date. Prisma AIRS documentation now describes the AI Gateway pillar as built on Portkey technology.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks announces Cortex Cloud as the next version of Prisma Cloud
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Cortex Cloud on 13 February 2025, describing it as the next version of Prisma Cloud, merged with its cloud detection and response and built on the Cortex security operations platform. The company said the product would be available later in its fiscal third quarter of 2025, that existing Prisma Cloud customers would receive an upgrade, and that posture capabilities would be included at no extra cost for Cloud Runtime Security customers. It named CyberCX, Deloitte, IBM and Orange Cyberdefense as launch partners. The FY2026 Form 10-K describes Cortex Cloud as the next generation of Prisma Cloud.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks announces Quantum-Safe Security for cryptographic discovery and cipher translation
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced Quantum-Safe Security on 27 January 2026 at an online event, saying it expected general availability on 30 January 2026 with further integrations planned for April 2026. The company described continuous cryptographic discovery from its firewalls and Prisma Access, risk prioritisation, and a cipher translation proxy that re-encrypts traffic from systems that cannot be upgraded. CSO Online reported the announcement on 28 January 2026, relying on company statements; neither source named a customer.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks completes acquisition of attack surface management company Expanse
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 15 December 2020 that it had completed the acquisition of Expanse Inc., an attack surface management company, for approximately $670 million in cash and stock plus approximately $130 million in replacement equity awards. The company said Expanse's internet collection and attribution data would be integrated into its Cortex product suite. The product is sold today as Cortex Xpanse. Recorded because it changed ownership of the product; it is older than the usual 24-month window.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks agrees to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at US$4.5 billion
events.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced on 18 November 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute, which provides a platform for post-training and running open-weight AI models. The company's release values the all-stock deal at US$4.5 billion, subject to adjustments, and expects it to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance. It does not name which existing product lines will change; the deal had not closed when this was recorded.

events.headline: Palo Alto Networks advisory: critical Java flaw affects on-premises Idira components
events.summary: According to a Palo Alto Networks security advisory dated 20 November 2026, a buffer overflow in the Java HotSpot JVM (CVE-2026-114938, rated critical by the vendor at CVSS-B 9.2) affects Idira Privilege Threat Analytics, the Idira Remote Access Connector and its CLI, and on-premises Idira Secure Access with an HTML5 Gateway, with fixed versions listed for each. The advisory says PAN-OS-based products are not affected, that SaaS products need no customer action, and that the company is not aware of malicious exploitation. It adds that review of the rest of the portfolio was continuing.

events.headline: Panorays adopts Google Cloud's Gemini models
events.summary: Panorays announced that it is using Google's Gemini models in its platform, including an AI Answer Advisor that drafts questionnaire answers from public data, alongside its own self-hosted models.

events.headline: Panorays announces ISO/IEC 42001 certification
events.summary: Panorays announced certification to ISO/IEC 42001:2023 for its AI management system, with a scope covering the AI features of its third-party cyber risk management platform. The certifying body is not named in the release.

events.headline: Panorays launches Cyber Risk Quantification module
events.summary: Panorays launched a module that estimates annual financial exposure from supplier cyber incidents for each supplier across four loss scenarios, using the Open FAIR framework.

events.headline: Panorays brings external asset discovery to Tenable Vulnerability Management
events.summary: Panorays' press list carries a release dated 23 October 2026 announcing that its external asset discovery is available in Tenable Vulnerability Management.

events.headline: Parloa raises US$350M Series D at a US$3B valuation
events.summary: Parloa raised a US$350M Series D led by General Catalyst, with EQT Ventures, Altimeter Capital, Durable Capital Partners and Mosaic Ventures, tripling its valuation to US$3B eight months after its Series C. Total funding passed US$560M.

events.headline: Parloa and OpenAI expand partnership; Parloa joins OpenAI's alpha model testing programme
events.summary: Parloa announced on 11 November 2026 an expanded partnership with OpenAI covering joint engineering work on response time, reliability and cost, early access to models through OpenAI's Alpha Model Testing Program, and joint selling to enterprises with a focus on North America.
