events.summary: Reported by The Hacker News on 2026-01-13 and SecurityBrief UK on 2026-01-15: AppOmni found a flaw, CVE-2025-12420 (CVSS 9.3), that let an unauthenticated attacker impersonate any user through the Virtual Agent API and trigger Now Assist AI Agents actions as that user. The Hacker News reported that ServiceNow updated most hosted instances on 2025-10-30, published an advisory in January 2026, and that there was no evidence of exploitation.

events.headline: ServiceNow discloses unauthorised queries of some customer instances
events.summary: Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-06-09 and The Hacker News on 2026-06-10: ServiceNow told customers that a flaw allowing unauthenticated access to an API endpoint had been used to query tables in a subset of customer instances, mainly on the Australia release, and that it applied a fix to hosted instances on 2026-06-05. BleepingComputer reported that a later ServiceNow advisory attributed the activity to likely security research linked to bug bounty submissions. Neither article reported AI agent involvement.

events.headline: ServiceNow appoints Danielle Fontaine as chief accounting officer
events.summary: ServiceNow disclosed in a Form 8-K that Danielle Fontaine became chief accounting officer and corporate controller on 2026-02-17, with the previous holder, Kevin McBride, moving to executive vice president, accounting and corporate services.

events.headline: ServiceNow launches AI Control Tower, later renamed Super Intelligence Control Tower
events.summary: ServiceNow announced AI Control Tower as generally available on 2025-05-06 at its Knowledge 2025 conference, describing it as a central place to govern, manage and secure AI agents, models and workflows from ServiceNow and from other vendors. The vendor's site and documentation now call the product Super Intelligence Control Tower; the date of the renaming was not found.

events.headline: ServiceNow closes acquisition of identity security company Veza
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2025-12-02 that it would buy Veza, an identity security company founded in 2020 with about 230 staff and nearly 150 enterprise customers, for undisclosed terms; an update to the release says the deal closed on 2026-03-02. ServiceNow said Veza's Access Graph would be built into its AI Control Tower to govern what AI agents can reach.

events.headline: ServiceNow expands AI Control Tower to AI assets outside its own platform
events.summary: The Register reported on 2026-05-05 that ServiceNow had expanded AI Control Tower into five areas (discovery, observation, governance, security and measurement), with 30 new connectors to AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, SAP, Oracle and Workday, runtime tracing from its March 2026 purchase of Traceloop and permission mapping from Veza. The update ships with the Australia platform release.

events.headline: ServiceNow announces agentic continuous control monitoring for Integrated Risk Management
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2026-11-10 agentic capabilities for continuous control monitoring in its Integrated Risk Management product, extending monitoring to cloud, identity, SaaS and on-premises tools through more than 100 pre-built integrations. The press release says the monitoring works alongside the company's Super Intelligence Control Tower and that general availability is expected in the first quarter of 2027.

events.headline: ServiceNow introduces Autonomous CRM Engine in controlled availability
events.summary: ServiceNow announced on 2026-11-12 Autonomous CRM Engine, a tool that maps how a customer's existing CRM is used, designs a target configuration and deploys approved changes into ServiceNow. The press release says the product is in controlled availability, with expanded capabilities expected in 2027.

events.headline: ServiceNow reported to have cut more staff in the UK, US and India; number not disclosed
events.summary: Reported by NowBen on 2026-11-05 and by CTech on 2026-11-06: ServiceNow carried out a further round of layoffs affecting employees in the UK, the US and India, which NowBen described as the third round of 2026 and said many employees learned of on 4 November. Neither outlet gives a number and ServiceNow has not disclosed one. Both quote a company statement that it is making "necessary changes to how we are structured" and is managing headcount to end 2026 where it started. CTech adds that ServiceNow's quarterly filing shows US$167 million of severance costs in the first nine months of 2026, and that its shares fell about 27% the day after third-quarter results.

events.headline: Sierra raises US$950M at a valuation above US$15B
events.summary: Sierra announced a US$950M funding round led by Tiger Global and GV, valuing the company at more than US$15B. SiliconANGLE also named Benchmark, Sequoia and Greenoaks as investors. CMSWire reported that the round took total capital raised above US$1B, following US$350M in September 2025 at a US$10B valuation.

events.headline: Sierra acquires browser-agent infrastructure company Anon
events.summary: Sierra announced that Anon, which built infrastructure for AI agents to sign in to and operate websites that have no API, is joining Sierra. Terms were not disclosed. Sierra said the technology will let its agents work in systems without APIs.

events.headline: Sierra announces a PCI DSS v4.0.1 attestation of compliance
events.summary: Sierra's trust centre announced on 2025-11-01 that the company holds a PCI DSS attestation of compliance. Its product page describes the status as PCI DSS Level 1 Service Provider, with cardholder data handled in separate infrastructure.

events.headline: Sierra introduces Horizon for longer-running agent tasks
events.summary: Sierra published a post introducing Horizon on 2026-07-16. Its home page describes Horizon as covering long-horizon planning, customer context, outcome optimisation and proactive engagement, and Horizon has its own service-specific terms.

events.headline: Sierra releases version 1.0 of the Personal Agent Protocol
events.summary: Sierra published on 2026-11-13 version 1.0 of the Personal Agent Protocol, a specification for how consumers' personal AI agents connect to companies' agents, websites and APIs, together with an implementation kit and validator. Sierra's post says the protocol builds on existing standards including MCP, OpenAPI and OAuth, that design partners now number more than 100, and that Shopify has enabled it for the merchants on its platform.

events.headline: Skyflow launches a data privacy vault edition for India's DPDP rules
events.summary: Skyflow's press page lists coverage dated 2025-12-01 of the launch of a DPDP data privacy vault aimed at Indian enterprises. The linked articles were not read; details are limited to the headlines.

events.headline: Skyflow and Coralogix announce privacy-safe observability partnership
events.summary: Skyflow's press page lists a release dated 2026-03-20 announcing work with Coralogix on observability that keeps sensitive data protected. The release itself could not be retrieved; details are limited to the headline.

events.headline: Skyflow launches Skyflow for Glean for enterprise AI search
events.summary: Skyflow's press page lists a release dated 2026-08-25 launching Skyflow for Glean, described as runtime data control for enterprise AI search. The release itself could not be retrieved; details are limited to the headline.

events.headline: Snowflake acquires Postgres provider Crunchy Data
events.summary: Snowflake's 10-K for fiscal 2026 records the acquisition of Crunchy Data Solutions, Inc. on 6 June 2025 for US$164.5 million in cash.

events.headline: Snowflake appoints Brian Robins as chief financial officer
events.summary: Snowflake's 10-K for fiscal 2026 lists executive transitions including a new chief financial officer, Brian Robins, in September 2025 and a new chief revenue officer, Michael Gannon, in March 2025. The filing gives months only; the first of September is used.

events.headline: Court denies motions to dismiss data-breach class claims against Snowflake
events.summary: Snowflake disclosed in its fiscal 2026 10-K that in the consolidated multidistrict litigation in the District of Montana over the 2024 customer-account incidents, the court on 28 and 29 October 2025 denied motions to dismiss the consumer and financial institution claims; answers were filed on 19 December 2025 and the case is in discovery. A separate class action is pending in British Columbia.

events.headline: Class action filed against Snowflake alleging copyright infringement in model training
events.summary: Snowflake disclosed in its fiscal 2026 10-K that a class action filed on 21 November 2025 in the District of Montana alleges copyright infringement related to training of the company's large language model; Snowflake filed its answer on 22 January 2026 and the case is in discovery.

events.headline: Court dismisses securities class complaint against Snowflake with leave to amend
events.summary: Snowflake disclosed in its fiscal 2026 10-K that on 17 February 2026 the Northern District of California granted its motion to dismiss the second amended complaint in a securities class action filed in February 2024, allowing a third amended complaint; that five derivative suits are stayed; and that a second securities class action was filed on 24 February 2026.

events.headline: Snowflake acquires observability company Observe
events.summary: Snowflake's 10-K for fiscal 2026 records the acquisition of Observe, Inc. on 2 February 2026 for preliminary consideration of about US$596.2 million in cash and shares.

events.headline: Snowflake marks recent Cortex Search updates as generally available
events.summary: A Snowflake release note dated 12 March 2026 is titled as moving recent Cortex Search updates to general availability. The body of the note was not captured; earlier release notes list multi-indexing and custom vector embeddings as previews in December 2025.

events.headline: Snowflake makes Snowflake Intelligence, Cortex Agents and Cortex AI Functions generally available
events.summary: Snowflake's 2025 release notes record general availability on 2025-11-04 of Cortex Agents, Cortex AI Functions, the Snowflake-managed MCP server and the conversational application then called Snowflake Intelligence. SiliconANGLE reported the same day that more than 1,000 customers had used Snowflake Intelligence during testing.

events.headline: Snowflake agrees to acquire Natoma, a Model Context Protocol platform for AI agents
events.summary: Snowflake's first-quarter fiscal 2027 results release of 2026-05-27 states that in May 2026 it agreed to acquire Natoma, a Model Context Protocol platform for enterprise AI agents, to extend governance to AI-driven workflows. The release gives no price; the date shown is the date of the release, and completion was not confirmed in the sources read.

events.headline: Snowflake renames Snowflake Intelligence as Snowflake CoWork
events.summary: CIO reported on 2026-06-02 and SiliconANGLE on 2026-06-03 that Snowflake renamed its conversational agent application Snowflake Intelligence as Snowflake CoWork at its Summit conference, adding connectors to work tools and a shared context layer. Snowflake's documentation now uses the CoWork name and refers to its coding agent as CoCo.

events.headline: Snyk for Government receives FedRAMP Moderate authorization
events.summary: Snyk announced on 2025-04-24 that Snyk for Government had completed the FedRAMP process at the Moderate level. The release does not name the sponsoring agency.

events.headline: Snyk acquires AI-agent security lab Invariant Labs
events.summary: Snyk announced on 2025-06-24 that it had acquired Invariant Labs, an ETH Zurich spin-off that builds guardrails for AI agents and scans MCP servers. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Snyk cuts about 20% of staff in fourth round of layoffs
events.summary: Reported by Globes on 2026-06-24 and ISMG on 2026-06-25 as about 90 jobs. Reported by CTech and Tech.eu on 2026-10-01, citing the company's UK filing, as a reduction of approximately 203 employees, about 20% of the global workforce, with an expected cost of up to US$13.8 million.

events.headline: Snyk reported under interim chief executive Ken MacAskill
events.summary: ISMG reported on 2026-06-25 that Ken MacAskill was interim chief executive. Globes reported on 2026-06-24 that Peter McKay, chief executive since 2019, had announced earlier in 2026 that he would step down. The exact handover date was not sourced; the event is dated to the ISMG report.

events.headline: Snyk discloses access to its Salesforce data through vendor Klue
events.summary: Disclosed by Snyk on its status page from 2026-06-19, marked resolved on 2026-07-08: an unauthorised party accessed Snyk's Salesforce data through an integration with the vendor Klue. Snyk said the data was business contact information and titles and descriptions of some support cases, and that its platform was not involved.

events.headline: McCauley v. Snyk filed in federal court in North Carolina
events.summary: CourtListener lists McCauley v. Snyk, Inc. (W.D.N.C., 3:26-cv-00522), filed on 2026-07-01. The listing does not show the claims; no outcome and no press report were found.

events.headline: Socket acquires reachability analysis start-up Coana
events.summary: Socket announced on 2025-04-23 that it had acquired Coana, a Danish start-up founded in 2022 by researchers from Aarhus University whose engine determines whether vulnerable code in a dependency can be called. The Coana team joined Socket. The price was not disclosed.

events.headline: Socket acquires extension security company Secure Annex
events.summary: Socket announced on 2026-04-28 that it had acquired Secure Annex, a one-person company founded in November 2024 that analyses browser and editor extensions, and that its founder was joining Socket. The price was not disclosed. BankInfoSecurity reported the deal on 2026-04-30.

events.headline: Socket raises US$60 million Series C at US$1 billion valuation
events.summary: Socket announced a US$60 million Series C led by Thrive Capital, with Andreessen Horowitz, Abstract Ventures and Capital One Ventures taking part. SecurityWeek and BankInfoSecurity reported a US$1 billion valuation and total funding of about US$125 million.

events.headline: Socure agrees to acquire risk decisioning company Effectiv for US$136M
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported that Socure would pay US$136M for Effectiv, a fraud and risk orchestration and decisioning platform founded in 2021, with the deal expected to close in November 2024 and Effectiv's team joining Socure.

events.headline: Socure raises US$156M at a reported US$5.2 billion valuation
events.summary: SiliconANGLE and Biometric Update reported a US$156M investment led by Summit Partners, with Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Wells Fargo and Docusign among participants, combining primary capital with an employee tender offer and valuing Socure at US$5.2 billion.

events.headline: Socure acquires agentic AI investigations company Fravity
events.summary: SiliconANGLE and Biometric Update reported that Socure acquired Fravity, whose agents support fraud and compliance investigations, for an undisclosed price; the technology is to be offered as RiskOS Agents.

events.headline: Snir v. Socure filed in federal court in New Jersey
events.summary: CourtListener lists Snir v. Socure, Inc. (D.N.J., 2:26-cv-06334), filed on 2026-05-29, and Socure, Inc. v. Snir (D. Del.), filed by Socure on 2026-06-09. The listing does not show the claims; no outcome and no press report were found.

events.headline: Sonar acquires AutoCodeRover
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2025-02-19 that Sonar had acquired AutoCodeRover, maker of an autonomous AI agent that fixes code. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Sonar adds malicious package detection to SonarQube Advanced Security
events.summary: Sonar announced malicious package detection in SonarQube Advanced Security, new security rules for GitHub Actions, a beta command-line tool that scans AI-generated code, and an integration that shows SonarQube static analysis findings inside the Wiz platform.

events.headline: Sonar acquires AI code review company Gitar
events.summary: Sonar announced it had acquired Gitar, whose platform reviews and fixes code and CI failures in GitHub and GitLab pull requests. Terms were not disclosed. Gitar stays available as a standalone product and its leaders joined Sonar.

events.headline: SonarQube Server 2026.5 LTA released with agents for self-managed deployments
events.summary: Sonar announced general availability of SonarQube Server 2026.5 LTA, making Sonar Vortex, the Hunter Agent and the Remediation Agent purchasable with the Enterprise and Data Center editions, with central governance of the LLMs they use.

events.headline: Sonar joins OpenAI's Daybreak cyber partner programme
events.summary: Sonar announced it had joined OpenAI's Daybreak Defense Network, giving it access to OpenAI's cyber models, which it plans to use in the SonarQube Hunter Agent.

events.headline: Thoma Bravo completes take-private acquisition of Sophos
events.summary: Sophos announced completion of its acquisition by Thoma Bravo in an all-cash deal valuing the company at about US$3.9 billion (US$7.40 per share), after which its shares stopped trading on the London Stock Exchange. Recorded although older than 24 months because it changed ownership of the vendor; dated from the release.

events.headline: Sophos completes acquisition of Secureworks
events.summary: Sophos announced completion of its all-cash acquisition of Secureworks, valued at about US$859 million (US$8.50 per share). Secureworks became a wholly owned subsidiary and its shares stopped trading on Nasdaq. The Register reported the closing date as 3 February 2025.

events.headline: Sophos cuts about 6% of combined workforce after Secureworks deal
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch and The Register on 2025-02-13: Sophos confirmed layoffs of roughly 6% of the combined Sophos and Secureworks workforce, attributing them to roles no longer needed once Secureworks ceased to be a public company and to duplicated roles. Sophos did not disclose the number of people affected.

events.headline: Federal dockets show patent and copyright suits filed against Sophos in 2025-2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): suits filed against Sophos entities include Long Horizon Technologies LLC v. Sophos Limited (E.D. Tex., filed 2026-11-08), Arc Link LLC v. Sophos Limited (patent, E.D. Tex., filed 2026-06-18), Fast Corporation Ltd. v. Sophos Ltd. (copyright, S.D.N.Y., filed 2026-03-25) and Sulaco Enterprises LLC v. Sophos Limited (patent, E.D. Tex., filed 2025-12-16). The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Sophos says Salesloft Drift compromise exposed support-case data of 20 customers
events.summary: Disclosed by Sophos in an advisory published 2025-09-03: following the Salesloft Drift compromise, limited support-case data of 20 customers held in a third-party system was affected. Sophos stated that its core Sophos and Secureworks systems and Salesforce instances were not affected, that it rotated secrets and revoked trusts related to Drift, and that it was contacting the affected customers.

events.headline: Sourcegraph ends Cody Free and Pro; Cody becomes Enterprise-only
events.summary: Sourcegraph announced on 2025-06-25 that new sign-ups for Cody Free and Cody Pro were closed and both plans would end on 2025-07-23, and that Enterprise Starter would no longer include Cody. It said Cody Enterprise customers were not affected.

events.headline: Sourcegraph and Amp become separate companies; Dan Adler becomes Sourcegraph CEO

quote.text: we've decided that it's best for both products to go forward in separate, focused companies.

events.summary: Sourcegraph announced on 2025-12-02 that its Amp coding agent would continue in a separate company founded by Quinn Slack and Beyang Liu, who remain on Sourcegraph's board, and that Dan Adler, previously CFO, became Sourcegraph CEO. Sourcegraph keeps code search. Investors Craft, Redpoint, Sequoia, Goldcrest and a16z sit on both boards. Amp's own post names the new entity Amp Frontier Corporation. Neither post mentions Cody.

events.headline: Sourcegraph lowers credit costs for Deep Search and Code Finder and changes service-account billing
events.summary: Sourcegraph announced on 2026-11-19 that a Deep Search now costs 50 credits instead of 70, a Code Finder call through MCP costs 3 credits instead of 11, and Smart Hovers no longer use credits, effective the same day for all customers. The post also says service accounts used for searches and other product workflows are billed on the same model as human users from that date.

events.headline: Sourcegraph announces that Cody will reach end of life on 31 January 2027
events.summary: According to a post by Sourcegraph's chief executive Dan Adler dated 2026-11-09, Sourcegraph will end of life its Cody coding assistant on 2027-01-31. The post acknowledges that developers and enterprise teams still use Cody, including its IDE integrations and APIs, and says Deep Search and Sourcegraph's MCP integrations can support many of those workflows but are not one-for-one replacements for every Cody capability. It asks Cody customers to contact their account team to plan a transition. The post does not say whether Cody is still sold to new customers or what support is provided until that date; the company itself continues, focusing on code search, Deep Search, MCP and Agentic Batch Changes.

events.headline: Strix opens its commercial platform after a beta
events.summary: Strix announced on 2026-04-13 that the Strix Platform, a hosted product built around its open-source testing agents with scheduling, findings history, auto-fix and integrations, was available more broadly after a beta with early users. PR security reviews were announced the next day.

events.headline: Strix becomes available on AWS Marketplace
events.summary: Strix announced on 2026-10-20 that its platform can be bought through AWS Marketplace, with private offers for negotiated terms. The listing describes a software-as-a-service product with contract options up to an Enterprise tier that adds VPC or on-premises deployment.

events.headline: Sublime Security raises US$60 million Series B
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported a US$60 million Series B for Sublime Security with IVP, Citi Ventures, Index Ventures, Decibel Partners and Slow Ventures investing, bringing total funding to US$93.8 million.

events.headline: Sublime Security raises US$150 million Series C led by Georgian
events.summary: Sublime Security announced a US$150 million Series C led by Georgian, with new investors Avenir and 01A and existing investors Index Ventures, IVP, Citi Ventures and Slow Ventures. SecurityWeek put total funding at more than US$240 million.

events.headline: Sublime Security makes Email DLP generally available
events.summary: Sublime announced general availability of Email Data Loss Prevention as an add-on for Enterprise customers on Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, in Sublime-hosted and supported self-hosted environments.

events.headline: Sublime Security makes tailored phishing simulations and training generally available
events.summary: Sublime announced general availability of Tailored Phishing Simulations and Training, an add-on to Sublime Email Security that builds simulations from attacks detected in the customer's environment and delivers training when an employee clicks.

events.headline: Francisco Partners completes US$1.7 billion take-private of Sumo Logic
events.summary: Sumo Logic announced that Francisco Partners had completed its acquisition of the company for US$12.05 per share in cash, an equity value of about US$1.7 billion. The shares stopped trading on Nasdaq; a Form 25 was filed on 2023-05-12 and a Form 15 terminating registration on 2023-05-22, after which the company stopped filing public financial reports.

events.headline: Sumo Logic names Chris Malone chief executive and Conor Burns chief financial officer
events.summary: Sumo Logic announced Chris Malone, previously chief executive of Applause, as CEO and Conor Burns as CFO. The announcement quoted a Francisco Partners senior operating partner who chairs the Sumo Logic board. It did not mention the outgoing chief executive.

events.headline: Sumo Logic makes its SOC Analyst Agent generally available
events.summary: At Black Hat USA 2026 Sumo Logic made its SOC Analyst Agent generally available. The agent investigates SIEM alerts automatically and returns verdicts with supporting evidence, and analysts can continue an investigation in conversation with the Mobot assistant. The company also announced further Dojo AI agents and an MCP server that connects external AI tools to its SIEM and log analytics.

events.headline: Sumo Logic names Tom Bonos chief revenue officer
events.summary: Sumo Logic announced Tom Bonos, previously at Applause, as chief revenue officer, the third senior appointment from that company within two months.

events.headline: Federal dockets show copyright and patent suits filed against Sumo Logic in 2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Saflor v. Sumo Logic, Inc., a copyright suit, was filed on 2026-09-23 in N.D. Cal., and Atomic IP LLC v. Sumo Logic, Inc., a patent suit, was filed on 2026-01-05 in W.D. Tex. An appeal, Wasicek et al. v. Sumo Logic, Inc. et al., was filed in the Ninth Circuit on 2025-06-17. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Sumo Logic releases AWS Observability Solution v3.0.0 with 20 regions and Marketplace deployment
events.summary: Sumo Logic announced on 2026-11-18 an expanded AWS Observability Solution that adds the Zurich, Melbourne and New Zealand regions, for 20 supported AWS regions, and can be bought and deployed through AWS Marketplace Quick Launch. The press release says version 3.0.0 is available to Sumo Logic customers now. The release concerns observability rather than the Cloud SIEM product.

events.headline: Three individuals registered as persons with significant control of Sum and Substance Ltd
events.summary: Companies House records show that on 24 May 2024 three individuals were notified as persons with significant influence or control over Sum and Substance Ltd, the UK company behind Sumsub. A Cyprus company, Raritex Trade Ltd, had been registered as holding 75% or more of the shares from April 2019 until 2 October 2023, and between those dates the company had stated that it had no registrable person. The register does not show whether control changed in substance.

events.headline: Sumsub and Jelou announce an identity verification partnership
events.summary: Sumsub's newsroom lists a 5 November 2026 announcement of a partnership with Jelou to connect identity verification with financial-services journeys started in WhatsApp.

events.headline: Federal docket shows patent suit filed against Sum and Substance Ltd.
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): FinTegrity LLC v. Sum and Substance Ltd., a patent suit, was filed on 2025-03-12 in the Eastern District of Texas (2:25-cv-00292). No termination date is shown. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Sumsub joins ITU Study Group 17 on security standards as an Associate member
events.summary: Sumsub announced on 2026-11-10 that it has joined the International Telecommunication Union as an Associate member of Study Group 17, which leads the UN agency's security standardisation work. The company says it will contribute to recommendations on digital identity, biometric liveness detection and security for AI systems.

events.headline: Sweet Security extends its runtime CNAPP to Windows
events.summary: Sweet Security's press release index records a 2025-10-30 announcement that its runtime CNAPP now covers Windows workloads. The release itself was not read.

events.headline: Sweet Security raises US$75M Series B
events.summary: SecurityWeek reported on 2025-11-12 that Sweet Security had raised a US$75 million Series B led by Evolution Equity Partners with Glilot Capital Partners, Key1 Capital and Munich Re Ventures, taking total funding to US$120 million, and had introduced an AI security platform alongside its runtime CNAPP.

events.headline: Sweet Security launches virtual patching
events.summary: Sweet Security's press release index records a 2026-10-19 announcement of virtual patching intended to protect production workloads before a permanent fix is deployed. The release itself was not read.

events.headline: Sweet Security adds Reachability mapping of internet routes to cloud workloads
events.summary: Sweet Security announced on 2026-11-17 a Reachability feature that maps how the internet reaches, or is configured to reach, each workload, distinguishing routes seen in runtime traffic from routes that configuration allows. The company's post says the feature is available to all Sweet customers.

events.headline: Synack launches Active Offense, built on its Sara agentic AI architecture
events.summary: Synack announced Active Offense, which uses its Sara (Synack Autonomous Red Agent) architecture to check scanner output for weaknesses that can really be exploited and passes selected findings to the Synack Red Team for human review. The release says it was integrated into the Synack platform at launch.

events.headline: Synack announces Sara Pentest, AI-led testing of hosts and web applications
events.summary: Synack announced Sara Pentest, which uses separate AI agents for reconnaissance, attack simulation and verification against hosts and web applications, with a Synack triage team checking exploitable findings. Help Net Security carried the announcement on 2025-11-17; a later Synack release says early customer deployments began in October 2025.

events.headline: Synack announces general availability of Sara AI Pentesting
events.summary: Synack announced that Sara AI Pentesting is generally available through the Synack platform and on the AWS, Microsoft and Google Cloud marketplaces. It covers web applications and infrastructure, with findings validated by the Synack Red Team. No customer is named in the release.

events.headline: NetSPI and Synack announce an agreement to merge
events.summary: NetSPI and Synack announced a definitive agreement to merge, stating combined revenue of more than US$200M. BankInfoSecurity reported on 2026-09-03 that the combined firm would be led by NetSPI and majority owned by KKR, NetSPI's majority owner since 2022, with about 800 staff. IT Brief reported an expected close in October. Deal terms were not published.

events.headline: NetSPI and Synack complete their merger
events.summary: Synack states that the merger with NetSPI was completed on 2026-10-05; NetSPI's page says it closed in October 2026 after regulatory approvals. Both say each company continues to deliver its own platform, services and agreements for now, that no combined product or contract exists yet, and that Synack's FedRAMP Moderate authorisation is unchanged and does not extend to NetSPI products.

events.headline: Sysdig names Hatem Naguib as chief executive
events.summary: Sysdig announced the appointment of Hatem Naguib, formerly chief executive of Barracuda, as CEO and board member. The release does not name the outgoing chief executive.

events.headline: Sysdig launches Sysdig Secure AI
events.summary: Sysdig's newsroom lists a press release dated 2026-08-04 announcing Sysdig Secure AI, described as bringing machine-speed cloud defence to security teams.

events.headline: Sysdig launches Sysdig AI Defense for runtime security of AI agents
events.summary: Sysdig's newsroom lists a press release dated 2026-11-04 announcing Sysdig AI Defense, a separate offering that applies runtime security to actions taken by AI agents.

events.headline: Sysdig makes its MCP server for Sysdig Monitor generally available
events.summary: Sysdig announced on 2026-11-18 that its MCP server for monitoring is generally available, connecting AI assistants to live Kubernetes, container and cloud monitoring data in Sysdig Monitor under the same team permissions as the product's interface. The post concerns Sysdig Monitor rather than Sysdig Secure.

events.headline: Tricentis announces acquisition of Tabnine

quote.text: Bringing our technology into that platform is exactly what it was built for.

events.summary: Tricentis, a software-testing company, announced on 2026-07-30 that it had acquired Tabnine and would integrate Tabnine's Enterprise Context Engine into its Agentic Quality Engineering Platform. No price was disclosed; CTech reported an estimate of tens of millions of dollars and that existing customers would continue to receive support for Tabnine's products. The release does not say what happens to the Tabnine coding assistant or brand. On 2026-11-20 tabnine.com redirected to Tricentis pages while Tabnine documentation continued to publish releases.

events.headline: Tanium and Censys announce an exposure management partnership
events.summary: Tanium announced a partnership with Censys to combine Censys's map of internet infrastructure with Tanium's endpoint data, so that externally exposed assets can be found, prioritised and remediated in one workflow.

events.headline: Tanium releases External Attack Surface Management and Attack Path Mapping
events.summary: Tanium stated that External Attack Surface Management and Attack Path Mapping were generally available in its platform from 2026-06-22; its knowledge base dates the first Attack Path Mapping release to 2026-06-19. The company presented both again at Black Hat USA on 2026-08-03.

events.headline: Tanium Atlas becomes generally available to cloud customers
events.summary: Tanium announced general availability of Tanium Atlas, an AI console first introduced in May 2026, for commercial and US government cloud customers. The release says Atlas pauses for approval before consequential actions and that customers in regions without AI support can route requests through the United States.

events.headline: Tanium discloses exposure of its Salesforce data through the Klue breach
events.summary: Disclosed by Tanium on 2026-06-18 and reported by Help Net Security on 2026-06-19: a breach at Klue, a third-party service connected to Tanium's Salesforce environment, allowed sales account data and business contact information to be taken. Tanium stated that its products and cloud infrastructure were not affected and that it blocked the Klue integration.

events.headline: Co-founder Orion Hindawi returns as Tanium chief executive
events.summary: Tanium announced that co-founder Orion Hindawi, chief executive from 2016 to 2023, returned to the role with immediate effect, replacing Dan Streetman, who had been appointed in February 2023 and left the board. Co-founder David Hindawi returned as chairman.

events.headline: Teleport discloses exposure of internal chat transcripts through sub-processor Notion
events.summary: Disclosed by Teleport on 2026-11-11: its sub-processor Notion told it on 9 November 2026 of a data breach affecting Teleport's chat transcripts in the Notion AI app. Teleport said the breach did not occur through its own systems or involve its products, that the transcripts contained links to internal pages and one office guest Wi-Fi password, which it rotated, and no credentials or specific customer data. It notified customers mentioned in the transcripts on 10 November, disabled Notion's AI features and rated the risk to customers as low.

events.headline: Teleport patches critical remote authentication bypass (CVE-2025-49825)
events.summary: Reported by SecurityWeek on 2025-06-23: Teleport warned of a critical flaw (CVSS 9.8) allowing remote bypass of SSH authentication, fixed in versions 17.5.2 and earlier maintenance lines. Cloud customers were patched automatically, self-hosted agents had to be updated, and no exploitation in the wild was known. Teleport's trust centre lists a root-cause analysis and indicator-of-compromise instructions for the flaw.

events.headline: Teleport makes Beams, its runtime for AI agents in production infrastructure, generally available
events.summary: Teleport announced in a press release dated 2026-11-10 that Beams, in public beta since March 2026, became generally available on 2026-11-09. According to Teleport, Beams runs AI agents in isolated micro-VMs with no standing privileges, reviewed access requests, secretless connections to infrastructure, session monitoring and a kill switch, and is built on its Infrastructure Identity Platform. The release does not state pricing.

events.headline: Teleport gains AWS Security Competency status for identity and access management
events.summary: Teleport announced on 2026-11-19 that it has earned AWS Security Competency status in the Identity and Access Management category, an Amazon Web Services partner designation. This is a partner-programme recognition announced by the vendor, not an independent security certification.

events.headline: Tenable completes acquisition of Vulcan Cyber
events.summary: Tenable announced it had closed its acquisition of Vulcan Cyber Ltd., an exposure management company, saying the technology would add third-party data flows, prioritisation and remediation automation to its exposure management platform. The price was not disclosed in the release.

events.headline: Tenable appoints Steve Vintz and Mark Thurmond as permanent co-CEOs
events.summary: Tenable's board appointed Steve Vintz (chief financial officer since 2014) and Mark Thurmond (chief operating officer since 2020) as permanent co-chief executives after they had served as interim co-CEOs. The FY2025 annual report records termination benefits tied to the passing of the former chairman and chief executive.

events.headline: Tenable discloses exposure of Salesforce-held customer contact and support-case data
events.summary: Disclosed by Tenable on 2025-09-03 and reported by BankInfoSecurity on 2025-09-08: an unauthorised user accessed part of Tenable's Salesforce instance through the Salesloft Drift integration, exposing business contact details and the subject lines and initial descriptions of support cases. Tenable stated that its products and the data held in them were not affected, and that it revoked credentials and removed the Drift application.

events.headline: Tenable uses OpenAI models in its CyberAgents Exchange AI Inspector
events.summary: Tenable announced that the AI Inspector for its CyberAgents Exchange, an open hub for security AI agents and skills, uses OpenAI GPT cyber models as one step in vetting listed components, alongside a skills inspection engine from Tenable One AI Exposure and review by its research team.

events.headline: Federal docket shows Securities Exchange Act suit naming Tenable Holdings
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Donoghue v. Tenable Holdings, Inc. was filed on 2026-10-05 in the Southern District of New York (1:26-cv-08800) under the Securities Exchange Act, naming the company and an individual. No termination date is shown. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: UK SFO and French PNF open bribery and corruption investigation into Thales
events.summary: The UK Serious Fraud Office announced on 2024-11-21 that it had opened an investigation, run jointly with France's Parquet National Financier, into suspected bribery and corruption at Thales. Thales disclosed in its 2025 consolidated financial statements that the investigation concerns four group entities in France and the United Kingdom and the performance of a project in Asia, that it remained ongoing, and that Thales denies the allegations and is cooperating. The Register reported on 2024-11-22 that Thales said it would cooperate. Nothing in the sources links the investigation to the data-security product line.

events.headline: Thales launches Luna 8 hardware security module built for post-quantum algorithms
events.summary: Thales announced Luna 8, a new generation of its network hardware security module using a Thales-designed cryptographic processor, available as a network appliance. The vendor said FIPS 140-3 Level 3 and Common Criteria assessments were in progress. Luna HSMs are one of the root-of-trust options for CipherTrust Manager.

events.headline: Federal docket shows patent suit filed against Thales DIS CPL USA
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): CardAuth Solutions LLC v. Thales DIS CPL USA, Inc., a patent suit, was filed on 2026-04-24 in the Western District of Texas (1:26-cv-01065). No termination date is shown. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber acquires Zero-Shot Security, developer of the NARC threat-intelligence mapping model
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 8 January 2025 that it had acquired Zero-Shot Security, whose language-model-based system, Natural Attack Reading and Comprehension (NARC), maps described threat behaviour to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Terms were not disclosed. Zero-Shot's founder joined Tidal Cyber as director of artificial intelligence, and the company said NARC would be built into Enterprise Edition.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber relaunches its platform as the Threat-Led Defense Platform
events.summary: In a release dated 17 July 2025, Tidal Cyber introduced what it calls Threat-Led Defense and renamed its platform accordingly. The release says the platform maps ATT&CK techniques and sub-techniques down to specific adversary procedures, calculates residual risk for each technique from coverage mapping, and aligns with MITRE D3FEND, CIS and NIST frameworks. It gave no availability date and named no customer.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber raises US$10 million Series A led by Bright Pixel Capital
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced a US$10 million Series A round on 3 September 2025, led by Bright Pixel Capital, the technology investment arm of Sonae, with existing investors USAA, Squadra, Capital One, Veteran Ventures, Task Force X and Ultratech taking part. SecurityWeek reported the round the same day and put total funding at US$15 million.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber launches NARC, an AI engine that extracts adversary procedures from threat reports
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 3 November 2025 that NARC was available within its platform. The release says NARC reads unstructured material such as threat-intelligence reports, incident summaries and red-team findings, turns it into ATT&CK-aligned procedures and links those to groups, software and campaigns. It did not say which edition includes NARC, name the underlying model provider or name a customer.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber and advisory firm CGS CyberDefense announce a partnership
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 27 January 2026 a partnership pairing its platform with the advisory services of CGS CyberDefense. The release says CGS will turn the platform's coverage findings into prioritised security actions for clients in regulated sectors, among which it lists financial services.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber and threat research lab Crimson7 announce a partnership
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 26 February 2026 a partnership with Crimson7, a threat research lab. The release says Crimson7's mapped threat hunts are added to the Tidal Cyber platform as detection capabilities, showing which ATT&CK techniques are being hunted and where coverage is missing.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber separates its own threat intelligence from MITRE ATT&CK content in the platform
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 13 May 2026 a new architecture, aligned with ATT&CK version 19, that keeps ATT&CK as the technique-level structure and presents the company's own intelligence as procedure-level content with source attribution. The release says users can bring in vulnerability data and see its effect on procedures and attack likelihood. It gave no availability details.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber announces threat-led asset visibility and vulnerability prioritisation
events.summary: Tidal Cyber announced on 13 July 2026 two additions to its platform: a view of which assets matter to adversary procedures and where defences have blind spots, and ranking of vulnerabilities by their link to adversary procedures. The release did not say whether the platform discovers assets or scans for vulnerabilities itself or takes that data from other tools, and it gave no availability, edition or customer details.

events.headline: Tidal Cyber adds a Model Context Protocol server for use with AI assistants
events.summary: In a release dated 31 July 2026 and published on 3 August 2026, Tidal Cyber announced a Model Context Protocol server that lets approved AI assistants query the platform's threat profiles, coverage maps and recommendations in natural language, with authenticated, tenant-scoped access. It cites ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot as examples of such assistants and says the capability is included in the platform.

events.headline: Together AI announces completion of SOC 2 Type 2 examination
events.summary: Together AI announced it had completed a SOC 2 Type 2 examination by an independent auditor covering access management, encryption, incident response and change management.

events.headline: Amended class action complaint filed against Together AI over RedPajama dataset
events.summary: According to a first amended class action complaint filed on 20 April 2026 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (No. 3:25-cv-09578-RFL), four authors allege that Together Computer, Inc. used pirated copies of their books to build and distribute its RedPajama training dataset. The allegations have not been tested in court in any document reviewed.

events.headline: Together AI certified to ISO/IEC 27001:2022
events.summary: Together AI's trust centre announced ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification on 29 May 2026; a blog post on 10 June 2026 names A-LIGN as the certification body and gives the scope as the management system supporting its global platform.

events.headline: Together AI raises US$800M Series C at US$8.3B valuation
events.summary: TechCrunch and SiliconANGLE reported an US$800M Series C led by Aramco Ventures with Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, NVIDIA and others, at a US$8.3B valuation, with annual bookings above US$1.15B.

events.headline: Together AI discloses unauthorised download of stored customer prompt samples
events.summary: According to a disclosure published by Together AI's chief executive on 2026-11-21, an unauthorised party downloaded samples of customer prompts that the company had stored in a private Hugging Face repository after a credential for that repository was committed to a public GitHub repository by an AI coding agent. The company says the samples came from serverless inference requests to three models, mainly on four days in June and July 2026, that the party searched them for credentials to other services, and that its review of whether personal or other customer data was exposed is continuing. Together AI does not state how many customers or requests were affected and says it is working with a forensic firm and law enforcement and has made zero data retention the default for new accounts.

events.headline: Together AI launches Storage Accelerator caching for its GPU clusters
events.summary: Together AI announced on 2026-11-19 the Together Storage Accelerator, a caching layer that keeps data read from S3-compatible storage and Hugging Face Hub on a GPU cluster's local NVMe drives so later reads are served inside the cluster. The company's post says it is available now and included at no extra cost with every Together GPU Cluster; the speed figures quoted are from Together's own tests.

events.headline: Tonic.ai acquires the Fabricate synthetic data product from Mockaroo's founder
events.summary: Tonic.ai announced it had acquired Fabricate, a product that generates relational synthetic data from schemas or prompts, built by Mockaroo. Terms were not disclosed; Mockaroo's founder joined Tonic.ai to lead the product. The date is that of the press release as republished.

events.headline: Tonic.ai launches a global partner programme
events.summary: Tonic.ai announced a partner programme for systems integrators, managed service providers and resellers, with build, resell and refer tracks and role-based certifications.

events.headline: Tonic.ai and Carahsoft announce public-sector distribution partnership
events.summary: Tonic.ai announced that Carahsoft will act as its master government aggregator, making Fabricate, Structural and Textual available to US public-sector buyers through Carahsoft's contracts and resellers.

events.headline: Tonic.ai approved to de-identify Spirit Airlines dataset being sold to Google
events.summary: Tonic.ai announced that the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York approved its contract to act as independent third party de-identifying a corporate dataset that Google is buying from Spirit Airlines in bankruptcy proceedings.

events.headline: Transmit Security raises US$543 million Series A, its first outside funding
events.summary: Transmit Security announced a US$543 million Series A led by Insight Partners and General Atlantic, with Cyberstarts, Geodesic, SYN Ventures, Vintage and Artisanal Ventures, at a US$2.2 billion pre-money valuation. Press described the company as self-funded until then. Citi Ventures and Goldman Sachs Asset Management were announced as joining the round in September 2021. Recorded although older than 24 months because it brought outside shareholders into the company.

events.headline: Transmit Security says Mosaic is certified against the FAPI 2.0 security profile
events.summary: The vendor's blog of 31 March 2025 says Mosaic has been certified against FAPI 2.0, the OpenID Foundation's security profile for financial-grade APIs, citing support for mutual TLS, private-key client authentication, pushed authorization requests and sender-constrained tokens. The certification listing itself was not checked.

events.headline: Transmit Security adds transaction monitoring to its detection and response service
events.summary: The vendor's release announcement of 8 May 2026 lists Transaction Monitoring as generally available: real-time evaluation of transactions through SDK and backend APIs, a journey step, a portal for investigating transactions and built-in payment-fraud detections. A blog of 16 June 2026 introduced it as part of Detection and Response Services. The documentation page read on 2026-11-22 still describes the backend API and the portal page as early availability.

events.headline: Transmit Security names Matt Thompson chief executive; co-founder Mickey Boodaei becomes chairman
events.summary: Transmit Security named Matt Thompson, previously president and chief commercial officer of Socure, as chief executive. BankInfoSecurity and CTech reported that co-founder Mickey Boodaei, chief executive since the company's founding in 2014, becomes chairman and stays involved in product strategy.

events.headline: Transmit Security unveils Agentic Trust for detecting and governing AI agents
events.summary: Alongside its change of chief executive, the vendor announced Agentic Trust for financial institutions and merchants: detection of AI-agent traffic in online channels, classification of the agent and its intent, and controls to allow, limit, hold for customer approval or stop an agent's actions. The release gives no general-availability date or price.

events.headline: STG launches Trellix from merged McAfee Enterprise and FireEye
events.summary: Symphony Technology Group announced the launch of Trellix, a new business formed from its merger of McAfee Enterprise and FireEye, which the release dates to October 2021. The McAfee Enterprise secure service edge products were to become a separate business.

events.headline: Trellix appoints Vishal Rao as chief executive
events.summary: Trellix announced that Vishal Rao, from STG portfolio company Skyhigh Security, would succeed Bryan Palma as chief executive and lead both companies. Palma had led Trellix since 2021.

events.headline: Trellix reports breach of part of its source code repository
events.summary: Reported by SecurityWeek on 2026-05-04 and BleepingComputer on 2026-05-08: Trellix said on 1 May 2026 that there had been unauthorised access to a portion of its source code repository, that it was investigating with forensic experts and had notified law enforcement, and that it had found no evidence its release or distribution process was affected. BleepingComputer reported that the RansomHouse group claimed responsibility, which Trellix said it was looking into.

events.headline: Trellix appoints Joe Chen as chief technology officer
events.summary: Trellix announced Joe Chen as chief technology officer, replacing an interim appointee, with a stated focus on strengthening its research and development processes.

events.headline: Federal dockets show employment and patent suits filed against Trellix entities in 2025-2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Hastings v. Trellix Public Sector, LLC, an employment civil-rights suit, was filed on 2026-09-02 in S.D. Ga., and Quickvault, Inc. v. Musarubra US LLC, a patent suit, was filed on 2025-11-10 in E.D. Tex. Neither shows a termination date. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Trend Micro renames its enterprise business TrendAI
events.summary: Trend Micro announced that its enterprise cybersecurity business now operates under the name TrendAI, with the platform named TrendAI Vision One. The listed company remains Trend Micro Incorporated; the release names Rachel Jin as head of TrendAI.

events.headline: Trend Micro warns of exploited command injection flaws in on-premises Apex One
events.summary: Reported by SecurityWeek and Help Net Security on 2025-08-06: Trend Micro disclosed two command injection vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-54948 and CVE-2025-54987) in the management console of on-premises Apex One, said it had seen at least one attempt to exploit one of them, and issued a temporary fix tool ahead of a patch expected in mid-August 2025. The affected product is the on-premises predecessor line, not the product tracked here.

events.headline: Federal dockets show two suits filed against Trend Micro in W.D. Tex. in 2025-2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): ZapFraud Inc. v. Trend Micro Incorporated, a patent suit, was filed on 2026-07-20, and Congruent Media Resourcing LLC v. Trend Micro Incorporated was filed on 2025-11-13, both in the Western District of Texas. Neither shows a termination date. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Trustible raises US$4.6 million seed round led by Lookout Ventures
events.summary: Technical.ly reported on 2025-06-10 that Trustible had raised an oversubscribed US$4.6 million seed round led by Lookout Ventures, with angel investors taking part, following a US$1.6 million pre-seed round in 2023.

events.headline: Kofax renames itself Tungsten Automation
events.summary: Kofax announced on 16 January 2024 that it had changed its name to Tungsten Automation, saying the name reflected its move from document capture to AI-powered workflow automation. Products including TotalAgility were renamed under the new brand.

events.headline: Clearlake Capital and TA Associates complete acquisition of Kofax from Thoma Bravo
events.summary: Kofax announced on 25 July 2022 that Clearlake Capital Group and TA Associates had completed their acquisition of the company from Thoma Bravo. Financial terms were not disclosed. The company was renamed Tungsten Automation in January 2024.

events.headline: Tungsten Automation reports unauthorised access to its internal IT network affecting 5,556 people
events.summary: Reported by sharedserviceslink on 10 September 2025 and by ClaimDepot on 23 August 2025, both citing breach notifications filed with US state attorneys general: an unauthorised party accessed Tungsten Automation's internal IT network on or about 20 May 2025, the company detected suspicious activity on 27 May 2025, and files containing personal information of at least 5,556 people were obtained. Notices were sent from 22 August 2025 with 24 months of identity monitoring. The reports describe internal IT systems and do not mention the company's customer cloud services.

events.headline: Peter Hantman becomes chief executive of Tungsten Automation; Reynolds Bish moves to executive chairman
events.summary: Tungsten Automation announced on 7 July 2025 that Peter Hantman, president and chief operating officer since November 2023, had been promoted to chief executive officer effective 1 July 2025, and that Robert Watson had been appointed chief financial officer. Reynolds C. Bish, chief executive since 2007, became executive chairman.

events.headline: Tungsten Automation launches its unified platform and a tiered TotalAgility release
events.summary: Tungsten Automation announced on 16 September 2025 the Tungsten Automation Platform and a TotalAgility release sold in three tiers: Standard for intelligent document processing, Advanced for workflow automation and Enterprise for knowledge discovery.

events.headline: Tungsten Automation announces FedRAMP High authority to operate for TotalAgility Cloud
events.summary: Tungsten Automation announced on 19 March 2026 that the Tungsten TotalAgility Cloud Platform had received a FedRAMP High authority to operate. The release does not name the sponsoring agency. The FedRAMP Marketplace entry could not be opened in this review.

events.headline: Tungsten Automation announces GovRAMP Authorized status for TotalAgility Cloud
events.summary: Tungsten Automation announced on 29 June 2026 that Tungsten TotalAgility Cloud had achieved GovRAMP Authorized status, the US state and local government cloud security programme formerly called StateRAMP, in part through its partnership with the hosting platform FedHIVE.

events.headline: Tungsten Automation announces IRAP assessment at PROTECTED level for TotalAgility Cloud in Australia
events.summary: Tungsten Automation announced in July 2026 that its TotalAgility Cloud Platform and InvoiceAgility Cloud Platform had been independently assessed at the PROTECTED level under the Australian Infosec Registered Assessors Program. The assessor is not named in the release.

events.headline: turbopuffer takes new financing from Thrive Capital and Lachy Groom
events.summary: BetaKit reported on 2025-12-19 that turbopuffer had raised new financing from existing backer Lachy Groom and new investor Thrive Capital. The amount, stage and valuation were not disclosed. The date recorded is the date of the report.

events.headline: UiPath acquires Peak AI
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch on 2025-03-13: UiPath acquired Peak, a Manchester-founded company that builds decision-making AI for pricing and inventory, for an undisclosed cash price. UiPath's Form 10-K confirms the acquisition of Peak AI Limited in March 2025.

events.headline: UiPath acquires WorkFusion, maker of AI agents for financial crime compliance
events.summary: UiPath announced on 2026-02-06 that it had acquired WorkFusion, whose pre-built AI agents handle sanctions-screening alert review, adverse media monitoring, KYC and transaction-monitoring investigations for banks. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: UiPath names Hitesh Ramani chief financial officer
events.summary: UiPath disclosed in a Form 8-K that Hitesh Ramani, previously deputy chief financial officer and chief accounting officer, became chief financial officer on 2026-09-03. Ashim Gupta stepped down as chief financial officer and continues as chief operating officer. Yazdi Bagli joined the board the same day.

events.headline: UiPath IXP generative extraction for unstructured documents becomes generally available
events.summary: UiPath's release notes record that generative extraction for unstructured and complex documents launched as part of UiPath IXP on 2025-08-01, generally available in the United States and Europe regions and in public preview in Canada, Australia and Japan.

events.headline: UiPath named a launch partner for Google Cloud's Gemini for healthcare
events.summary: In a press release dated 2026-11-10, UiPath said it is a launch partner for Google Cloud's Gemini for healthcare. The UiPath MCP Server lets Gemini users start and monitor automations and hand work to agents that run on the UiPath Platform under the customer's existing permissions and audit controls. UiPath said the server is in preview for joint UiPath and Google Cloud customers.

events.headline: UpGuard raises US$75M Series C led by Springcoast Partners
events.summary: UpGuard announced a US$75 million Series C led by Springcoast Partners with existing investors August Capital, Square Peg Capital and Pelion Venture Partners. SecurityBrief described it as a minority round.

events.headline: UpGuard introduces Risk Automations
events.summary: UpGuard's press page lists the launch of Risk Automations, a platform product for triggered workflows, alerts and ticketing, on 2026-03-03.

events.headline: Novacoast acquires UpGuard's managed vendor assessment business
events.summary: UpGuard announced that Novacoast acquired its managed vendor assessments service business, with the delivering analysts moving to Novacoast from 2026-11-15. Customers continue to use the UpGuard platform. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Upwind raises US$100M
events.summary: Upwind announced on 2 December 2024 that it had secured US$100M; TechCrunch later described this as its 2024 Series A.

events.headline: Upwind raises US$250M Series B at a reported US$1.5B valuation
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 29 January 2026 that Upwind raised a US$250M Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Salesforce Ventures and Picture Capital, at a US$1.5B valuation. The vendor's own posts on the round are dated 26 January 2026.

events.headline: Upwind acquires AI security startup Aegis
events.summary: Upwind acquired Aegis, an Israeli AI security startup founded in early 2026, whose founders now lead a new Upwind AI Security Labs unit. Terms were not disclosed; Ynetnews cited Israeli press estimates of tens of millions of dollars in a stock-based deal.

events.headline: Upwind raises US$400M Series C at a reported US$3.8B valuation
events.summary: Upwind announced a US$400M Series C led by Bessemer Venture Partners with Canapi Ventures, TCV, Greylock and Salesforce Ventures among participants, bringing total funding to more than US$800M. SecurityWeek reported a US$3.8B valuation.

events.headline: Upwind launches Upwind Response with automated runtime containment
events.summary: Upwind announced Upwind Response on its blog on 2026-11-12. It combines Runtime Containment, which Upwind says blocks an attacker's network access and stops the malicious process during an active attack with temporary, reversible actions, with live threat-feed dashboards and a consolidated issues feed reachable through Upwind MCP. Upwind said it is available to every existing and new customer; pricing was not stated.

events.headline: EQT agrees to sell controlling stake in Utimaco to SGT Capital
events.summary: EQT Private Equity announced the sale of its controlling stake in Utimaco to SGT Capital, with EQT remaining a minority owner and closing expected in the fourth quarter of 2021. The price was not disclosed. Help Net Security reported that Bain Capital Credit provided financing.

events.headline: Utimaco sells its lawful interception business to INVISION and PINOVA
events.summary: Utimaco announced that investment firms INVISION and PINOVA acquired its telecom solutions division, which makes lawful interception systems, in a transaction that closed on 2025-09-30. Terms were not disclosed. Utimaco said it would focus fully on data security and cybersecurity.

events.headline: u.trust Anchor module behind the Se-Series HSM validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3
events.summary: The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program registry lists the Utimaco u.trust Anchor hardware module under certificate #5223, validated to FIPS 140-3 overall Level 3 on 2026-04-01 with a sunset date of 2031-03-31. Utimaco announced the certification of the u.trust General Purpose HSM Se-Series on 2026-05-12 and cites this certificate on the product page.

events.headline: Utimaco launches Quantum Protect post-quantum package for the Se-Series HSM
events.summary: Utimaco announced Quantum Protect, a firmware application package for the u.trust General Purpose HSM Se-Series adding ML-KEM, ML-DSA, LMS, HSS, XMSS and XMSS-MT, activated in the field, together with a free simulator. SLH-DSA was described as planned.

events.headline: Utimaco says Quantum Protect algorithms passed NIST algorithm validation testing
events.summary: Utimaco announced that the LMS, ML-KEM and ML-DSA implementations in its Quantum Protect package passed NIST Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program testing. No certificate numbers were given, and these algorithms do not appear on the HSM's FIPS 140-3 module certificate.

events.headline: Utimaco launches u.trust General Purpose HSM CSe-Series
events.summary: Utimaco announced the CSe-Series, a tamper-active model positioned above the Se-Series with up to 31 containerised HSMs, and listed FIPS 140-3 Level 4 certification as pending. On 2026-11-20 the NIST modules-in-process list showed a u.trust Anchor CSe submission at the comment-resolution stage.

events.headline: Utimaco launches Enterprise Key Manager as a Service for Microsoft Azure BYOK
events.summary: Utimaco announced a hosted key-management service for Microsoft's bring-your-own-key function, built on the u.trust General Purpose HSM and its virtual Enterprise Secure Key Manager, and said it had been a Microsoft external key management partner since June 2025.

events.headline: Utimaco appoints Heino Erdmann as chief financial officer
events.summary: Utimaco announced that Heino Erdmann became chief financial officer from 2025-01-01, succeeding Martin Stamm, who retired at the end of 2024.

events.headline: Utimaco appoints Axel Deininger as chief innovation officer
events.summary: Utimaco announced that Axel Deininger, chief executive of secunet from 2019 to 2025, joined its management board as chief innovation officer.

events.headline: Delinea and Utimaco integrate Secret Server with the Se-Series HSM
events.summary: Delinea and Utimaco announced an integration in which keys protecting credentials held in Delinea Secret Server are stored in the u.trust General Purpose HSM Se-Series.

events.headline: Keyfactor and Utimaco expand partnership on HSM-backed PKI
events.summary: Keyfactor and Utimaco announced an expanded partnership pairing the Keyfactor EJBCA hardware appliance with Utimaco's u.trust General Purpose HSM, which the release says can be upgraded in the field with ML-KEM and ML-DSA.

events.headline: Microsoft, Marvell and Utimaco announce Azure Payment HSM v2 preview
events.summary: Utimaco announced that its Atalla payments software module, running on Marvell LiquidSecurity hardware, underpins Azure Payment HSM v2, in public preview from 2026-09-17 in two regions. This concerns the payment HSM line, not the general-purpose Se-Series.

events.headline: ValidMind and Genpact announce model risk management as a service partnership
events.summary: ValidMind and Genpact announced a partnership to offer model risk management as a service to financial institutions, combining ValidMind's platform with Genpact's advisory services.

events.headline: ValidMind appoints Jan Larsen as chief revenue officer
events.summary: ValidMind announced that Jan Larsen, previously a member of its advisory board, joined as chief revenue officer.

events.headline: ValidMind becomes available on AWS Marketplace
events.summary: ValidMind announced availability on AWS Marketplace, with integrations for Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and billing through the customer's AWS account.

events.headline: ValidMind releases open-source Atryum and opens early access to Agent Authority
events.summary: ValidMind released Atryum, an open-source control layer that checks AI agent tool calls against policy and logs decisions, and opened early access to Agent Authority, a commercial product built on it.

events.headline: Varonis completes acquisition of database activity monitoring firm Cyral
events.summary: Varonis completed its acquisition of Cyral, Inc. on 17 March 2025, adding database activity monitoring to its platform, according to its annual report. The price was not broken out in the sections reviewed.

events.headline: Varonis completes acquisition of email security firm SlashNext
events.summary: Varonis completed its acquisition of SlashNext, Inc., an email security company, on 28 August 2025, according to its annual report. Trade press put the price at up to US$150 million.

events.headline: Varonis cuts about 5% of its workforce alongside third-quarter 2025 results
events.summary: Reported by BankInfoSecurity and CTech on 2025-10-29: Varonis cut about 5% of its workforce when it announced third-quarter 2025 results and lowered full-year guidance. BankInfoSecurity put the number at roughly 120 people and reported that the company attributed the quarter to weaker on-premises subscription renewals and an under-performing federal business. Both outlets reported a share-price fall of more than 45% the next day.

events.headline: Securities class action filed against Varonis and certain executive officers
events.summary: Disclosed by Varonis in its Form 10-K filed 2026-02-04: a purported class action was filed against the company and certain of its executive officers in January 2026. A plaintiff law firm notice dated 2026-01-14 describes a class period of 4 February 2025 to 28 October 2025 and allegations about statements on converting existing customers to the SaaS product. The allegations are untested; no ruling was found. The date used here is that of the law firm notice, as the filing date was not confirmed from a primary source.

events.headline: Varonis announces acquisition of AI security firm AllTrue.ai
events.summary: Varonis announced it would acquire AllTrue.ai, a company that inventories AI models and agents and the data they can reach. SecurityWeek, citing a Wall Street Journal report, put the price at US$150 million; Varonis did not disclose it.

events.headline: Varonis adds LLM Gateway and MCP Gateway to Atlas AI Security
events.summary: The Varonis changelog records the release of an LLM Gateway for controlling AI model usage and spend and an MCP Gateway for governing agent tool access, both within Atlas AI Security, followed on 12 November by an Agent Manifest feature.

events.headline: Federal docket shows employment discrimination suit filed against Varonis
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Kinzie v. Varonis Systems, Inc., an employment suit under the Americans with Disabilities Act, was filed on 2025-11-19 in the District of Montana (9:25-cv-00195). No termination date is shown. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Varonis sets 22 December stockholder vote on US$6.3B all-cash sale to Proofpoint
events.summary: Varonis filed a definitive merger proxy with the SEC on 2026-11-16 calling a virtual special meeting for 2026-12-22 (record date 2026-11-16) to vote on its sale to Proofpoint, a Thoma Bravo portfolio company, for US$49.75 per share in cash. The deal, announced in a joint release filed on 2026-10-15 and valued at about US$6.3B, is expected to close in the first half of 2027 subject to stockholder and regulatory approvals; Varonis would then leave Nasdaq and become private. The proxy says US antitrust notifications were filed on 2026-10-19 and that clearances in five other jurisdictions are also required.

events.headline: Insight Partners completes its acquisition of Veeam at a valuation of about US$5 billion
events.summary: Veeam announced that Insight Partners had completed the acquisition announced on 9 January 2020, at a valuation of about US$5 billion, and that the company would move its headquarters to the United States from Switzerland with a new chief executive. TechCrunch reported the deal and that Insight had invested US$500 million in Veeam the year before. Insight Partners is a financial investor, so Veeam remains an active vendor under its own name.

events.headline: Veeam valued at US$15 billion in a US$2 billion secondary share sale led by TPG
events.summary: Veeam announced a US$2 billion secondary offering led by TPG, with Temasek, Neuberger Berman Capital Solutions and others, valuing the company at US$15 billion. The company said it had US$1.7 billion of annualised recurring revenue as of September 2024. BankInfoSecurity reported the chief executive saying Insight Partners would remain the controlling investor. Existing holders sold the shares, so no new capital went to the company.

events.headline: Veeam discloses a critical remote-code-execution flaw in Backup & Replication 12
events.summary: Disclosed by Veeam on 2025-03-19 in knowledge base article KB4724: CVE-2025-23120, rated critical (CVSS 9.9), allowed an authenticated domain user to run code on a domain-joined backup server. It affected version 12.3.0.310 and earlier version 12 builds and was fixed in version 12.3.1. The flaw does not appear in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue version read on 2026-11-23.

events.headline: Veeam discloses a second critical flaw affecting domain-joined backup servers
events.summary: Disclosed by Veeam on 2025-06-17 in knowledge base article KB4743: CVE-2025-23121, rated critical (CVSS 9.9), allowed an authenticated domain user to run code on a domain-joined backup server, and CVE-2025-24286, rated high, let a user with the Backup Operator role alter jobs to run code. Both were fixed in Veeam Backup & Replication 12.3.2. Neither appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue version read on 2026-11-23.

events.headline: Veeam launches Veeam Data Platform v13
events.summary: Veeam announced version 13 of Veeam Data Platform, together with an integration interface for additional hypervisors. The lifecycle policy dates Veeam Backup & Replication 13 to November 2025, with support until November 2028.

events.headline: Veeam completes its US$1.725 billion acquisition of Securiti AI
events.summary: Veeam announced it had completed the acquisition of Securiti AI, a data security posture management and AI governance vendor, for US$1.725 billion, taking on about 600 employees; Securiti's founder joined Veeam as a president. TechCrunch reported the agreement on 21 October 2025 as a mix of cash and stock. Securiti's products are rated separately under Securiti.

events.headline: Veeam cryptographic module receives FIPS 140-3 validation
events.summary: NIST's Cryptographic Module Validation Program lists certificate 5156 for the Veeam Cryptographic Module based on the OpenSSL FIPS Provider, a software module validated at overall level 1 on 13 February 2026 by Lightship Security, active until 10 March 2030.

events.headline: Veeam Data Platform v13.1 becomes generally available
events.summary: Veeam announced general availability of version 13.1, adding support for six more hypervisors, malware scanning of file shares, expanded threat detection for Azure, automated Active Directory forest recovery, and post-quantum and hybrid FIPS cryptography options. The release notes give 29 July 2026 as the download date.

events.headline: Veeam discloses a critical authorisation bypass fixed in Backup & Replication 13.1.2
events.summary: Disclosed by Veeam on 2026-10-27 in knowledge base article KB4948: CVE-2026-108142, rated critical (CVSS v4.0 9.1), allowed an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authorisation on the CDP Coordinator Service in version 13.0 and 13.1 builds; two medium-severity path traversal flaws were fixed in the same builds, 13.1.2 and 13.0.3. Veeam said the flaws were reported through its HackerOne programme; version 12 is not affected. None appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue version read on 2026-11-23.

events.headline: TA Associates growth investment values Veracode at US$2.5B
events.summary: Veracode announced on 2022-03-15 a growth investment from TA Associates valuing the company at US$2.5 billion, with existing majority investor Thoma Bravo keeping a minority position. Closing was expected in the second quarter of 2022; completion was not verified. Dated to the announcement.

events.headline: Veracode acquires Phylum's malicious-package technology
events.summary: Veracode announced on 2025-01-06 that it had acquired certain assets of Phylum, Inc., including its malicious package analysis and package firewall technology, for integration into its composition analysis product. Terms were not disclosed.

events.headline: Veriff appoints Rob Brazier as chief product officer
events.summary: Veriff announced Rob Brazier, who previously held product leadership roles at Apollo GraphQL, Grammarly and Twilio, as chief product officer.

events.headline: Veriff announces FIDO Alliance Document Authenticity certification
events.summary: Veriff announced that its fully automated identity verification mode received FIDO Alliance Document Authenticity certification after testing by Ingenium Biometrics, covering 19 document types from 12 countries.

events.headline: Veriff appoints Philippe de Passorio as chief revenue officer
events.summary: Veriff announced Philippe de Passorio, previously senior vice president of sales for North America at Adyen, as chief revenue officer.

events.headline: Veriff introduces Presence Verification for deepfake and coercion detection
events.summary: Veriff announced Presence Verification, which it describes as combining deepfake and injection detection, coercion detection and device and network signals into one automated decision.

events.headline: Federal dockets show three suits filed against Veriff OU in S.D.N.Y. in January 2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Reed v. Veriff OU (filed 2026-01-19), Stockton v. Veriff OU (filed 2026-01-20) and McLaughlin v. Veriff OU (filed 2026-01-21) were opened in the Southern District of New York, each also naming Verizon Value, Inc. No termination dates are shown. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: WALLIX PAM receives German BSI fixed-time security certification, recognised by ANSSI
events.summary: WALLIX announced on 2025-10-07 that WALLIX PAM had obtained the fixed-time security certification (BSZ) of Germany's Federal Office for Information Security, which France's ANSSI recognises as equivalent to its CSPN certification. The vendor's about page gives the certified version as 12.0.14, the date as 2025-09-29 and the certificate as BSI-DSZ-BSZ-0020-2025.

events.headline: WALLIX publishes critical advisories for Bastion REST API and Access Manager SAML
