events.summary: Published by WALLIX on 2026-07-20: advisory WSA-2026-07-0001 describes an unauthenticated privilege escalation in the REST API of WALLIX Bastion 12.3.0 to 12.3.6 and 12.4.0, rated critical (CVSS 4.0 score 10.0) and fixed in 12.3.7 and 12.4.1; WSA-2026-07-0002 describes an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the SAML service provider of WALLIX Access Manager, rated high (8.7). The advisories said researchers planned to publish technical details in September 2026.

events.headline: WALLIX publishes three batches of Bastion advisories covering REST API, RDP and SSH proxies
events.summary: Published by WALLIX on 2026-10-26: advisories WSA-2026-10-0501 to 0507 (REST API authorisation flaws, one critical), 0601 to 0623 (RDP proxy, one critical and ten high) and 0701 to 0717 (SSH proxy, one critical and eight high) for WALLIX Bastion, with fixes in versions 12.0.27 and 12.5.0. No CVE identifiers were assigned.

events.headline: NextStage AM converts EUR 5 million of WALLIX bonds into shares
events.summary: WALLIX announced on 2026-08-11 that NextStage AM had converted all the bonds it subscribed in 2023 into 312,499 new shares, adding EUR 5.0 million to equity and reducing debt by the same amount, and taking the share count to 7,099,569. The release also refers to a non-dilutive financing of EUR 25 million, extendable to EUR 65 million, announced on 2026-07-28.

events.headline: Ricoh Innovation Fund makes a strategic investment in Weaviate
events.summary: Dealroom News reported on 2026-06-16 that Ricoh had invested in Weaviate through the RICOH Innovation Fund, in a deal announced in March 2026, and plans to combine its document-capture technology with Weaviate's database. The amount was not disclosed and the day of the announcement is not given in the source, so the first of the month is used.

events.headline: Weaviate releases version 1.40 of its database
events.summary: Weaviate's blog announced release 1.40 on 26 October 2026, making named-vector dropping and 4-bit rotational quantization generally available and adding a new filtered-search strategy. A separate post on 22 October 2026 announced deprecation of the GraphQL API with migration paths.

events.headline: Weaviate announces ISO 27001 certification
events.summary: An announcement on Weaviate's trust centre dated 17 September 2025 says the company was assessed against ISO 27001 by external auditors Sensiba and that the certificate is available to registered visitors. The certificate itself was not reviewed.

events.headline: CoreWeave agrees to acquire Weights & Biases
events.summary: CoreWeave announced on 2025-03-04 an agreement to acquire Weights & Biases, a San Francisco AI developer platform founded in 2017, with the price undisclosed and closing expected in the first half of 2025. The release said customers could keep deploying on-premise or with the infrastructure provider of their choice. TechCrunch reported the same day, citing The Information, a price of US$1.7 billion.

events.headline: CoreWeave completes acquisition of Weights & Biases
events.summary: CoreWeave's Form 10-K for FY2025 records the acquisition of Weights and Biases, Inc. on 2025-05-05, and CoreWeave's site gives the same completion date. CoreWeave said it remained committed to the interoperability of the Weights & Biases platform across deployment options and infrastructure providers.

events.headline: CoreWeave launches Forge and moves Weights & Biases cloud accounts into it
events.summary: CoreWeave announced CoreWeave Forge on 2026-09-30, combining Weights & Biases Models with OpenPipe post-training and marimo notebooks, and introducing Agent Lens for agent observability. On the same date the Weights & Biases multi-tenant application moved to forge.coreweave.com with sign-in through CoreWeave, and its documentation moved into CoreWeave's documentation site; Dedicated Cloud and Self-Managed addresses were unchanged and the SDK and API endpoints kept working.

events.headline: WitnessAI raises $58 million led by Sound Ventures and launches Agentic Security
events.summary: WitnessAI announced US$58 million in strategic funding led by Sound Ventures, with Fin Capital, Samsung Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures and Forgepoint Capital Partners, and existing investors Google Ventures and Ballistic Ventures. SecurityWeek put total funding at over US$85 million. The company announced Agentic Security, which extends monitoring and run-time protection to AI agents and MCP servers, at the same time.

events.headline: WitnessAI completes SOC 2 Type II audit
events.summary: WitnessAI announced on 2025-10-21 that it had completed a SOC 2 Type II audit. The release does not name the auditor, the trust services criteria covered or the audit period.

events.headline: Google completes US$32B all-cash acquisition of Wiz
events.summary: Google completed its acquisition of Wiz on 2026-03-11, a year after announcing it. Wiz joined Google Cloud, keeps its brand, and both companies say its products continue to work across Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud. Press reports say US review concluded in November 2025 and the European Commission approved the deal unconditionally in February 2026.

events.headline: Google signs agreement to acquire Wiz for US$32B in cash
events.summary: Google LLC announced a definitive agreement to acquire Wiz, Inc. for US$32 billion in cash, subject to regulatory approvals. Google said Wiz products would stay available on other major clouds.

events.headline: Wiz releases its AI Security Agent in public preview
events.summary: Wiz announced on its blog on 2026-11-16 that the Wiz AI Security Agent is in public preview through the Wiz Preview Hub. Wiz says the agent discovers AI applications and agents, including ones defined only in code, compares each agent's intended purpose with its tools and permissions, and links AI-specific risks such as prompt injection to cloud context in the Wiz Security Graph. No pricing was given.

events.headline: Writer raises US$200 million Series C at a US$1.9 billion valuation
events.summary: Writer announced on 2024-11-12 a US$200 million Series C co-led by Premji Invest, Radical Ventures and ICONIQ Growth at a US$1.9 billion valuation, with Salesforce Ventures, Adobe Ventures, B Capital, Citi Ventures, IBM Ventures and Workday Ventures participating. TechCrunch reported that this brought total funding to US$326 million.

events.headline: Writer announces ISO/IEC 27001, 27701 and 42001 certifications
events.summary: Writer announced on 2025-05-28 that it had been certified to ISO/IEC 27001, 27701 and 42001, naming A-LIGN as the certification body.

events.headline: Writer adds direct access to Amazon Bedrock models and an agent supervision suite
events.summary: Writer announced on 2025-12-02, at AWS re:Invent, that customers could use Amazon Bedrock models and Bedrock Guardrails inside its agent platform, and introduced a supervision and orchestration suite for approving and monitoring agents.

events.headline: Writer releases Palmyra X6 model and an upgraded agent harness
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2026-08-13 that Writer released Palmyra X6, which it described as a post-trained variant of Z.ai's open-source GLM-5.2, alongside harness changes that Writer said could cut costs for basic tasks by up to half. Writer's models page calls Palmyra X6 the default model across its platform.

events.headline: Writer launches Enterprise Brain context layer in early access
events.summary: Writer announced Enterprise Brain on 2026-09-09 as a governed context layer for its agents, in early access for selected customers, with Agent Memory, WRITER Meet and WRITER for Slack generally available.

events.headline: Writer renames WRITER AI Studio to Control Center
events.summary: Writer said on its blog on 2026-11-20 that WRITER AI Studio is now called Control Center, reflecting its role as the admin hub for agent governance after agent building moved into the main app. The navigation is reorganised into seven sections covering usage, activity logs, build governance, integrations, security, billing and settings. Writer said existing configurations and permissions are unchanged, and announced no pricing change.

events.headline: Irish Data Protection Commission opens inquiry into use of X posts to train Grok
events.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission announced on 2025-04-11 an inquiry into X Internet Unlimited Company to determine whether personal data in public X posts by EU and EEA users was lawfully processed to train xAI's Grok models. No outcome was found in this review.

events.headline: xAI employee's API key for private Grok models exposed on GitHub for about two months
events.summary: Reported by KrebsOnSecurity on 2025-05-01 and GBHackers on 2025-05-05: an xAI employee published a private API key on GitHub that stayed valid for about two months and gave access to at least 60 private and fine-tuned models. GitGuardian said it alerted the employee on 2025-03-02 and xAI's security team on 2025-04-30, after which the repository was removed. KrebsOnSecurity reported that xAI did not respond to requests for comment.

events.headline: xAI lays off at least 500 data annotation workers
events.summary: Reported by TechCrunch and Reuters on 2025-09-13, citing Business Insider: xAI laid off at least 500 workers, about a third of the team that labels data for Grok. The company pointed to a post saying it would expand its specialist AI tutor team.

events.headline: xAI launches Grok Business and Grok Enterprise
events.summary: xAI announced Grok Business, a self-serve team plan, and Grok Enterprise, which adds custom single sign-on, directory sync and an Enterprise Vault option with a dedicated data plane and customer-managed encryption keys. The post said customer data is not used for training.

events.headline: xAI raises US$20 billion Series E
events.summary: xAI announced an upsized US$20 billion Series E with investors including Valor Equity Partners, StepStone Group, Fidelity, Qatar Investment Authority, MGX and Baron Capital Group, and strategic investors NVIDIA and Cisco Investments. It was the last round before SpaceX acquired the company.

events.headline: European Commission opens Digital Services Act proceedings against X over Grok images
events.summary: Reported by the Associated Press on 2026-01-27 and BankInfoSecurity on 2026-02-17: the European Commission opened formal proceedings against X under the Digital Services Act over whether it assessed and mitigated risks from Grok on X, after Grok generated non-consensual sexualised images. AP reported that the case covers Grok on X, not the standalone Grok service, and that X pointed to an earlier statement on its policies. No outcome was found in this review.

events.headline: SpaceX acquires xAI
events.summary: xAI stated on 2026-02-02 that SpaceX had acquired it. SpaceX's later quarterly report says X.AI Holdings Corp. became a wholly owned subsidiary on that date through a share exchange accounted for as a common control merger. Reuters reported that a person familiar with the deal valued SpaceX at US$1 trillion and xAI at US$250 billion, with xAI investors receiving 0.1433 SpaceX shares per xAI share.

events.headline: UK Information Commissioner's Office opens formal investigations into X and X.AI over Grok
events.summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office announced on 2026-02-03 formal investigations into X Internet Unlimited Company and X.AI LLC over their processing of personal data in relation to Grok and its potential to produce harmful sexualised images and video. The ICO stated it had not reached a view on whether data protection law was infringed.

events.headline: Two more xAI co-founders leave, taking departures to six of twelve
events.summary: TechCrunch reported on 2026-02-10 and eWeek on 2026-02-12 that co-founders Yuhuai (Tony) Wu and Jimmy Ba left xAI in the same week, so that six of the company's twelve co-founders had departed, five of them within a year. eWeek reported that Elon Musk described a reorganisation following the SpaceX merger.

events.headline: SpaceXSI agrees to give Anthropic access to its Colossus 1 supercomputer
events.summary: The vendor announced an agreement to give Anthropic access to Colossus 1, a cluster it describes as having more than 220,000 NVIDIA GPUs. The post said Anthropic plans to use the capacity for Claude Pro and Claude Max subscribers and had expressed interest in orbital compute capacity. No financial terms were given.

events.headline: Former xAI engineer sues xAI and SpaceX alleging dismissal for raising safety concerns
events.summary: Reported by Reuters on 2026-06-10 and Digit on 2026-06-11: former xAI engineer Devin Kim sued xAI and its parent SpaceX in California state court, alleging he was dismissed in September 2025 for raising safety concerns about Grok. The suit claims retaliation and wrongful discharge and seeks unspecified damages. Reuters reported that xAI and SpaceX did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

events.headline: Parent company SpaceX lists on Nasdaq
events.summary: SpaceX, the vendor's owner since February 2026, filed its final IPO prospectus with the SEC on 2026-06-12; its Class A shares trade on Nasdaq under SPCX. Engadget reported on 2026-07-07 that SpaceX went public in June. The amount raised was not confirmed from the sources reviewed.

events.headline: xAI is rebranded SpaceXAI
events.summary: Engadget reported on 2026-07-07 that xAI was rebranded SpaceXAI with a new logo in a post on X on 2026-07-06, following SpaceX's February acquisition, and that the website already showed the new name while official filings did not yet.

events.headline: Grok 4.7 released
events.summary: The vendor introduced Grok 4.7, which it describes as its most capable reasoning model, on 2026-09-21. The API lists it at US$2 input and US$6 output per million tokens with a 500,000-token context window, and the release notes say it is served on the US regional endpoint.

events.headline: SpaceXAI is renamed SpaceXSI
events.summary: Fox Business reported on 2026-10-04 that Elon Musk said SpaceX's AI division would be renamed from SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, for 'super intelligence'. The vendor's Enterprise Terms, last updated 2026-10-27, name the contracting entity as SpaceX Super Intelligence LLC, and its site uses the SpaceXSI name. The date on which the legal entity name changed was not found.

events.headline: Federal dockets show at least ten new suits naming X.AI Corp. since mid-September 2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): the ten most recent of 58 dockets naming X.AI were all filed between 2026-09-17 and 2026-11-19. They include several Doe v. X.AI Corp. cases in W.D. Ark., NAACP v. X.AI in the Fifth Circuit, Carter v. X.AI Corp. in W.D. Tenn., Mueller v. X.AI Corp. in N.D. Ill., Saylor v. X.AI Corp. in C.D. Cal. and Al-Khatahtbeh v. X.AI Corp. in N.D. Cal. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: XBOW raises US$120M Series C at a valuation above US$1 billion
events.summary: XBOW announced a US$120M Series C led by DFJ Growth and Northzone, with Sofina, Alkeon Capital, Altimeter, NFDG Ventures and Sequoia Capital. SecurityWeek reported a valuation above US$1 billion and US$237M raised in total.

events.headline: XBOW adds US$35M to its Series C from strategic investors
events.summary: XBOW announced a further US$35M of Series C financing from Accenture Ventures, DNX Ventures, Liberty Global Tech Ventures, NVentures (the venture arm of NVIDIA), Samsung Ventures and SentinelOne S Ventures. SecurityWeek reported total funding of more than US$270M.

events.headline: XBOW and Onapsis report 14 jointly found SAP vulnerabilities fixed in SAP's November patch day
events.summary: XBOW said on its blog on 2026-11-13 that 14 of the 36 vulnerabilities Onapsis Research Labs helped SAP fix in the November 2026 Security Patch Day were found in collaboration with XBOW, across seven SAP Security Notes for SAP NetWeaver components. The most severe, CVE-2026-109803, is rated CVSS 9.9. The post describes a research collaboration and does not announce a formal commercial agreement.

events.headline: Schwarz Group acquires majority stake in XM Cyber
events.summary: Schwarz Group, the German retail group, announced it had acquired a majority stake in XM Cyber, which would continue to operate independently under its own brand. Schwarz did not disclose the price; TechCrunch and SecurityWeek reported US$700M.

events.headline: Schwarz Digits, XM Cyber and SentinelOne deepen security alliance
events.summary: Schwarz Digits, XM Cyber and SentinelOne announced a deeper partnership to offer a combined security suite running on Schwarz Digits' STACKIT cloud, with XM Cyber's platform already available to German-based companies through STACKIT.

events.headline: XM Cyber links external attack surface discovery to internal validation
events.summary: XM Cyber announced enhanced external attack surface management that checks whether an external exposure is exploitable in the customer's environment and models onward attack paths to critical assets.

events.headline: CrowdStrike agrees to buy XM Cyber's intellectual property
events.summary: CrowdStrike announced a definitive agreement to acquire XM Cyber's intellectual property, including more than 45 patents and source code, alongside an expanded partnership with Schwarz Digits. It said it would acquire no revenue or customers and that XM Cyber would continue as a standalone business under a licence, supporting existing customers.

events.headline: CrowdStrike completes purchase of XM Cyber's technology assets
events.summary: CrowdStrike's registration statement filed on 2026-09-11 states that it completed its acquisition of the technology assets of XM Cyber Ltd. on 8 September 2026 and issued 2,118,022 Class A shares to an affiliate within Schwarz Digits. The cash component is not stated in the filing.

events.headline: Federal docket shows suit against XM Cyber, Inc. removed to C.D. Cal.
events.summary: According to a federal docket indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Ryan Stark v. XM Cyber, Inc. was opened on 2026-08-28 in the Central District of California (5:26-cv-04964) by a notice of removal. The nature of suit is not shown and the claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Yubico shares begin trading on Nasdaq Stockholm's main market
events.summary: Yubico's investor pages state that its share has been listed on Nasdaq Stockholm since 2024-12-05, following approval announced on 2024-11-28. The investor site also carries a section on an earlier listing on Nasdaq First North Growth Market. A change of listing venue, not of control.

events.headline: Yubico discloses a low-severity FIDO protocol conformance flaw in YubiKey firmware
events.summary: Yubico published advisory YSA-2025-02 (CVE-2025-29991) on 2025-04-02: YubiKey 5 Series, 5 FIPS Series, Bio Series and Security Key Series firmware 5.4.1 to 5.7.3 checked only a 16-byte signature where FIDO PIN/UV Auth Protocol Two requires 32 bytes. Yubico rated it Low (CVSS 2.2), reported no known exploitation and said firmware 5.7.4, released 2025-04-01, addresses it.

events.headline: Yubico chief executive steps down; chief operating officer becomes acting CEO
events.summary: Yubico announced on 2025-12-17 that chief executive Mattias Danielsson was stepping down after about sixteen years with the company and that chief operating officer Jerrod Chong had been appointed acting CEO.

events.headline: Yubico starts cost saving programme including employee reductions
events.summary: Yubico announced on 2026-03-26, with preliminary first-quarter estimates, that it had started a cost saving programme during the quarter including employee reductions in its global workforce. Its interim report for the third quarter of 2026 says the programme was completed earlier in the year and shows 506 employees at 2026-09-30 against 536 a year earlier. The number of roles cut was not stated in the pages read.

events.headline: Jerrod Chong appointed chief executive of Yubico
events.summary: Yubico's investor press release list shows the release 'Jerrod Chong appointed CEO of Yubico' dated 2026-05-04; the third-quarter 2026 report is signed by him as President and CEO.

events.headline: YubiKey 5 Cryptographic Module validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 2
events.summary: The NIST Cryptographic Module Validation Program lists certificate #5291 for the YubiKey 5 Cryptographic Module (Yubico, Inc.), FIPS 140-3 overall Level 2, validated on 2026-05-22 and active until 2031-05-21.

events.headline: Yubico unveils YubiID identity platform in early access and a post-quantum-ready YubiKey in public beta
events.summary: In a release for its Capital Markets Day on 2026-11-19, Yubico said YubiID, a digital identity platform extending the company into software and lifecycle services, is in limited early access with design partners, and that a next-generation, post-quantum-ready YubiKey is in public beta. It restated the financial targets adopted on 2026-11-05: average annual net sales growth of 15-20% over five years and an EBIT margin moving toward 20% by 2031.

events.headline: Zafran Security raises US$60 million Series C led by Menlo Ventures
events.summary: SecurityWeek and SiliconANGLE reported that Zafran raised a US$60 million Series C led by Menlo Ventures, with Sequoia Capital, Cyberstarts, PSP Growth, Vintage Investment Partners and Knollwood Investment, bringing total funding to US$130 million. Alongside the round the company introduced Agentic Exposure Management, which uses AI agents to check exposure to new flaws, propose mitigations and find the owner of a vulnerable system.

events.headline: Zafran launches Attack Chain Killswitch with Google Threat Intelligence
events.summary: Zafran announced Attack Chain Killswitch, which draws multi-step attack paths across cloud and on-premises systems using Google Threat Intelligence and Mandiant investigations, scores each chain and points to the mitigation or fix that breaks the most chains. Choosing a fix creates a work item routed to the owner in a ticketing tool. Availability was not stated.

events.headline: Zafran announces Offensive Validation, AI-agent attack testing for its exposure platform
events.summary: Zafran announced Offensive Validation on its website on 2026-11-18 as a new part of its exposure management platform. Zafran says AI agents test internal and internet-facing assets to show which exposures are actually exploitable, check whether mitigations and fixes hold, and run inside isolated sandboxes under customer-set rules of engagement. The post does not state whether the feature is generally available or give pricing.

events.headline: Zenity raises $125 million Series C led by Norwest
events.summary: Zenity announced a US$125 million Series C led by Norwest, with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Qumra Capital, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joining existing investors Vertex Ventures, Third Point Ventures, DTCP and Intel Capital. SiliconANGLE put total funding at US$185 million. Fortune reported that the chief executive declined to give a valuation.

events.headline: Zenity adds incident correlation and agentic browser coverage
events.summary: Help Net Security reported on 2025-12-04 that Zenity had added an Issues view that correlates posture findings and run-time anomalies into incidents, coverage of agentic browsers including ChatGPT Atlas and Perplexity Comet through its device agent, and an open-source tool named Safe Harbor.

events.headline: Zenity Labs launches AI Total, a free service that tests agent skills in a sandbox
events.summary: Zenity announced AI Total, a free threat-intelligence service from Zenity Labs that runs AI agent skills in a sandbox and reports a verdict based on observed behaviour. The announcement presents it as separate from the commercial platform and says other AI supply-chain components are planned.

events.headline: Zero Networks raises US$55 million Series C led by Highland Europe
events.summary: Zero Networks announced a US$55 million Series C on 2025-06-03, led by Highland Europe with F2 Venture Capital, PICO Venture Partners, Venrock and U.S. Venture Partners, taking total funding to more than US$100 million. A Highland Europe principal joined the board.

events.headline: Zero Networks extends its microsegmentation to Kubernetes
events.summary: Zero Networks announced on 2025-10-28 extended Kubernetes microsegmentation using eBPF and native Kubernetes controls, with discovery of workloads and services and central management of segmentation rules. The release did not state general availability.

events.headline: Zero Networks announces Network Map 2.0
events.summary: Help Net Security reported on 2026-03-11 that Zero Networks announced Network Map 2.0, a continuously updated map of asset-to-asset communication across on-premises, cloud, IoT/OT and Kubernetes environments, with policy simulation before rollout.

events.headline: Zero Networks launches AI Segmentation for AI agents and services
events.summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 2026-04-21 that Zero Networks launched AI Segmentation, platform capabilities for identity-based control of AI agents, limits on AI-driven lateral movement and a natural-language compliance and risk engine, available as part of the platform.

events.headline: Haveli Investments completes take-private acquisition of ZeroFox
events.summary: ZeroFox Holdings announced on 13 May 2024 that Haveli Investments, a private equity firm based in Austin, Texas, had completed its acquisition of the company. Stockholders received US$1.14 per share in cash and the shares and warrants were delisted from Nasdaq. SecurityWeek had reported the agreement on 6 February 2024 with an enterprise value of roughly US$350 million. The company continues to trade under its own name. Recorded although older than 24 months because it changed the vendor's ownership.

events.headline: ZeroFox sells its IDX breach response subsidiary to Kingswood Capital Management
events.summary: ZeroFox announced on 25 November 2024 that it had sold its subsidiary IDX, a breach response and notification business acquired in 2022, to Kingswood Capital Management, with the deal signed and closed on 22 November 2024. The company said the sale let it concentrate on digital risk protection, threat intelligence and attack surface management. No price was given.

events.headline: ZeroFox appoints a new chief technology officer and chief revenue officer
events.summary: ZeroFox announced on 2 December 2025 that Shon Myatt had joined as chief technology officer and Kyle Novellano as chief revenue officer. The release did not say what happened to their predecessors.

events.headline: ZeroFox finance chief Andrew McKenna also becomes chief operating officer
events.summary: ZeroFox announced on 12 February 2026 that its chief financial officer, Andrew McKenna, had taken the combined role of chief operating officer and chief financial officer. He joined the company in 2024.

events.headline: ZeroFox and Reality Defender integrate deepfake detection into ZeroFox's platform
events.summary: ZeroFox and Reality Defender announced on 2 June 2026 an integration in which Reality Defender's API returns verdicts on whether voice, video and images are AI-generated inside the ZeroFox platform, for use by analysts in investigations and takedowns.

events.headline: ZeroFox launches AI Analytics for reporting inside its platform
events.summary: ZeroFox announced on 11 June 2026 a platform feature called AI Analytics, with interactive dashboards on alert trends and takedown outcomes, a plain-language query assistant, and scheduled PDF and CSV reports.

events.headline: ZeroFox launches the HNTR platform and HNTR Executive Protection
events.summary: ZeroFox announced on 28 July 2026 the general availability of HNTR, which it described as a new AI-first platform bringing its digital risk protection and threat intelligence together, and of HNTR Executive Protection as the first application on it. SiliconANGLE reported the launch the same day. The vendor's site now presents its solutions under the HNTR platform name.

events.headline: US Commerce Department adds Zhipu companies to the Entity List
events.summary: According to the US Consolidated Screening List published by the Department of Commerce, Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology Co., Ltd. (also listed as Zhipu AI and Beijing Knowledge Atlas Technology Co., Ltd.) and six affiliated Zhipu companies were added to the Bureau of Industry and Security Entity List with effect from 16 January 2025 (90 FR 4617). A licence is required for all items subject to the Export Administration Regulations, with a presumption of denial.

events.headline: Zhipu lists H shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange
events.summary: The company's H shares were first listed on the Main Board of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 8 January 2026 under stock code 2513, according to its interim results announcement. It was then named Knowledge Atlas Technology Joint Stock Company Limited.

events.headline: Zhipu completes placing of new H shares raising about HK$31.4 billion net
events.summary: The company's interim results announcement states that a placing of up to 19,780,000 new H shares at HK$1,588 each, agreed on 9 July 2026, completed on 13 July 2026 with net proceeds of about HK$31,374.95 million.

events.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3
events.summary: Z.ai's release notes list GLM-5.3 on 18 August 2026 and GLM-5.3-Flash on 26 August 2026. Weights for both are published on Hugging Face, and the interim results announcement says a coding subscription was opened to all users at the same time.

events.headline: US agencies' advisory names Z.AI among China-based companies alleged to have distilled US models
events.summary: CISA, the NSA and the FBI published advisory AA26-251A on 8 September 2026. It names Z.AI among six China-based companies and alleges that by mid-2026 it had distilled billions of tokens of output from US companies' models to develop its model's reasoning, in breach of those companies' terms. The advisory is an allegation by the agencies; no response from the company was found.

events.headline: Zilliz announces SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for its cloud service
events.summary: In a press release dated 2025-08-11 Zilliz announced SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certifications, participation in the EU-US Data Privacy Framework with the UK extension and Swiss framework, and what it called readiness for HIPAA workloads. The release names no auditor and gives no certificate dates.

events.headline: Milvus project publishes critical authentication bypass in Milvus Proxy (CVE-2025-64513)
events.summary: The Milvus project published security advisory GHSA-mhjq-8c7m-3f7p on 2025-11-10, rated critical. It stated that an unauthenticated attacker could bypass authentication in the Milvus Proxy and gain full administrative access to a cluster. Versions before 2.4.24, 2.5.21 and 2.6.5 were affected and those versions carry the fix. The advisory does not say whether the flaw was exploited and does not mention Zilliz Cloud.

events.headline: Zilliz Cloud adds a Business Critical plan with customer-managed keys and cross-region recovery
events.summary: A Zilliz blog post dated 2025-11-12 introduced the Business Critical plan for Zilliz Cloud, with customer-managed encryption keys, global clusters with multi-region replicas and failover, full-path encryption in transit, and support for business associate agreements. Pricing is by quote.

events.headline: Milvus project publishes critical unauthenticated access flaw on metrics port (CVE-2026-26190)
events.summary: The Milvus project published security advisory GHSA-7ppg-37fh-vcr6 on 2026-02-11, rated critical with a CVSS score of 9.8. It stated that Milvus exposed TCP port 9091 by default with a debug endpoint protected by a predictable default token and a REST API registered without authentication. Versions before 2.5.27 and 2.6.0 to 2.6.9 were affected; 2.5.27 and 2.6.10 carry the fix. The advisory does not cite observed attacks and does not mention Zilliz Cloud.

events.headline: Zilliz launches Vector Lakebase in public preview on Zilliz Cloud
events.summary: Zilliz announced Vector Lakebase on 2026-06-10 as a Zilliz Cloud release in public preview. It adds on-demand search, batch analytics and search over tables in a customer's external data lake to the vector database, on storage held in object stores. Blocks & Files reported on 2026-06-15 that it understood the offering to be available on Zilliz Cloud only.

events.headline: Zilliz announces Milvus 3.0
events.summary: Zilliz's news page lists the announcement of Milvus 3.0, described as making the open-source database lake-native, on 2026-08-01. The project's release page showed 3.0.6 as the latest release and a continuing 2.6 line when read on 2026-11-21.

events.headline: Milvus project publishes six advisories on missing authentication and authorization checks
events.summary: The Milvus project's advisory list showed six advisories published on 2026-10-28, two rated high and four rated moderate, the latter covering access-control checks on telemetry, import-job, collection-description and statistics interfaces. The two high advisories were read: GHSA-gg6q-4562-83ww states that legacy REST routes on the metrics port authenticated callers but skipped role checks (versions 2.6.10 to before 2.6.25 and 3.0.0 to before 3.0.3; fixed in 2.6.25 and 3.0.3), and GHSA-hr46-v5qw-wr2q states that two streaming gRPC methods on the proxy could be reached without credentials (versions 2.6.2 to 2.6.22 and 3.0.0; fixed in 2.6.23 and 3.0.1). Neither cites observed attacks or mentions Zilliz Cloud. A further moderate advisory published on 2026-09-27 stated that import could bypass collection-level access control. The four moderate advisories of 2026-10-28 were read from the list only.

events.headline: Zscaler completes acquisition of Red Canary
events.summary: Zscaler's fiscal 2026 annual report records the acquisition of Red Canary, Inc., a managed detection and response company, on 1 August 2025. Red Canary was excluded from the year's internal-control assessment as a newly acquired business.

events.headline: Zscaler discloses Salesforce data access through Salesloft Drift compromise
events.summary: Zscaler disclosed on 2025-08-30 that attackers used stolen Salesloft Drift OAuth tokens to gain limited access to its Salesforce data, including business contact details, licensing information and plain-text content of some support cases. Zscaler stated that its products, services and infrastructure were not affected and that it revoked the integration and rotated tokens. The post was updated on 3 and 7 September 2025.

events.headline: Zscaler EVP of Corporate Strategy Raj Judge resigns as officer and director
events.summary: Zscaler reported in a Form 8-K that Raj Judge resigned as an officer and as a member of the board on 15 April 2026, with his departure from the company effective 31 July 2026.

events.headline: Zscaler acquires Symmetry Systems
events.summary: Zscaler's fiscal 2026 annual report records the acquisition of Symmetry Systems, Inc., dating the related share issuance to 27 May 2026. The report also lists SPLXAI Inc. and SquareX Holdings, Inc. as businesses acquired during the fiscal year.

events.headline: Zscaler announces restructuring cutting about 3% of headcount
events.summary: Zscaler disclosed in a Form 8-K filed on 2026-09-03 that on 2026-09-01 it committed to a plan to restructure and reduce its workforce by approximately 3% worldwide, with expected charges of US$30.0M to US$33.0M, saying resources would be reallocated to AI and growth initiatives.

events.headline: Zscaler names Ross Tackett Chief Revenue Officer, succeeding Mike Rich
events.summary: Zscaler reported in a Form 8-K dated 24 September 2026 that Ross Tackett would become Chief Revenue Officer on 1 October 2026, succeeding Mike Rich, who stays as an adviser until 31 December 2026.

events.headline: Federal dockets show employment and patent suits filed against Zscaler in 2025-2026
events.summary: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): Ulrick v. Zscaler, Inc., an employment civil-rights suit, was filed on 2026-10-12 in S.D. Ind.; patent suits were filed by Congruent Media Resourcing LLC on 2026-08-10 (N.D. Tex.), StealthPath IP Inc. on 2025-12-08 (E.D. Tex.) and UMBRA Technologies Ltd. on 2025-10-23 (E.D. Tex.). None shows a termination date. The claims were not reviewed.

events.headline: Zscaler acquires AI red-teaming company SPLX
events.summary: Zscaler announced on 2025-11-03 that it had acquired SPLX, a company founded in 2023 that offered AI asset discovery, automated AI red teaming, run-time guardrails and prompt hardening. The price was not disclosed. SecurityWeek reported that SPLX had raised US$9 million. Zscaler said the technology would be added to its Zero Trust Exchange platform.
